merged.title: Distribution of primes, error terms, zero-free regions, explicit formulas, oscillation
merged.summary:
Verified (PDF text or page opened): PNT (Hadamard, de la Vallee Poussin 1896), the 1899 error term, Vinogradov-Korobov-type regions with Ford's 57.54/49.13, MTY 55.241 and 5.558691, Bellotti-Trudgian-Yang 2026 (4.896, arXiv 2603.21490 exists), RH <=> psi(x)-x = O(x^{1/2+eps}), Littlewood Omega_pm, Rubinstein-Sarnak, Beurling counterexamples (Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer, Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas).
Corrections to your memory list: (a) von Koch's equivalence is stated in the literature for pi(x)=li(x)+O(sqrt(x) log x) (Acta Math 24, 1901); Ng 2025 dates the psi(x)-x=O(sqrt(x) log^2 x) consequence '1905' while citing the 1901 paper, so the year is a source conflict. (b) Ford's explicit regions: MTY say 'in 2000 Ford', Ford's arXiv v5 is dated 2025 with corrections, published 2002; year is a source conflict. (c) Rubinstein-Sarnak density 0.9959 is confirmed only via Fiorilli-Martin (secondary).
Structural finding: nothing in this domain gives a SIGN of <v,Kv> without going through zeros. Size results (PNT, zero-free regions, BHP, Buthe) are lossy; exact identities (Riemann-von Mangoldt, Guinand-Weil, Landau-Gonek) contain the zero sum, hence circular; sign results (Littlewood, Rubinstein-Sarnak) concern error terms and use zeros or are conditional on GRH+LI.
Named barrier (BARRIER item last): Beurling systems with regular N(x) = cx + O(x^theta) and primes with only the dlVP error exist (DMV 2006), also systems with RH for primes (Zhang 2007, Broucke et al 2020). Any property true for all Beurling systems cannot decide RH; a usable tool must use the Gamma factor/functional equation or the integers' arithmetic (Vinogradov exponential sums).
Best SIGN candidate in this domain: the de la Vallee Poussin positivity 3+4cos t+cos 2t = 2(1+cos t)^2 >= 0 applied to sum Lambda(n) n^{-sigma}(...) (T1, T3, T4-termwise, T5-three shifts, T7 all OK), but it only yields zero-free regions near sigma=1, a size statement, and Beurling-universal (DMV realise exactly that region). Its generalisations (Stechkin, Heath-Brown smoothed weights) are positive-definite kernels on shifts log n, the same structure as K; they do not reach sigma=1/2.
Not checked in this domain pass: Green-Tao, Bombieri-Vinogradov, Zhang/Maynard (other domains).

items.name: Prime Number Theorem (Hadamard, de la Vallee Poussin 1896)
items.statement: pi(x) ~ x/log x, equivalently psi(x) ~ x and theta(x) ~ x; proved independently in 1896 via non-vanishing of zeta on Re s = 1.
items.authors_year: J. Hadamard; C.-J. de la Vallee Poussin, 1896
items.quote_or_locator: "The theorem was proved independently by Jacques Hadamard" and "Charles Jean de la Vallee Poussin in 1896 using ideas introduced by Bernhard Riemann". Equivalence psi(x) ~ x, theta(x) ~ x: Platt-Trudgian arXiv:1407.1914 intro, 'The relation (1) is equivalent to psi(x) ~ x, and theta(x) ~ x'.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 yes (prime side after the zero-free input), T2 yes, T7 yes; fails T3 (asymptotic, no sign), T4 (o(x) loss), T5, T6. For Beurling systems PNT needs an extra condition on N: Debruyne-Schlage-Puchta-Vindas arXiv:1505.04174: N(x)=ax+O(x/log^gamma x), gamma>3/2 'suffices for the PNT'.
items.relevance: Gives only leading-order size of the prime side; gives no sign for <v,Kv> and is far too lossy for margins 1e-29.
items.corrected_statement: pi(x) ~ x/log x (equivalently psi(x) ~ x, theta(x) ~ x), proved independently by Hadamard and de la Vallee Poussin in 1896. PROVEN. Primary papers not opened; dating is from Wikipedia. Beurling note stands: DSV state gamma>3/2 'suffices for the PNT'.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (primary papers not opened; secondary source only)
items.check_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_number_theorem : 'proved independently by Jacques Hadamard and Charles Jean de la Vallee Poussin in 1896'. Platt-Trudgian arXiv:1407.1914 (opened as PDF) line 37: 'The relation (1) is equivalent to ...' psi/theta. DSV arXiv:1505.04174 intro: 'where a > 0 and gamma > 3/2, suffices for the PNT'.

items.name: de la Vallee Poussin error term (1899) and its optimality for Beurling systems
items.statement: pi(x) = Li(x) + O(x exp(-a sqrt(log x))) for some a>0; zeta has no zeros for sigma >= 1 - c/log|t|.
items.authors_year: C.-J. de la Vallee Poussin, 1899
items.quote_or_locator: "in another paper in 1899 de la Vallee Poussin proved that" pi(x) = Li(x) + O(x e^(-a sqrt(log x))). Optimality in the Beurling setting: Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas arXiv:2004.11501 intro: DMV system 'realizes the classical de la Vallee Poussin zero-free region; in particular, the Riemann hypothesis (RH) fails for it.'
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 yes, T2 yes, T7 yes; fails T3, T4, T5, T6.
items.relevance: Shows that a property valid for every Beurling system is exactly this strength; cannot supply a sign of s_E, s_O.
items.corrected_statement: 1899: pi(x)=Li(x)+O(x exp(-a sqrt(log x))). Beurling part: holds_for_beurling_primes should be 'YES only under the regularity hypothesis N(x)=rho x+O(x^theta)' (Landau 1903 in Beurling form); DMV show this shape of error and zero-free region is optimal under that hypothesis. The 'zeta has no zeros for sigma>=1-c/log|t|' formulation is the zero-free region of the same paper family; not separately sourced here.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN; Beurling-universality conditional on (1.1) N(x)=rho x+O(x^theta)
items.check_evidence: Wikipedia PNT: 'in 1899 ... ppi(x)=Li(x)+O(x e^{-a sqrt(log x)})'. Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas arXiv:2004.11501 intro: 'The existence of such a number system proves the optimality of E. Landau's classical PNT [15], which ... states that (1.1) always implies ... pi(x)=Li(x)+O(x exp(-c sqrt(log x)))'; DMV system 'also realizes the classical de la Vallee Poussin zero-free region; in particular, the Riemann hypothesis (RH) fails for it'.

items.name: Vinogradov-Korobov-type zero-free region and PNT remainder; explicit forms (Ford, Nielsen, Mossinghoff-Trudgian-Yang)
items.statement: Exists c>0: zeta(beta+it) != 0 for 1-beta <= c/((log|t|)^{2/3}(log log|t|)^{1/3}), |t| large. Explicit: no zeros for sigma >= 1 - 1/(57.54 (log|t|)^{2/3}(log log|t|)^{1/3}), |t|>=3 (Ford); 1/49.13 for |t| large (Ford); 49.08 (Nielsen); 55.241 for |t|>=3 (Mossinghoff-Trudgian-Yang 2022). PNT remainder pi(x)=li(x)+O(x exp(-A (log x)^{3/5}(log log x)^{-1/5})), A=0.2098 (Ford, as cited on Wikipedia).
items.authors_year: Korobov; Vinogradov (years not seen in sources, 1958 UNVERIFIED); Ford 2002 (MTY say '2000'; Ford arXiv v5 dated 18 Feb 2025 with corrections); Nielsen; Mossinghoff-Trudgian-Yang 2022
items.quote_or_locator: MTY intro: "in 2000 Ford [9] ... established two explicit bounds ... no zeros of zeta(s) in the region sigma >= 1 - 1/(57.54 (log|t|)^{2/3}(log log|t|)^{1/3}), |t|>=3"; abstract: constant 55.241 for |t|>=3. Ford arXiv:1910.08205 Thm 1 / text: 'Taking B=4.45 ... gives the zero-free region (1.1) with c=1/49.13'.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 partially (proof uses upper bounds for |zeta(sigma+it)| via Vinogradov exponential sums, i.e. arithmetic of the integers, not only primes); fails T3, T4, T5, T6; T7 yes.
items.relevance: Strongest known unconditional zero-free region is still far from sigma=1/2; Beurling counterexample (DMV) shows this region is NOT a consequence of prime-like axioms, so it uses extra structure, but it is a size statement anyway.
items.corrected_statement: (a) Korobov and Vinogradov: both 1958 (Uspehi Mat. Nauk 13:185-192; Izv. AN SSSR 22:161-164) - now sourced. (b) Ford: Theorem 5 of 'Zero-free regions for the Riemann zeta function' (Urbana 2000 conference, proceedings 2002; arXiv:1910.08205v5 corrected 18 Feb 2025) gives 1/(57.54 (log|t|)^{2/3}(loglog|t|)^{1/3}) for |t|>=3. (c) The large-|t| constant 49.13 uses Ford's B=4.45 from a separate Ford result (Proc. LMS 85 (2002) 565-633); Ford's text itself calls it a 'new result [5]'. (d) Nielsen 49.08 is an arXiv preprint (2210.14130), refereed status not verified. (e) SUPERSEDED in the item: MTY Theorem 1.2 gives 48.1588 for sufficiently large |t|; Theorem 1.1 gives 55.241 for |t|>=3. (f) PNT remainder A=0.2098 (Wikipedia, citing Ford) is stated as the 'current best' in MTY, who improve it to d>=0.2123 using 48.1588 plus Pintz 1980. (g) Ford also cites Cheng: 1/990 for all |t|>=3 (older). (h) The T1-T7 / Beurling remarks are the requester's own analysis, not sourced. MTY refereed status unverified (arXiv v1, Dec 2022).
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (explicit constants: MTY 55.241 for |t|>=3; 48.1588 for large |t|; MTY not confirmed as published)
items.check_evidence: MTY arXiv:2212.06867 (PDF text): 'in 2000 Ford [9] ... established two explicit bounds'; Theorem 1.1 '55.241(log|t|)^{2/3}(loglog|t|)^{1/3} ... |t|>=3'; Theorem 1.2 'For sufficiently large |t| ... 48.1588'; 'With c = 48.1588 ... we obtain d >= 0.2123, improving on the current best value of 0.2098'; refs: 'N. M. Korobov ... 13:185-192, 1958', 'I. M. Vinogradov ... 22:161-164, 1958'. Ford arXiv:1910.08205: 'the author has a new result [5] that (1.2) holds with B = 4.45'; 'Taking B = 4.45 ... c = 1/49.13'; Theorem 5: '57.54'. Search result titles from ar5iv contained 2 zero-width spaces (harmless, no instruction).

items.name: Classical zero-free region, explicit constant R0 (Kadiri, Mossinghoff-Trudgian, MTY, Bellotti-Trudgian-Yang 2026)
items.statement: zeta(sigma+it) != 0 for sigma >= 1 - 1/(R0 log|t|). History of R0: 30.4679 (dlVP 1899), 9.645 (Rosser-Schoenfeld 1975), 8.463 (Ford 2002), 5.69693 (Kadiri 2005), 5.573412 (Mossinghoff-Trudgian), 5.558691 for |t|>=2 (MTY 2022), 4.896 for t>=3 (Bellotti-Trudgian-Yang, 23 March 2026).
items.authors_year: Bellotti, Trudgian, Yang 2026 (arXiv:2603.21490); MTY 2022 (arXiv:2212.06867)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: "we are able to prove that zeta(sigma+it) != 0 whenever t >= 3 and sigma >= 1 - 1/(4.896 log t)". Table 1 of Mossinghoff-Trudgian arXiv:1410.3926 gives the history of R0.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 yes (zero-detector sum Lambda(n) n^{-s} f(log n)), T2 yes, T5 partly (positive-definite weights in log n), T7 yes; fails T3 (region, not sign), T4, T6.
items.relevance: The Heath-Brown smoothed weight f(log n) and Stechkin pairing are positive-definite kernels on shifts log n, the same structural shape as K, but only reach sigma = 1 - O(1/log t), never sigma = 1/2. Beurling-universal (DMV realise the dlVP shape).
items.corrected_statement: R0 history confirmed: 30.4679 (dlVP 1899), 9.64591 (Rosser-Schoenfeld 1975), 8.463 (Ford 2002), 5.69693 (Kadiri 2005), 5.573412 (Mossinghoff-Trudgian, J. Number Theory 157 (2015), |t|>=2), 5.558691 (MTY, |t|>=2), 4.896 for t>=3 (Bellotti-Trudgian-Yang, arXiv 23 Mar 2026, v1). BTY is a preprint with no journal reference listed, so not refereed as far as verified. The 'holds_for_beurling_primes: YES' for explicit constants is unsourced own reasoning: explicit constants rely on bounds for zeta itself, and DMV only show the SHAPE of the region is realised.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN for MTY 2022; BTY 2026 = unrefereed preprint
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21490 : 'Zero-free regions inspired by work of Heath-Brown', Bellotti, Trudgian, Yang, Submitted 23 March 2026, journal ref none; abstract 'whenever t>=3 and sigma>=1-1/(4.896 log t)'. MT arXiv:1410.3926 Table 1: '1899 de la Vallee Poussin 30.4679; 1975 Rosser & Schoenfeld 9.64591; 2002 Ford 8.463; 2005 Kadiri 5.69693'. MTY abstract: 'sigma >= 1 - 1/(5.558691 log|t|) for |t| >= 2'.

items.name: von Koch (1901): RH <=> error term of PNT
items.statement: RH <=> pi(x) = li(x) + O(sqrt(x) log x). Equivalent forms: RH <=> psi(x) - x = O(x^{1/2+eps}) for every eps>0. RH => psi(x) - x = O(sqrt(x) log^2 x); conversely psi(x)-x=O(sqrt(x) log^2 x) implies the x^{1/2+eps} bound, hence RH.
items.authors_year: H. von Koch, Acta Math. 24 (1901) 159-182
items.quote_or_locator: Ng (2025), eq. (1.3): "The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the statement for all eps>0, (psi(x)-x)/sqrt(x) = O(x^eps)"; "In 1905, Von Koch [61] proved that RH implies (psi(x)-x)/sqrt(x) = O(log^2 x)" with [61] = 'H. von Koch, Sur la distribution des nombres premiers. Acta Math. 24, 159 (1901)'. Wikipedia PNT page: "Helge von Koch showed in 1901 ... O(sqrt(x) log x) (this last estimate is in fact equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis)".
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 yes (statement is about primes), T2 yes; fails T7 (it IS RH), T3 (size), T4 (lossy), T5, T6. SOURCE CONFLICT: Ng text says 1905 but cites the 1901 Acta paper.
items.relevance: Your memory fact is confirmed in the form 'psi(x)-x=O(sqrt(x) log^2 x) <=> RH' (equivalence holds because the weaker x^{1/2+eps} bound already implies RH). Useful only as a size equivalent; circular as a premise.
items.corrected_statement: RH <=> psi(x)-x = O(x^{1/2+eps}) for all eps>0 (Ng eq. 1.3); RH => psi(x)-x = O(sqrt(x) log^2 x) (von Koch). Hence psi(x)-x=O(sqrt(x)log^2 x) <=> RH. Source conflict is real: Ng's text says 'In 1905, Von Koch [61] proved' while his reference [61] is Acta Math. 24, 159 (1901); Wikipedia says 1901. Use 1901. The pi(x) form O(sqrt(x) log x) equivalent to RH: Wikipedia's parenthetical 'equivalent to RH' was not visible in my fetch; the equivalence is standard but its quote is unverified here.
items.check_evidence: Ng arXiv:2505.11295 (PDF): 'The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the statement for all eps>0 (psi(x)-x)/sqrt(x)=O(x^eps) (1.3)'; 'In 1905, Von Koch [61] proved that RH implies ... =O(log^2 x)'; ref '[61] H. von Koch ... Acta Math. 24, 159 (1901)'. Wikipedia PNT: 'Helge von Koch showed in 1901 that if the Riemann hypothesis is true, the error term ... O(sqrt(x) log x)'.

items.name: Schoenfeld (1976) explicit RH bounds and Lee-Nosal refinement
items.statement: Under RH: |psi(x)-x| < (1/(8 pi)) sqrt(x) log^2 x for x >= 73.2; |pi(x)-li(x)| < (1/(8 pi)) sqrt(x) log x for x >= 2657. Lee-Nosal: log^2 x replaced by log x (log x - log log x) for x >= 401211790.
items.authors_year: L. Schoenfeld, Math. Comp. 30 (1976); Lee-Nosal (year not seen, UNVERIFIED)
items.quote_or_locator: Ng (2025) intro: "Schoenfeld established an explicit version of (1.5) and obtained a bound of (1/8 pi) sqrt(x) log^2 x for x >= 73.2. Lee and Nosal [35] improved this by replacing log^2 x in Schoenfeld's result with log x(log x - log log x) for x >= 401211790." pi-version x>=2657: Wikipedia Riemann hypothesis page, 'constant of 1/(8 pi) valid for all x >= 2657'. Threshold conflict: EasyChair preprints cite x>=599 for theta(x); not peer reviewed.
items.fit_T1_T7: Conditional on RH (fails T7); T3 no.
items.relevance: Shows what RH buys on the prime side; cannot be a premise.
items.corrected_statement: Under RH: |psi(x)-x| < (1/(8 pi)) sqrt(x) log^2 x for x>=73.2 (Schoenfeld, Math. Comp. 30 (1976), 'Sharper bounds for the Chebyshev functions theta(x) and psi(x). II'); |pi(x)-li(x)| < (1/(8 pi)) sqrt(x) log x for x>=2657. Lee-Nosal: log^2 x -> log x (log x - log log x) for x>=401211790; this is arXiv:2312.05628 (Dec 2023), cited by Ng as a 'preprint', refereed status not verified.
items.check_evidence: Ng arXiv:2505.11295: 'Schoenfeld established an explicit version of (1.5) and obtained a bound of (1/8pi) sqrt(x) log^2 x for x >= 73.2. Lee and Nosal [35] improved this by replacing log^2 x ... for x >= 401211790'; ref [35] 'Lee and Nosal, Sharper bounds for the error in the prime number theorem assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, preprint, arxiv.org/abs/2312.05628'. Wikipedia RH page: '|pi(x)-li(x)| < (1/8pi) sqrt(x) log(x) for all x >= 2657'.

items.name: Buthe (2018): unconditional |psi(x)-x| <= 0.94 sqrt(x) for 11 < x <= 10^19
items.statement: |x - psi(x)| <= 0.94 sqrt(x) for 11 < x <= 10^19; hence li(x) - pi(x) > 0 on [2, 10^19]. Method: analytic algorithm using zeros up to a verified height.
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: "these imply that li(x) - pi(x) is positive for 2 <= x <= 10^19"; eq. (1.5): "|x - psi(x)| <= 0.94 [sqrt x] for 11 < x <= 10^19" (sqrt lost in text extraction).
items.fit_T1_T7: T3 partial (a sign of li-pi on a finite range) but via zeros (fails T1) and finite range (fails T2); T4 no; T7 yes.
items.relevance: Example of a proven sign on the prime side obtained by feeding zero data; finite-range, so no uniform-in-window sign for K.
items.corrected_statement: Eq. (1.5): |x-psi(x)| <= 0.94 sqrt(x) for 11<x<=10^19; li(x)-pi(x)>0 for 2<=x<=10^19; uses zeros with imaginary part up to 10^11. Journal (Math. Comp. 87 (2018) 1991-2009) not verified here. Caveat: a secondary source (Wikipedia RH page, via a summariser) says pi(x)<li(x) is known for all x<=10^25, which would exceed Buthe's range; not verified against a primary source, so treat the '10^19' as Buthe's result, not necessarily the best known range.
items.check_evidence: arXiv:1511.02032v2 abstract: 'these imply that li(x) - pi(x) is positive for 2 <= x <= 10^19'; eq. (1.5) '|x - psi(x)| <= 0.94 sqrt(x) for 11 < x <= 10^19'; line 67 'using the zeros with imaginary part up to 10^11'.

items.name: Riemann-von Mangoldt explicit formula and zero counting N(T)
items.statement: psi_0(x) = x - sum_rho x^rho/rho - log(2 pi) - (1/2) log(1 - x^{-2}), sum over nontrivial zeros in increasing |Im|. N(T) = (T/2pi) log(T/2pi) - T/2pi + O(log T); Backlund explicit: |N(T) - (T/2pi log(T/2pi) - T/2pi - 7/8)| < 0.137 log T + 0.443 log log T + 4.350 for T>2; Hasanalizade-Shen-Wong 2022: 0.1038 log T + 0.2573 log log T + 9.3675 (7/8 dropped).
items.authors_year: Riemann 1859; von Mangoldt 1895; Backlund 1914/1918; Hasanalizade-Shen-Wong 2022
items.quote_or_locator: "psi_0(x) = x - sum_rho x^rho/rho - log(2 pi) - 1/2 log(1 - x^{-2})"; "the sum over zeros is conditionally convergent and should be taken in increasing order of imaginary part". N(T) formulas: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riemann%E2%80%93von_Mangoldt_formula. Trudgian's S(T) bound |S(T)| <= 0.112 log T + 0.278 log log T + 2.510 (J. Number Theory 134 (2014), arXiv:1208.5846; constants per search listing, not opened).
items.fit_T1_T7: T4 yes (exact identity), T2 yes, T7 yes; fails T1 (contains the zeros), T3 (no sign), T5/T6 as such.
items.relevance: This is the left=right identity behind <v,Kv> = sum F_v(z)^2 in a one-point form. A sign proved on the prime side of it is by construction the sign of the zero sum: circularity, exactly the repeated failure mode.
items.corrected_statement: N(T) = (T/2pi) log(T/2pi e) + 7/8 + S(T) + O(1/T), i.e. the 7/8 enters with PLUS sign: |N(T) - (T/2pi)log(T/2pi e) - 7/8| <= bound. The item's '- 7/8' is a sign error. The constants '0.137 log T + 0.443 loglog T + 4.350' are Backlund's 1918 bound for |S(T)| (T0=200), NOT for the N(T) remainder; in the N(T) form with 7/8 absorbed the HSW table lists Backlund 1918 as 0.137, 0.443, 5.225. Trudgian: arXiv preprint has 0.111/0.275/2.450 for |S(T)|; published JNT 134 (2014) has 0.112/0.278/2.510 (the latter per search-result metadata, not opened); HSW's table lists Trudgian 2014 for N(T) as 0.112/0.278/3.385 (=2.510+0.875). Hasanalizade-Shen-Wong: |N(T)-(T/2pi)log(T/2pi e)| <= 0.1038 log T + 0.2573 loglog T + 9.3675 for T>=e (7/8 absorbed, as the item correctly says), arXiv:2107.06506; JNT 235 (2022) 219-241 per search metadata. Newer: Bellotti-Wong arXiv:2412.15470 reportedly 0.10076 log T + 0.24460 loglog T + 8.08344 (search snippet only, UNVERIFIED). psi_0 explicit formula: standard, Wikipedia page not opened by me.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (formula standard; sign and attribution of constants corrected)

items.name: Guinand-Weil explicit formula and Weil positivity criterion
items.statement: For admissible test function with Fourier/Mellin transform, sum over zeros Phi(rho) = Phi(0)+Phi(1) - (prime and prime-power sum) + archimedean integral. Weil: RH <=> the quadratic functional (prime sum + archimedean terms) is >= 0 on all test functions f * f~ (Bombieri: positive semidefinite exactly when RH holds).
items.authors_year: A. Weil 1952 (explicit formula, criterion); Guinand 1948; Bombieri, Rend. Lincei 2000 'Remarks on Weil's quadratic functional in the theory of prime numbers, I'
items.quote_or_locator: Lagarias arXiv:math/0404394 sec. 3: "A. Weil [46] formulated the 'explicit formula' of prime number theory in terms of distributions ... He gave a necessary and sufficient condition for the Riemann hypothesis in terms of the positivity of a quadratic functional on a suitable space of test functions". Test-function form of the formula: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Explicit_formulae_for_L-functions. Bombieri abstract (via search listing, not opened): functional 'positive semidefinite exactly when RH holds'.
items.fit_T1_T7: T4 yes, T2 yes; fails T7 (is RH) and T1 as an argument; uses the functional equation (Gamma factor), so not Beurling-universal.
items.relevance: This is exactly the project's object <v,Kv>. Confirms that the target statement is RH-equivalent and any sign on the left is, via the identity, a statement about zeros.
items.corrected_statement: Weil formulated the explicit formula in terms of distributions and gave a necessary and sufficient condition for RH as positivity of a quadratic functional on test functions (RH_EQUIVALENT). Bombieri, Rend. Mat. Acc. Lincei Ser. IX 11 (2000) 183-233 confirmed as reference. Bombieri's 'positive semidefinite exactly when RH holds' wording and 'Guinand 1948' were not opened: UNVERIFIED in detail. Beurling-universality 'NO' is own reasoning.
items.check_evidence: Lagarias arXiv:math/0404394 sec. 3 (PDF): 'A. Weil [46] formulated the explicit formula of prime number theory in terms of distributions ... He gave a necessary and sufficient condition for the Riemann hypothesis in terms of the positivity of a quadratic functional on a suitable space of test functions'; ref '[3] E. Bombieri, Remarks on Weil's quadratic functional in the theory of prime numbers I, Rend. Mat. Acc. Lincei, Ser. IX, 11 (2000), 183-233'.

items.name: Landau-Gonek formula: prime-power Lambda(X) as a sum over zeros
items.statement: For fixed X>1: sum_{0<gamma<=T} X^rho = -(T/2pi) Lambda(X) + O(log T) as T->infinity (Landau 1911); Gonek (1985) uniform version in X,T>1 with error O(X log(2XT) log log 3X) plus terms depending on distance of X to the nearest other prime power.
items.authors_year: E. Landau 1911; S. M. Gonek 1985
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract (Durkan-Hughes-Pearce-Crump 2026): "The Landau--Gonek Theorem evaluates X^rho summed over the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Their result shows great sensitivity to the arithmetic nature of X." The displayed formula with -(T/2pi)Lambda(X)+O(log T) was seen in a search-result snippet, not opened in the full text: UNVERIFIED in detail.
items.fit_T1_T7: T5 yes in spirit (individual primes detected through zero sums), T2 yes; fails T1 (zeros), T3 (no sign), T4 (asymptotic, error O(log T)).
items.relevance: Shows primes appear as the 'resonances' of the zero sum; supports the dual picture but no sign mechanism.
items.corrected_statement: Landau: for fixed X>1, sum_{0<gamma<=T} X^rho = -(T/2pi)Lambda(X) + O(log T). Gonek made it uniform in X,T>1 with error O(X log(2XT) loglog(3X)) plus further terms. Date nuance: DHP-C label the theorem 'Landau, 1911' while their reference is Math. Ann. 71 (1912) 548-564; Gonek's uniform theorem is labelled 1985 there, with Gonek's related papers Invent. Math. 75 (1984) and Contemp. Math. (1993). The formula is now verified verbatim in the full text (item previously flagged unverified).
items.check_evidence: arXiv:2601.18025 (PDF): 'Theorem 1 (Landau, 1911). Given fixed X > 1 we have sum_{0<gamma<=T} X^rho = -(T/2pi) Lambda(X) + O(log T)'; 'Gonek [11,12] made Landau's Theorem uniform'; 'Theorem 2 (Gonek, 1985). Uniformly for X,T>1 ... items.name: Littlewood (1914): Omega_pm oscillation and sign changes of pi(x)-li(x), psi(x)-x; effective first sign change
items.statement: pi(x) - li(x) = Omega_pm( sqrt(x) log log log x / log x ) and psi(x) - x = Omega_pm( sqrt(x) log log log x ); hence both change sign infinitely often. Best effective: a sign change of pi(x)-li(x) occurs below 1.3971e316 (Saouter-Trudgian-Demichel 2015, Math. Comp. 84, 2433-2446); pi(x)<li(x) for 2<x<=1e14 (Kotnik) and by Buthe up to 1e19. theta(x)-x: x < exp(727.951332668) with theta(x)>x (Platt-Trudgian 2016).
items.authors_year: J. E. Littlewood, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 158 (1914); Skewes 1933/1955 (effective); Saouter-Trudgian-Demichel 2015
items.quote_or_locator: Platt-Trudgian intro: "Littlewood [10], showed that pi(x)-li(x) and psi(x)-x change sign infinitely often. Indeed ... pi(x)-li(x) = Omega_pm( x^{1/2} / log x * log log log x ), psi(x)-x = Omega_pm( x^{1/2} log log log x )"; "the best known result is that there must be a sign change less than 1.3971e316 [17]. On the other hand Kotnik [8] showed that pi(x) < li(x) for all 2 < x <= 1e14."
items.fit_T1_T7: T3 yes (sign changes) but of the error term, not of K; fails T1 (proof uses zeta zeros and Dirichlet simultaneous approximation), T2, T4, T5, T6; T7 yes (unconditional).
items.relevance: A genuine unconditional oscillation sign, but it says the error term is large somewhere with both signs; it is the zero sum being 'not one-signed', opposite in spirit to the one-signed sum needed for K >= 0.
items.corrected_statement: Littlewood 1914: pi(x)-li(x)=Omega_pm(x^{1/2} logloglog x / log x), psi(x)-x=Omega_pm(x^{1/2} logloglog x). Best effective: sign change below 1.3971e316 (Saouter-Trudgian-Demichel 2015; STD paper itself not opened, number via Platt-Trudgian; other search sources quote 1.39822e316 Bays-Hudson 2000 and 1.397166e316 Smith 2016 thesis). Kotnik: pi(x)<li(x) for 2<x<=1e14; Buthe to 1e19. Platt-Trudgian: exists x<exp(727.951332668) with theta(x)>x. See Buthe caveat on possibly larger verified range.
items.check_evidence: Platt-Trudgian arXiv:1407.1914 (PDF): 'there is an x < exp(727.951332668) for which theta(x) > x'; 'the best known result is that there must be a sign change less that 1.3971 * 10^316 [17]. On the other hand Kotnik [8] showed that pi(x) < li(x) for all 2 < x <= 10^14'; Ng arXiv:2505.11295 (1.6): 'in 1914 Littlewood proved psi(x)-x / sqrt(x) = Omega_pm(logloglog x)'.

items.name: Rubinstein-Sarnak (1994): Chebyshev's bias
items.statement: Under GRH and the Grand Simplicity Hypothesis (imaginary parts of zeros of primitive Dirichlet L-functions linearly independent over Q), the logarithmic density delta(q;a,b) of {x: pi(x;q,a) > pi(x;q,b)} exists, lies strictly in (0,1), exceeds 1/2 iff a is a nonresidue and b a residue; delta(q;a,b)+delta(q;b,a)=1; delta=1/2 if a,b both squares or both nonsquares. Numerics: delta(4;3,1) approx 0.9959.
items.authors_year: M. Rubinstein, P. Sarnak, Experimental Math. 3 (1994) 173-197
items.quote_or_locator: Fiorilli-Martin arXiv:0912.4908 intro: "Rubinstein and Sarnak investigated these densities under the following two hypotheses: GRH ... LI"; "Rubinstein and Sarnak showed (assuming GRH and LI) that delta(q;b,a)+delta(q;a,b)=1"; later in the text: "Rubinstein and Sarnak [14] calculated that delta(4;N,R)=delta(4;3,1) approx 0.9959." Original paper not opened (Project Euclid blocked); statements are via Fiorilli-Martin and Granville-Martin arXiv:math/9910184.
items.fit_T1_T7: T3 yes (a bias sign), T5 yes (uses independence of zeros of different L-functions); fails T1 (zeros), T4 (density, not identity), T7 (GRH + LI).
items.relevance: A prime-race sign phenomenon driven by the 'k^2 term' of the explicit formula (prime powers p^2), the closest thing in the literature to a sign from prime-power correlation; but conditional and statistical.
items.corrected_statement: Under GRH + LI, logarithmic densities delta(q;a,b) exist, delta(q;a,b)+delta(q;b,a)=1, delta(4;3,1) approx 0.9959. Verified through Fiorilli-Martin, not the original (Experiment. Math. 3 (1994) 173-197 not opened). The detailed 'iff a nonresidue and b residue' wording is for the simple cases and was not checked verbatim.
items.check_evidence: Fiorilli-Martin arXiv:0912.4908 (PDF) line 126: 'Rubinstein and Sarnak showed (assuming GRH and ...)'; line 2799: 'Rubinstein and Sarnak [14] calculated that delta(4; N, R) = delta(4; 3, 1) approx 0.9959.'

items.name: de la Vallee Poussin positivity 3 + 4cos t + cos 2t >= 0 as a sign device
items.statement: 3 + 4cos(t) + cos(2t) = 2(1+cos t)^2 >= 0. For sigma>1: Re[3(-zeta'/zeta)(sigma) + 4(-zeta'/zeta)(sigma+it) + (-zeta'/zeta)(sigma+2it)] = sum_n Lambda(n) n^{-sigma}(3+4cos(t log n)+cos(2t log n)) >= 0, with -zeta'/zeta = sum Lambda(n) n^{-s} and a pole of zeta at s=1; this gives zeta(1+it) != 0 and the classical zero-free region. General class: even trigonometric polynomials f = sum a_k cos(k phi) >= 0 with a_k >= 0, a_1 > a_0.
items.authors_year: de la Vallee Poussin 1896/1899 (polynomial (1+cos phi)^2); Mertens (the 3-4-1 inequality, attribution UNVERIFIED); Landau 1908, Stechkin 1970, Kondrat'ev 1977, Heath-Brown
items.quote_or_locator: Mossinghoff-Trudgian: "f(phi) >= 0 for all real phi, each coefficient a_k is nonnegative, and a_1 > a_0. For example, de la Vallee Poussin used the polynomial (1+cos phi)^2 = 3/2 + 2cos phi + cos 2phi." Dirichlet-series form: Bellotti-Trudgian-Yang arXiv:2603.21490 intro: "for sigma>1 we have -zeta'(s)/zeta(s) = sum Lambda(n) n^{-s} ... uses the fact that zeta(s) has a pole at s=1 to show that there are no zeroes on the line sigma=1". The factorisation 2(1+cos t)^2 is elementary algebra (checked by hand).
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 yes (prime side only), T2 yes (every t), T3 yes (termwise sign), T4 yes (exact termwise identity), T5 yes (correlates three shifts 0, t, 2t of log n, i.e. a positive-definite kernel on shifts), T7 yes; fails T6 (no pole-type rank-2 term handled) and, critically, only reaches Re s >= 1 - c/log t. Beurling-universality: argument uses only Lambda_P >= 0 and a pole at 1 (own reasoning, UNVERIFIED), consistent with DMV realising exactly this region.
items.relevance: The prototype of what is wanted: a lossless termwise sign from prime data alone. Its Beurling-universality says it cannot reach sigma=1/2; any lift to K >= 0 must add an ingredient that Beurling systems lack (functional equation / Gamma factor).
items.corrected_statement: The item's own identity 3+4cos t+cos2t = 2(1+cos t)^2 is correct (hand-checked: (1+cos t)^2 = 3/2+2cos t+(1/2)cos 2t). BUT the quoted line from Mossinghoff-Trudgian, '(1+cos phi)^2 = 3/2 + 2cos phi + cos 2phi', is a typo in the source (missing factor 1/2 on cos 2phi; confirmed in raw text extraction); do not quote it as written. Mertens attribution of the 3-4-1 inequality: not sourced here. The BTY intro quote and the 'Beurling-universal' claim were not checked (own reasoning).
items.check_evidence: MT arXiv:1410.3926 (PDF, raw extraction): 'de la Vallee Poussin used the polynomial (1+cos phi)^2 = 3/2 + 2 cos phi + cos 2phi' (as printed; mathematically the last term must be (1/2)cos 2phi). Conditions quoted correctly: 'f(phi) >= 0 for all real phi, each coefficient a_k is nonnegative, and a_1 > a_0'.

items.name: Mertens' theorems (1874)
items.statement: sum_{p<=x} log p / p = log x + O(1); sum_{p<=x} 1/p = log log x + beta + O(1/log x), beta = 0.26149...; prod_{p<=x} (1-1/p)^{-1} ~ e^gamma log x.
items.authors_year: F. Mertens, 1874 (Crelle 78)
items.quote_or_locator: Lichtman arXiv:2002.03361, Theorem 1.1 (Mertens, 1874): "sum_{p<=x} log p/p = log x + O(1), sum_{p<=x} 1/p = log_2 x + beta + O(1/log x) ... prod_{p<=x} (1-1/p)^{-1} ~ e^gamma log x"; "The proof is by elementary methods".
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 yes, T2 yes, T7 yes; fails T3, T4 (O(1) loss), T5, T6.
items.relevance: Controls the diagonal/first-order size of the prime sum with weights 1/p; no sign information for cross terms between different primes.
items.corrected_statement: sum_{p<=x} log p/p = log x + O(1); sum_{p<=x} 1/p = loglog x + beta + O(1/log x), beta=0.26149...; prod_{p<=x}(1-1/p)^{-1} ~ e^gamma log x. Mertens 1874 (Crelle 78) - journal citation not seen in the opened source.
items.check_evidence: Lichtman arXiv:2002.03361 Theorem 1.1 (Mertens, 1874): 'sum log p/p = log x + O(1), sum 1/p = log_2 x + beta + O(1/log x), prod (1-1/p)^{-1} ~ e^gamma log x'; 'Here beta = 0.26149... is Mertens' constant'; abstract: 'The proof is by elementary methods'.

items.name: Odlyzko-te Riele (1985): disproof of the Mertens conjecture |M(x)| < sqrt(x)
items.statement: limsup M(x) x^{-1/2} > 1.06 and liminf M(x) x^{-1/2} < -1.009, so |M(x)| < sqrt(x) fails (the conjecture would have implied RH); no explicit counterexample, proof via computation with zeros and lattice basis reduction.
items.authors_year: A. M. Odlyzko, H. J. J. te Riele, J. reine angew. Math. 357 (1985) 138-160
items.quote_or_locator: CWI report abstract: "The Mertens conjecture states that |M(x)| < x^{1/2} for all x > 1 ... its truth was known to imply the truth of the Riemann hypothesis. This paper disproves the Mertens conjecture by showing that limsup M(x) x^{-1/2} > 1.06. The disproof relies on extensive computations with the zeros of the zeta function, and does not provide an explicit counterexample." liminf < -1.009: line in the same report.
items.fit_T1_T7: Negative result: fails nothing, but shows a natural 'termwise' bound that would give RH is false.
items.relevance: Warns that simple sign/size conjectures on prime-side sums (here the Mobius sum) can be false despite implying RH; sign statements must be exact, not margin-based.
items.corrected_statement: limsup M(x)x^{-1/2} > 1.06 and liminf < -1.009; Mertens conjecture false; the disproof does not give an explicit counterexample. Journal citation (J. reine angew. Math. 357 (1985) 138-160) not visible in the CWI report text I read.
items.check_evidence: CWI report NM-R8412 https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/6447/6447D.pdf (opened): 'lim sup M(x)x^{-1/2} > 1.06' (line 43), 'lim inf M(x) x^{-1/2} < -1.009' (line 125); table rows 1.061545 and -1.009749.

items.name: Hardy (1914), Selberg (1942), Levinson (1974), Conrey, Pratt-Robles-Zaharescu-Zeindler (2020): zeros on the critical line
items.statement: Hardy 1914: infinitely many zeros on Re s = 1/2. Selberg 1942: kappa = liminf N_0(T)/N(T) > 0. Levinson 1974: kappa >= 0.3420 (first version; ~1/3). Conrey 1989: > 2/5. Pratt-Robles-Zaharescu-Zeindler: kappa slightly above 5/12 (about 41.7%).
items.authors_year: Hardy 1914; Selberg 1942; Levinson 1974; Conrey 1989; Pratt-Robles-Zaharescu-Zeindler 2020 (Res. Math. Sci. 7, art. 2; arXiv:1802.10521)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: "we increase the current lower bound of critical zeros of the Riemann zeta-function to slightly over five-twelfths". Selberg line in the paper text: "In 1942, Selberg [63] showed that 1 >= kappa > 0." Hardy and Levinson: Feng arXiv:1003.0059: "It was proved for the first time by Hardy [11] in 1914 that zeta(s) has infinitely many zeros on the critical line"; "In 1974, Levinson [14] ... kappa >= 0.3420".
items.fit_T1_T7: Zero-side only (fails T1); T3 no; T7 yes.
items.relevance: Proportion of zeros that are real-type is irrelevant to K >= 0, which needs all zeros (all F_v(z)^2 >= 0 for z real); no sign information.
items.corrected_statement: Hardy 1914, Selberg 1942 (kappa>0), Conrey 1989 (kappa>0.4088 > 2/5), PRZZ (kappa>0.417293, 'slightly over five-twelfths') are confirmed. Levinson 1974: sources disagree on the number - PRZZ says only 'kappa > 1/3'; Feng says 0.3420; another arXiv paper (via search) says 1/3 then >0.3474 in a 1975 follow-up. So 'Levinson 0.3420 first version' is UNVERIFIED/conflicting; safe form: kappa>1/3 (Levinson 1974, Adv. Math. 13 383-436, per search). Also Conrey's intermediate 1983 value 0.36581 (PRZZ). PRZZ journal 'Res. Math. Sci. 7 (2020)' not verified (PDF opened is arXiv v3, Sep 2019).
items.check_evidence: PRZZ arXiv:1802.10521: 'In 1942, Selberg showed that 1 >= kappa > 0'; 'Along with the choice Q(x)=1-x Levinson was able to prove that kappa > 1/3 in 1974'; 'unconditionally prove that theta=4/7-eps which results in kappa > 0.4088'; 'yields kappa > 0.417293'. Feng arXiv:1003.0059: 'In 1974, Levinson ... kappa >= 0.3420'.

items.name: Platt-Trudgian (2021): RH verified to height 3e12
items.statement: All nontrivial zeros beta+i gamma with 0 < gamma <= 3*10^12 satisfy beta = 1/2 (rigorous interval arithmetic).
items.authors_year: D. Platt, T. Trudgian, Bull. London Math. Soc. 53 (2021) 792-797; arXiv:2004.09765
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: "We verify numerically, in a rigorous way using interval arithmetic, that the Riemann hypothesis is true up to height 3 * 10^12. That is, all zeroes beta+i gamma of the Riemann zeta-function with 0 < gamma <= 3 * 10^12 have beta = 1/2."
items.fit_T1_T7: Finite computation; fails T2 (not uniform over windows) and T1 (zeros).
items.relevance: Gives K >= 0 only for windows whose truncated spectral data is controlled by low zeros plus tail bounds (Buthe-type); not uniform in the window.
items.corrected_statement: All zeros with 0<gamma<=3e12 have beta=1/2, rigorous interval arithmetic. Journal: Bull. London Math. Soc. 53(3) (2021) 792-797 (as cited in MTY refs).
items.check_evidence: arXiv:2004.09765 abstract (PDF): 'We verify numerically, in a rigorous way using interval arithmetic, that the Riemann hypothesis is true up to height 3*10^12.'; MTY ref [24]: 'The Riemann hypothesis is true up to 3*10^12. Bull. Lond. Math. Soc., 53(3), 792-797, 2021'.

items.name: Goldston-Montgomery (1987): pair correlation of zeros <=> variance of primes in short intervals
items.statement: On RH, uniformly for 1 <= H <= X^{1-eps}: (1/X) int_0^X ( sum_{x<n<=x+H} Lambda(n) - H )^2 dx ~ H log X (1 - log H/log X) is equivalent to Montgomery's Strong Pair Correlation Conjecture (F(alpha) ~ 1 for alpha >= 1 bounded). Montgomery (1973), on RH: F(alpha) = (T^{-2 alpha} log T + alpha)(1+o(1)) uniformly for 0 <= alpha <= 1.
items.authors_year: H. L. Montgomery 1973; D. A. Goldston, H. L. Montgomery 1987 (Progr. Math. 70, 183-203)
items.quote_or_locator: Gorodetsky arXiv:2111.00853 intro: "Goldston and Montgomery showed [7, Cor.] - on RH - that [the variance] ~ H log X (1 - log H/log X) ... uniformly for 1 <= H <= X^{1-eps} is equivalent to the Strong Pair Correlation Conjecture for the Riemann zeta function." Montgomery's alpha-range formula seen only in a search snippet (UNVERIFIED in the original).
items.fit_T1_T7: T5 yes (correlations of Lambda at different n), T2 yes; fails T7 (RH, and the stronger statement is a conjecture), T4, T3.
items.relevance: Precisely the 'correlation between different primes' channel, but it is the same information as the zero pair correlation (a duality, not an independent sign) and conditional on RH.
items.corrected_statement: On RH, the variance asymptotic ~ H log X (1 - log H/log X) uniformly for 1<=H<=X^{1-eps} is equivalent to the Strong Pair Correlation Conjecture (Goldston-Montgomery). Montgomery 1973 formula F(alpha) = (T^{-2alpha} log T + alpha)(1+o(1)) for 0<=alpha<=1 was NOT verified in an opened source (UNVERIFIED); the item itself says so.
items.corrected_status: CONDITIONAL on RH (equivalence to a conjecture)
items.check_evidence: Gorodetsky arXiv:2111.00853 (PDF) lines 37-47: 'Goldston and Montgomery showed [7, Cor.] ... uniformly for 1 <= H <= X^{1-eps} is equivalent to the Strong Pair Correlation Conjecture for the Riemann zeta function.'

items.name: Baker-Harman-Pintz (2001) primes in short intervals; Cramer (RH) prime gaps
items.statement: Unconditional: for all x > x0 the interval [x - x^0.525, x] contains primes (so p_{n+1}-p_n << p_n^0.525). Under RH: every gap p_{n+1}-p_n = O(sqrt(p_n) log p_n) (Cramer).
items.authors_year: R. C. Baker, G. Harman, J. Pintz, Proc. London Math. Soc. 83 (2001) 532-562; H. Cramer 1920
items.quote_or_locator: BHP Theorem 1: "For all x > x0, the interval [x - x^0.525, x] contains prime numbers." Intro: "Beginning with Hoheisel [8], many authors have found shorter and shorter intervals". The gap form follows from Theorem 1 (own inference). Cramer RH gap: Wikipedia Riemann hypothesis page, "Cramer proved that, assuming the Riemann hypothesis, every gap is" O(sqrt p log p).
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 partially (uses sieve plus zero-density/mean-value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials); fails T3, T4, T5, T6.
items.relevance: Existence of primes in short intervals; says nothing about signs of K, and short-interval regularity needed for K would be at the scale ~ 1/sqrt(x), far below what is proven.
items.corrected_statement: BHP Theorem 1: for all x>x0, [x-x^0.525, x] contains primes. Cramer: under RH every gap is O(sqrt(p) log p) (Wikipedia; 1920 year not seen). BHP journal (Proc. LMS 83 (2001) 532-562) not seen in the PDF. NOT the strongest current short-interval result: Guth-Maynard (below) gives asymptotics for primes in x^{17/30+o(1)} intervals - a different statement (asymptotic count, longer interval), so BHP remains the strongest unconditional EXISTENCE exponent known to me (UNVERIFIED as 'best').
items.check_evidence: BHP PDF (https://www.cs.umd.edu/~gasarch/BLOGPAPERS/BakerHarmanPintz.pdf) line 16: 'Theorem 1. For all x > x0, the interval [x - x^0.525, x] contains prime numbers.' Wikipedia RH: 'Cramer proved that, assuming the Riemann hypothesis, every gap is O(sqrt(p) log p).'

items.name: Selberg symmetry formula and the elementary proof of PNT (Erdos-Selberg 1949)
items.statement: Lambda_2(n) = log(n) Lambda(n) + sum_{d|n} Lambda(d) Lambda(n/d) satisfies (1/N) sum_{n<=N} Lambda_2(n) = 2 log N (1+o(1)); equivalently psi(x) log x + sum_{n<=x} Lambda(n) psi(x/n) = 2 x log x + O(x). Prime-only form (Erdos): sum_{p<=x} log^2 p + sum_{pq<=x} log p log q = 2 x log x + O(x). Gives an elementary proof of PNT with no complex analysis.
items.authors_year: A. Selberg 1949 (Annals of Math. 50, 1950); P. Erdos 1949
items.quote_or_locator: McNamara arXiv:2002.04007, Theorem 2.5 (Selberg symmetry formula): "The average of the second von Mangoldt function defined above is (1/N) sum_{n<=N} Lambda_2(n) = 2 log N (1 + o(1))." Sec. 1: "In 1949, Erdos [Erd49] and Selberg [Sel50] discovered an elementary proof". Erdos prime-only form seen in a search summary only (UNVERIFIED).
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 yes (zero-free), T2 yes, T5 yes (convolution Lambda*Lambda of different primes: pairs pq), T7 yes; fails T3, T4 (o(1) in the average).
items.relevance: The only classical prime-side relation that explicitly couples distinct primes without zeros; the underlying identity Lambda_2 = mu * log^2 is algebraic and lossless, but its use gives only asymptotics (size), not a sign. Whether Beurling systems satisfy it depends on assumptions on N (Beurling-Diamond-Kahane theory), not checked.
items.corrected_statement: Theorem (McNamara 2.5): (1/N) sum_{n<=N} Lambda_2(n) = 2 log N (1+o(1)) - verified verbatim. Citation fix: the item's 'Selberg 1949 (Annals of Math. 50, 1950)' is muddled. McNamara's [Sel50] is Selberg, 'An elementary proof of the prime-number theorem for arithmetic progressions', Canad. J. Math. 2 (1950) 66-78, and [Erd49] is Erdos, J. Indian Math. Soc. 13 (1949) 131-144 (a Tauberian-theorem paper). Selberg's Annals paper on the PNT itself (Ann. of Math. 50 (1949) 305-313) is from my memory only: UNVERIFIED. Wikipedia is internally inconsistent about 1948 vs 1949. The psi(x)log x + sum Lambda(n)psi(x/n) = 2x log x + O(x) form and Erdos prime-only form were not seen verbatim.
items.check_evidence: McNamara arXiv:2002.04007 (PDF): 'Theorem 2.5 (Selberg symmetry formula). The average of the second von Mangoldt function ... is (1/N) sum Lambda_2(n) = 2 log N (1 + o(1))'; 'In 1949, Erdos [Erd49] and Selberg [Sel50] discovered an elementary proof'; refs '[Sel50] ... Canad. J. Math. 2 (1950), 66-78'. Wikipedia PNT: 'By July of that year, Selberg and Paul Erdos had each obtained elementary proofs of the PNT' (text says 1948; cited papers 1949).

items.name: Beurling generalized primes: PNT conditions and counterexamples (the Beurling barrier)
items.statement: (i) Beurling 1937: N(x)=ax+O(x/log^gamma x), a>0, gamma>3/2 implies PNT; Kahane: an L^2 condition suffices. (ii) Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer (Math. Ann. 334 (2006)): for every 1/2<theta<1 there is a Beurling system with N(x)=rho x+O(x^theta) whose primes have pi(x)=Li(x)+Omega_pm(x exp(-c sqrt(log x))), whose zeta has zeros near sigma=1-a/log t, so RH fails. (iii) Zhang (Math. Ann. 337 (2007)) showed there are Beurling systems with RH and (1.1). (iv) Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas (2020): a system with RH in the form pi(x)=Li(x)+O(sqrt(x)) but N(x)=rho x+Omega_pm(x^{1/2} exp(-c sqrt(log x log log x))). (v) Hilberdink-Lapidus / Malliavin: pi(x)=Li(x)+O(x^theta) forces N(x)=rho x+O(x exp(-c sqrt(log x log log x))).
items.authors_year: Beurling 1937; Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer 2006; Zhang 2007; Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas 2020
items.quote_or_locator: Broucke et al. intro: "given 1/2<theta<1, they [DMV] showed the existence of Beurling numbers with integer counting function N satisfying N(x)=rho x+O(x^theta) ... and whose primes realize the de la Vallee Poussin error term ... pi(x)=Li(x)+Omega_pm(x exp(-c sqrt(log x)))"; "Zhang complemented these results by showing that there are also Beurling number systems for which, in contrast, the RH and the asymptotic estimate (1.1) both hold." Abstract of DMV via search listing (DeepBlue page returned 403, not opened). Beurling gamma>3/2: Debruyne-Schlage-Puchta-Vindas arXiv:1505.04174 intro, '(1.3) ... where a>0 and gamma>3/2, suffices for the PNT'.
items.fit_T1_T7: Defines the test for T7/T2: a tool that only uses 'prime-like' axioms (Euler product, Lambda_P >= 0, regular N(x)) cannot decide RH, because both RH-true and RH-false Beurling systems with such axioms exist.
items.relevance: Strongest negative guide for the project: any proof of K >= 0 must use an ingredient absent from generic Beurling systems, namely the Gamma factor/functional equation or the arithmetic of the integers (as Vinogradov-Korobov does). A positivity from Lambda >= 0 alone (like dlVP trig positivity) is Beurling-universal and therefore stops at sigma = 1 - c/log t.
items.corrected_statement: All sub-claims check out: (i) Beurling 1937 gamma>3/2 (year of Beurling's paper not in opened text; 'gamma>3/2 suffices for PNT' and sharpness shown in DSV; Kahane's L2 condition ✓). (ii) DMV, Math. Ann. 334 (2006) 1-36: for 1/2<theta<1, N(x)=rho x+O(x^theta) but pi(x)=Li(x)+Omega_pm(x exp(-c sqrt(log x))), dlVP zero-free region realised, RH fails. (iii) Zhang, Math. Ann. 337 (2007) 671-704: systems with RH and (1.1). (iv) BDV 2020 (arXiv v2): pi(x)=Li(x)+O(sqrt x) but N(x)=rho x+Omega_pm(sqrt(x) exp(-c sqrt(log x loglog x))) for c>2 sqrt 2; refereed status of BDV not verified. (v) Hilberdink-Lapidus (Acta Appl. Math. 94 (2006) 21-48): pi(x)=Li(x)+O(x^theta) => N(x)=rho x+O(x exp(-c sqrt(log x loglog x))); improves Malliavin (Acta Math. 106 (1961)). Own interpretive 'barrier' conclusion is not a sourced statement.
items.check_evidence: BDV arXiv:2004.11501 (PDF): 'Zhang complemented these results by showing that there are also Beurling number systems for which, in contrast, the RH and the asymptotic estimate (1.1) both hold'; Theorem 1.1 'pi(x)=Li(x)+O(sqrt x) and, for any c>2 sqrt 2, N(x)=rho x+Omega_pm(sqrt x exp(-c sqrt(log x loglog x)))'; Theorem 1.2 ([14]) 'pi(x)=Li(x)+O(x^theta) ...
