merged.title: Proven facts about zeta zeros
merged.summary: This domain is the zero side of the identity. By construction every item fails T1 (uses zeros) or gives no sign. Nothing here is a sign for the prime-built matrix K. Main findings: (1) Classical results (Hardy 1914, Selberg 1942, Levinson 1974, Conrey 1989, PRZZ 2020) give proportions of zeros on the line (record kappa > 0.417293). They are SIZE statements through Levinson mollifiers; they do not use the Weil form and do not touch the sign of <v,Kv>. (2) The only crossover to the project is the Alpoge-Furman (Claude) preprint arXiv:2608.13637 (Aug 2026, not refereed, Lean claim not independently confirmed by me) and Lamzouri arXiv:2609.02882. They compress Weil's Hermitian form to a finite matrix and count inertia (Sylvester) and rank. This is the best SIGN-type mechanism found (it takes SIZE from the prime side, tr and Frobenius norm, and inertia from the zero side), but the proven ceiling is 2/3 (0.6725 optimised) because the prime side is only controlled for band-width <= 1 (needs Hardy-Littlewood prime pairs beyond). The paper itself says nothing distinguishes 'two thirds' from 'all' and that the inputs also hold for Davenport-Heilbronn and Epstein functions where the RH analogue fails. (3) Bombieri 2000 proves that the negative index of truncated Weil forms equals half the number of off-line zeros: this is the formal statement of the circularity of the ~65 attempts. (4) Yoshida 1992 is the only classical unconditional K >= 0 on small windows (support 2L <= log 2, which by my inference from n >= 2 contains no prime at all); Zhu 2026 (preprint, certified computation) pushes to support 1.6 with margin 8.9e-18 and states that going further 'requires cancellation in the prime comb'. (5) Rodgers-Tao Lambda >= 0 means RH is 'barely true': no slack, which matches the 1e-29 margins. Named barriers: circularity (Bombieri), zero-side-only methods blind to RH (Davenport-Heilbronn/Epstein controls), band-width-1 wall, Lambda = 0. Best candidate for a SIGN source from this domain: none unconditional beyond Yoshida/Zhu windows; the AF compression is the right framework, but it supplies counts, not the sign of K. Noise to ignore: math.GM preprints claiming 'almost all zeros on the line' (arXiv 1805.07741, 2205.09042) are unrefereed with no uptake found.

items.name: Hardy 1914: infinitely many zeros on the critical line
items.statement: There are infinitely many nontrivial zeros of zeta with real part 1/2 (N0(T) -> infinity).
items.authors_year: G. H. Hardy, 1914 (C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 158, 1012-1014)
items.quote_or_locator: ProofWiki: "There exist an infinite number of nontrivial zeroes of the Riemann ζ function on the critical line." Citation: Hardy, C.R. Acad. Sci. Vol. 158, pp. 1012-1014 (secondary source; original not opened).
items.fit_T1_T7: Fails T1 (about zeros), T3 (no sign), T4. Proof uses real-valued Z(t) and the theta functional equation, which a generic Beurling zeta lacks.
items.relevance: Existence of on-line zeros only; no information about the sign of <v,Kv> or s_E, s_O.
items.corrected_statement: Hardy (C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 158 (1914), 1012-1014) proved that infinitely many nontrivial zeros of zeta lie on Re s = 1/2.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN. Primary Hardy note not opened. Confirmed by two independent sources. The 'fit_T1_T7' reasoning in the item is the author's own and was not checked.
items.check_evidence: https://proofwiki.org/wiki/Critical_Line_Theorem lists the citation 'Sur les Zéros de la Fonction ζ(s) de Riemann (C.R. Acad. Sci. Vol. 158: pp. 1012-1014)'. WebSearch results also give 'Hardy's original application in 1914 of Z(t) was to show that ζ(s) has infinitely many zeros on the critical line' (arXiv:1601.06512). Secondary sources only.

items.name: Hardy-Littlewood 1921 (N0(T) >> T) and Selberg 1942 (positive proportion)
items.statement: Hardy-Littlewood: N0(T) >= A T. Selberg: kappa = liminf N0(T)/N(T) > 0, i.e. a positive proportion of nontrivial zeros lies on Re s = 1/2 (equivalently N0(T) > c T log T).
items.authors_year: Hardy-Littlewood 1921 (Math. Z. 10); A. Selberg 1942 (Skr. Norske Vid. Akad. Oslo I, no. 10, 1-59)
items.quote_or_locator: PRZZ intro: "In 1942, Selberg [63] showed that 1 ≥ κ > 0. This means that a positive proportion of non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta-function lies on the critical line." Ref [63]: Skr. Norske Vid. Akad. Oslo I, (10):1-59, 1942. HL21 via Alpoge-Furman intro: "Hardy and Littlewood [HL21] subsequently showed that their number up to height T is ≫ T."
items.fit_T1_T7: Fails T1, T3, T4. Selberg's method counts sign changes of Z(t) and uses the functional equation; Davenport-Heilbronn functions also have a positive proportion on the line (Selberg-type results do not use RH).
items.relevance: Shows methods that count on-line zeros do not need RH; they give no sign for the prime-built form.
items.corrected_statement: Hardy-Littlewood 1921: N0(T) >> T. Selberg 1942: N0(T) >> T log T, i.e. a positive proportion of zeros lies on Re s = 1/2 (Selberg's constant was not made explicit).
items.corrected_status: PROVEN. The Selberg quote in the item is verified verbatim. The Hardy-Littlewood quote attributed to Alpoge-Furman ('HL21 ... >> T') is NOT in arXiv v2 of 2608.13637 (no 'HL21' string). Support for HL21 is only WebSearch summaries ('Hardy and Littlewood showed a lower bound of order T'). Math. Z. 10 citation not opened.
items.check_evidence: PRZZ arXiv:1802.10521 text, line ~407: 'In 1942, Selberg [63] showed that 1 ≥ κ > 0. This means that a positive proportion of non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta-function lies on the critical line.' The item's remark that Davenport-Heilbronn functions also have a positive proportion on the line is a separate claim; see the Davenport-Heilbronn row.

items.name: Levinson 1974: kappa >= 1/3, zeros simple
items.statement: At least one third of the nontrivial zeros are on Re s = 1/2 (Levinson's mollified derivative method). Heath-Brown and independently Selberg: Levinson's zeros are simple.
items.quote_or_locator: PRZZ: "Along with the choice Q(x) = 1 - x Levinson was able to prove that κ > 1/3 in 1974." Alpoge-Furman intro: "Heath-Brown [HB79] (and independently Selberg) observed that Levinson's zeros are in fact simple." DOI from Wikipedia 'Norman Levinson' (search result).
items.fit_T1_T7: Fails T1, T3, T4. Uses zeta'/zeta on the line, the functional equation and mean values with mollifiers; PRZZ note Levinson's method 'is a gamble'.
items.relevance: Proportion bound only; says nothing about positivity of the Weil form on a window.
items.corrected_statement: Levinson, Adv. Math. 13 (1974) 383-436, doi 10.1016/0001-8708(74)90074-7: more than one third of the zeros lie on the critical line. Heath-Brown, Bull. LMS 11 (1979): these zeros are simple (Alpoge-Furman cite this as [HB79]).
items.corrected_status: PROVEN. The 'independently Selberg' attribution and the quoted Alpoge-Furman sentence are not in arXiv v2 of 2608.13637. v2 line 118 says only 'Levinson's mollifier method [Lev74] gave 1/3 (simple, by [HB79])'. Treat 'independently Selberg' as UNVERIFIED.
items.check_evidence: PRZZ arXiv:1802.10521 line ~442: 'Along with the choice Q(x) = 1 − x Levinson was able to prove that κ > 1/3 in 1974.' Line ~449: 'Levinson's method is a gamble as it could produce negative bounds'. The DOI and pages are confirmed by a WebSearch bibliographic hit (Advances in Mathematics 13(4), pp. 383-436, DOI 10.1016/0001-8708(74)90074-7).

items.name: Conrey 1989: more than two fifths on the line
items.statement: kappa > 2/5 (the mollifier of length theta = 4/7 - eps via Deshouillers-Iwaniec gives kappa > 0.4088 per PRZZ).
items.authors_year: J. B. Conrey, J. reine angew. Math. 399 (1989) 1-26
items.quote_or_locator: Bibliographic record (search result): Crelle 399 (1989) 1-26, MR1004130. PRZZ (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1802.10521) line: "[Conrey] uses results from Deshouillers and Iwaniec [26, 27] on exponential sums to unconditionally prove that θ = 4/7 − ε which results in κ > 0.4088." Note: PRZZ ref [15] (J. Number Theory 1983) gives only 0.36581; do not mix them.
items.fit_T1_T7: Fails T1, T3, T4. Uses Kloosterman-sum estimates (modular/Dirichlet structure), not prime-like axioms.
items.relevance: Same as Levinson; no sign for K.
items.corrected_statement: Conrey (J. reine angew. Math. 399 (1989) 1-26) proved kappa > 0.4088 (hence > 2/5) using theta = 4/7 - eps via Deshouillers-Iwaniec. The item's headline 'kappa > 2/5' is correct but understates 0.4088.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN. Crelle volume and pages not independently opened; the PRZZ citation is the support.
items.check_evidence: PRZZ arXiv:1802.10521 line ~473: 'Conrey in [16] ... uses results from Deshouillers and Iwaniec [26, 27] on exponential sums to unconditionally prove that θ = 4/7 − ε which results in κ > 0.4088.' The item's warning not to mix this with the 1983 value 0.36581 was not checked.

items.name: PRZZ 2020: more than five-twelfths of the zeros on the line (current published record)
items.statement: kappa > 0.417293 (so > 5/12) and kappa* >= 0.407511 for zeros that are simple and on the line; unconditional. Earlier steps: Bui-Conrey-Young 2011 (>41%), Feng 2012 (0.4128).
items.authors_year: K. Pratt, N. Robles, A. Zaharescu, D. Zeindler, Res. Math. Sci. 7 (2020), art. 2, doi 10.1007/s40687-019-0199-8
items.quote_or_locator: Section 1: "An interim optimization ... yields κ > 0.417293 and κ∗ ≥ 0.407511 where κ∗ denotes the proportion of simple zeros on the critical line." Theorem 1.2: "More than five-twelfths of the non-trivial zeros ... are on the critical line."
items.fit_T1_T7: Fails T1, T3, T4, T5-T6 (no prime correlations). Twisted second moment with ratios conjecture techniques; needs the functional equation.
items.relevance: Best published proportion before 2026; does not bear on the sign of the window form.
items.corrected_statement: PRZZ, Res. Math. Sci. 7 (2020), art. 2, doi 10.1007/s40687-019-0199-8, Thm 1.2: more than 5/12 of the zeros are on the line. Section 1: kappa > 0.417293 and kappa* >= 0.407511. Feng's 0.4128 carried a gap that was later repaired, so it is not clean as a 'step'. Conflict: Alpoge-Furman (2608.13637, Thm A remark) give 5/12 as the previous record for the proportion of SIMPLE on-line zeros (N0^s/N), whereas PRZZ give kappa* >= 0.407511 for that quantity. Open point: which figure is the right record for simple on-line zeros.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (peer-reviewed). Bui-Conrey-Young value per PRZZ is kappa > 0.4105 ('>41%' is fine). 'BCY 2011' year not verified.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1802.10521, line ~592: 'An interim optimization of the parameters at our disposal yields κ > 0.417293 and κ∗ ≥ 0.407511 where κ∗ denotes the proportion of simple zeros on the critical line.' Line ~594: 'Theorem 1.2. More than five-twelfths of the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta-function are on the critical line.' Line ~498: 'in [8, 48, 58, 60], a gap was found in Feng's argument ... validating Feng's claim that θF = 1/2 − ε and κ > 0.4128.' Journal ref confirmed on the arXiv abstract page.

items.name: Alpoge-Furman (Claude) 2026: >= 2/3 of zeros simple and on the line, unconditional (PREPRINT)
items.statement: PREPRINT, not refereed (arXiv v1 13 Aug 2026, v2 19 Aug 2026): liminf N0*(T,2T)/N(T,2T) >= 2/3; at least (2/3 - o(1))N zeros are simple and on the critical line (Thm A,B); at least (5/6 - o(1))N are distinct (Thm C); optimised constants 0.6725, 0.6725, 0.83625 (Thm D); also for primitive Dirichlet L-functions (Thm E). Method: Montgomery 1973 argument made unconditional by a rank-trace inequality for a finite compression of Weil's Hermitian form plus Sylvester's law of inertia; prime side uses prime powers n <= (T/2pi)^lambda, lambda <= 1.
items.authors_year: CLAUDE (argument), L. Alpoge, R. Furman (responsibility for communication), arXiv:2608.13637, Aug 2026; follow-up simplification Y. Lamzouri arXiv:2609.02882 (Sep 2026, preprint)
items.quote_or_locator: I read the Anthropic-hosted PDF (dated Aug 10, 2026; https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/564f962e60643842f5fcb4a17c9dbc8f608f1c37.pdf): "We prove unconditionally that liminf N0*(T,2T)/N(T,2T) ≥ 2/3"; "The Riemann hypothesis, classically needed to read the zero side as a positive sum over real ordinates, is replaced by linear algebra applied to a finite compression of Weil's Hermitian form". Lean repo https://github.com/anthropics/zeta-23-lean: README states the CI criterion 'no sorry outside the trusted comparator statement files' but does NOT itself state sorry-free or list axioms (not confirmed by me). Lamzouri abstract (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.02882, via fetch summary): a 'conceptually simpler, unconditional proof' of 67.25% / 83.62%; the Claude proof was 'technically intricate'.
items.fit_T1_T7: Fails T1 and T3 for K: the SIZE comes from the prime side (tr G, ||G||_F^2 evaluated unconditionally), the structure (Sylvester (1,1) blocks, rank <= number of on-line points) comes from the zero side. T2 no (one high-frequency band [T,2T]); T4 no (inequalities with o(N)); T5 yes (Montgomery-Vaughan Hilbert inequality sees prime pairs, only for band-width <= 1); T6 pole term is traded for an oscillatory density of size O(sqrt(X)/(1+|tau|)), negligible on [T,2T] (Prop 5.7), so rank-2 pole is not treated at low frequency; T7 yes (Chebyshev-Mertens + Weil explicit formula). Beurling UNKNOWN: needs a functional equation and Gamma factor; paper says the certificate is empty for Davenport-Heilbronn functions without Euler product (Prop 5.6 fails).
items.relevance: Closest published relative of our setting (finite compression of Weil form, prime-built tr and Frobenius norm). Gives counts of on-line zeros via inertia, not the sign of <v,Kv>. Recorded here as unverified: refereeing pending, independent expert verdict not found; Lean claim only via the paper and a tracker.
items.corrected_statement: arXiv:2608.13637 'More than two thirds of the zeta zeros are simple and on the critical line', L. Alpöge and R. Furman. v1 13 Aug 2026, v2 19 Aug 2026. No journal ref on arXiv. Comments: 'Proof discovered autonomously by Claude (Anthropic); verified and communicated by the listed authors. Lean formalization available.' It proves at least 2/3 simple and on-line, at least 5/6 distinct. With the Montgomery-Taylor window the constants are 0.6725 and 0.8362 (the paper gives 0.83625...). It also covers primitive Dirichlet L-functions (Thm B). Correction 1: the Lean claim is stated in the paper itself (not only in the README). It says the main theorems' '#print axioms ... returns only the three standard axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, with no sorry' at repo tag v1.0. That is the authors' claim; I did not run the Lean code. Correction 2: the Lean kernel does NOT check the ceiling statement (the 0.682 bound) in full; the interval-arithmetic enclosures EnclOK are 'not checked by the Lean kernel'. The paper says Thm A/B formalization is independent of that. Correction 3: the item's note on Thm D ('0.6725, 0.6725, 0.83625') was not matched; the abstract gives 0.6725 and 0.8362.
items.corrected_status: PREPRINT, not refereed; no independent expert verdict found. Existence and content of the claim CONFIRMED against the arXiv v2 PDF I opened. Truth of the theorem remains UNVERIFIED by me. Lamzouri arXiv:2609.02882 (v1 2 Sep 2026, v2 8 Sep 2026, no journal ref) independently gives a 'conceptually simpler, unconditional proof' of 67.25% simple and on-line and 83.62% distinct, and replaces the matrix framework with a single Hilbert-space inequality. Still a preprint.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13637 (abstract page and PDF text via pdftotext). Abstract: 'We prove unconditionally that at least two thirds of the nontrivial zeros ... are simple and lie on the critical line, and that at least five sixths are distinct; the previous unconditional records are 5/12 and 0.6603.' 'the Riemann hypothesis ... is replaced by a rank–trace inequality applied to a finite compression of Weil's Hermitian form, with Sylvester's law of inertia handling off-line pairs.' Sec 1.4 'What the results are not': 'The inputs are insensitive to o(N) off-line zeros and hold for Davenport–Heilbronn and Epstein zeta functions, for which the analogue of RH is false.' Lamzouri: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.02882.

items.name: Barrier of the compression method: band-width 1 and 'two thirds = all'
items.statement: Within the Alpoge-Furman framework: restriction lambda <= 1 is essential (for X >> T log T the off-diagonal prime sums need Hardy-Littlewood prime-pair information, equivalently Montgomery's pair correlation for alpha > 1). 'Remark 1.1': no certificate reading only bandwidth-one data and holding configuration by configuration can exceed 0.68185 for simple zeros. Inputs (functional equation, explicit formula, mean values of Dirichlet polynomials of length <= T) are satisfied by Davenport-Heilbronn and Epstein functions, where the RH analogue is false. PREPRINT status as above.
items.authors_year: Alpoge-Furman (Claude), arXiv:2608.13637, Aug 2026 (preprint)
items.quote_or_locator: Sec 1.5: "The inputs—the functional equation, the explicit formula, and mean values of Dirichlet polynomials of length ≤ T—are insensitive to o(N) off-line zeros"; Sec 7.5(a): "Nothing in the method distinguishes between 'two thirds' and 'all'"; Remark 1.1: "can certify a proportion of simple zeros exceeding 0.68185"; Sec 7.2: "For Davenport–Heilbronn-type functions without Euler product ... the certificate is empty."
items.fit_T1_T7: Names exactly where T5 breaks: correlations of different primes beyond log n ~ log T are the unproven Hardy-Littlewood level; the method gets sign information (inertia) from zeros and magnitude from primes, so it fails T1 where it gets sign.
items.relevance: Tells us what extra prime-side input a sign proof needs: pair-type information at band-width > 1. YES for Beurling in the sense that the stated inputs are also met by objects with RH-analogue false (Davenport-Heilbronn, Epstein); the 'planted-zero Beurling' controls appear only in Appendix C of the same preprint, I did not see their results.
items.corrected_statement: The substance is confirmed in arXiv v2 of 2608.13637, but the numbers and section numbers do not match v2. The item quotes the 10 Aug Anthropic-CDN PDF, which I did not open. v2 says: sec 7.2 'Nothing in the method distinguishes between "two thirds" and "all"' (item: sec 7.5(a)); the bandwidth-one ceiling is 'approximately 0.682', with p0 <= 0.6818287 and the bound 'below 0.6819' (item: 'Remark 1.1 ... 0.68185' — string '0.68185' absent from v2); the 'inputs insensitive to o(N) off-line zeros ... Davenport-Heilbronn and Epstein' sentence is in sec 1.4 (item: 1.5). The item's quote 'For Davenport–Heilbronn-type functions ... the certificate is empty' was not found; the v2 line near 'empty' concerns an 'intended upper-bound route'.
items.corrected_status: Preprint (v2). The 'holds_for_beurling_primes: YES' entry is the item author's inference. The Beurling 'planted-zero' controls (Appendix C) were not read. Treat the sec 1.5, 7.5(a), 0.68185 and DH-'empty' quotes as UNVERIFIED for v2. The CDN PDF is not an arXiv version.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.13637 v2 text: sec 1.4 'insensitive to o(N) off-line zeros'; 'The ceiling over the broader class of all bandwidth-one certificates is approximately 0.682; see §7.2.'; '...is below 0.6819 for both windows'; 'Nothing in the method distinguishes between "two thirds" and "all".'

items.name: Bohr-Landau 1914: almost all zeros are near the line
items.statement: For every sigma > 1/2, N(sigma,T) = o(N(T)): all but an infinitesimal proportion of zeros lie in any neighbourhood of Re s = 1/2.
items.authors_year: H. Bohr, E. Landau, 1914
items.quote_or_locator: Secondary only (search-result summary of Revesz-Pintz arXiv:2407.12746, not verbatim): "Bohr and Landau proved in 1914 that N(σ,T)=o(N(T)) if σ>1/2". Original not opened.
items.fit_T1_T7: Fails T1 and T3 (about zeros, density). Carlson-type density theorems exist for Beurling zeta functions under Axiom A (Pintz, Broucke, Revesz-Pintz 2024), with weaker exponents.
items.relevance: Shows that off-line zeros are rare in density but allowed in number; compatible with the margin 1e-29 only as a statement about density, not as a sign.
items.corrected_statement: Standard statement (sources in search results, not verbatim): Bohr and Landau showed in 1914 that for every sigma > 1/2, N(sigma,T) = O(T^(1-eps(sigma))), hence o(N(T)). The item's cited source (Revesz-Pintz arXiv:2407.12746, abstract) does NOT mention Bohr-Landau. It is about zero-density estimates for Beurling zeta functions. One search result dates the original observation to 1913.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (classical) but not source-verified by me. Original paper (C. R. Acad. Sci. 158 (1914), 106-110, per a reference-list snippet) not opened. The item's 'Carlson-type density theorems for Beurling zeta under Axiom A (Pintz, Broucke, Revesz-Pintz)' is confirmed.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.12746 abstract page (Pintz's earlier papers prove Carlson-type density theorems under Knopfmacher's Axiom A; this paper assumes the Ramanujan condition and obtains Turan-type strength). Bohr-Landau support is only WebSearch snippets from arXiv:1812.11729 and arXiv:2602.04022 ('proved in 1914 that almost all zeros lie within any prescribed neighbourhood of the critical line').

items.name: Zero density: Ingham 1940, Huxley 1972, Guth-Maynard 2024
items.statement: N(sigma,T) <= T^{3(1-sigma)/(2-sigma)+o(1)} (Ingham); <= T^{3(1-sigma)/(3sigma-1)+o(1)} (Huxley, better for sigma > 3/4); Guth-Maynard Theorem 1.2: N(sigma,T) <= T^{15(1-sigma)/(3+5sigma)+o(1)}, combined with Ingham for sigma <= 7/10: N(sigma,T) <= T^{30(1-sigma)/13+o(1)} (eq. 1.4), improving exponent 12/5 to 30/13. Corollary 1.3: primes in short intervals of length x^{17/30+eps} (old exponent 7/12).
items.authors_year: Ingham 1940; Huxley 1972; L. Guth, J. Maynard, arXiv:2405.20552v2 (7 Apr 2026; thanks 'anonymous referees', journal not stated on arXiv)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: "we deduce a zero density estimate N(σ,T) ≤ T^{30(1−σ)/13+o(1)} and asymptotics for primes in short intervals of length x^{17/30+o(1)}." Intro: "The exponent 30/13 improves on the previous exponent of 12/5 due to Huxley [Hu]." (I read the full PDF text.)
items.fit_T1_T7: Fails T1, T3, T4. Size bound on off-line zeros; the Density Hypothesis exponent 2 is still open. Uses large values of Dirichlet polynomials on integers n^{it} (multiplicative structure of the integers), not prime-like axioms; Beurling versions are weaker (Revesz-Pintz 2407.12746).
items.relevance: Strongest proven control of off-line zeros; useful for tail estimates (zeros far outside a window), not for a sign.
items.corrected_statement: Ingham: N(sigma,T) <= T^{3(1-sigma)/(2-sigma)+o(1)}. Huxley: T^{3(1-sigma)/(3sigma-1)+o(1)}. Guth-Maynard Thm 1.2: N(sigma,T) <= T^{15(1-sigma)/(3+5sigma)+o(1)}. Combined with Ingham for sigma <= 7/10: T^{30(1-sigma)/13+o(1)} (eq. 1.4). Cor 1.3: primes in short intervals y >= x^{17/30+eps} (previous 7/12). Ingham/Huxley years are not stated in the paper; the item's 1940 and 1972 are UNVERIFIED.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN. Guth-Maynard: arXiv v1 31 May 2024, v2 7 Apr 2026; the PDF thanks 'anonymous referees'; no journal ref on arXiv.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.20552 text, eq. (1.2)-(1.4): 'Combining this with Ingham's estimate when σ ≤ 7/10, we obtain N(σ,T) ≤ T^{30(1−σ)/13+o(1)}. The exponent 30/13 improves on the previous exponent of 12/5 due to Huxley [Hu].' 'Corollary 1.3 ... y ∈ [x^{17/30+ε}, x^{0.99}]'. 'The exponent 17/30 improves on the previous exponent 7/12 due to Huxley [Hu].'

items.name: Zero-free region: Hadamard and de la Vallee Poussin 1896; explicit Vinogradov-Korobov region (Ford)
items.statement: zeta(1+it) != 0 (1896), hence the prime number theorem; de la Vallee Poussin: pi(x) = Li(x) + O(x exp(-a sqrt(log x))). Vinogradov-Korobov/Ford explicit region: no zeros with sigma >= 1 - 1/(57.54 (log|t|)^{2/3} (log log|t|)^{1/3}) for |t| >= 3 (Ford 2002; 2023 arXiv 2306.10680 reports constant 54.004).
items.authors_year: J. Hadamard, C. J. de la Vallee Poussin 1896; K. Ford 2002 (explicit Vinogradov-Korobov); 2023 improvement
items.quote_or_locator: Wikipedia: "found independently by Jacques Hadamard and Charles Jean de la Vallée Poussin and appeared in the same year (1896)"; error O(x e^{-a sqrt(log x)}). Ford constant 57.54 from secondary citations (search results to arXiv:2306.10680 and Springer doi 10.1007/s40993-023-00498-y); Ford's own theorem not opened.
items.fit_T1_T7: Fails T1, T3, T4. A Beurling system need not satisfy PNT (Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer type examples), so a zero-free line needs extra axioms.
items.relevance: Controls the archimedean/prime balance far from the line; does not give positivity of the form.
items.corrected_statement: 1896 Hadamard and de la Vallée Poussin: zeta(1+it) != 0, hence PNT with error O(x exp(-a sqrt(log x))). Ford's explicit Vinogradov-Korobov region has constant 57.54 for |t| >= 3 (Ford, Ramanujan J. 2002; arXiv:1910.08205 posted 2019). Later explicit improvements: Bellotti arXiv:2306.10680 (19 Jun 2023): sigma >= 1 - 1/(54.004 (log|t|)^{2/3}(loglog|t|)^{1/3}) for |t| >= 3, with 48.0718 for large |t|. Mossinghoff-Trudgian-Yang arXiv:2212.06867 (Dec 2022): 55.241. The item's attribution '2023 improvement' lacks an author. Its Springer doi 10.1007/s40993-023-00498-y could not be tied to the 54.004 result; UNVERIFIED mapping.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN. The 57.54 constant and the 54.004 value are confirmed. The Bellotti, MTY and Ford (1910.08205) pages were opened or shown by search; Bellotti's journal status is not stated on arXiv. The 'Ford 2002' year was not verified by me.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.10680 abstract page: 'For |t| ≥ 3: 54.004 ... Asymptotically 48.0718'. https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.06867: 'σ ≥ 1 − 1/(55.241(log|t|)^{2/3}(log log|t|)^{1/3})', |t| >= 3. A WebSearch result states that Ford's constant is 57.54 for all |t| >= 3. Wikipedia PNT page not reopened by me.

items.name: Landau-Gonek formula: zero sum of x^rho equals -(T/2pi) Lambda(x)
items.statement: For fixed x > 1: sum over zeros 0 < gamma <= T of x^rho = -(T/2pi) Lambda(x) + O(log T) (Landau 1911/12). Gonek's uniform version (x, T both varying, x integer) has error O(x log(2xT) log log(3x)).
items.authors_year: E. Landau, Math. Ann. 71 (1912) 548-564; S. M. Gonek, Contemp. Math. 143 (1993) 395-413
items.quote_or_locator: F. Aryan, 'On an extension of the Landau-Gonek formula': "In 1911 Landau [7] proved that for fixed x>1" followed by the formula; Gonek version: "−(T/2π)Λ(x) + O(x log 2xT log log 3x)" (fetch summary; formula rendering garbled on the page).
items.fit_T1_T7: Zero-side view of prime powers: the zeros 'see' Lambda(x) as a delta, i.e. the dual of our identity. Fails T1 (uses zeros), T3 (no sign), T4 (error terms). Needs the functional equation (Stirling) so Beurling NO.
items.relevance: Dictionary between our F_v(z)^2 zero sum and the prime sum, with an error; no sign.
items.corrected_statement: For fixed x > 1: sum_{0<gamma<T} x^rho = -(T/2pi) Lambda(x) + O(log T) (Landau, Math. Ann. 71 (1912)). Gonek's uniform form, for integer x: -(T/2pi) Lambda(x) + O(x log(2xT) log log(3x)) (Contemp. Math. 143 (1993)). Aryan's paper dates Landau to 1911 in text and 1912 in the reference list.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN. Original Landau and Gonek papers not opened; relied on Aryan's restatement (arXiv:1902.05473, no journal ref on arXiv).
items.check_evidence: https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1902.05473 (fetch): 'For fixed x>1: sum_{0<Im ρ<T} x^ρ = −(T/2π)Λ(x) + O(log T)'; Gonek uniform: '−(T/2π)Λ(x) + O(x log(2xT) log log(3x))', citing Gonek, Contemp. Math. 143 (1993).

items.name: Montgomery 1973 pair correlation (conditional on RH)
items.statement: Assume RH. F(alpha) = (T/2pi log T)^{-1} sum_{0<gamma,gamma'<=T} T^{i alpha (gamma-gamma')} w(gamma-gamma'), w(u) = 4/(4+u^2). Then F(alpha) = (1+o(1)) T^{-2 alpha} log T + alpha + o(1) uniformly for 0 <= alpha <= 1-eps (|alpha| <= 1 in later forms). Consequence: at least 2/3 of zeros are simple (on RH). Conjecture F(alpha) = 1 + o(1) for alpha > 1 bounded.
items.authors_year: H. L. Montgomery, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 24 (1973) 181-193, MR0337821
items.quote_or_locator: Wikipedia: "Under the Riemann hypothesis, for |α| ≤ 1 ... F(α) = T^(−2|α|) log(T)(1 + o(1)) + |α| + o(1)"; citation: Montgomery (1973) pp. 181-193, MR 0337821. Original not opened. Alpoge-Furman: Montgomery's prime-side evaluation 'with band-width ≤ 1, which is unconditional'.
items.fit_T1_T7: T5 yes (prime-pair correlation via Hilbert-type inequality, band-width <= 1); fails T1 (zero side) and T3 on its own; RH needed only to read the zero side as positive.
items.relevance: Template for turning prime-side second moments into zero-side information; the RH step is exactly the circular step.
items.corrected_statement: Under RH, F(alpha) = (1+o(1)) T^{-2 alpha} log T + alpha + o(1) for 0 <= alpha < 1 (extended to |alpha| <= 1 in later work). Montgomery's 2/3 of zeros are simple on RH. Later RH-conditional refinements raise this to about 67.9% (as stated in the BGST abstract).
items.corrected_status: CONDITIONAL (on RH). Original Montgomery paper not opened; the item cites Wikipedia. The BGST abstract describes the theorem as Montgomery's, 'assuming RH', and states the 67.9% consequence.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.04799 abstract: 'Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), Montgomery proved a theorem concerning pair correlation of zeros ... One consequence ... assuming RH, at least 67.9% of the nontrivial zeros are simple.'

items.name: Unconditional Montgomery theorem (Baluyot-Goldston-Suriajaya-Turnage-Butterbaugh 2024)
items.statement: Montgomery's F(alpha) asymptotic (|alpha| <= 1) holds as a statement over ALL complex zeros, without RH (zeros summed with complex ordinates). Application: at least 61.7% of zeros are simple under the weaker hypothesis that zeros with T^{3/8} < gamma <= T lie within 1/(2 log T) of the line (or a strong zero-density hypothesis); the method gives no information on being on the line.
items.authors_year: S. A. C. Baluyot, D. A. Goldston, A. I. Suriajaya, C. L. Turnage-Butterbaugh, Acta Arith. 214 (2024) 357-376, doi 10.4064/aa230612-20-3 (arXiv:2306.04799)
items.quote_or_locator: Fetch of arXiv abstract page: removes RH from Montgomery's theorem; "the method of proof neither requires nor provides any information" about whether zeros lie on the critical line; published Acta Arith. 214 (2024), 357-376 (arXiv listing).
items.fit_T1_T7: Prime-side evaluation is unconditional (T7 ok, T5 ok at band-width <= 1, T2 for a high-frequency band). Zero side stays complex-ordinate sum, so no sign (fails T3).
items.relevance: Unconditional prime-side second moment; the one rigorous bridge from prime correlations to a quadratic zero sum without RH.
items.corrected_statement: BGST, Acta Arith. 214 (2024) 357-376, doi 10.4064/aa230612-20-3 (arXiv:2306.04799, v1 7 Jun 2023): an unconditional form of Montgomery's pair-correlation theorem. Application: assuming that all zeros with T^{3/8} < gamma <= T satisfy |beta - 1/2| < 1/(2 log T), at least 61.7% of those zeros are simple. The same holds under a strong zero-density hypothesis. 'Neither requires nor provides any information' on whether the zeros are on the line.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (theorem unconditional); the 61.7% application is CONDITIONAL on the stated hypothesis. Journal ref from the arXiv listing; I did not open the journal page.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.04799 abstract: 'The method of proof neither requires nor provides any information on whether any of these zeros are on or not on the critical line where β = 1/2. We also obtain the same result under the weaker assumption of a strong zero-density hypothesis.' The 'complex ordinates' framing in the item is the author's paraphrase.

items.name: Box hypothesis gives 2/3 simple and on the line (Goldston-Suriajaya et al. 2025)
items.statement: CONDITIONAL: if all zeros with T < gamma <= 2T lie in a vertical box of width b/log T around the line with b = 0.3185, then at least 2/3 of zeros are simple and on the critical line. Does not assume RH itself.
items.authors_year: S. A. C. Baluyot, D. A. Goldston, A. I. Suriajaya, C. L. Turnage-Butterbaugh, arXiv:2501.14545 (2025)
items.quote_or_locator: Fetch summary: with b=0.3185 they prove "at least 2/3 of zeros are simple and on the critical line"; hypothesis described as weaker than RH.
items.fit_T1_T7: Fails T1, T7 (hypothesis on zeros). Isolated the obstruction (termwise positivity off the line) that Alpoge-Furman later replaced by linear algebra.
items.relevance: Shows the exact point where an unproven zero-location input enters Montgomery's argument.
items.corrected_statement: BGST, 'Pair Correlation of Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function I: Proportions of Simple Zeros and Critical Zeros', arXiv:2501.14545 (v3): if all zeros with T < gamma <= 2T lie in a box of width b/log T around the line, with b = 0.3185, then at least 2/3 are simple and on the line. The paper is submitted and under review (no journal ref).
items.corrected_status: CONDITIONAL (on the box hypothesis). Preprint, not refereed.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14545 abstract: '...with b = 0.3185 that at least 2/3 of zeros are simple and on the critical line'; eq. near line 115: 'N0s(B0.3185) ≥ 0.66666908 + o(1) log T'. Page comments: submitted for publication, under review.

items.name: Simple zeros on RH: 19/27 (Bui-Heath-Brown 2013)
items.statement: Assuming RH, at least 19/27 of the zeros of zeta are simple (Conrey-Ghosh-Gonek had RH + Generalised Lindelof).
items.authors_year: H. M. Bui, D. R. Heath-Brown, Bull. London Math. Soc. 45 (2013) 953-961, doi 10.1112/blms/bdt026
items.quote_or_locator: arXiv abstract: "We are able to remove this hypothesis by careful use of the generalised Vaughan identity." The value 19/27 and the RH assumption are from a search-result summary (arXiv:1302.5018 title/abstract), full text not opened.
items.fit_T1_T7: Fails T1, T3, T7 (assumes RH). Uses Vaughan identity and Montgomery-type moments.
items.relevance: RH-conditional; not usable as a source of unconditional sign.
items.corrected_statement: Bui and Heath-Brown (arXiv:1302.5018): assuming RH, at least 19/27 of the zeros are simple, removing the Generalised Lindelöf Hypothesis that Conrey-Ghosh-Gonek (Proc. LMS 76 (1998) 497-522) needed.
items.corrected_status: CONDITIONAL (RH). The journal ref Bull. LMS 45 (2013) 953-961 appears in the item and is cited in Alpoge-Furman's bibliography as [BHB13] Bull. Lond. Math. Soc.; volume and pages not independently checked.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.5018 abstract page: 'at least 19/27 of the zeros of the Riemann zeta-function are simple, assuming the Riemann Hypothesis (RH)'; it lists related DOI 10.1112/blms/bdt026.

items.name: De Bruijn-Newman constant: Lambda >= 0 (Rodgers-Tao), Lambda <= 0.22 (Polymath15), Lambda <= 0.2 (Platt-Trudgian)
items.statement: 0 <= Lambda <= 0.2. Rodgers-Tao: Lambda >= 0 (Newman's conjecture). Polymath15: Lambda <= 0.22 unconditionally. Platt-Trudgian Corollary 2: Lambda <= 0.2 using RH verified to height H > 2.51e12 and Polymath15 Table 1. RH is equivalent to Lambda <= 0.
items.authors_year: B. Rodgers, T. Tao, Forum Math. Pi 8 (2020) e6 (arXiv:1801.05914); D.H.J. Polymath, Res. Math. Sci. (arXiv:1904.12438, 2019); D. Platt, T. Trudgian (arXiv:2004.09765, 2020)
items.quote_or_locator: Rodgers-Tao intro: "Newman conjectured the complementary lower bound Λ ≥ 0, and noted that this conjecture asserts that if the Riemann hypothesis is true, it is only 'barely so'." Theorem 1: "One has Λ ≥ 0." Platt-Trudgian (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.09765): "Corollary 2. We have Λ ≤ 0.2." Polymath abstract (arXiv 1904.12438): "new unconditional upper bound Λ ≤ 0.22".
items.fit_T1_T7: T4 barrier: Lambda = 0 means RH, if true, has zero slack, so any sign proof must be lossless at the margin. The proof of Lambda >= 0 uses Montgomery-type pair correlation, i.e. zero-side input.
items.relevance: Matches the observed 1e-29 margins: no loss is allowed; a size-type argument can only certify Lambda > 0.
items.corrected_statement: 0 <= Lambda <= 0.2. Rodgers-Tao: Lambda >= 0 (Forum Math. Pi 8 (2020) e6, doi 10.1017/fmp.2020.6, arXiv:1801.05914). Polymath15: Lambda <= 0.22 (Res. Math. Sci. 6(3), 2019, arXiv:1904.12438). Platt-Trudgian Cor. 2: Lambda <= 0.2, obtained from Polymath15's tables once RH is verified to height H > 2.51e12. RH is equivalent to Lambda <= 0.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN. Verbatim PT text opened. Rodgers-Tao journal data and the Polymath15 journal come from search snippets and the Wikipedia article on the de Bruijn-Newman constant; the Rodgers-Tao 'barely so' quote was not checked.
items.check_evidence: Platt-Trudgian PDF (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.09765): 'Rodgers and Tao [27] proved that Λ ≥ 0 ... the authors [Polymath] prove that Λ ≤ 0.22 ... may take Λ ≤ 0.2 provided one has shown H > 2.51 · 10^12 ... Corollary 2. We have Λ ≤ 0.2.' https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Bruijn–Newman_constant: 'Λ ≤ 0.2, from Platt and Trudgian in April 2020 ... Rodgers and Tao Λ ≥ 0'.

items.name: RH verified to height 3e12 (Platt-Trudgian 2021)
items.statement: All zeros beta + i gamma with 0 < gamma <= 3*10^12 have beta = 1/2 (rigorous interval arithmetic). Earlier: Platt 2017 to 3*10^10; Gourdon / Wedeniwski claims (unpublished) are higher.
items.authors_year: D. Platt, T. Trudgian, arXiv:2004.09765 (2020), related DOI 10.1112/blms.12460 (journal not stated on the arXiv page)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: "that the Riemann hypothesis is true up to height 3·10^12. That is, all zeroes β+iγ of the Riemann zeta-function with 0<γ≤3·10^12 have β=1/2."
items.fit_T1_T7: Finite verification: fails T2 (not all windows), T3 for K in general; fine for windows whose zero sum is dominated by low zeros.
items.relevance: Gives a computational positive sign only where the window is tied to zeros below 3e12; in the identity <v,Kv> = sum F_v(z)^2 this is a finite check for fixed v, not uniform.
items.corrected_statement: Platt-Trudgian: all zeros with 0 < gamma <= 3*10^12 have beta = 1/2, by interval arithmetic. Published in Bull. London Math. Soc. (2021), doi 10.1112/blms.12460 (journal name taken from a search listing, not the arXiv page). Platt 2017 (3*10^10) and the Gourdon/Wedeniwski statement were not checked.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.09765 abstract: 'all zeroes β+iγ of the Riemann zeta-function with 0<γ≤3·10^12 have β=1/2.' Related DOI 10.1112/blms.12460 on the abstract page; X-MOL listing says published 2021-01-22 in the Bull. LMS.

items.name: Bombieri 2000: negative index of truncated Weil form counts off-line zeros
items.statement: Weil's functional is positive semidefinite iff RH. If RH fails with only finitely many zeros off the line, then for large enough truncation the number of negative eigenvalues of the truncated quadratic form equals half the number of off-line zeros. Also re-proves Yoshida's positivity for small support.
items.authors_year: E. Bombieri, Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. 11 (2000) 183-233
items.quote_or_locator: Fetch of the EuDML record: "If the Riemann Hypothesis fails with only finitely many zeros off the critical line, the number of negative eigenvalues equals half the number of such zeros, provided the truncation is large enough" (condensed from the abstract; full text not opened).
items.fit_T1_T7: Precise form of the circularity: the sign (inertia) of a prime-built K IS the off-line zero count. Any prime-only argument for K >= 0 therefore proves RH (fails T7 as a route).
items.relevance: Formal reason why the ~65 attempts were circular; also tells what a proof must produce: zero negative eigenvalues of the truncations, uniformly.
items.corrected_statement: Bombieri, 'Remarks on Weil's quadratic functional in the theory of prime numbers, I', Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. 11 (2000) 183-233. The functional is positive semidefinite iff RH. If RH fails with only finitely many zeros off the line, then for large enough truncation the number of negative eigenvalues equals half the number of off-line zeros. He also re-proves Yoshida's theorem that the form is positive definite for small t. The title includes 'I', and the item's paper title was missing.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN. Abstract-level verification only (EuDML and Mathdoc records through search); full text not opened. The 'lossless: true' tag and the circularity interpretation are the item author's.
items.check_evidence: https://eudml.org/doc/252338 (abstract via search): 'if the Riemann Hypothesis is false but only with finitely many non-trivial zeros off the critical line we show that the number of negative eigenvalues is precisely one-half of the number of zeros failing to satisfy the Riemann Hypothesis, provided the truncation is big enough.' 'and prove again Yoshida's theorem that it is positive definite if t is sufficiently small.'

items.name: Yoshida 1992: Weil form positive on small support
items.statement: Weil's quadratic form Q(f) is positive for test functions with supp f in [-L,L] when 2L <= log 2. (RH is equivalent to positivity for every L.) Re-proved by Bombieri (2000) and by Connes-Consani with trace-formula methods. My inference (not stated in the source): in this range no prime power n >= 2 enters the autocorrelation support [-2L,2L], so the positivity is a statement about the archimedean plus pole part only.
items.authors_year: H. Yoshida, 'On Hermitian forms attached to zeta functions', Adv. Stud. Pure Math. 21 (1992) 281-325
items.quote_or_locator: Zhu (2026), Sec 1.1: "Yoshida [3] proved positivity for 2L ≤ log 2, and Connes–Consani [6] re-proved this range ... only prime powers with log n < 2L contribute"; Ref [3]: Adv. Stud. Pure Math. 21, 1992, 281–325. Yoshida chapter: https://projecteuclid.org/ebooks/advanced-studies-in-pure-mathematics/Zeta-Functions-in-Geometry/chapter/On-Hermitian-Forms-attached-to-Zeta-Functions/10.2969/aspm/02110281.pdf (not read).
items.fit_T1_T7: Only genuine unconditional K >= 0 in this domain: T1 yes, T3 yes, T7 yes; fails T2 (only 2L <= log 2). Beurling UNKNOWN because I did not read the proof; it plausibly uses only the archimedean part plus the pole, which is not prime-specific.
items.relevance: Direct sign statement for small windows; the project's windows should be compared with this threshold (log 2 on the autocorrelation scale) to see if they are already covered.
items.corrected_statement: Zhu (v2) states: 'Yoshida [3] proved positivity for 2L ≤ log 2, and Connes–Consani [6] re-proved this range by trace-formula and von Neumann algebra methods ... only prime powers with log n < 2L contribute.' Yoshida, Adv. Stud. Pure Math. 21 (1992) 281-325. The item's inference that no prime power n >= 2 enters when 2L <= log 2 is arithmetically right (log n < 2L <= log 2 implies n < 2). The sharp log 2 threshold is attributed to Yoshida only through Zhu; the Yoshida chapter was not read, and a search snippet describes his log 2/2 threshold as coming from a sample computation. Zhu also notes 'claims beyond log 2 exist in unrefereed preprints'.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (per secondary attribution in a preprint). Not confirmed from Yoshida's own text. 'Only genuine unconditional K >= 0 in this domain' is overstated: Zhu's certified computation (preprint) and Bombieri's re-proof for small support also exist.
items.check_evidence: Zhu arXiv:2608.24827v2 PDF, Sec 1.1 (lines ~130-133): 'Yoshida [3] proved positivity for 2L ≤ log 2 ... (Claims beyond log 2 exist in unrefereed preprints ...)'. Search snippet on Yoshida's introduction: https://projecteuclid.org/ebooks/advanced-studies-in-pure-mathematics/Zeta-Functions-in-Geometry/chapter/On-Hermitian-Forms-attached-to-Zeta-Functions/10.2969/aspm/02110281.pdf (not opened). Bombieri abstract: see the Bombieri row.

items.name: Zhu 2026 (PREPRINT): certified Weil positivity up to support 1.6, and the 'prime comb' wall
items.statement: PREPRINT, not refereed (arXiv:2608.24827v2, 2 Sep 2026), computer-certified: Q(f) >= 8.9e-18 ||f||_2^2 for all supp f in [-0.8,0.8] (autocorrelation support 1.6, 2.3 times the classical range), also for complex test functions; unconditional variational upper bounds lambda*(L) down to 3.2e-283 at L = 2; lambda*(0.8) in [8.9e-18, 2.27e-17]; empirical law -ln lambda*(L) ~ 2 pi^2 N(T*)/ln N(T*), T* = 2 pi e^{2L} (fitted, not derived). Any certificate of this type must resolve frequencies up to T1(L) = 2 pi e^{A_L}, A_L ~ 4 e^L (doubly exponential in L).
items.authors_year: X. Zhu, arXiv:2608.24827, Aug-Sep 2026 (preprint)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract (read in full PDF text): "We prove, by certified computation, that Q(f) ≥ 8.9 × 10^-18 ||f||_2^2 for all supp f ⊆ [−0.8, 0.8]"; "Passing the resulting wall thus requires cancellation in the prime comb, a concrete arithmetic problem."
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 yes (geometric side only), T3 yes at fixed L, T4 margin 1e-17 certified; fails T2 (finite L) and states its own wall: doubly exponential cost. Specific finite computation for zeta, Beurling NO.
items.relevance: Same object as our windows: positive margin shrinks like a Landau-Widom rate; confirms that a uniform sign needs cancellation among primes (T5). Not independently re-run by me; not refereed.
items.corrected_statement: Zhu, arXiv:2608.24827 'Weil positivity in compact windows: a finite reduction, certified two-sided bounds, and a Landau-Widom decay law' (v1 25 Aug 2026, 9-page announcement; v2 2 Sep 2026, 34 pages; no journal ref). The text states: Q(f) >= 8.9e-18 ||f||_2^2 for all supp f within [-0.8, 0.8] (autocorrelation support 1.6); 8.9e-18 <= lambda*(0.8) <= 2.27e-17; certified upper bounds down to 3.2e-283 at L = 2; empirical law -ln lambda*(L) = C N(T*)/ln N(T*), C = 20.13... ≈ 2π², T* = 2π e^{2L}, fitted to four points (residuals under 0.7%, not derived); and a barrier threshold T1(L) = 2π e^{A_L}, A_L ~ 4 e^L, doubly exponential in L. The 'prime comb' sentence is verbatim.
items.corrected_status: All numbers match the v2 text. Computer-assisted claim, preprint, not refereed, and I did not re-run the certificates. The abstract says 'Passing the resulting wall thus requires cancellation in the prime comb, a concrete arithmetic problem.' The 'Beurling NO' entry is the item author's inference.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.24827 (v2 PDF, pdftotext): 'We prove, by certified computation, that Q(f) ≥ 8.9 × 10^−18 ∥f∥²₂ for all supp f ⊆ [−0.8, 0.8]'; '3.2 × 10^−283 at L = 2'; 'Any certificate of the one-stroke type must resolve frequencies up to T1(L) = 2π e^{A_L}, where A_L ∼ 4e^L'; eq.
