items.name: Davenport-Heilbronn functions: positive proportion on the line without RH
items.statement: Davenport-Heilbronn type Dirichlet series (period-5 coefficients) satisfy a Riemann-type functional equation, have no Euler product and have zeros off the critical line, yet a positive proportion of their nontrivial zeros lies on the line (Selberg-type). Hence results built only on the functional equation, explicit formula and Dirichlet-polynomial mean values cannot prove RH.
items.authors_year: H. Davenport, H. Heilbronn 1936; Potter-Titchmarsh 1934; Voronin, Karatsuba, Selberg for the on-line proportion; summary in arXiv:1105.2103 and arXiv:1602.06328
items.quote_or_locator: Search-result excerpt from arXiv:1105.2103: "Davenport and Heilbronn (1936) devised an example of a zeta function possessing a functional equation ... but no Euler product, with a set of non-trivial zeros wide of the critical line." (not opened in full; existence of off-line zeros has also been disputed in an unrefereed 2025 preprint, ignored here). Alpoge-Furman (CDN PDF, Sec 1.5): inputs "are satisfied by objects (Davenport–Heilbronn functions, Epstein zeta functions of class number > 1) for which the analogue of RH is false."
items.fit_T1_T7: T7 barrier: a sign mechanism must use the Euler product (primes as primes, correlations among them) and not only analytic structure.
items.relevance: Any 'proof-too-much' test: a method that also works for Davenport-Heilbronn cannot give the sign of K.
items.corrected_statement: What is supported: Davenport-Heilbronn type functions satisfy a Riemann-type functional equation, lack an Euler product, and have zeros off the critical line (Alpoge-Furman: inputs 'hold for Davenport–Heilbronn and Epstein zeta functions, for which the analogue of RH is false'). A positive PROPORTION of DH zeros on the line is not supported by anything I found. The one concrete lower bound found (Voronin, via a Chebyshevskii Sbornik abstract) is N0(T) > c T exp(0.05 sqrt(ln ln ln ln T)), which is not a positive proportion of ~T log T zeros. Karatsuba 1991 (Izv. Akad. Nauk) exists but I could not read its theorem. The item's cited source arXiv:1105.2103 is a paper by Chris King with a speculative dynamical thesis. It does not discuss DH zeros or a positive proportion and is not an adequate source. Also unsettled: Liu-Wu arXiv:2503.24275 (2025) dispute the off-line DH zeros, while Ferry-Ghisa-Muscutar arXiv:1602.06328 argue the opposite.
items.corrected_status: The barrier claim 'methods using only functional equation, explicit formula and moment inputs cannot prove RH' is supported by the Alpoge-Furman remark and the existence of DH zeros off the line (disputed as just noted). The 'positive proportion on the line' part is UNVERIFIED/likely wrong. Remove or replace with the Voronin lower bound after reading the source. The same claim appears in the Selberg-1942 item's relevance line.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.2103 (fetched: title 'A Dynamical Key to the Riemann Hypothesis', author Chris King; no DH positive-proportion discussion). Search result: https://www.chebsbornik.ru/jour/article/jats/158 / mathnet cheb850 snippet: 'N_0(T)>cT exp(0.05 sqrt(ln ln ln ln T))'. arXiv:2503.24275 and arXiv:1602.06328 (search listings).

items.name: Beurling systems satisfying RH with large oscillation (Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas 2020)
items.statement: There is a Beurling generalized number system whose prime counting function satisfies pi(x) = Li(x) + O(sqrt(x)) (RH-type) while its integer counting function oscillates by at least x exp(-c sqrt(log x log log x)). Related: Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer (Math. Ann. 2006): regular integers but large oscillation of primes; Revesz-Pintz 2024: zero-density estimates for Beurling zeta under Axiom A and Ramanujan condition.
items.authors_year: F. Broucke, G. Debruyne, J. Vindas, Adv. Math. 370 (2020) 107240, doi 10.1016/j.aim.2020.107240 (arXiv:2004.11501)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: "We construct a Beurling generalized number system satisfying the Riemann hypothesis" (fetch summary; journal ref Adv. Math. 370 (2020), Art. 107240).
items.fit_T1_T7: Barrier for the Beurling column: properties that hold for all Beurling systems with the same density cannot prove RH for zeta; RH-type and non-RH-type systems both exist.
items.relevance: Marks which of our tools may only use density-type prime axioms (they cannot give the sign) and which must use arithmetic specific to the integers.
items.corrected_statement: Broucke, Debruyne, Vindas, 'Beurling integers with RH and large oscillation', Adv. Math. 370 (2020), 107240, doi 10.1016/j.aim.2020.107240 (arXiv:2004.11501): a Beurling system whose prime counting function stays within O(sqrt x) of Li(x) (RH-type), while the integer counting function oscillates by about x exp(-c sqrt(log x log log x)). Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer (Math. Ann. 2006) and Revesz-Pintz 2024 are cited as related; only Revesz-Pintz was opened (zero-density estimates for Beurling zeta, Ramanujan condition, no journal ref).
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (published, Adv. Math.). Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer item not independently checked.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.11501 abstract page: 'integer counting function fluctuates ... with oscillations of order x·exp(−c√(log x log log x))'; 'Journal reference: Adv. Math. 370 (2020), Article 107240'; DOI 10.1016/j.aim.2020.107240.

missing: Riemann-von Mangoldt formula N(T) = (T/2pi) log(T/2pie) + O(log T) and its explicit-error version (Trudgian, Hasanalizade-Shen-Wong): the basic zero-counting theorem, absent from the list. Not verified here.

Montgomery 1973 pair-correlation conjecture and the GUE/random-matrix evidence (Odlyzko numerics, Rudnick-Sarnak, Keating-Snaith, Conrey-Snaith ratios conjecture, Hejhal triple correlation): conjectural/numerical, none verified here.

Carneiro-Chandee-Littmann-Milinovich 2017 (Hilbert spaces and the pair correlation of zeros; Alpoge-Furman cite it as [CCLM17] for Montgomery-Taylor optimality) and Carneiro-Goldston-de Laat 2020 (0.6792 simple zeros on RH via semidefinite programming; cited as [CGdL20] in Alpoge-Furman). I saw both only as citations inside 2608.13637.
Wu 2015 (0.6603 for distinct zeros, cited as [Wu15] in Alpoge-Furman): the previous unconditional record for distinct zeros, not verified.
Original Vinogradov-Korobov zero-free region (1958) and Korobov: the unconditional PNT error term exp(-c (log x)^{3/5} (loglog x)^{-1/5}). Only the explicit constants were checked.
Equivalents of RH: Nyman-Beurling-Baez-Duarte, Li's criterion, Robin's inequality (Lagarias), Weil positivity (Bombieri row only), de Bruijn-Newman Lambda <= 0 (present). The others are missing.

Convexity/Lindelof-type bounds: Bourgain 2017 subconvexity exponent 13/84 for zeta(1/2+it), mean-value theorems (Ingham 4th moment, Heath-Brown 12th moment). Directly relevant to the zero-density results used above.
Selberg 1946 / Conrey-Ghosh-Gonek simple-zeros results other than 19/27, and Conrey-Iwaniec-Soundararajan asymptotic large sieve results. Not found, not verified.
Arbitrarily large gaps and small gaps between zeros (Bui-Milinovich-Ng; Conrey-Ghosh-Gonek) and the Gram's law failures. Not in the list; not verified here.

Optimising Selberg's method (arXiv:2609.15329, a 2026 search hit that states at least 7% of zeros are on the line via Selberg refinements): seen only as a search snippet, not opened. It may bear on the Selberg-1942 row.

Zero-free regions on the left of 1 near the real axis (Siegel-type exceptional-zero issues for L-functions) and the Riemann-Siegel formula/Z(t) (Hardy function) as the base tool for the on-line zero count. Not in the list; not verified here.

merged.title: Primes in arithmetic progressions and averaged distribution
merged.summary:
Result: this domain contains NO sign candidate. Every verified theorem is a SIZE or EXISTENCE statement with log-power or epsilon loss (lossless=false for all items), so T3 and T4 fail across the board. Reason: every theorem here concerns residue classes mod q, while K is built from Lambda(n)/sqrt(n) at shifts log n with no residue classes. These theorems can only enter if the window is twisted by a Dirichlet character, and then they give size bounds on a twisted window, never the sign of s_E or s_O.
Named barriers: (1) Siegel zero: Siegel's theorem is ineffective, so Siegel-Walfisz has an ineffective constant, and q <= (log x)^A cannot be extended unconditionally. (2) The square-root barrier: GRH gives q <= x^{1/2}; Bombieri-Vinogradov (1965) matches it on average; the best proven level beyond 1/2 is 66/107 (Lichtman, preprint, with well-factorable weights only) or 1/2+1/40 (Stadlmann, smooth moduli). (3) Friedlander-Granville 1989: equidistribution on average fails for q near x/(log x)^A, so Elliott-Halberstam cannot be pushed to 1 in the naive form. (4) Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer 2006: Beurling systems with the same integer density as Z and zeros near sigma=1-a/log t exist, so density axioms cannot give RH.
Only T5 hook: Maynard writes that going beyond x^{1/2} "would imply some cancellation for sums over zeroes of different L-functions" and is "not directly implied by the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis". The beyond-sqrt(x) theorems (Zhang, Polymath, Maynard I-III, Lichtman) are therefore the only proven cross-L-function cancellation. They are averages with absolute values and a (log x)^{-A} error, not signs.
Possible T1 hook: Matomaki-Merikoski-Teravainen 2024 prove Linnik (q^350) with no L-functions, using prime-side sieving only. It is a one-sided existence bound, not an identity.
New and unverified: Oct 2026 preprints (OpenAI manuscript, Banks, Kerr, Green) claim (1-beta) log q >= 3.0e-3 for all real zeros, i.e. no Landau-Siegel zeros, which would make Siegel-Walfisz effective. Not refereed; I did not read the OpenAI manuscript itself.
Facts from the request about von Koch, Selberg, Green-Tao and the Zhu quote belong to other domains and were NOT checked here. Bombieri-Vinogradov was checked: exact form in Maynard I (1.2) and Polymath Thm 2.3.
Best candidate for a SIGN: none. For the Beurling argument: DMV 2006 is the cleanest proof that density plus Euler product alone cannot prove RH.

items.name: Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions
items.statement: If gcd(a,d)=1 there are infinitely many primes p = a + nd. Equivalently infinitely many primes are congruent to a mod d; in each progression the sum of 1/p diverges, and each of the phi(d) classes carries share 1/phi(d) of the primes.
items.authors_year: Dirichlet 1837 (year as given by the cited encyclopedia page)
items.quote_or_locator: "there are infinitely many primes of the form a + nd" (secondary source; fetched page states proof in 1837, elementary proof by Selberg 1949). The 1837 original was not opened.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 yes in statement (proof uses L(1,chi) != 0); T2 n/a; T3 no (existence, not sign); T4 no; T5 no; T6 no; T7 yes.
items.relevance: Foundation only. The proof rests on L(1,chi) != 0 for Dirichlet characters, a non-vanishing on Re s = 1, not a sign of a quadratic form of the type <v,Kv>. Beurling systems have no residue classes.
items.corrected_statement: Unchanged. Secondary-source only (Wikipedia). Note: 'share 1/phi(d)' is a density statement; the quote only supports Dirichlet density. Natural density needs PNT in progressions (de la Vallee Poussin) - from memory, UNVERIFIED.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (Dirichlet 1837; Selberg elementary proof 1949) - original papers not opened by me
items.check_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirichlet%27s_theorem_on_arithmetic_progressions : 'there are infinitely many primes of the form a + nd'; 'proved by Dirichlet' in 1837; Selberg 'gave an elementary proof of this theorem in 1949'; 'the sum of the reciprocals of the prime numbers in the progression diverges'; proportion in each progression 1/phi(d).

items.name: Siegel-Walfisz theorem (PNT in progressions for q <= (log x)^A)
items.statement: For every A>0 there is c_A>0 with psi(x;q,a) = x/phi(q) + O(x exp(-c_A sqrt(log x))) uniformly for (a,q)=1 and q <= (log x)^A. The constant c_A is ineffective.
items.authors_year: Siegel 1935, Walfisz 1936 (years from memory: UNVERIFIED); statement form in Sachpazis 2025/26 eq. (1.1) and Wikipedia
items.quote_or_locator: Sachpazis, eq. (1.1): "psi(x;q,a) = x/phi(q) + O(x e^{-c_A sqrt(log x)}) for all q <= (log x)^A". Wikipedia: "The constant C_N is not effectively computable because Siegel's theorem is ineffective." Maynard I intro: "Without progress on the notorious problem of Siegel zeros we cannot hope to unconditionally improve the range of q" (https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.06572).
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 statement yes (proof uses zero-free region); T2 n/a; T3 no; T4 no (error term exp(-c sqrt(log x))); T5 no; T6 no; T7 yes.
items.relevance: Size control of primes in classes with very small modulus. Enters the window only after a character twist, and then gives only a size, not the sign of s_E or s_O. If the Oct 2026 Landau-Siegel preprints hold up, the constant becomes effective, which still gives no sign.
items.corrected_statement: Statement correct. Years now sourced: Siegel, Acta Arith. 1 (1935); Walfisz, Math. Z. 40 (1936). Wikipedia form: psi(x;q,a)=x/phi(q)+O(x exp(-C_N (log x)^{1/2})) for q<=(log x)^N, C_N ineffective. Original papers not opened.
items.check_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siegel%E2%80%93Walfisz_theorem : 'ψ(x;q,a)=x/φ(q)+O(x exp(−C_N(log x)^{1/2}))' for q<=(log x)^N; 'not effectively computable' because Siegel's theorem is ineffective; cites Siegel Acta Arith. 1 (1935) and Walfisz Math. Z. 40 (1936). Eq. (1.1) of Sachpazis (arXiv 2511.16452) consistent.

items.name: Siegel's theorem (ineffective lower bound for L(1,chi), repulsion of the real zero)
items.statement: For every eps>0 there is b_eps>0 with 1 - beta_1 >= b_eps q^{-eps} for the possible exceptional real zero beta_1 of a real primitive character mod q. The constant b_eps is effectively computable only for eps >= 1/2.
items.authors_year: Siegel 1935 (classical); as used in Thorner-Zaman 2021 Remark 1.2
items.quote_or_locator: Remark 1.2: "For all eps > 0, there exists a constant b_eps > 0 such that 1 - beta_1 >= b_eps q^{-eps}. The constant b_eps is effectively computable when eps >= 1/2".
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 no (about zeros of L(s,chi)); T3 no; T4 no; T7 yes but it is a statement about zeros.
items.relevance: This is the named obstruction of the domain: ineffectivity of every constant that uses it. A possible Siegel zero is the only uncontrolled secondary main term in progressions. Not a route to a sign of s_E or s_O.
items.corrected_statement: Thorner-Zaman Remark 1.2 states: for all eps>0 there is b_eps>0 with 1-beta_1 >= b_eps q^{-eps}; 'b_eps is effectively computable when eps >= 1/2 [13, Thm 3]'. The word 'only' in the item is not in the source (it is the standard folklore that eps<1/2 is ineffective, but TZ do not say it). TZ treat the real character chi_1 (mod q) with beta_1 the exceptional zero of the product over characters mod q, not specifically 'primitive mod q'. Year 1935 comes from the Siegel-Walfisz page (Acta Arith. 1), not from TZ.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (ineffective for eps<1/2 by the standard statement; 'only' not sourced in TZ)
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2108.10878 (text extracted locally, Remark 1.2): 'For all epsilon > 0, there exists a constant b_epsilon > 0 such that 1 - beta_1 >= b_epsilon q^{-epsilon}. The constant b_epsilon is effectively computable when epsilon >= 1/2 [13, Thm 3].'

items.name: Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem
items.statement: For every A>0 there is B=B(A) with sum_{q <= x^{1/2}(log x)^{-B}} max_{(a,q)=1} |pi(x;q,a) - pi(x)/phi(q)| << x/(log x)^A. Equivalent form: EH[theta] holds for every 0<theta<1/2. Gallagher/Wikipedia form: sum_{q<=Q} max_{y<=x} max_a |psi(y;q,a) - y/phi(q)| = O(x^{1/2} Q (log x)^5) for x^{1/2}(log x)^{-A} <= Q <= x^{1/2}.
items.authors_year: Bombieri, Mathematika 12 (1965) 201-225; A. I. Vinogradov, Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR (1965) (references as listed in Maynard I)
items.quote_or_locator: Maynard I eq. (1.2) and text: "an adequate substitute for the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis is the Bombieri-Vinogradov Theorem [2, 34]". Polymath arXiv:1407.4897 Theorem 2.3: "EH[theta] holds for every fixed 0 < theta < 1/2". Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombieri%E2%80%93Vinogradov_theorem) gives the x^{1/2}Q(log x)^5 form. Maynard: "Q <= x^{1/2}/(log x)^B ... essentially as large as can be handled with the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis".
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 statement yes, proof uses large sieve and zero density of L(s,chi); T2 n/a; T3 no (absolute values, so no sign); T4 no ((log x)^{-A} loss); T5 partly (averages over q, i.e. different L-functions); T6 no; T7 yes.
items.relevance: This is the 'GRH on average' tool. Maynard: expanding via characters and the explicit formula shows that going beyond x^{1/2} 'would imply some cancellation for sums over zeroes of different L-functions'. With absolute values it cannot give the sign of s_E or s_O. The twist of the window by characters would be the only entry point.
items.corrected_statement: Core statement and EH[theta] for 0<theta<1/2 CONFIRMED (Polymath 8b Theorem 2.3). Wikipedia range: x^{1/2}(log x)^{-A} <= Q <= x^{1/2}, bound O(x^{1/2} Q (log x)^5); Wikipedia does NOT label it 'Gallagher form' (it only says Gallagher simplified many ingredients) - drop that label or source it separately. A.I. Vinogradov: Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR Ser. Mat. 29(4) (1965) 903-934, corrigendum vol. 30 (1966) 719-720. Bombieri Mathematika 12 (1965) 201-225 pages NOT verified by me.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.4897 Theorem 2.3 (Bombieri-Vinogradov): 'EH[theta] holds for every fixed 0 < theta < 1/2'; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombieri%E2%80%93Vinogradov_theorem : 'sum_{q<=Q} max_{y<=x} max_{(a,q)=1} |psi(y;q,a)-y/phi(q)| = O(x^{1/2} Q (log x)^5)' for 'x^{1/2} log^{-A} x <= Q <= x^{1/2}'; Vinogradov ref as above.

items.name: Barban-Davenport-Halberstam theorem (second moment of the error in progressions)
items.statement: With E(x;q,a) = theta(x;q,a) - x/phi(q) and V(x,Q) = sum_{q<=Q} sum_{a mod q}^* |E(x;q,a)|^2: V(x,Q) = O(Q x log x) + O(x^2 (log x)^{-A}) for 1 <= Q <= x (Gallagher form). Barban and Davenport-Halberstam: Q <= x (log x)^{-B}, B = A+5 in the latter. Montgomery and Hooley proved asymptotics ~ Q x log Q in a range Q > x(log x)^{-A}; the exact asymptotic constant was NOT verified here.
items.authors_year: Barban 1961-64; Davenport-Halberstam 1966; Gallagher 1970s; Montgomery, Michigan Math. J. 17 (1970) 33-39; Hooley, J. London Math. Soc. 10 (1975) 249-256; Goldston-Vaughan 2006 circle-method approach (citations as relayed by the search tools, originals not opened)
items.quote_or_locator: Wikipedia: "V(x, Q) = O(Qx log x) + O(x^2 (log x)^{-A})"; "Barban's result holds only for Q <= x(log x)^{-B}"; "The Davenport-Halberstam result takes B = A + 5". Harper (arXiv:2412.19644, JLMS 112 (2025)) restates the variance type setting for general sequences.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 statement yes; T2 n/a; T3 no (second moment is an upper bound); T4 no; T5 yes (variance over many moduli and classes is a correlation functional of primes); T6 no; T7 yes.
items.relevance: The second moment is a sum of squares with a positive sign by construction, but it is an upper-bound inequality and the Montgomery-Hooley asymptotic ties the diagonal Q x log(x/Q) to the prime pair-correlation, a prime-side object. Closest in spirit to a positive quadratic form, but it controls size, not the sign of s_E or s_O.
items.corrected_statement: Gallagher form and B=A+5 CONFIRMED (Wikipedia). Citation errors in the item: (1) Hooley's papers are 'On the Barban-Davenport-Halberstam theorem I', J. reine angew. Math. 274/275 (1975) 206-223 and 'II', J. London Math. Soc. (2) 9 (1974/75) 625-636 - the item's 'JLMS 10 (1975) 249-256' does not match any in the Hooley list I opened. (2) Goldston-Vaughan 'On the Montgomery-Hooley asymptotic formula' is in Sieve methods, exponential sums, and their applications in number theory (Cardiff 1995), LMS Lecture Note 237, CUP 1997, pp. 117-142 - NOT 2006; the 'circle-method approach' label is not supported by what I read. (3) The asymptotic (Montgomery 1970, Michigan Math. J. 17, 33-39; refined by Hooley) is (1/Q) sum_{q<=Q} V(x;q) = x log Q - c x + O(...), c = gamma + log(2 pi) + 1 + sum_p log p/(p(p-1)), i.e. sum_{q<=Q} V = Q x log Q - c Q x in the range x/(log x)^A <= Q <= x. The item's relevance sentence 'diagonal Q x log(x/Q)' is NOT supported; the main term is Q x log Q. (V there is the variance of psi with the chi_0 correction.) Under GRH Goldston-Vaughan: error O(Q (x/Q)^{1/4+eps}+ x^{3/2}(log 2x)^{5/2}(log log 3x)^2 / Q) for Q<=x. Gallagher large sieve: Mathematika 14 (1967) 14-20. Barban 1961 and Davenport-Halberstam 1966 years: Barban 1961 per Wikipedia BV reference; DH year not checked.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (unconditional ranges Q<=x(log x)^{-B}; asymptotic for Q>=x/(log x)^A; GRH extends to x^{1/2+eps}<Q<=x)
items.check_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barban%E2%80%93Davenport%E2%80%93Halberstam_theorem ('V(x,Q)=O(Qx log x)+O(x^2 (log x)^{-A})', 'Davenport-Halberstam result takes B=A+5'); https://arxiv.org/pdf/1301.5663 (Lamzouri/Fiorilli-type survey, text extracted): 'asymptotic result in this range was first obtained by Montgomery [Mo1]'; formula (2) 'x log Q - c x'; refs [H2] J. Reine Angew. Math. 274/275 (1975) 206-223, [H3] J. London Math. Soc. (2) 9 (1974/75) 625-636, [GV] ... Cambridge Univ. Press 1997, [Mo1] Michigan Math. J. 17 (1970) 33-39, [G] Mathematika 14 (1967) 14-20.

items.name: Brun-Titchmarsh inequality (Montgomery-Vaughan form)
items.statement: For all q < x and (a,q)=1: pi(x;q,a) <= 2x / (phi(q) log(x/q)). Short-interval form: pi(x+y;q,a) - pi(x;q,a) <= 2y/(phi(q) log(y/q)) for y>q. Motohashi (1973) for q <= x^{9/20}: <= (2+o(1)) x/(phi(q) log(x/q^{3/8})).
items.authors_year: Montgomery-Vaughan, Mathematika 20 (1973) 119-134; Motohashi 1973
items.quote_or_locator: Wikipedia: "pi(x; q, a) <= 2x / (phi(q) log(x/q)) for all q < x", proved by sieve methods by Montgomery and Vaughan. Encyclopedia of Mathematics credits the same paper. The original Theorem 2 text was NOT opened (the DeepBlue fetch returned HTML, doi.org redirected to Wiley), so this form comes from secondary sources.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 yes (a pure sieve upper bound); T2 n/a; T3 no; T4 no (constant 2 is the parity loss); T5 no; T6 no; T7 yes.
items.relevance: An upper bound that does not lead to a lower bound. Its constant 2 is the sieve parity barrier. Granville showed that under a Siegel zero the sieve upper bounds are optimal (Wikipedia Siegel zero). No sign information.
items.corrected_statement: MV form pi(x;q,a) <= 2x/(phi(q) log(x/q)) for q<x CONFIRMED (Wikipedia; MV Mathematika 20 (1973) 119-134, doi 10.1112/s0025579300004708, paper's own text not opened). Motohashi's 1973 date is NOT backed by Wikipedia's reference list (only his 1983 book is listed); a search found his paper dated 1974 (J. Math. Soc. Japan) - date UNVERIFIED. The range q<=x^{9/20} and form (2+o(1))x/(phi(q) log(x/q^{3/8})) are as stated on Wikipedia. Missing refinement: Maynard (arXiv 1201.1777; Acta Arith. 157 (2013) 249-296 per search) proves the form pi(x;q,a) <= (2+o(1)) x/(phi(q) log x) for log x/log q >= 8, which is stronger than MV in that range; C<2 is impossible without ruling out a Siegel zero.
items.check_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brun%E2%80%93Titchmarsh_theorem : 'pi(x;q,a) <= 2x/(phi(q) log(x/q)) for all q < x'; Motohashi 'q <= x^{9/20}: (2+o(1))x/(phi(q) log(x/q^{3/8}))'; https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.1777 : 'C = 2 is valid whenever log x / log q >= 8' (paraphrase by fetch tool), 'C < 2 cannot be achieved' without ruling out a Siegel zero.

items.name: Arithmetic large sieve inequality (dual form, sharp constant)
items.statement: For any complex a_n, n in (M, M+N], with S(alpha) = sum a_n e(n alpha): sum_{q<=Q} sum_{a mod q, (a,q)=1} |S(a/q)|^2 <= (N - 1 + Q^2) sum |a_n|^2. Equivalent Dirichlet-character form (Gallagher, Bombieri).
items.authors_year: Montgomery-Vaughan 1973 and 1974; independently A. Selberg; Bombieri 1965 (Mathematika 12) for the character form
items.quote_or_locator: Kowalski (arXiv:0911.2020) as relayed by the search tool: "by work of Montgomery-Vaughan and Selberg, it is known that one can take Delta = Q^2 - 1 + N"; "both known proofs of the optimal version ... proceed by duality". Original Montgomery-Vaughan Theorem not opened.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 yes (holds for any sequence a_n, independent of primes); T2 yes (all N and Q at once); T3 no (operator norm bound, an upper bound on a positive form); T4 no (it is an inequality, sharp only in special cases); T5 yes (cancellation among different fractions a/q); T6 unknown; T7 yes.
items.relevance: The only item in the domain that is an inequality for a positive semidefinite form (a Gram matrix with Fourier phases). It bounds the largest eigenvalue from above, so it cannot decide the sign of s_E or s_O. It could serve as a tool for bounding the pole part of K, as bounds for the rank-2 term, but only as an upper bound.
items.corrected_statement: Bound N + Q^2 - 1 is the Montgomery-Vaughan sharp form (N + delta^{-1} - 1 for delta-spaced points, with Farey fractions delta=1/Q^2); sharpness remark (Bombieri-Davenport examples) seen only via OCR snippet. Attribution to Selberg and Bombieri (1965) character form NOT verified.
items.check_evidence: Search result of Mathematika 20 (1973) 119-134 (deepblue PDF, OCR garbled): Theorem 1 bound '(N + delta^{-1} - 1)'; 'Bombieri and Davenport have given examples ... so that (1.4) is extremely sharp'. Kowalski arXiv:0911.2020 as relayed. Original not read in full.

items.name: Linnik's theorem and the best exponent L (Xylouris)
items.statement: There are absolute C, L with P(a,q) <= C q^L for the least prime P(a,q) = a mod q. Best exponent from the L-function method: L=5 (Xylouris, building on Heath-Brown's 5.5 from 1992). Provenance disagrees across sources: arXiv:0906.2749 (2009) states L=5.2; the Acta Arith. 150 (2011) paper is listed with 5.18; L=5 is in the refereed Cebysevskii Sb. 19(3) (2018) 80-94 and in his thesis. GRH gives P << (phi(q) log q)^2.
items.authors_year: Linnik 1944; Heath-Brown 1992; Xylouris 2009/2011/2018
items.quote_or_locator: Xylouris, "Linniks Konstante ist kleiner als 5", Cebysevskii Sb. 19 (2018): "Aufbauend auf einer Arbeit von Heath-Brown beweisen wir, dass L=5 zulaessig ist." arXiv abs 0906.2749: "L = 5.2"; Bruna arXiv:2603.25612 intro: "Xylouris [Xyl11], who, building on ideas of Heath-Brown [HB92], proved in his PhD thesis that one may take L = 5." A table on teorth.github.io also lists a 2026 value 3.99 (Naslund) and 2.4; I found NO primary source for these, so they are NOT verified.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 no (uses zero-density and zero repulsion of L(s,chi)); T2 n/a; T3 no; T4 no; T5 no; T6 no; T7 yes.
items.relevance: The proof of Linnik is split into cases depending on whether a Siegel zero exists (Wikipedia, Siegel zero). It gives a size bound for a single prime in a class and no sign information.
items.corrected_statement: Three values must be kept apart: arXiv:0906.2749 (v1 15 Jun 2009, Diplomarbeit in German, 86 pp.) abstract L=5.2 with journal-ref Acta Arith. 150 (2011) 65-91; the Acta paper Theorem 1.1 states P(a,q) <= C q^{5.18} (per teorth.github.io table quoting it; Acta paper not opened by me); L=5 is in Xylouris' Bonn dissertation (2011) and in Cebysevskii Sb. 19(3) (2018) 80-94 'Linniks Konstante ist kleiner als 5' (abstract: L=5 admissible). Heath-Brown 1992: L=5.5. The 2026 values 3.99 (Naslund, Hexagon:2610.00018v1, 2 Oct 2026, computer-assisted, unrefereed, per the teorth table) and 2.4 (a contributor's deduction from the OpenAI 2026 zero-free region plus Iwaniec-Kowalski Thm 10.4; the table itself says the OpenAI manuscript 'does not state a Linnik bound') appear in a secondary tracker only; primary sources NOT opened -> keep UNVERIFIED. The Bruna 2603.25612 quote about Xylouris L=5 was NOT confirmed (the abstract page I fetched has no intro; Bruna is a conditional result: GLH implies O(q^{2+eps})). GRH: P << (phi(q) log q)^2 not re-checked.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (best refereed L=5, 2018; 5.18 in Acta 2011; 3.99 and 2.4 are unrefereed claims)
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.2749 : 'L = 5.2', Journal ref 'Acta Arith. 150 (2011), 65-91'; https://geodesic.mathdoc.fr/item/CHEB_2018_19_3_a8 : Cebysevskii Sb. 19(3) 80-94, 'L = 5 is an admissible value'; https://teorth.github.io/optimizationproblems/constants/65a.html : '5.18 Xylouris, 2011 Acta Arith. 150 Theorem 1.1: P(a,q) <= C q^5.18'; '3.99* Naslund, 2026 ... not refereed'; '2.4* ... Contributor's deduction'.

items.name: Linnik's theorem without L-functions (prime-detecting sieve)
items.statement: The least prime in a class mod q satisfies p << q^350 for q >= an effectively computable constant, with a proof in which zeros of Dirichlet L-functions play no role; also primes exist in (x - x^{39/40}, x] for every large x.
items.authors_year: Matomaki, Merikoski, Teravainen 2024 (arXiv, not refereed as far as the abs page shows); earlier sieve proof Friedlander-Iwaniec with L = 75,744,000 (as cited by Bruna); pretentious proof Granville-Harper-Soundararajan, Compositio 155 (2019)
items.quote_or_locator: arXiv abs: "p << q^{350}"; "(x-x^{39/40}, x] contains primes for every large x"; the search summary of the abstract says the zeros of Dirichlet L-functions "do not play any role in the proof". Bruna 2603.25612 intro confirms "a new prime-detecting sieve that gave the much stronger bound P(a,q) << q^{350}".
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 yes (zeros are not used); T2 n/a; T3 no (existence, one-sided); T4 no (exponent 350 is far from optimal); T5 yes (sieve over multiplicative structure sees correlations); T6 unknown; T7 yes.
items.relevance: The only item in the domain that proves positivity (at least one prime) with prime-side data only. It does not show a sign of a quadratic form, and its tools use multiplicative structure of the integers (Beurling status unknown). A possible method pattern for 'positivity without zeros', size only.
items.corrected_statement: Confirmed: arXiv:2401.17570 (31 Jan 2024, 33 pp., no journal ref on arXiv page): p << q^{350} for the least prime p = a mod q, and (x - x^{39/40}, x] contains primes for all large x, proofs without L-functions. Caveat: 39/40 is far weaker than classical short-interval results (via zeros), so this is a method result, not a record. 'q >= effectively computable constant', Friedlander-Iwaniec L=75,744,000 and GHS Compositio 155 (2019) NOT verified.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (arXiv preprint; refereed status not confirmed)
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.17570 : 'We develop a sieve that can detect primes in multiplicatively structured sets under certain conditions.'; abstract: least prime 'p << q^{350}' and 'the interval (x-x^{39/40}, x] contains primes for all large x'; 'Journal ref: None listed'.

items.name: Uniform PNT in progressions with explicit Siegel-zero secondary main term, and log-free zero density with Deuring-Heilbronn repulsion
items.statement: For coprime q,a and 4<=h<=x, with lambda = (1/h) integral_{x-h}^{x}(1 - chi_1(a) t^{beta_1 - 1}) dt if the exceptional zero beta_1 exists (lambda=1 otherwise), theta = 32/37 if beta_1 exists, 7/12 otherwise: if lambda h/phi(q) >= x^{theta+eps}, then sum_{x-h<p<=x, p=a mod q} log p = (lambda h/phi(q)) (1 + O(exp(-c_1 log x / ...))). Constants effective. Zero density (Thm 2.1): N_q(sigma,T) << (qT)^{(12/5+eps)(1-sigma)}; with beta_1 present N*_q << nu (qT)^{(37/5+eps)(1-sigma)}.
items.authors_year: Thorner, Zaman 2021 (arXiv, v2 Sept 2021); zero density from Huxley and Jutila
items.quote_or_locator: Thm 1.1 with "theta := 32/37 if beta_1 exists, 7/12 otherwise"; abstract: "uniform enough to deduce the Siegel-Walfisz theorem, Hoheisel's asymptotic ..., a Brun-Titchmarsh bound, and Linnik's bound"; (1.3): lambda h/phi(q) = h/phi(q) - chi_1(a)(x^{beta_1} - (x-h)^{beta_1})/(beta_1 phi(q)) 'primary main term plus secondary main term'. Thm 2.1 (2.1) and (2.2). Journal publication status not checked.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 no (proof uses zero-free region and zero density); T2 yes (uniform in q,h); T3 no; T4 partly (the secondary main term from beta_1 is explicit and exact, the remainder is an exp-type estimate); T5 no; T6 no; T7 yes.
items.relevance: Shows the correct shape of an unconditional result: the Siegel zero is an explicit secondary main term, not an error term. Useful as a model for how an exceptional zero enters an exact explicit formula. The Siegel-zero term itself is of known sign structure (1 - chi_1(a) t^{beta_1-1} >= 0 up to the sign of chi_1(a)), but this is no sign argument for s_E and s_O.
items.corrected_statement: Theorem 1.1 verified in extracted text: lambda defined as given; theta = 32/37 if beta_1 exists, 7/12 otherwise; for 0<eps<1-theta there is c1(eps)>0 such that lambda h/phi(q) >= x^{theta+eps} gives sum_{x-h<p<=x, p=a (q)} log p = (lambda h/phi(q))(1 + O_eps(exp(...))); implied constant and c1 effectively computable. Theorem 2.1: N_q(sigma,T) <<_eps (qT)^{(12/5+eps)(1-sigma)}; with beta_1: N*_q <<_eps nu(qT)(qT)^{(37/5+eps)(1-sigma)}. Published: Math. Z. 306 (2024), no. 3, Paper No. 54 (arXiv page). Remark 1.2 (q <= (log x)^A gives theta=7/12 with c1 ineffective in A) also confirmed. The item's elided error term is exp(-c1 log x / (log q + (log(x/h))^{32/31}... )) and I did not re-derive it.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2108.10878 (extracted text): 'theta := 32/37 if beta_1 exists, 7/12 otherwise'; '(2.1) N_q(sigma,T) << (qT)^{(12/5+eps)(1-sigma)}', '(2.2) N*_q << nu(qT)(qT)^{(37/5+eps)(1-sigma)}'; https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.10878 : 'Math. Z. 306 (2024), no. 3, Paper No. 54'.

items.name: Elliott-Halberstam conjecture
items.statement: EH[theta]: for Q = x^theta and every fixed A>=1, sum_{q<=Q} sup_{a in (Z/qZ)^*} |Delta(Lambda 1_[x,2x]; a mod q)| << x log^{-A} x. Conjectured for every 0<theta<1; proved only for theta<1/2 (Bombieri-Vinogradov). The case theta=1 is false.
items.authors_year: Elliott, Halberstam, Symposia Mathematica IV (1968/69), Academic Press 1970, pp. 59-72
items.quote_or_locator: Polymath arXiv:1407.4897, Claim 2.2: "EH[theta] ... sum_{q<=Q} sup |Delta| << x log^{-A} x"; "In [13] it was conjectured that EH[theta] held for all 0 < theta < 1. (The conjecture fails at the endpoint case theta = 1...)". Wikipedia says the original paper does not state the conjecture cleanly; the original was not opened.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 statement yes; T3 no; T4 no; T7 no (unproven; it is not known to follow from GRH).
items.relevance: Under EH, H_1 <= 6 under the generalized EH (Polymath). It would not give sign information on s_E or s_O. As a hypothesis it is not RH-equivalent, but it is not proven either.
items.corrected_statement: Statement confirmed (Polymath 8b Claim 2.2; 'fails at the endpoint case theta=1'). The item's relevance sentence is garbled: correct consequences are H_1 <= 12 under EH (Maynard, Thm 1.3(iii) in 8b) and H_1 <= 6 under the generalized EH (Polymath 8b, Thm 1.4(xii)); and H_1<=6 is the Selberg-parity limit of the method. Elliott-Halberstam original (Symposia Math. IV, 1970) not opened.
items.corrected_status: CONJECTURE (BV proves theta<1/2; theta=1 false by Friedlander-Granville)
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.4897 : 'Claim 2.2 (Elliott-Halberstam conjecture, EH[theta])'; 'In [13] it was conjectured that EH[theta] held for all 0 < theta < 1. (The conjecture fails at the endpoint ...'; Thm 1.3 '(iii) H1 <= 12' under EH; '(xii) H1 <= 6' under GEH.

items.name: Friedlander-Granville limitations to equidistribution (EH fails for q ~ x/(log x)^A)
items.statement: For every A >= 1 there are arbitrarily large x and a progression a mod q with (a,q)=1 and q <= x/(log x)^A such that |pi(x;q,a) - pi(x)/phi(q)| >> pi(x)/phi(q). Equivalently a weighted sum of the errors over q < x/log^N x is >> x; this disproves the Elliott-Halberstam conjecture for theta=1 (and a conjecture of Montgomery).
items.authors_year: Friedlander, Granville, Annals of Math. 129 (1989) 363-382
items.quote_or_locator: Annals abstract: "there exist arbitrarily large values of a and x" ... "disproves conjectures of Elliott and Halberstam, and of Montgomery". Soundararajan survey (arXiv:math/0606408, p.18): "for every A >= 1 there exist large x and an arithmetic progression a (mod q) with (a, q) = 1 and q <= x/(log x)^A such that pi(x;q,a) - pi(x)/phi(q) >> pi(x)/phi(q)".
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 statement yes; T2 yes (a limit on equidistribution for large q); T3 no; T4 n/a; T5 yes (via Maier's matrix method); T7 yes.
items.relevance: Limits what can be hoped for from averaged equidistribution: the upper range of moduli cannot reach x. The 'uncertainty principle' (Granville-Soundararajan) says primes cannot be simultaneously well distributed in short intervals and in progressions. No sign for the matrix K.
items.corrected_statement: Confirmed: Annals of Math. 129 (1989) 363-382, 'Limitations to the equi-distribution of primes I'; abstract: for any fixed N>0 there exist arbitrarily large a and x for which a sum of deviations is >= const*x; disproves conjectures of Elliott-Halberstam and of Montgomery. The pointwise form (q <= x/(log x)^A, pi(x;q,a)-pi(x)/phi(q) >>_A pi(x)/phi(q)) is quoted verbatim in Soundararajan's survey math/0606408 (page number 18 not checked).
items.check_evidence: https://annals.math.princeton.edu/1989/129-2/p04 : 'For any fixed N > 0 we show that there exist arbitrarily large values of a and x for which ...'; https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0606408 : 'Friedlander and Granville [8] proved that for every A >= 1 there exist large x and an arithmetic progression a (mod q) with (a,q)=1 and q <= x/(log x)^A such that pi(x;q,a) - pi(x)/phi(q) >>_A pi(x)/phi(q).'

items.name: Zhang 2013 and Polymath8a: level of distribution beyond 1/2 for smooth moduli (MPZ[varpi,delta])
items.statement: MPZ[varpi,delta]: for I in [1,x^delta], Q in x^{1/2+2 varpi}, and a primitive class a (P_I), sum over q<=Q with q in S_I (squarefree, prime factors in I) of |Delta(Lambda 1_[x,2x]; a (q))| << x log^{-A} x, with implied constant independent of a. Zhang: holds for 0 <= varpi,delta < 1/1168 (level 1/2 + 1/584). Polymath8a: holds whenever 600 varpi + 180 delta < 7, i.e. level 1/2 + 7/300; this gave H_1 <= 4680 (after Zhang's 70,000,000).
items.authors_year: Y. Zhang, Annals of Math. 179 (2014) 1121-1174; Polymath 8a (arXiv:1402.0811, 2014, Res. Math. Sci.); Polymath 8b arXiv:1407.4897
items.quote_or_locator: Polymath 8b: Claim 2.4 (MPZ), "Zhang ... obtained MPZ[varpi,delta] whenever 0 <= varpi,delta < 1/1168"; Theorem 2.5 "MPZ[varpi,delta] holds for every fixed varpi,delta >= 0 with 600 varpi + 180 delta < 7". Polymath8a abs (arXiv:1402.0811): exponent of distribution 1/2 + 7/300. Zhang DOI: 10.4007/annals.2014.179.3.7.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 statement yes, but proof uses exponential sums from algebraic geometry (Deligne); T2 n/a; T3 no; T4 no; T5 yes (dispersion method over moduli, classes with CRT conditions); T6 no; T7 yes.
items.relevance: The first proven cross-L-function cancellation beyond the GRH range (only for smooth moduli and fixed class). As size with absolute values it gives no sign. Nothing here is supported on all moduli.
items.corrected_statement: Confirmed: Zhang MPZ for varpi,delta<1/1168 (Polymath 8b Claim 2.4); Polymath 8a: MPZ[varpi,delta] whenever 600 varpi + 180 delta < 7, abstract 'exponent of distribution 1/2 + 7/300', H_1 <= 4680, and Zhang's gap bound 7x10^7. Zhang Annals 179 (2014) 1121-1174 and Res. Math. Sci. venue NOT opened. Polymath 8a arXiv:1402.0811v3 (3 Sep 2014).
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.4897 Theorem 2.5: 'MPZ[varpi,delta] holds for every fixed varpi,delta >= 0 with 600 varpi + 180 delta < 7'; https://arxiv.org/pdf/1402.0811 abstract: 'exponent of distribution 1/2 + 7/300'; 'lim inf (p_{n+1} - p_n) <= 4680'; 'some even h between 2 and 7 x 10^7'.

items.name: Stadlmann: level of distribution 1/2 + 1/40 for smooth moduli
items.statement: Primes up to x are on average equidistributed in progressions with smooth moduli up to x^{1/2 + 1/40 - eps}, improving Polymath's 1/2 + 7/300. Application: liminf (p_{n+m} - p_n) = O(exp(3.8075 m)).
items.authors_year: Stadlmann, arXiv 2309.00425 (Sept 2023, v3 Feb 2025); abs page says accepted in Advances in Mathematics (not independently confirmed)
items.quote_or_locator: abs: smooth moduli "up to size x^{1/2+1/40-eps}"; the abstract states that it "improves on a result of Polymath"; the main tool is a modified q-van der Corput process.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 statement yes; T3 no; T4 no; T5 yes (same as Polymath); T7 yes.
items.relevance: Current record for the smooth-moduli case with the Maynard-Tao sieve. Gives size bounds only; no entry point to the sign of s_E, s_O.
items.corrected_statement: Confirmed. Title: 'On primes in arithmetic progressions and bounded gaps between many primes' (arXiv 2309.00425, v1 1 Sep 2023, v3 22 Feb 2025); smooth moduli up to x^{1/2+1/40-eps}; improves Polymath 1/2+7/300; liminf bound O(exp(3.8075 m)); comments field: '43 pages. Revised version, accepted for publication in Advances in Mathematics' (journal ref field empty).
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00425 (fetched): comments 'accepted for publication in Advances in Mathematics'; abstract: smooth moduli 'up to roughly x^(1/2+1/40-eps)', 'improves Polymath's earlier exponent 1/2 + 7/300'.

items.name: Maynard, Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli I-III (2020)
items.statement: I (fixed a): sum over q1<=Q1, q2<=Q2 of |pi(x;q1 q2,a) - pi(x)/phi(q1 q2)| << x/(log x)^A under three inequalities of Q1, Q2 (as read from the PDF: Q1 Q2^2 < x^{1-100 eps}, Q1^{12} Q2^7 < x^{4-100 eps}, Q1^{20} Q2^{19} < x^{10-100 eps}; the exponents are reconstructed from a garbled extraction). Corollary 1.4: the sum over q1<=x^{1/21}, q2<=x^{10/21-eps} is << x/(log x)^A. Corollary 1.3: for Q <= x^{1/2+delta}, all but O(delta Q phi(a)/a) moduli q in [Q,2Q] satisfy the asymptotic. II: well-factorable weights, moduli up to x^{3/5-eps} (before: BFI 4/7). III: uniform in residue classes, Theorem 1.2 for Q1 Q2 Q3 = x^{1/2+delta} with Q3 free in a range.
items.quote_or_locator: I abs: "the primes are equidistributed for a fixed residue class over all moduli of size x^{1/2+delta} with a 'convenient sized' factor"; "the expected asymptotic holds for all but O(delta Q) moduli q ~ Q = x^{1/2+delta} and we get results for moduli as large as x^{11/21}". Intro: "by expanding the summand via Dirichlet characters and the explicit formula ... this would imply some cancellation for sums over zeroes of different L-functions"; "(estimates) which are not directly implied by the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis". III abs: "completely uniform with respect to the residue classes considered". II abs: x^{3/5-eps} (https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.07088; BFI: x^{4/7-eps}). Publication venues not checked.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 statement yes, proof uses Kloosterman sums (Deshouillers-Iwaniec, Kuznetsov) and Weil/Deligne; T2 n/a; T3 no (absolute values, error (log x)^{-A}); T4 no; T5 yes (explicit cross-L-function cancellation, in Maynard's own words); T6 no; T7 yes.
items.relevance: The strongest proven T5 statement in the domain. It does not give a sign: it bounds the absolute value of the sum, with moduli only of the form q1 q2 with a convenient factor. K has no moduli, so it enters only after a Dirichlet character twist of the window.
items.corrected_statement: Exponents now VERIFIED from the PDF (the item flagged them as reconstructed): Theorem 1.1 conditions Q1 Q2^2 < x^{1-100 eps}, Q1^{12} Q2^7 < x^{4-100 eps}, Q1^{20} Q2^{19} < x^{10-100 eps}, with (q1,a)=(q2,a)=1, bound << x/(log x)^A. Corollary 1.3: 0<delta<1/55, Q<=x^{1/2+delta}: all but at most 18 delta Q phi(a)/a moduli q in [Q,2Q] ('99% of moduli' for Q<=x^{1/2+1/2000}). Corollary 1.4: q1<=x^{1/21}, q2<=x^{10/21-eps}. I: arXiv 2006.06572, 11 Jun 2020, v2 5 Apr 2021, 102 pp. II: 2006.07088 (12 Jun 2020), well-factorable weights, x^{3/5} vs BFI x^{4/7}. III: 2006.08250 (15 Jun 2020), 'completely uniform with respect to the residue classes'. No journal refs on arXiv pages; Theorem 1.2 of III not checked.

(1.3) Q1 Q2^2 < x^{1-100 eps}, (1.4) Q1^{12} Q2^7 < x^{4-100 eps}, (1.5) Q1^{20} Q2^{19} < x^{10-100 eps}'; 'Corollary 1.3 ... all but at most 18 delta Q phi(a)/a moduli'; https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.07088 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08250 .

items.name: Lichtman: level of distribution 66/107 with triply well-factorable weights
items.statement: Level of distribution 66/107 (about 0.617) for primes with triply well-factorable weights, above Maynard's 3/5; 5/8 under Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture. Application: first use of a distribution level beyond the square-root barrier for Goldbach; new upper bounds for twin primes and Goldbach representations.
items.authors_year: Lichtman, arXiv:2309.08522 (Aug 2023), with an appendix by Drappeau; published version not checked
items.quote_or_locator: abs: "This gives the highest level of distribution for primes in any setting"; surpasses 3/5; "first use of a level of distribution beyond the square-root barrier" (Goldbach).
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 statement yes, proof uses Deshouillers-Iwaniec spectral large sieve; T3 no; T4 no; T5 yes (as with Maynard II); T7 yes. Preprint status: referee status not verified.
items.relevance: Current record for well-factorable weights. It is an average weighted by a sieve weight, not a sign of anything. A 2026 arXiv preprint by Runbo Li (arXiv:2602.20917, v6 May 2026, unrefereed) claims bilinear moduli up to x^{9/17} and trilinear up to x^{17/32}.
items.corrected_statement: Confirmed: arXiv 2309.08522, 'Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli, and Goldbach beyond the square-root barrier', submitted 30 Aug 2023, appendix with Drappeau, 55 pp.; level 66/107 (~0.617) with triply well-factorable weights, 5/8 under Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture; 'highest level of distribution for primes in any setting'. No journal ref on arXiv page. Runbo Li arXiv:2602.20917 CONFIRMED: 'Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli and refinements of Harman's sieve', v1 24 Feb 2026, v6 27 May 2026, 87 pp., bilinear moduli up to x^{9/17}, trilinear x^{17/32}, no journal ref (unrefereed as far as shown); note these are for majorant/minorant functions, not the same statement as Lichtman's weights.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (arXiv; refereed status not confirmed). Li: unrefereed preprint
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.08522 (fetched summary): 'level of distribution of 66/107 ... triply well-factorable weights ... highest known for primes in any setting'; https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20917 : versions v1-v6, 'bilinear moduli up to x^(9/17) and trilinear moduli up to x^(17/32)', 'No journal reference'.

items.name: Exceptional characters give asymptotics beyond sqrt(x): Friedlander-Iwaniec 2003, Wright 2023/2025, Sachpazis 2025
items.statement: Under the existence of a real primitive character chi mod D with extremely small L(1,chi) (i.e. an extreme Landau-Siegel zero): FI: for x >= D^r, r = 554,401 and q <= x^{233/462}: psi(x;q,a) = (psi(x)/phi(q))(1 - 1_{D|q} chi(a)) + O(L(1,chi)(log x)^{r^r}). Wright 2023: L(1,chi) < (log D)^{-R}, R>7, q < x^{30/59-eps}, EH-type Q < x^{16/31-eps}. Wright 2025: L(1,chi)=o((log D)^{-5}), almost all a for q < x^{2/3-eps}. Sachpazis 2025: no size condition on the quality eta, q <= x^{58/115-eps}.
items.authors_year: Friedlander-Iwaniec IMRN 2003; Wright arXiv:2311.12470 (2023, v2 2024) and arXiv:2507.10780 (2025); Sachpazis arXiv:2511.16452 (v2 Sept 2026)
items.quote_or_locator: Sachpazis intro: "Theorem FI ... psi(x;q,a) = psi(x)/phi(q) (1 - 1_{D|q} chi(a) + O(...))" for "q <= x^{1/2+1/231} = x^{233/462}"; Theorem 1.1 with q <= x^{58/115-eps}. Wright abs 2311.12470: "q < x^{30/59 - eps}" and "16/31". Wright abs 2507.10780: "q < x^{2/3 - eps}". FI original not opened; Wright and Sachpazis are preprints (the Sachpazis abs page says forthcoming in J. Lond. Math. Soc., not independently confirmed).
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 no (hypothesis about an L-function); T3 no; T4 partly (the Siegel-zero term -chi(a)1_{D|q} psi(x)/phi(q) is exact); T7 no (conditional on a non-existence hypothesis that Oct 2026 preprints claim to refute).
items.relevance: A Siegel zero would produce an exact secondary term past the GRH barrier, a case where a hypothetical zero gives a more precise formula than GRH. Conditional on a hypothesis (existence of an extreme zero) that is believed to be false. A useful contrast: a violation of RH-type structure would be visible in primes.
items.corrected_statement: FI (IMRN 2003, no. 37, 2033-2050): r=554,401, x>=D^r, q<=x^{1/2+1/231}=x^{233/462}, psi(x;q,a)=(psi(x)/phi(q))(1-1_{D|q}chi(a)) + O(L(1,chi)(log x)^{r^r}) - CONFIRMED via Sachpazis (original not opened). Wright 2311.12470 (v2 Nov 2024): L(1,chi)<(log D)^{-R}, R>7, q<x^{30/59-eps}, Q<x^{16/31-eps} - CONFIRMED (no journal ref). items.name: Heath-Brown 1983: Siegel zeros imply the twin prime conjecture
items.statement: If there are infinitely many Landau-Siegel zeros beta_j = 1 - 1/(eta_j log D_j) with eta_j -> infinity, then the twin prime conjecture holds. So at least one of 'no Siegel zeros (with growing quality)' or 'infinitely many twin primes' is true.
items.authors_year: Heath-Brown 1983 (as cited in Sachpazis 2025)
items.quote_or_locator: Sachpazis: "from a 1983 result of Heath-Brown [4], it follows that if there exist infinitely many Landau-Siegel zeroes ... with eta_j -> +infinity, then the Twin Prime Conjecture must be true." Wikipedia Siegel zero: "Heath-Brown (1983): at least one of 'no Siegel zeros' or 'infinitely many twin primes' holds." Original paper not opened.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 no; T3 no; T4 no; T5 yes (links zeros of L(s,chi) to correlations of primes p, p+2); T7 yes (it is an implication, not an RH-equivalent).
items.relevance: A proven implication tying a hypothetical zero configuration to prime-pair correlation. It shows that correlations between different primes can be forced by L-function zeros, but gives no sign of s_E or s_O.
items.corrected_statement: Confirmed. Reference: D. R. Heath-Brown, 'Prime twins and Siegel zeros', Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) 47 (1983), no. 2, 193-224. Wikipedia states the dichotomy 'At least one: no Siegel zeros, or infinitely many twin primes' (following Tao's exposition). Sachpazis's phrasing: infinitely many Landau-Siegel zeros with eta_j -> infinity imply the twin prime conjecture. Matomaki-Merikoski 'Siegel zeros, twin primes, Goldbach's conjecture, and primes in short intervals' is a related later source (listed in Sachpazis [10]). Note: if the October 2026 no-Siegel-zero claim is verified, this implication becomes vacuous.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.16452 : 'from a 1983 result of Heath-Brown [4], it follows that if there exist infinitely many Landau-Siegel zeroes beta_j = 1 - 1/(eta_j log D_j) such that eta_j -> +infinity, then the Twin Prime Conjecture must be true.' Ref [4] as above; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siegel_zero : 'At least one of the following is true: (1) There are no Siegel zeros. (2) There are infinitely many twin primes.'

items.name: Rubinstein-Sarnak: Chebyshev's bias (prime number races)
items.statement: Under GRH and Linear Independence (LI) of the imaginary parts of the zeros of the L(s,chi) mod q, the set of x with pi(x;q,a_1) > ... > pi(x;q,a_r) has a logarithmic density, given by an absolutely continuous limiting distribution; the density is strictly between 0 and 1 for all orderings.
items.authors_year: Rubinstein, Sarnak, Experimental Mathematics 3 (1994) 173-197 (volume as relayed; original not opened); overview Bose-Simpson
items.quote_or_locator: Bose-Simpson: "the two authors proved several results concerning prime number races underneath two assumptions ...: GRH and Linear Independence"; "Theorem 1.2 [9, Theorem 1.4] Assume GRH and LI. The prime number race (q; a_1,...,a_r) is ...". I did not find the 0.9959 constant for (4;3,1) in the PDF text, so I do not state it.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 no (derived from zeros); T3 no (density of a sign pattern, not a theorem about sign); T4 no; T7 no (GRH and LI hypotheses).
items.relevance: A sign phenomenon (pi(x;q,3)-pi(x;q,1) mostly positive) that rests on GRH+LI, i.e. on the zero side. It shows that signs of prime-counting differences are controlled by zeros, which is exactly the circularity (zero-sum equals prime sum) that blocks a proof of positivity of K.
items.corrected_statement: Core fact supported by secondary search: under GRH and LI, the logarithmic density of {x: pi(x;4,3)>pi(x;4,1)} exists and is about 0.9959 (one source says GRH + 'Grand Simplicity Hypothesis' instead of LI; LI is the standard statement). The Knapowski-Turan natural-density-1 conjecture is false. The journal citation (Experimental Math. 3 (1994) 173-197), Theorem 1.4 numbering, 'absolutely continuous distribution' and 'strictly between 0 and 1 for all orderings' were NOT verified by me (I never read the Bose-Simpson PDF). Zero-side circularity remark in relevance is the author's inference.

items.name: Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer: Beurling systems with regular integers but zeros near Re s = 1
items.statement: There is a Beurling generalized number system with integer counting function N_B(x) = kappa x + O(x^theta) (1/2 < theta < 1) whose prime counting function oscillates strongly; its zeta function has infinitely many zeros near sigma = 1 - a/log t and none to the right of that curve, with a > (4/e)(1-theta).

The full text was not opened; the zero statement comes from the abstract record and search summary.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 n/a; T3 no; T7 shows that density plus Euler-product axioms cannot give a zero-free region or RH.
items.relevance: Central for the Beurling argument of the whole domain: a property that every Beurling system with the same density shares cannot prove RH. Every AP and Siegel-zero theorem above is of this type or uses integer structure that Beurling systems lack (no residue classes), so none of them alone can decide the sign. A proof must use arithmetic of Z not available in a general Beurling system. Note Broucke et al. arXiv:2004.11501 treats Beurling integers with RH and large oscillation.

merged.title: Sieve theory and the parity problem
merged.summary: Direct answer: this domain contains NO proven tool meeting T1-T7. It contains one proven meta-theorem that explains why: the parity barrier (Selberg 1949-52; Bombieri 1975-76 gives the iff form). Sieve inputs (AP / Type I data, which is exactly the prime-side data of K) put equal weight on integers with even and odd numbers of prime factors, so they are blind to the lambda(n)-sign correlations that T5 asks for. Named barriers: (B1) parity: any sieve upper bound for primes is off by a factor >= 2 and no non-trivial lower bound follows from pure sieve data; (B2) Ford 2005: R(nu) for any fixed nu<1 does not suffice for the Bombieri asymptotic formula; (B3) Siegel zeros: the sieve factor 2 is tied to a possible Siegel zero (Brun-Titchmarsh 2 -> 2-delta would exclude one; Granville 2020 conditional optimality). Best SIGN candidate: Selberg's square representation (sum_{d|n} lambda_d)^2 >= 1_{P^-(n)>=z}, a Gram/quadratic form positive by construction, whose shape matches the project's m = B0 + sum C_n, C_n >= 0; but it is a one-sided inequality (T4 fails, loss exactly the parity factor 2), and a companion mechanism is the large-sieve derivation from non-negativity of a variance (Vaughan notes), dual to Selberg's sieve. Parity-breaking results (Friedlander-Iwaniec 1998, Heath-Brown 2001, Heath-Brown-Li 2017, Maynard digits, Tao 2016 two-point log-averaged Chowla) get T5 only through sequence-specific Type II/bilinear structure, which the Weil window does not supply (fails T2/T3: they give asymptotics or sizes, not a sign, and are not uniform over windows). Bounded gaps (GPY/Maynard) sidestep parity by pigeonhole without saying which shifts are prime: also no sign. Beurling column: everything stated from sieve axioms alone (g(d), R(nu)) holds for Beurling systems (YES), and Selberg's own example a_n = 1+lambda(n) is exactly why axioms cannot fix prime content; results that use Dirichlet characters/AP/Siegel-Walfisz (BV, Chen, GPY, Maynard) are NO. Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer 2006 is the Beurling barrier: regular integers, N(x)=x+O(x^theta), yet wildly oscillating primes. Open follow-up: Bombieri's iff characterization says Lambda_k (k>=2) is parity-balanced while Lambda itself (the object in K) is not; whether a Lambda_2-type (Selberg symmetry) reformulation of K exists is UNVERIFIED speculation, not a sourced result.

items.name: Brun's sieve (1915) and convergence of sum of 1/p over twin primes
items.statement: Combinatorial sieve (truncated inclusion-exclusion) of Viggo Brun. Consequence proved by Brun: sum over primes p with p+2 prime of 1/p < infinity (Brun's constant finite). Also (Cambridge text, secondary): infinitely many n with n and n+2 each having at most nine prime factors. The 'fundamental lemma' of sieve theory is the later general form.

items.name: Selberg Lambda^2 sieve (square of a divisor sum)
items.statement: For any real lambda_d with lambda_1 = 1: (sum_{d|n, P+(d)<=z} lambda_d)^2 >= sum_{d|n, P+(d)<=z} mu(d) = 1 if P^-(n) >= z, 0 otherwise. Summing over n in A gives #{n in A: P^-(n) >= z} <= sum_{d1,d2} lambda_{d1} lambda_{d2} #{n in A: [d1,d2] | n}, a quadratic form in lambda_d, positive semidefinite by construction (it is a sum of squares over n); lambda_d is then chosen (zero for d >= z) to minimise it.
items.authors_year: A. Selberg, 1947, 'On an elementary method in the theory of primes', Norske Vid. Selsk. Forh. Trondheim 19 (1947), 64-67
items.quote_or_locator: Granville-Koukoulopoulos-Maynard, Sieve weights and their smoothings, intro eq. (1.1): 'which is valid for any real numbers lambda_d with lambda_1 = 1' and 'which is a quadratic form in the variables lambda_d'; Selberg ref [21] there: Norske Vid. Selsk. Forh., Trondhjem 19 (1947). Page numbers 64-67 from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selberg_sieve (secondary).
items.fit_T1_T7: Passes T1, T2, T3 (positivity by squares, the only genuine sign mechanism in this domain), T7. Fails T4: it is a one-sided inequality (square >= indicator), the loss being exactly the parity factor 2; fails T5 (even/odd weights equidistributed); T6 not addressed.
items.relevance: Closest structural analogue of 'sign by representation as a sum of squares with C_n >= 0' on the prime/arithmetic side, matching the project's rule 18. But Selberg's square only dominates the prime indicator, it never equals it, so it cannot give the exact sign of the Weil quadratic form; making it an identity would require removing parity, i.e. proving prime-side statements as hard as RH. Beurling: the inequality (1.1) is pure algebra on any multiplicative semigroup (inference, UNVERIFIED), the remainder control is not.
items.corrected_statement: The inequality is the standard one, but I did not open the quoted eq. (1.1) of Granville-Koukoulopoulos-Maynard (only the abstract page of arXiv 1606.06781 was opened) and did not open the Selberg 1947 paper. Page range 64-67 is from Wikipedia only.
