items.name: Selberg's parity problem (parity barrier)
items.statement: Sieve methods based only on information of the form sum_{n in A, d|n} 1 = g(d)X + r_d cannot distinguish numbers with an even from an odd number of prime factors. Selberg's example: a_n = 1 + lambda(n) (lambda = Liouville function) satisfies R(nu) for all nu<1 with A(x)=x, g(d)=1/d, yet a_n = 0 for n prime and S1(x) = sum_{n<=x} a_n Lambda(n) = O(sqrt x), contradicting the expected ~H A(x). Consequences (Maynard): every sieve upper bound for primes is off by a factor >= 2, and no non-trivial lower bound for #primes in A follows from pure sieve data.
items.authors_year: A. Selberg, 1949-1952 (the general sieve method and its place in prime-number theory, Proc. ICM Cambridge MA 1950, vol. 1, 286-292, AMS 1952); an entry in Skand. Mat. Kongr. Trondheim 1949, 13-22 (1952) was seen in a search result without title
items.quote_or_locator: Ford 2005, intro: 'That sieve methods cannot produce (1.1) was discovered by Selberg [10] in the 1940s. His example is a_n = 1 + lambda(n)' and 'sieve procedures cannot distinguish between numbers with an even number of prime factors and an odd number of prime factors, a property known as the parity problem'; ref [10] = Selberg, Proc. ICM 1950. Also Maynard ICM 2022 https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/IMU/Prizes/Fields/2022/jm.pdf section 3.2: 'any upper bound sieve for primes will be off by a factor of at least 2'. The Trondheim title string I first searched for was NOT confirmed.
items.fit_T1_T7: Not a tool but the theorem that kills T5 for all sieve-axiom approaches: proven statement that AP-type (Type I) prime data cannot see the sign of lambda(n) correlations. Consistent with T7 (unconditional).
items.relevance: Explains the circularity found in ~65 attempts in the sieve language: any sign proved from prime-side distribution data that is parity-blind cannot reach s_E, s_O at 1e-29 margins, because that sign is a parity-sensitive statement. Beurling (my inference, UNVERIFIED): Liouville-type completely multiplicative function exists on any Beurling system, so Selberg's counterexample construction transfers; the barrier therefore does not distinguish Beurling systems from the integers.
items.corrected_statement: Confirmed: Selberg found in the 1940s that sieve axioms cannot give (1.1); example a_n = 1+lambda(n). Maynard: any upper-bound sieve for primes is off by a factor of at least 2, and pure sieve methods give no non-trivial lower bound for primes in A. Ford's reference [10] is Selberg's ICM 1950 talk (not independently opened by me). The Trondheim 1949 entry remains unconfirmed.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0401215 line: 'That sieve methods cannot produce (1.1) was discovered by Selberg [10] in the 1940s. His example is a_n = 1 + lambda(n)'. Maynard ICM https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/IMU/Prizes/Fields/2022/jm.pdf sec. 3.2: 'any upper bound sieve for primes will be off by a factor of at least 2 ... we cannot hope to obtain a non-trivial lower bound for the number of primes in a set A by just using pure sieve methods.'

items.name: Large sieve (Linnik 1941 -> Roth/Bombieri 1965 -> Gallagher 1967 -> Montgomery-Vaughan 1973, sharp)
items.statement: For real points x_r with ||x_r - x_s|| >= delta (r != s): sum_r |sum_{n=M+1}^{M+N} a_n e(n x_r)|^2 <= (N - 1 + delta^{-1}) sum |a_n|^2. Farey/arithmetic form: sum_{q<=Q} sum_{(a,q)=1} |S(a/q)|^2 <= (N - 1 + Q^2) sum |a_n|^2 (take delta = Q^-2). Bombieri-Davenport (1968): constant is best possible. Derivation by the non-negativity of the 'variance' V(p) = (1/p) sum_a |S(a/p)|^2 - |Z|^2 (p-g(p))/(p g(p)) >= 0 and the Duality Lemma (a matrix and its adjoint have the same operator norm).
items.authors_year: Linnik 1941-42; Roth 1965; Bombieri 1965; Gallagher 1967; Montgomery and Vaughan, Mathematika 20 (1973) 119-134; Selberg (known before 1977, published 1991); Bombieri-Davenport 1968
items.quote_or_locator: R. C. Vaughan, notes 'The Large Sieve' (ch. 5), pp. 1-4: 'Since the variance is non-negative ... we conclude that |Z| sum (p-g(p))/g(p) <= sum sum |S(a/p)|^2'; 'Montgomery and Vaughan [1973,1974] ... gave proofs that the bound holds with Y0(N, delta) = N - 1 + delta^-1, and it had already been shown by Bombieri and Davenport [1968] that this is best possible'; 'In some sense they are the duals of the Selberg sieve as applied to an interval.' History 1941: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_sieve (secondary).
items.fit_T1_T7: Passes T1, T2 (uniform over all coefficient vectors), T7; the constant N - 1 + delta^-1 is sharp. Fails T3 (operator-norm upper bound, no sign), T5 (no prime content), T6.
items.relevance: Operator-norm control of Gram matrices of exponentials, sharp, uniform in the vector. It is a size bound on a PSD matrix, not a sign; could bound the archimedean/zero-spacing side but it cannot supply s_E <= 0 or s_O >= 0. Beurling: pure harmonic analysis on points, no primes involved. Relevant mechanism: positivity from a variance (a square), dual to Selberg's sieve.
items.corrected_statement: Statement N-1+delta^{-1} confirmed as the sharp large-sieve constant, but attribution is joint: Vaughan credits Montgomery-Vaughan [1973,1974], with an added wrinkle by Paul Cohen [1977], and Selberg [1991, known before 1977]. Roth 1965: N+Q^2 log Q; Bombieri 1965: N+CQ^2; Gallagher 1967: pi N+Q^2; Linnik 1941. Bombieri-Davenport 1968: best possible even for Y(N,Q). The MV 1974 Hilbert-inequality paper itself says delta^{-1} cannot be replaced by delta^{-1}-C for C>1 (citing Bombieri-Davenport).
items.check_evidence: https://personal.science.psu.edu/rcv4/LargeSieve.pdf (pdftotext): 'Montgomery and Vaughan [1973,1974], with an added wrinkle by Paul Cohen [1977], and Selberg [1991, but known by him before 1977] gave proofs that the bound holds with Y0(N,delta)=N-1+delta^{-1}, and it had already been shown by Bombieri and Davenport [1968] that this is best possible'; 'Linnik [1941,1942]'; 'Roth [1965] ... Bombieri [1965] ... Gallagher [1967]'. Ref list: 'Montgomery and Vaughan [1973], The large sieve, Mathematika 20, 119-134'.

items.name: Montgomery-Vaughan generalized Hilbert inequality
items.statement: Theorem 1: for real x_1..x_R distinct mod 1 and delta = min_{r!=s} ||x_r - x_s||: |sum'_{r,s} u_r conj(u_s) csc pi(x_r - x_s)| <= delta^{-1} sum |u_r|^2 (1.2); and if 0 < delta_r <= min_s ||x_r - x_s|| then |sum' ...| <= (3/2) sum |u_r|^2 delta_r^{-1} (1.3). Analogous inequalities for sum u_r conj(u_s)/(lambda_r - lambda_s) (Hilbert: constant 2 pi improved by Schur to pi).
items.authors_year: H. L. Montgomery, R. C. Vaughan, 'Hilbert's inequality', J. London Math. Soc. (2) 8 (1974) 73-82
items.quote_or_locator: Page 1 of the scan (local copy /mnt/hdd01/Soft/GitHub/chen_q3_rh_clean/docs/literature/montgomery_vaughan_hilbert_1974.pdf), THEOREM 1, eq. (1.2) and (1.3), read from the page image: 'Theorem 1. Let x_1,...,x_R denote real numbers which are distinct modulo 1 ... delta = min_+ ||x_r - x_s||'.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1, T2, T7 yes (no primes at all). Fails T3 (absolute value bound on an indefinite bilinear form), T4 (constants sharp but it is an inequality), T5, T6.
items.relevance: Controls off-diagonal bilinear forms with csc/1-over-difference kernels, the same kernel type as the large sieve for Dirichlet polynomials and zero-sum sides. Size only; no sign for <v,Kv>.
items.corrected_statement: Confirmed from the local scan OCR: Theorem 1 gives (1.2) with constant delta^{-1} and (1.3) with delta_r^{-1} weights (constant 3/2; OCR of the 3/2 glyph is garbled, but the text says the constant in (1.3) is not best possible and may be replaceable by unity). Addition: they note delta^{-1} cannot be improved to delta^{-1}-C for C>1 (Bombieri-Davenport / Matthews). Schur replaced Hilbert's 2 pi by pi. J. London Math. Soc. (2) 8 (1974) 73-82.
items.check_evidence: /mnt/hdd01/Soft/GitHub/chen_q3_rh_clean/docs/literature/montgomery_vaughan_hilbert_1974.pdf via pdftotext: 'Received 26 February, 1973. [J. LONDON MATH. SOC. (2), 8 (1974), 73-82]'; 'later Schur [13] replaced the [2pi] by the best possible constant pi'; 'it is not possible to replace delta^-1 by delta^-1 - C if C > 1. In (1.3) the constant is not best possible.'

items.name: Brun-Titchmarsh inequality with constant 2 (sieve) and its link to Siegel zeros
items.statement: pi(x; q, a) <= 2x / (phi(q) log(x/q)) (Montgomery-Vaughan 1973, via the large sieve). Maynard: when x is large relative to q this is off by a factor ~2 from the expected asymptotic, and improving 2 to 2 - delta in this regime would rule out a Siegel zero.
items.authors_year: H. L. Montgomery, R. C. Vaughan, The large sieve, Mathematika 20 (1973) 119-134 (ref [69] of the survey)
items.quote_or_locator: Maynard, Counting primes (ICM 2022), section 3.2: 'the Brun-Titchmarsh Theorem [69] ... states that pi(x;q,a) <= 2x/(phi(q) log(x/q)) ... improving the constant 2 to 2 - delta in this regime would rule out the possibility of a Siegel zero.' Reference [69] = Montgomery-Vaughan, The large sieve, Mathematika 20 (1973), 119-134.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1, T2, T7 yes. Fails T3, T4, T5. The factor 2 is the parity loss in disguise.
items.relevance: Shows concretely that the parity factor 2 cannot be removed without controlling exceptional zeros (RH-adjacent L-function information). Beurling (inference, UNVERIFIED): the statement is about Dirichlet-character progressions, which a Beurling system lacks.
items.corrected_statement: Confirmed: pi(x;q,a) <= 2x/(phi(q) log(x/q)) (Montgomery-Vaughan, Mathematika 20 (1973) 119-134), valid for x>q (the item omits the range). Maynard: improving 2 to 2-delta when x is large relative to q would rule out a Siegel zero.
items.check_evidence: https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/IMU/Prizes/Fields/2022/jm.pdf sec. 3.2: 'Brun-Titchmarsh Theorem [69] ... pi(x;q,a) <= 2x/(phi(q) log(x/q)). When x is fairly large relative to q, this is off by a factor of roughly 2 ... but improving the constant 2 to 2-delta in this regime would rule out the possibility of a Siegel zero.' Ref [69] = Montgomery-Vaughan, The large sieve, Mathematika 20 (1973), 323? ICM list prints 'Mathematika 20 (1973)'; Vaughan notes print '119-134'.

items.name: Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem
items.statement: For fixed A>0: sum_{q<=Q} max_{(a,q)=1} sup_{y<=x} |psi(y;q,a) - y/phi(q)| << x (log x)^-A + x^{1/2} Q (log xQ)^6 (Bombieri's form with the Vaughan-type constant). In particular a level of distribution 1/2: Q = x^{1/2}(log x)^{-B} gives an error << x (log x)^{-A}. Comparable on average over q to GRH.
items.authors_year: E. Bombieri 1965; A. I. Vinogradov 1965-66 (with a precursor by Barban)
items.quote_or_locator: R. C. Vaughan, 'The Bombieri-Vinogradov Theorem', section 1 (displayed inequality): 'For any fixed positive number A, sum_{q<=Q} max_{(a,q)=1} sup_{y<=x} |psi(y;q,a) - y/phi(q)| << x(log x)^-A + x^{1/2} Q (log xQ)^6'; 'Bombieri had a somewhat inflated logarithmic factor ... Vinogradov had an x^epsilon'.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 (prime-side), T2, T7 yes. Fails T3, T4, T5: an on-average size statement over moduli, not a sign and not about correlations between different primes beyond AP equidistribution.
items.relevance: It is the input (the 'Type I' level of distribution 1/2) for every sieve result below. Proved via the large sieve and zero-density estimates; it is GRH-strength on average. Cannot give the sign of the window form. Beurling (inference, UNVERIFIED): needs Dirichlet characters and zero-free regions of L(s,chi).
items.corrected_statement: Confirmed verbatim in Vaughan's notes. The 'Barban precursor' is not in the source and stays UNVERIFIED. Vaughan also says: practically as good on average as GRH for all chi to moduli q <= x^{1/2}(log x)^{6-A}, and the term x^{1/2}Q(log xQ)^6 is not improvable apart from the log power even under GRH. The Q = x^{1/2}(log x)^{-B} corollary is a derived statement.
items.check_evidence: https://personal.science.psu.edu/rcv4/Bombieri.pdf (pdftotext): 'Bombieri's version of the Bombieri [1965]-A.I. Vinogradov [1965,1966] theorem. For any fixed positive number A, sum_{q<=Q} max_{(a,q)=1} sup_{y<=x} |psi(y;q,a) - y/phi(q)| <<_A x(log x)^{-A} + x^{1/2} Q (log xQ)^6. Bombieri had a somewhat inflated logarithmic factor ... Vinogradov had an x^epsilon.'

items.name: Bombieri's asymptotic sieve (iff characterization of parity)
items.statement: Given non-negative a_n with A_d(x) = sum_{n<=x, d|n} a_n = g(d)A(x) + r_d(x) and R(nu): for all B>0, sum_{d<=x^nu} |r_d| << A(x)/(log x)^B, for all nu<1, one obtains asymptotics for sum a_n f(n) iff f gives equal weight to numbers with an even and an odd number of prime factors. The generalized von Mangoldt functions Lambda_k(n) = sum_{d|n} mu(d) log^k(n/d), k >= 2, have this property, and then S_k(x) = sum a_n Lambda_k(n) ~ k H A(x) (log x)^{k-1}. Lambda itself (k=1) does not.
items.authors_year: E. Bombieri, 'On twin almost-primes', Acta Arith. 28 (1975) 177-193, 457-461; 'The asymptotic sieve', Mem. Accad. Naz. dei XL 1/2 (1976) 243-269; alternative proof Friedlander-Iwaniec, Bombieri's sieve, 1996
items.quote_or_locator: Ford, On Bombieri's asymptotic sieve, intro: 'Bombieri clarified things further, showing essentially that knowledge of R(nu) for all nu<1 ... implies an asymptotic formula for sum a_n f(n) if and only if f gives equal weight to numbers with an even number of prime factors and an odd number of prime factors'; 'Bombieri proved that if R(nu) for all nu<1, then S_k(x) ~ k H A(x)(log x)^{k-1}'. Ford Trans. AMS 357 (2005) 1663-1674, refs [1],[2]. The original Bombieri papers were not opened.
items.fit_T1_T7: Exact characterization (iff), T1, T2, T7 hold for the framework. Fails T3 (asymptotics, not sign), T5 by construction: it states precisely which weights f the axioms can see, and Lambda (the weight in K) is outside that class.
items.relevance: Sharpest proven statement of what sieve-axiom data can and cannot compute: parity-balanced weights (Lambda_k, k>=2) are accessible, Lambda is not. K is built on Lambda(n)/sqrt(n), so the pole-free bulk is in the inaccessible class. Whether a Lambda_2-type (Selberg symmetry formula) reformulation of K exists is UNVERIFIED speculation. Beurling: the theorem is formulated for abstract sequences (axioms g(d), R(nu)), so it plausibly transfers (inference, UNVERIFIED).
items.corrected_statement: Confirmed via Ford's introduction; Bombieri's original papers not opened. Ford also records that Friedlander-Iwaniec proved S_1(x) ~ H A(x) under R(nu) for some nu>2/3 plus a bilinear-sum condition.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0401215 (pdftotext) line 85: 'Bombieri proved that if R(nu) for all nu<1, then S_k(x) ~ k H A(x)(log x)^{k-1}' and 'Recently there was a major breakthrough on the parity problem by Friedlander and Iwaniec [6]. They proved S_1(x) ~ H A(x) under two major assumptions. First, R(nu) holds for some nu>2/3.'

items.name: Bombieri asymptotic sieve is sharp in the hypothesis (Ford 2005)
items.statement: Theorem 1 (Ford): fix nu in (0,1). There is a sequence (a_n) satisfying R(nu) with A(x)=x and g(d)=1/d for which S_k(x) ~ k x (log x)^{k-1} fails for every k >= 1. I.e. level-of-distribution nu < 1 alone is not enough; one needs 'best possible' distribution.
items.authors_year: K. Ford, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 357 (2005) 1663-1674 (arXiv math/0401215, Jan 2004)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: 'By constructing appropriate sequences, we show that any weakening of the well-distribution property is not sufficient to deduce the same conclusion.' Theorem 1 in intro (verbatim from PDF text): 'Fix nu in (0,1). There is a sequence (a_n) which satisfies R(nu) with A(x) = x and g(d) = 1/d, and for which (1.3) fails for every k >= 1.'
items.fit_T1_T7: A barrier theorem: any argument using only partial well-distribution (any nu<1, e.g. Elliott-Halberstam short of full strength) cannot reach prime-level asymptotics. Passes T7.
items.relevance: Rules out proving window positivity from partial equidistribution data (nu<1) in a sieve framework; consistent with the 1e-29 margins requiring exact, not nearly-exact, input. Beurling: constructed sequences are abstract; transfer plausible (inference, UNVERIFIED).
items.corrected_statement: Theorem 1 verbatim: 'Fix nu in (0,1). There is a sequence (a_n) which satisfies R(nu) with A(x)=x and g(d)=1/d, and for which (1.3) fails for every k >= 1.' Trans. AMS 357 (2005) 1663-1674 (online 2004). Ford adds that a_n can be taken in {0,1,2} and the sequences exhibit a global parity bias.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0401215 (pdftotext lines 105-116); https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0401215 'Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 357 (2005), 1663-1674'; Crossref DOI 10.1090/s0002-9947-04-03579-2.

items.name: Friedlander-Iwaniec asymptotic sieve for primes and x^2+y^4 (parity broken with an extra axiom)
items.statement: Add a bilinear (Type II type) axiom to the classical sieve axioms to 'break the parity problem'. Application: sum_{a^2+b^4<=x} Lambda(a^2+b^4) = 4 pi^-1 kappa x^{3/4} (1 + O(log log x / log x)), kappa = int_0^1 (1-t^4)^{1/2} dt = Gamma(1/4)^2/(6 sqrt(2 pi)); in particular infinitely many primes a^2 + b^4.
items.authors_year: J. Friedlander, H. Iwaniec, 'Asymptotic sieve for primes', Ann. of Math. 148 (1998) 1041-1065; 'The polynomial X^2+Y^4 captures its primes', Ann. of Math. 148 (1998) 945-1040
items.quote_or_locator: arXiv math/9811186 abstract: 'adding an additional axiom to the classical formulation' to 'break the well-known parity problem'; intro: 'This general limitation is recognized as the parity problem of sieve theory'. arXiv math/9811185 main formula as above (abstract page). Companion: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9811186
items.fit_T1_T7: Parity genuinely broken, so partially T5-type (sees the sign of lambda via a bilinear estimate over the specific sequence). Fails T2 (depends on the sequence a^2+b^4, Gaussian-integer factorization, Type II bounds for that set), T3 (asymptotic count, not a sign), T4 (error O(loglog x/log x)).
items.relevance: Template for 'extra structure breaks parity': the Weil window supplies no analogous multiplicative symmetry (like Z[i]), so the bilinear axiom is not available. Beurling: relies on Gaussian-integer structure (Hecke characters), absent from generic Beurling systems (inference, UNVERIFIED).
items.corrected_statement: Formula confirmed exactly: sum_{a^2+b^4<=x} Lambda(a^2+b^4) = 4 pi^{-1} kappa x^{3/4}(1+O(loglog x/log x)), kappa = int_0^1 (1-t^4)^{1/2} dt = Gamma(1/4)^2/(6 sqrt(2 pi)). Note that arXiv math/9811185 is the X^2+Y^4 paper (Ann. of Math. 148 (1998) 945-1040); the 'Asymptotic sieve for primes' paper is math/9811186 (1041-1065). The additional axiom is a bilinear-sum condition; Ford notes R(nu) with nu>2/3 is required.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9811185 'This article proves that there are infinitely many primes of the form a^2 + b^4, in fact getting the asymptotic formula' with the displayed formula; https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9811186 'adding an additional axiom to the classical formulation breaks the well-known parity problem'; Crossref DOIs 10.2307/121034 (p.945) and 10.2307/121035 (p.1041).

items.name: Heath-Brown: primes of the form x^3 + 2y^3
items.statement: There are infinitely many primes x^3+2y^3 with integers x,y. Precisely, there is c>0 such that with eta = (log X)^-c, the number of such primes with X < x, y <= X(1+eta) is sigma_0 eta^2 X^2/(3 log X) {1 + O((log log X)^-1/6)}, sigma_0 = prod_p (1 - (nu_p - 1)/p), nu_p = #solutions of x^3 = 2 (mod p). Product conditionally convergent.
items.authors_year: D. R. Heath-Brown, Acta Math. 186 (2001) 1-84
items.quote_or_locator: First two pages of the scan (read from page images): 'THEOREM. There are infinitely many primes of the form x^3+2y^3 with integer x, y. More specifically, there is a positive constant c such that, if eta = eta(X) = (log X)^-c, then the number of such primes with X<x,y<=X(1+eta) is sigma_0 eta^2X^2/(3 log X){1+O((log log X)^-1/6)}'. Contents list: 'The Type I estimates', 'The Fundamental Lemma sieve bounds', 'a large sieve estimate'.
items.fit_T1_T7: Parity broken via factorization in Q(2^{1/3}) and a special Type II structure (Maynard survey: 'After switching to prime ideals, Heath-Brown is essentially able to classify those m1, m2 for which there is an n with m1 n, m2 n in A'). Fails T2, T3, T4.
items.relevance: Second proof-of-concept that parity can be beaten when A has algebraic structure; the Weil window has none. Beurling: uses number-field ideal factorization: NO (inference, UNVERIFIED).
items.corrected_statement: Bibliographic data confirmed (Acta Math. 186 (2001) 1-84). The displayed asymptotic, the exponent (log log X)^{-1/6} and the constant sigma_0 were not re-opened by me and rest on the earlier session's reading of page images.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (existence of infinitely many such primes is the main theorem); detailed asymptotic UNVERIFIED

items.name: Chen's theorem (1966, 1973)
items.statement: Every sufficiently large even integer is a prime plus a number with at most two prime factors (p + P2); and for even h>0 there are infinitely many primes p such that p+h is prime or a product of two primes (p+2 = P2 case: twin-prime approximation). Proof: weighted sieve (Selberg/Rosser type) with Bombieri-Vinogradov; stops at P2 because of parity.
items.authors_year: J.-R. Chen, Kexue Tongbao 17 (1966) 385-386 (announcement); Sci. Sinica 16 (1973) 157-176 (proof); Ross simplification 1975
items.quote_or_locator: Secondary source: 'every sufficiently large even number can be written as the sum of either two primes or a prime and a semiprime'. Journal reference confirmed via Maynard's survey ref [9]: 'J.-R. Chen, On the representation of a larger even integer as the sum of a prime and the product of at most two primes. Sci. Sinica 16 (1973), 157-176'. Pintz arXiv:1004.1065 abstract: 'p+2 has at most two prime factors for infinitely many primes p'. Original paper not opened.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1, T7 yes for the statement; fails T3 (existence of almost-primes, no sign), T4, T5 (stops exactly at the parity wall).
items.relevance: Textbook case of parity limiting what the sieve can say: the last step from P2 to prime is blocked by parity. No contribution to the sign of <v,Kv>. Uses BV, which needs Dirichlet characters: NO for Beurling (inference, UNVERIFIED).
items.corrected_statement: Core confirmed: Chen, Sci. Sinica 16 (1973) 157-176, 'On the representation of a larger even integer as the sum of a prime and the product of at most two primes'. Survey: best sieve result for twin-type problems, announced 1966, published 1973 (and 1978). Not verified by me: the Kexue Tongbao 17 (1966) 385-386 pages, the general-even-h version of the twin statement, and 'Ross simplification 1975'. items.name: Goldston-Pintz-Yildirim: small gaps between primes (2005, Annals 2009)
items.statement: liminf_{n} (p_{n+1} - p_n)/log p_n = 0. Under the Elliott-Halberstam conjecture, primes differing by 16 or less infinitely often; 'even a much weaker conjecture implies that there are infinitely often primes a bounded distance apart'. Method: Selberg-type sieve weights (squares of divisor sums) applied to prime k-tuples.
items.authors_year: D. A. Goldston, J. Pintz, C. Y. Yildirim, 'Primes in Tuples I', arXiv math/0508185 (2005); Ann. of Math. 170 (2009) 819-862 (journal reference not verified in session)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: 'Assuming the Elliott-Halberstam conjecture, we prove that there are infinitely often primes differing by 16 or less.' and 'liminf (p_{n+1} - p_n)/log p_n = 0'. Journal volume: only 'GPY09' cited in Murty's survey https://hrj.episciences.org/1318/pdf, so volume/pages UNVERIFIED.
items.fit_T1_T7: Unconditional liminf=0 is PROVEN; the bounded-gap and 16 results are CONDITIONAL on EH. Uses prime-side data only (T1) and BV (T7 ok for the unconditional statement). Fails T3, T4; it uses a Selberg-square weight, so it has 'sign by squares' internally but only to show that some shifts are simultaneously prime.
items.relevance: Positivity-by-squares weights w_n >= 0 turn a count into an existence statement without ever saying which shifts are prime, which is how parity is sidestepped. This does not produce a sign for K. Uses level of distribution (Dirichlet characters): NO for Beurling (inference, UNVERIFIED).

items.name: Maynard (2013/2015) and Tao: bounded gaps; Polymath8b 246
items.statement: Maynard: for each k the prime k-tuples conjecture holds for a positive proportion of admissible k-tuples; liminf (p_{n+m} - p_n) < infinity for every m; liminf (p_{n+1} - p_n) <= 600; under EH liminf (p_{n+1} - p_n) <= 12 and liminf (p_{n+2} - p_n) <= 600. Polymath8b: H_1 <= 246 unconditionally, H_1 <= 6 under the generalized EH, H_m << m e^{(4 - 24/181) m} unconditionally. Method: multidimensional Selberg-type weights; proof quantity S = sum_n (sum_i 1_P(n+h_i) - k) w_n with w_n >= 0 sidesteps the parity problem 'via the pigeonhole principle' (Maynard).
items.authors_year: J. Maynard, Ann. of Math. 181 (2015) 383-413 (arXiv 1311.4600); T. Tao (independent, unpublished); D. H. J. Polymath, Res. Math. Sci. 1 (2014) Art. 12 (arXiv 1407.4897)
items.quote_or_locator: Maynard abstract: 'liminf(p_{n+m} - p_n) < infinity for any integer m. We also show that liminf(p_{n+1}-p_n) <= 600, and, if we assume the Elliott-Halberstam conjecture, that liminf(p_{n+1}-p_n) <= 12'. Polymath abstract https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.4897: 'H_1 <= 246 unconditionally'; 'H_1 <= 6' under generalized EH. Parity comment: Maynard ICM 2022 section 4 (Theorem 9 discussion): 'The fact that we do not have any control over which of the different n + h_i are prime, merely the fact that several of them are prime is what allows us to sidestep the parity phenomenon issue.' Journal volume of Maynard from the survey's ref [61].
items.fit_T1_T7: Unconditional numbers (600, 246) PROVEN; 12 and 6 CONDITIONAL on EH/GEH. T1, T7 yes. Fails T3, T4, T5, T6: existence of clusters via positive weights, no sign of a fixed quadratic form.
items.relevance: The only 'sees many primes at once' sieve technology, which is T5-flavoured (correlations of several shifts) but by pigeonhole, not by an identity; positivity enters only to conclude existence. Cannot determine a sign for a given matrix. Beurling: relies on Bombieri-Vinogradov-type level (Dirichlet characters): NO (inference, UNVERIFIED).
items.corrected_statement: Confirmed. Maynard (arXiv 1311.4600, Ann. of Math. 181 (2015) 383-413): liminf(p_{n+m}-p_n) finite for every m; liminf(p_{n+1}-p_n) <= 600; under EH <= 12 and liminf(p_{n+2}-p_n) <= 600. Polymath8b (Res. Math. Sci. 1 (2014) Art. 12): H_1 <= 246 unconditionally, H_1 <= 6 under generalized EH, H_m << m e^{(4-24/181)m} unconditionally (24/181 confirmed), H_m << m e^{2m} under EH. Tao's independent work is unpublished (Maynard's ICM wording).
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.4600 and https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.4897 (abstract: 'H_m << m e^{(4-24/181)m}'); Maynard ICM refs [61] Ann. of Math. 181 (2015) 383-413, [71] Res. Math. Sci. 1 (2014), Art. 12; ICM: 'and unpublished work of Tao'.

items.name: Beyond the Bombieri-Vinogradov range: Zhang 2014, Maynard 2020 (3/5), Lichtman 2021-23 (10/17, 66/107)
items.statement: Zhang: for moduli free of large prime divisors (smooth), a level of distribution above 1/2, giving liminf (p_{n+1} - p_n) < 7 x 10^7. Maynard (well-factorable weights): moduli up to x^{3/5 - epsilon}, improving the Bombieri-Friedlander-Iwaniec 4/7. Lichtman: modified linear sieve with moduli up to x^{10/17} (earlier 4/7 BFI, 7/12 Maynard) and, with triply well-factorable weights, level of distribution 66/107 ~ 0.617 (5/8 conditional on Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture); first use of a level beyond the square-root barrier for Goldbach.
items.authors_year: Y. Zhang, Ann. of Math. 179 (2014) 1121-1174; J. Maynard, arXiv 2006.07088 (Memoirs AMS per catalog listing); J. Lichtman, arXiv 2109.02851 (v2 2024) and arXiv 2309.08522 (2023, appendix with Drappeau)
items.quote_or_locator: Lichtman 2309.08522 abstract: 'level of distribution 66/107 ~ 0.617' and 'For the Goldbach problem, this is the first use of a level of distribution beyond the square-root barrier'; Maynard https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.07088: moduli up to x^{3/5-epsilon}, 'extends well-known work of Bombieri, Friedlander and Iwaniec'; Lichtman https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.02851: 'x^{10/17}'; Zhang https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2014/179-3/p07 (7 x 10^7 verified via search summary). Lichtman papers are preprints (arXiv); refereed status not verified in session.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1, T7 yes (unconditional; the 5/8 variant is CONDITIONAL on Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture). Fails T3, T4, T5.
items.relevance: Improves only the size/level of AP-equidistribution inputs; parity unchanged. Even full level 1 (EH) does not break parity (Ford, Selberg). No sign. Beurling (inference, UNVERIFIED): needs Kloosterman/automorphic input and characters.
items.corrected_statement: (1) Zhang, Ann. of Math. 179 (2014) 1121-1174: gaps below 7x10^7, using smooth moduli at level 1/2+1/584 (per AIM summary). (2) Maynard, 'Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli II: Well-factorable estimates' (arXiv 2006.07088) is PUBLISHED in Mem. Amer. Math. Soc. 306 (2025), DOI 10.1090/memo/1543: moduli up to x^{3/5-eps} for suitably well-factorable weights. (3) Lichtman 2109.02851 'A modification of the linear sieve, and the count of twin primes' is PUBLISHED in Algebra & Number Theory 19 (2025) 1-38: moduli up to x^{10/17}, vs 4/7 (BFI) and 7/12 (Maynard). (4) Lichtman 2309.08522 (66/107, ~0.617; 5/8 under Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture) remains an arXiv preprint as far as I could find; refereed status UNVERIFIED. The 10/17 and 3/5 figures are for different weight classes (linear-sieve weights vs well-factorable), not directly comparable.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (Zhang, Maynard 3/5, Lichtman 10/17 published); Lichtman 66/107 preprint (UNVERIFIED refereed); 5/8 CONDITIONAL

items.name: Large gaps between primes: Ford-Green-Konyagin-Maynard-Tao and Maynard (2014-2018)
items.statement: For large X, max_{p_{n+1}<=X} (p_{n+1} - p_n) >> log X * loglog X * logloglogloglog X / logloglog X (four nested logs in the numerator factor), proved with a generalization of a Pippenger-Spencer hypergraph covering theorem. Earlier: with f(X) -> infinity, G(X) >= f(X) log X loglog X logloglogloglog X/(logloglog X)^2 (Ford-Green-Konyagin-Tao) and the same for Maynard's independent proof, answering an Erdos question.
items.authors_year: K. Ford, B. Green, S. Konyagin, J. Maynard, T. Tao, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 31 (2018) 65-105; K. Ford, B. Green, S. Konyagin, T. Tao, Ann. of Math. 183 (2016) 935-974; J. Maynard, Ann. of Math. 183 (2016) 915-?
items.quote_or_locator: arXiv 1412.5029 abstract: 'Our main new ingredient is a generalization of a hypergraph covering theorem of Pippenger and Spencer'; journal 'J. Amer. Math. Soc., 31 (2018), no. 1, 65-105'. FGKT: https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.4505 ('Annals of Mathematics 183 (2016), 935-974'); Maynard: https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.5110 ('This answers a well-known question of Erdos'). Exact form of the logarithm exponent in the FGKMT abstract came from a fetch summary, so the displayed power of logloglog X is UNVERIFIED.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1, T7 yes. Fails T3, T4: lower bound on the largest gap, i.e. a size statement about the prime sequence's irregularity.
items.relevance: Uses sieve weights (Maynard) and covering constructions (Erdos-Rankin) to show primes avoid long intervals; shows how sieve-side tools exploit structure rather than parity. No sign for K. Beurling: the analogue would require the system's Dirichlet-progression input; UNKNOWN.
items.corrected_statement: The displayed bound in the item has one log too many. The arXiv abstract gives max_{p_{n+1}<=X}(p_{n+1}-p_n) >> log X * loglog X * logloglogloglog?? NO: it is (log X)(log log X)(log log log log X)/(log log log X), i.e. FOUR nested logs in the numerator factor and THREE in the denominator. The item's string 'logloglogloglog' has five and contradicts its own parenthetical 'four nested logs'. The same typo appears in the FGKT formula (its abstract I did not open, so the earlier-bound form is UNVERIFIED). Journals: FGKMT J. Amer. Math. Soc. 31 (2018) 65-105; FGKT Ann. of Math. 183 (2016) 935-974; Maynard Ann. of Math. 183 (2016) 915-933 (the item left the end page blank).

Maynard ICM refs [19],[20],[63]; Crossref Maynard 'Large gaps between primes' Ann. of Math. 183, 915-933, 10.4007/annals.2016.183.3.3.

items.name: Sieve weights and their smoothings (Granville-Koukoulopoulos-Maynard)
items.statement: Asymptotic formula for the 2k-th moments of partially smoothed Mobius divisor sums M_f(n; R) = sum_{d|n} mu(d) f(log d/log R): when 2k is small relative to the smoothing level A the moments are dominated by integers with only large prime factors (the intended behaviour of sieve weights); above the threshold A = (1/(2k)) C(2k,k) - 1 the main contribution comes from integers with many prime factors. Over finite fields and permutations the behaviour differs (explained via exceptional Dirichlet characters).
items.authors_year: A. Granville, D. Koukoulopoulos, J. Maynard, Ann. Sci. Ecole Norm. Sup. (4) 54 (2021) 1089-1177 (arXiv 1606.06781)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: 'the main contribution to the moments come from integers with only large prime factors' and 'which is not the intention when designing sieve weights'; threshold A = (1/2k) C(2k,k) - 1 from the ar5iv rendering of the abstract (search result summary).
items.fit_T1_T7: Exact asymptotics of 2k-th moments of Selberg-type weights (T4 partially: exact, with error terms), prime-side/multiplicative only (T1, T7), uniform in R (T2). Fails T3 (moments, not a sign) and T5 (no correlations of Lambda at different primes).
items.relevance: Quantifies when the squares (sum_{d|n} lambda_d)^2 behave like intended Selberg weights; a rare exact-moment result about the weights whose squares give the sign structure. Even-power moments are non-negative by construction, but this concerns sieve weights, not the Weil form. Beurling: the finite-field contrast suggests dependence on exceptional characters; UNKNOWN.
items.corrected_statement: Confirmed: asymptotics for 2k-th moments of partially smoothed Mobius divisor sums; threshold A = (1/(2k)) binom(2k,k) - 1. The abstract's wording is 'integers with quite a few prime factors' (item says 'many'). Published: Ann. Sci. Ecole Norm. Sup. (4) 54 (2021) 1089-1177. The finite-field / exceptional-character remark was not checked.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.06781: 'We obtain asymptotic formulas for the 2kth moments of partially smoothed divisor sums of the Mobius function'; 'The threshold for small occurs when A = (1/2k) C(2k,k) - 1'; Crossref ASENS 54, 1089-1177, 2021, 10.24033/asens.2478.

items.name: Tao: logarithmically averaged two-point Chowla and Elliott conjectures (parity barrier broken for correlations of lambda)
items.statement: For fixed integers a1,a2,b1,b2 with a1 b2 - a2 b1 != 0 and any function 1 <= omega(x) <= x tending to infinity: sum_{x/omega(x) < n <= x} lambda(a1 n + b1) lambda(a2 n + b2)/n = o(log omega(x)) as x -> infinity (lambda = Liouville function). Log-averaged Elliott conjecture for two-point correlations of more general bounded multiplicative functions. Tools: multiplicativity of lambda at small primes, Matomaki-Radziwill-Tao short-interval results, entropy decrement argument. Not the unweighted Chowla statement (o(x)).
items.authors_year: T. Tao, Forum Math. Pi 4 (2016) e8 (arXiv 1509.05422)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract (fetch summary): 'establish[es] the logarithmically averaged version' of the conjecture, 'thus breaking the "parity barrier" for this problem', tools 'the multiplicativity of the Liouville function at small primes' and 'a novel "entropy decrement argument"'. Forum Math. Pi reference from a search result page (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/forum-of-mathematics-pi/article/logarithmically-averaged-chowla-and-elliott-conjectures-for-twopoint-correlations/48514F53D73B2C1277BD7232630F0694).
items.fit_T1_T7: Sees correlations between lambda at different arguments (T5 for the Liouville function, not Lambda), unconditional (T7), prime-side/multiplicative only (T1). Fails T3 (o(.) bound, not a sign), T4 (lossy), T6; only two-point and only log-averaged.
items.relevance: The one result in this circle where parity is genuinely overcome for correlations, but for lambda(n)lambda(n+h) two-point sums with log-averaging and size o(log omega), not for the exact sign of a quadratic form with margins 1e-29. Higher-point Chowla remains open (Tao-Teraevaeinen odd order case is outside this domain and was not searched). Beurling: the proof uses analytic input about short-interval multiplicative functions of integers; UNKNOWN.
items.corrected_statement: Confirmed: for fixed a_i,b_i with a1b2-a2b1 != 0 and 1<=omega(x)<=x tending to infinity, sum_{x/omega<n<=x} lambda(a1n+b1)lambda(a2n+b2)/n = o(log omega(x)); log-averaged two-point Elliott for bounded multiplicative functions; tools include entropy decrement. Published: Forum Math. Pi 4 (2016) e8, DOI 10.1017/fmp.2016.6 (the arXiv page itself lists no journal ref). Maynard's ICM Theorem 12 states the lambda(n)lambda(n+1) = o(log x) case. Not the unweighted o(x) Chowla.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.05422 ('logarithmically averaged', 'breaking the parity barrier', v4 29 Jul 2016); Maynard ICM ref [74] 'Forum Math. Pi 4 (2016), e8'; Crossref 10.1017/fmp.2016.6.

items.name: Maynard: primes with restricted digits (2016, Inventiones 2019)
items.statement: There are infinitely many primes whose decimal expansion omits a fixed digit a_0. Proof: Hardy-Littlewood circle method plus Type I and Type II information in Harman's sieve; 'decorrelation of Diophantine and digital conditions', geometry of numbers, the large sieve and moment estimates from a Markov process. Base-q extension: Primes and polynomials with restricted digits (IMRN 2021).
items.quote_or_locator: arXiv abstract: 'We show there are infinitely many prime numbers which do not have the digit a_0 in their decimal expansion.' Method description and Inventiones 2019 reference come from a search-result summary (database record), not from the paper: UNVERIFIED beyond the abstract.
items.fit_T1_T7: Parity broken via Fourier/exponential-sum structure (Type II), a 2016-2019 result. Fails T2 (needs the digit-set Fourier structure), T3, T4.
items.relevance: Another instance of parity avoided by extra analytic structure of the set; no analogue for the Weil window. Interesting only because the proof uses a Markov-process moment estimate, but this is a different Markov structure from the Perron-Frobenius generator in our bulk. Beurling: depends on base-q digits and exponential sums: NO.
items.corrected_statement: Journal confirmed: Invent. Math. 217 (2019) 127-218. The base-q sequel is IMRN 2022, 10626-10648 (online April 2021), not 'IMRN 2021' as a volume. The method description (Harman sieve, large sieve, Markov-process moments) came from a search summary and was not re-checked against the paper.

items.name: Murty-Vatwani: Mobius equidistribution on shifted primes would break parity (twin primes)
items.statement: Conjecture: an analogue of Bombieri-Vinogradov for the Mobius function mu evaluated on shifted primes p+h in arithmetic progressions (equidistribution of mu(p+h)). Main theorem (conditional): for a fixed even h, this conjecture together with the Elliott-Halberstam conjecture (both for some theta<1) yields infinitely many primes p such that p+h is prime, i.e. parity barrier overcome conditionally.
items.authors_year: M. R. Murty, A. Vatwani, J. Number Theory 180 (2017) 643-659
items.quote_or_locator: Not read directly (paywalled). Secondary: search-result summary of the paper's abstract (Journal of Number Theory 180 (2017) 643-659): the conjecture 'on how the Mobius function is distributed over shifted primes in arithmetic progressions' plus Elliott-Halberstam 'would overcome the parity barrier'; a Fields Institute talk abstract https://gfs.fields.utoronto.ca/talks/twin-primes-and-parity-problem says it formulates 'an analogue of the Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem for the Mobius function'. Quote UNVERIFIED against the paper itself.
items.fit_T1_T7: Names the missing input exactly: Mobius/Liouville correlations with primes. Conditional (fails T7). Not a sign statement.
items.relevance: Identifies the same wall in the sieve language: the needed prime-side information is the sign cancellation of mu on shifted primes, which is as hard as RH-type statements. Useful as a precise conjectural target, but a conjecture cannot be used as a proof ingredient (T7).

The exact conjecture and theorem (including 'for some theta<1' for both hypotheses) were NOT read: the Queen's University PDF returned HTML, and the paper is paywalled. Only search-engine summaries support the description.

items.name: Granville: sieving intervals and Siegel zeros (2020)
items.statement: Assuming there exist (infinitely many) Siegel zeros, the (Rosser-)Jurkat-Richert bounds in the linear sieve cannot be improved; this gives conditional minor improvements to Brun-Titchmarsh and an improved conditional lower bound on the longest gaps between primes. Maynard cites it for the link between optimal sieve functions for the interval sieve and Siegel zeros.
items.authors_year: A. Granville, arXiv 2010.01211 (Oct 2020), preprint
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: 'Assuming that there exist (infinitely many) Siegel zeros' and 'we show that the (Rosser-)Jurkat-Richert bounds in the linear sieve cannot be improved'; Maynard ICM survey section 3.1: 'the optimal sieve functions are closely linked to the presence of Siegel zeros'. No journal reference found.
items.fit_T1_T7: Conditional on Siegel zeros (fails T7 as a tool). Barrier statement only.
items.relevance: Shows that the sieve loss is tied to possible exceptional zeros: improving it unconditionally would require L-function zero information, which is again RH-adjacent and circular for our purposes.
items.corrected_statement: Published: Acta Arith. 205 (2022) 1-19 (the item said no journal reference was found). Abstract confirmed: assuming infinitely many Siegel zeros, the (Rosser-)Jurkat-Richert bounds in the linear sieve cannot be improved; minor conditional improvements to Brun-Titchmarsh; conditional lower bound on the longest prime gaps.

items.name: Green-Tao: sieve majorant of the primes and transference (primes contain long APs)
items.statement: The primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions. Three ingredients: Szemeredi's theorem; a transference principle for suitably pseudorandom sets; and a result of Goldston and Yildirim that places the primes inside a pseudorandom set of 'almost primes' (Selberg-sieve weights) of positive relative density. This is a positive-measure majorant that sees multi-point correlations of primes.
items.authors_year: B. Green, T. Tao, arXiv math/0404188 (2004, v6 2007); Ann. of Math. 167 (2008) 481-547 (journal reference not verified in session)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: 'a transference principle that extends Szemeredi's theorem to suitably pseudorandom sets, and a result of Goldston and Yildirim that lets the primes be placed inside a pseudorandom set of almost primes with positive relative density' (paraphrased from the fetch summary). That the weights are Selberg-type squares was NOT verified on the page (the full text was not read).
items.fit_T1_T7: Handles correlations between different primes (T5) via a non-negative pseudorandom majorant, unconditional (T7), prime-side (T1), uniform in the progression length. Fails T3 (existence of patterns, not a sign), T4 (relative density, lossy majorant), T6.
items.relevance: A positive majorant nu >= 1_P with linear-forms control is the closest sieve object to 'positive weight that sees prime correlations'. Domain-adjacent (additive combinatorics); it gives existence of configurations, not exact signs. Beurling: the pseudorandom-majorant step depends on sieve level of distribution; UNKNOWN.
items.corrected_statement: Confirmed. Ann. of Math. 167 (2008) 481-547. Abstract: third ingredient is 'a recent result of Goldston and Yildirim' letting 'one place the primes inside a pseudorandom set of almost primes' of positive relative density. items.name: Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer: Beurling primes with large oscillation (barrier for the Beurling column)
items.statement: There is a Beurling generalized number system whose integer counting function is close to linear, N(x) = c x + O(x^theta) for 1/2 < theta < 1, but whose prime counting function oscillates by a large amount; its zeta function has infinitely many zeros near a curve just inside Re s = 1 (the abstract gives the constraint a > (4/e)(1 - theta) on the zero-curve parameter). Construction via classical analytic number theory and probability.
items.authors_year: H. G. Diamond, H. L. Montgomery, U. M. A. Vorhauer, Math. Ann. 334 (2006) 1-36
items.quote_or_locator: Search-result summary of the abstract (not the paper): near-linear integer count 'with error term O(x^theta), 1/2 < theta < 1', primes oscillate 'by a large amount', 'infinitely many zeros near a curve just inside Re s = 1'. DOI 10.1007/s00208-005-0638-2 from the Michigan DSpace record. Later related: https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.11501 (Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas).
items.fit_T1_T7: Not a sieve tool. Marks the limit: any property true for all Beurling systems with the same integer density cannot give RH, since there are such systems with RH-false prime distribution.
items.relevance: Directly relevant to the user's rule that a tool valid for every Beurling system with the same density cannot prove RH: DMV exhibit regular-integer systems with violently oscillating primes. Hence sieve-axiom results (YES in the Beurling column above: Brun, Selberg, parity, Bombieri) can at most constrain, never decide, the sign. A tool must use arithmetic specific to integers (e.g., characters, Gamma factors, Euler-product-plus-functional-equation), as in the Weil explicit formula itself.
items.corrected_statement: Journal confirmed: Math. Ann. 334 (2006) 1-36, DOI 10.1007/s00208-005-0638-2. Per the abstract (seen in repository search snippets, not the paper): N_B(x) = kappa x + O(x^theta), 1/2<theta<1; pi_B(x) = li(x) + Omega(x exp(-c sqrt(log x))); zeta_B has infinitely many zeros ON the curve sigma = 1 - a/log t and none to its right, with a > (4/e)(1-theta). So the item's 'violently oscillating primes' is too strong: the oscillation is at the scale of the classical PNT error term, and the point is that RH fails (zeros at distance ~1/log t from the line Re s=1). The relevance inference must be restricted to the class theta>1/2; the integers themselves have far smaller counting error, so it says nothing against RH for the integers.
items.check_evidence: Crossref 10.1007/s00208-005-0638-2; https://deepblue.lib.umich.edu/handle/2027.42/46253 (returned HTTP 403 to me; abstract text obtained via WebSearch snippet of deepblue copies: 'infinitely many zeros on the curve sigma = 1 - a/log t ... none to the right', 'a > (4/e)(1 - theta)'); later paper https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.11501.

The list has no item on the linear/beta sieve and its limits (sieve dimension, Jurkat-Richert) except via Granville.

Number Theory 169 (2016) 265-294 (confirmed via Crossref); Maynard, 3-tuples have at most 7 prime factors infinitely often, Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 155 (2013) 443-457 (ICM ref [60]). Both are absent.

Higher-point Chowla and Elliott: Tao and Terava inen, The structure of logarithmically averaged correlations of multiplicative functions, with applications to the Chowla and Elliott conjectures, Duke Math. J. 168 (2019) 1977-2027 (confirmed via Crossref): odd-order log-averaged Chowla. Also Matomaki-Radziwill, Multiplicative functions in short intervals, Ann. of Math. 183 (2016) 1015-1056 (ICM ref [54]), the input for Tao's two-point result. Whether the odd-order Tao-Teravainen statement is exactly 'odd k' was not checked: UNVERIFIED.

Green-Tao, Linear equations in primes, Ann. of Math. 171 (2010) 1753-1850 (ICM ref [32]) and The Mobius function is strongly orthogonal to nilsequences (ICM ref [33]); Bourgain-Sarnak-Ziegler, Disjointness of Moebius from horocycle flows (ICM ref [8]). These are Type I/II-free approaches to prime/Mobius correlations and belong with the parity-breaking items.

Other parity-breaking cases listed by Maynard ICM sec. 7: Merikoski on X^2+(Y^2+1)^2, Xiao on primes f(a,b^2) for binary quadratic forms, Li on prime values of a sparse polynomial sequence (Duke, to appear in the ICM list) and Maynard, Dense clusters of primes in subsets, Compos. Math. 152 (2016) 1517-1554 (ICM ref [62]).

Bombieri-Davenport 1966 (Goldbach / square-root barrier, mentioned in Lichtman's 2309.08522 abstract as the previous largest improvement) and Heath-Brown, Prime numbers in short intervals and a generalized Vaughan identity (ICM ref [36]): the Vaughan/Heath-Brown identity machinery producing the Type I/II sums that all items rely on. The Elliott-Halberstam conjecture itself (statement, range) has no entry.

Stadlmann, level of distribution for smooth moduli beyond 1/2+1/584 (a 2026 paper by Stadlmann and a bounded-gaps improvement 'to 240' appeared only in a search snippet with odd identifiers): UNVERIFIED, must be checked on arXiv before inclusion. Similarly Heath-Brown, Prime twins and Siegel zeros (1983) and Wu Jie / Cai Yingchun improvements of Chen's theorem were not searched: UNVERIFIED.
Harman, Prime-detecting sieves (the Harman sieve used in Maynard's digits paper) and Selberg's own collected papers vol. II (1991) are cited indirectly but have no entry; not searched.

merged.title: Additive patterns, randomness of Mobius, structure in primes
merged.summary: Result: nothing in this domain supplies a SIGN of <v,Kv> or of s_E, s_O. All 21 items below are PROVEN (or labelled otherwise), but they give existence, positive density, asymptotics with o(.) or log^-A error terms, or uniformity of Lambda/mu against nilsequences. That is SIZE or EXISTENCE with loss, so T3 and T4 fail, and margins of 1e-29 cannot be met by log^-A or (log x)^(1-c) savings. Almost every theorem here is about additive shifts (n, n+h, e(n alpha), x^2+ny^2, digits). The window problem lives at shifts log n, i.e. on the multiplicative/Mellin side, so there is no direct entry point. Items 1-3, 5-10, 13, 17-19 have no Beurling analogue at all (they use addition of integers). Named barriers found with sources: (a) the parity problem (Selberg 1949) blocks sieve lower bounds; Tao 2016 says his log-averaged 2-point Chowla result 'break[s] the parity barrier', but only logarithmically averaged and with o(1) savings; (b) Chowla for k>=2 is open without log averaging (MR 2015: 'remains unproven for any h1..hk with k>=2'); (c) Beurling systems with the same density and PNT-level data can have RH failing (Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer, quoted in Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas) or holding (Zhang), so axiom-level prime data cannot give RH. Best candidates for the K-matrix: the exact Vaughan/Heath-Brown decomposition of Lambda (lossless, valid for Beurling, TOOL only) and the Green-Tao-Ziegler structure/uniformity dichotomy for Lambda and mu (STRUCTURE, lossy). Neither gives a sign. Peer-review status was not verified for: Guo 2026 (arXiv v4 only), Pilatte (arXiv v3 Aug 2026), Maynard journal ref, Tao 2-point journal ref, Helfgott book. Green-Tao confirmed: arXiv math/0404188 (Apr 2004, v6 Sep 2007), Annals of Math 167 (2008) per annals.math.princeton.edu. Out of domain (not covered here): von Koch, Selberg, Bombieri-Vinogradov, and the Zhu quote.

items.name: Vinogradov three-primes theorem (with Vaughan's 1977 simplification)
items.statement: For N odd and any A>0: sum_{k1+k2+k3=N} Lambda(k1)Lambda(k2)Lambda(k3) = (1/2) G(N) N^2 + O_A(N^2 log^{-A} N), G(N)=prod_{p|N}(1-(p-1)^-2) prod_{p∤N}(1+(p-1)^-3). Hence every sufficiently large odd integer is a sum of three primes.
items.authors_year: I. M. Vinogradov 1937; simplified by R. C. Vaughan 1977 (via Vaughan's identity)
items.quote_or_locator: Wikipedia 'Vinogradov's theorem': 'r(N) = 1/2 G(N) N^2 + O(N^2 log^-A N)'; '1977: R. C. Vaughan found a much simpler minor-arc argument'. Secondary source; the original Vinogradov paper was not opened.
items.fit_T1_T7: Passes T1, T2 (all N), T7. Fails T3 (positivity of a count, not the sign of a quadratic form), T4 (log^-A error), T5 (3-fold additive correlation, but only through a main term), T6.
items.relevance: Shows how a sign (positivity of a prime count) is obtained only when the main term beats an O(log^-A) error; the margins s_E, s_O ~ 1e-29 admit no such error term. The input is addition of integers and exponential sums, which has no counterpart in the log-shift matrix K.
items.corrected_statement: r(N)=sum_{k1+k2+k3=N} Λ(k1)Λ(k2)Λ(k3) = (1/2)G(N)N^2 + O_A(N^2 log^-A N); G(N) as stated. Vinogradov 1937 (unconditional minor-arc bound), Vaughan 1977 simplification. Only a secondary source (Wikipedia) was opened; the original Vinogradov paper was not.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (formula and attribution confirmed via secondary source only; primary not opened)
items.check_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinogradov%27s_theorem : 'r(N)=1/2 G(N)N^2+O(N^2 log^-A N)'; G(N) with prod_{p|N}(1-1/(p-1)^2) prod_{p∤N}(1+1/(p-1)^3); 'In 1937' minor-arc bound; 'In 1977 R. C. Vaughan found a much simpler argument, based on ... Vaughan's identity'.

items.name: Helfgott: ternary Goldbach conjecture
items.statement: Every odd integer n > 5 is the sum of three primes.
items.authors_year: H. A. Helfgott, 2013 (arXiv v2 Jan 2014); full account arXiv:1501.05438 (book, 317 pages)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: 'asserts that every odd integer n greater than 5 is the sum of three primes. The present paper proves this conjecture.' Companion: arXiv:1205.5252 (minor arcs), arXiv:1305.2897 (major arcs, uses finite GRH verification up to bounded conductor and height). Journal publication not confirmed from the arXiv pages (UNVERIFIED).
items.fit_T1_T7: Passes T1, T7 (the GRH input is a finite numerical verification, not an assumption). Fails T3, T4 (explicit but lossy inequalities), T5, T6.
items.relevance: Shows the lossy but fully explicit style of circle-method work, including a finite computer verification of zeros in the major arcs (the same type of input that the window problem uses). It does not give a sign of K.
items.corrected_statement: Helfgott announced a proof in 2013 (arXiv 1312.7748, 79 pp, v1 30 Dec 2013, v2 17 Jan 2014, 'Minimal changes'); the full account is arXiv 1501.05438 (v2 27 Jan 2015, '317(+x) pages, 3 figures'). Neither arXiv page lists a journal reference. Author's publication page says the book 'The ternary Goldbach problem' is 'to appear in Ann. of Math. Studies' and is now ~561 pp+xvii and 'differs substantially from the draft from 2015'. A 2018 snapshot says widely accepted but not in a peer-reviewed journal. So: 'PROVEN' should read 'claimed complete proof, widely accepted, full text not confirmed as refereed/published'. The 317-page figure is for the 2015 draft only. Major-arc paper 1305.2897 uses a finite GRH verification (search snippet).
items.corrected_status: PROVEN by community consensus; refereed publication UNVERIFIED (book still 'to appear' per author page; date of page not seen)
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.7748 (versions, no journal ref); https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.05438 ('317(+x) pages'); author page https://www.math.ens.fr/~helfgott/anglais/publications.html (via search): 'currently 561pp.+xvii ... is to appear in Ann. of Math. Studies'. Verbatim abstract sentence 'The present paper proves this conjecture' was NOT seen (fetch returned paraphrase).

items.name: Chen's theorem (p + P_2)
items.statement: Every sufficiently large even integer is the sum of a prime and a number with at most two prime factors.
items.authors_year: Chen Jingrun, announced 1966, proof published 1973
items.quote_or_locator: 'the sum of either two primes or a prime and a semiprime'; 'first stated ... in 1966 ... published the detailed proof in 1973'. Secondary source, original not opened.
items.fit_T1_T7: Passes T1, T7. Fails T3 (existence), T4, T5, T6. Stopped by the parity problem.
items.relevance: Marks the exact limit of sieve methods: the representation cannot be sharpened to p+p without a parity-breaking input. Useful as a calibration of what 'size' tools can do.
items.corrected_statement: Every sufficiently large even number is a sum of a prime and a number with at most two prime factors (prime + semiprime). Announced 1966 (Kexue Tongbao 11(9):385-386), detailed proof 1973 (Sci. Sinica 16:157-176); simplified by Ross 1975 (J. London Math. Soc. 10(4):500-506). Secondary source only.
items.check_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chen%27s_theorem : 'every sufficiently large even number can be written as the sum of either two primes or a prime and a semiprime'; announced 1966, proof published 1973.

items.name: Parity problem (Selberg)
items.statement: Sieve methods cannot distinguish integers with an even number of prime factors from those with an odd number; for the set A of integers with no prime factor <= x^(1/2) split by parity, any Brun/Selberg-type sieve gives an upper bound >= (2+o(1))x/ln x for both parts, while one part is empty and the other is the primes in (x^(1/2), x].
items.authors_year: A. Selberg, 1949
items.quote_or_locator: 'sieve theory is unable to provide non-trivial lower bounds on the size of A' (Tao's formulation); Selberg example as described. Secondary source.
items.fit_T1_T7: It is a barrier. It says that tools which see only the density of Lambda and its level of distribution cannot give lower bounds. Relevant to T3 and T5.
items.relevance: Explains why sieve-type arguments give only size information, never the sign of a prime-weighted quadratic form. Any sign proof must use a parity-sensitive input such as multiplicativity of lambda (Tao 2016) or bilinear Type II sums.
items.corrected_statement: The parity problem was 'identified and named by Atle Selberg in 1949'. Selberg's example (numbers up to x with no prime factor <= x^{1/2}, split by parity of Omega) is rigorous for Brun/Selberg-type sieves (upper bound at least about 2x/ln x for both parts, one part empty). But the general principle is a heuristic limitation; Tao calls his formulation 'rough'. So 'PROVEN' holds only inside an axiomatic sieve framework; as a general statement it is a barrier principle, not a theorem.
items.corrected_status: BARRIER (rigorous only for the axiomatic sieve model; general form is a heuristic principle)
items.check_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parity_problem_(sieve_theory) : 'identified and named by Atle Selberg in 1949'; Tao: sieve theory 'is unable to provide non-trivial lower bounds on the size of A'; 'the set with an even number of factors is empty'.

items.name: Vaughan identity and Heath-Brown identity (exact decompositions of Lambda)
items.statement: Vaughan: Lambda(n) = a1(n)+a2(n)+a3(n)+a4(n) with a1=Lambda 1_{n<=U}, a2(n)=-sum_{mdr=n, m<=U, d<=V} Lambda(m)mu(d), a3(n)=sum_{hd=n, d<=V} mu(d) log h, a4(n) = -sum_{mk=n, m>U, k>1} Lambda(m) sum_{d|k, d<=V} mu(d). It comes from an exact expansion of -zeta'/zeta with truncated Dirichlet series. Heath-Brown (1982) generalises it to k-fold convolutions.
items.authors_year: R. C. Vaughan 1977; D. R. Heath-Brown 1982 (Can. J. Math. 34(6), 1365-1377)
items.quote_or_locator: 'found by R. C. Vaughan (1977)'; 'Vaughan's identity was generalized by Heath-Brown (1982)'. Secondary source, originals not opened.
items.fit_T1_T7: Passes T1, T2, T4 (exact identity), T7. Fails T3 (no sign by itself), T5 (it splits, but does not produce cancellation), T6.
items.relevance: The only lossless object in this domain. It rewrites the Lambda(n)/sqrt(n) part of K as Type I and Type II bilinear pieces without error. Because it is a formal Dirichlet-series identity it holds verbatim for any Beurling system, so by itself it cannot give a sign that is specific to the true primes; the estimates of the pieces are where the arithmetic enters.
items.corrected_statement: Decomposition Λ=a1+a2+a3+a4 is right, but a2 must be a2(n) = -sum_{md=n, m<=U, d<=V} Λ(m)μ(d); the item's 'mdr=n' is a typo copied from the Wikipedia rendering (Wikipedia itself shows the typo). Source: R. C. Vaughan, 'Sommes trigonométriques sur les nombres premiers', C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris Sér. A 285 (1977) 981-983; Heath-Brown, 'Prime numbers in short intervals and a generalized Vaughan identity', Canad. J. Math. 34(6) (1982) 1365-1377. The claims 'holds verbatim for Beurling systems' and 'lossless' are the item's own inference, not in any source opened.
items.check_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaughan%27s_identity : 'found by R. C. Vaughan in 1977'; C. R. Acad. Sci. 285, 981-983; 'generalized by Heath-Brown (1982)', Canad. J. Math. 34(6), 1365-1377. Primary papers not opened.

items.name: Davenport: Mobius is orthogonal to every additive character (s=1 case of Sarnak/MN(1))
items.statement: |E_{n in [N]} mu(n) e(alpha n)| << _A log^{-A} N uniformly in alpha in R, for every A > 0.
items.authors_year: H. Davenport, 1937 (Quart. J. Math. 8); cited in Green-Tao 2008/2012
items.quote_or_locator: Green-Tao intro: 'reduced by Fourier analysis to the estimate |E_{n in [N]} mu(n)e(alpha n)| <<_A log^-A N (1.1) ... required to hold uniformly for all alpha. This was established by Davenport [3] in the 1930s by modifying Vinogradov's method of bilinear forms'. Also: E mu(n) << exp(-c sqrt(log N)) 'is essentially equivalent to the prime number theorem'. Davenport's own paper was not opened.
items.fit_T1_T7: Passes T1, T2 (uniform in alpha), T7. Fails T3, T4, T5 (single-prime-product correlation with a character), T6.
items.relevance: This is the base layer of Mobius randomness: mu has no Fourier bias. The window matrix has entries Lambda(n)/sqrt(n) at shifts log n, not e(alpha n), so it enters at most as a size estimate for off-diagonal terms.
items.corrected_statement: |E_{n in [N]} μ(n)e(αn)| <<_A log^-A N uniformly in α in R (Davenport 1937: 'On some infinite series involving arithmetical functions. II', Quart. J. Math. Oxford 8 (1937) 313-320). Green-Tao note that E μ(n) << exp(-c sqrt(log N)) is 'essentially equivalent to the prime number theorem (with classical error term)'. Davenport's own paper not opened.
items.check_evidence: Green-Tao arXiv 0807.1736 PDF text: '|E_{n in [N]} mu(n)e(alpha n)| <<_A log^-A N (1.1) ... required to hold uniformly for all alpha. This was established by Davenport [3] in the 1930s'; ref [3] H. Davenport, Quart. J. Math. Oxf. 8 (1937), 313-320.

items.name: Green-Tao theorem: arithmetic progressions in the primes
items.statement: The primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions. Ingredients: Szemeredi's theorem; a transference principle (any subset of positive relative density of a sufficiently pseudorandom set contains arbitrarily long progressions); the Goldston-Yildirim almost-prime majorant.
items.authors_year: B. Green, T. Tao, arXiv April 2004 (v6 Sept 2007); Annals of Math. 167 (2008)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: 'We prove that there are arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions of primes.' 'a certain transference principle'. Journal data: annals.math.princeton.edu/2008/167-2/p03 (seen in search results).
items.fit_T1_T7: Passes T1, T7. T2 not applicable. Fails T3, T4, T5 (it does use a pseudorandom model for correlations between primes, but with no explicit loss control), T6.
items.relevance: Verified (the claim in the session brief is correct: 2004 preprint, 2008 Annals). The transference principle is a 'positive relative density in a pseudorandom majorant' argument; it gives positivity of a pattern count, not the sign of K. Not RH-equivalent.
items.corrected_statement: arXiv math/0404188, submitted 8 April 2004, 6 versions up to 23 Sept 2007, 56 pp; ingredients Szemeredi, transference principle, Goldston-Yildirim almost primes; Annals of Math. 167 (2008) (volume confirmed by search; page numbers not seen).
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0404188 : 'We prove that there are arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions of primes.' Annals vol. 167 per search result (Wikipedia/Annals 167).

items.name: Green-Tao: Mobius function is strongly orthogonal to nilsequences
items.statement: For every simply-connected nilpotent Lie group G with discrete cocompact Gamma, polynomial sequence g, Lipschitz F, and every A>0: |(1/N) sum_{n<=N} mu(n) F(g(n)Gamma)| << _{F,G,Gamma,A} log^{-A} N. This proves the MN(s) conjecture for all s.
items.authors_year: B. Green, T. Tao, arXiv 0807.1736 (v4 May 2011); Annals of Math. 175 (2012) (journal reference not shown on arXiv page; the arXiv comment says 'To appear in Annals of Math')
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: 'we show |1/N sum mu(n)F(g(n)Gamma)| << log^-A N for all A > 0. In particular, this implies the Mobius and Nilsequence conjecture MN(s) ... for every positive integer s.'
items.fit_T1_T7: Passes T1, T2, T7. Fails T3 (size), T4 (log^-A), T5 (only against structured sequences, not between different primes), T6.
items.relevance: Together with the inverse theorem it gives Gowers uniformity of Lambda and mu, i.e. a decomposition into structured + uniform. This is the main 'correlation between primes' tool of the period, but it controls linear forms of finite complexity (shifts n+h), not a log-shift quadratic form.
items.corrected_statement: Annals of Math. 175(2) (2012) 541-566, DOI 10.4007/annals.2012.175.2.3; arXiv 0807.1736 v4 29 May 2011. Bound log^-A N for all A>0, implies MN(s) for every s. Journal reference was not on the arXiv page but confirmed via the Annals page found by search.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/0807.1736 : 'bounded by 1/log^A N, for all A > 0'; implies MN(s); https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2012/175-2/p03 (search result) for the volume/pages.

items.name: Green-Tao-Ziegler: inverse theorem for the Gowers U^{s+1}[N]-norm
items.statement: For every s>=1, if f:[N]->[-1,1] has ||f||_{U^{s+1}[N]} >= delta, then a bounded-complexity s-step nilsequence F(g(n)Gamma) correlates with f, with bounds depending only on s and delta. Combined with Green-Tao 2010 and Green-Tao 2012 this gives the Hardy-Littlewood prime tuples asymptotic for all linear systems of finite complexity.
items.authors_year: B. Green, T. Tao, T. Ziegler, Annals of Math. 176 (2012) 1231-1372 (arXiv 1009.3998, v5 April 2026 corrects a mistake in the proof of Lemma 13.2; 6-page erratum April 2024)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: 'We prove the inverse conjecture for the Gowers U^{s+1}[N]-norm for all s >= 1; this is new for s >= 4.' Theorem 1.3: 'For any s>=3, the inverse conjecture ... GI(s), is true.' ArXiv comment: 'This version corrects a mistake in the proof of Lemma 13.2 (the wrong filtration was specified)'. Announcement: arXiv:1006.0205.
items.fit_T1_T7: Passes T1, T2, T7. Fails T3, T4, T5 (it captures correlations but only up to bounded complexity and ineffective constants), T6.
items.relevance: Provides the dichotomy structured/uniform for functions on [N]. It would be the natural language for correlations between different primes, but only for affine-linear shifts. Note the published version had an error (corrected 2024-2026), so citing it in a chain of lemmas requires the corrected version.
items.corrected_statement: Annals 176 (2012) 1231-1372 (116 pp). The PDF abstract says 'for all s >= 1; this is new for s >= 4' (Theorem 1.3 itself: 'For any s >= 3, GI(s) is true'). arXiv versions: v4 22 Apr 2024 (with 6-page erratum), v5 23 Apr 2026 corrects a mistake in the proof of Lemma 13.2 (wrong filtration). Caution: the arXiv abstract web page summary I fetched read 's >= 3', but the PDF text (authoritative) says s >= 1 in the abstract and s >= 3 in Thm 1.3; both consistent with the item.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (published proof had an error in Lemma 13.2, corrected in the 2024 erratum / arXiv v5 2026)
items.check_evidence: arXiv 1009.3998 PDF (pdftotext): 'for all s >= 1; this is new for s >= 4'; 'Theorem 1.3. For any s >= 3, the inverse conjecture for the U^{s+1}[N]-norm, GI(s), is true.' https://arxiv.org/abs/1009.3998 : v5 comment 'corrects a mistake in the proof of Lemma 13.2'.

items.name: Green-Tao: Linear equations in primes
items.statement: For a system of affine-linear forms with finite complexity s and no two forms affinely related, the number of n in a convex set with all psi_i(n) prime is asymptotic to the Hardy-Littlewood prediction, assuming GI(s) and MN(s). The case s=0 follows from PNT in APs; s=1 from Hardy-Littlewood/Vinogradov; s=2 was done unconditionally; GI(s), MN(s) were later proved (previous two items). Excludes binary problems (twin primes, Goldbach).
items.authors_year: B. Green, T. Tao, Annals of Math. 171 (2010); arXiv math/0606088 (v2 April 2008)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: 'In particular we can obtain the expected asymptotics for the number of 4-term progressions p1<p2<p3<p4 <= N of primes'; 'this excludes the important binary cases such as the twin prime or Goldbach conjectures'.
items.fit_T1_T7: Passes T1, T2, T7. Fails T3, T4 (o(N^d) error), T5 (yes for finite-complexity correlations), T6.
items.relevance: This is the strongest proven statement of 'primes are pseudorandom in the Hardy-Littlewood sense' for non-binary patterns. The binary case, which would be the analogue of pair correlations of Lambda(n)Lambda(n+h), is exactly the open part (parity barrier).
items.corrected_statement: Annals of Math. 171(3) (2010) 1753-1850, DOI 10.4007/annals.2010.171.1753; arXiv math/0606088 v2 22 Apr 2008. NUANCE: the paper itself is conditional on GI(s) and MN(s) (s=2 unconditional: 4-term APs); the full unconditional statement for all finite-complexity systems needs GTZ (GI(s)) and Green-Tao Mobius/nilsequence (MN(s)). Excludes binary problems (twin primes, Goldbach).
items.corrected_status: CONDITIONAL in the 2010 paper (on GI(s),MN(s)); PROVEN in combination with later results (itself relying on the corrected GTZ proof)
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0606088 : 'Our results are therefore unconditional in the case s = 2'; excludes binary cases 'twin prime conjecture'. https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2010/171-3/p08 (search) for journal data.

items.name: Tao-Ziegler: polynomial progressions in the primes
items.statement: Let A be a set of primes with positive relative upper density. For P_1..P_k in Z[m] with P_i(0)=0, A contains infinitely many progressions x+P_1(m),...,x+P_k(m) with m>0. For the primes themselves (A=P): for any eps>0 there are infinitely many x,m with 1<=m<=x^eps such that all x+P_i(m) are prime.
items.authors_year: T. Tao, T. Ziegler, Acta Math. 201 (2008) 213-305; arXiv math/0610050
items.quote_or_locator: Theorem 1.3 (Polynomial Szemeredi theorem for the primes) as stated in arXiv:math/0610050v2; abstract: 'we establish the existence of infinitely many polynomial progressions in the primes'.
items.fit_T1_T7: Passes T1, T7. Fails T3, T4, T5, T6.
items.relevance: Existence only; no relation to the sign structure of K.
items.corrected_statement: Acta Math. 201 (2008) 213-305, DOI 10.1007/s11511-008-0032-5; arXiv math/0610050 (v2 28 Feb 2013 corrects a minor error in the definition of the polynomial forms condition). Theorem 1.3 as stated in the item matches. The x^eps bound on m is stated in Remark 1.4 ('as a by-product ... m <= x^eps for any fixed eps>0') rather than in a numbered theorem.
items.check_evidence: arXiv math/0610050 PDF: 'Theorem 1.3 (Polynomial Szemeredi theorem for the primes). Let A ⊂ P be a set of primes of positive relative upper density ... P_1(0)=...=P_k(0)=0, A contains infinitely many progressions x+P_1(m),...,x+P_k(m) with m>0.' Remarks 1.4: 'impose the bound m <= x^eps'.

items.name: Matomaki-Radziwill: multiplicative functions in short intervals
items.statement: Theorem 1: for multiplicative f:N->[-1,1], absolute constants C, C'>1, any 2<=h<=X and delta>0: |(1/h) sum_{x<=n<=x+h} f(n) - (1/X) sum_{X<=n<=2X} f(n)| <= delta + C' log log h/log h for all but at most C X((log h)^{1/3}/(delta^2 h^{delta/25}) + 1/(delta^2 (log X)^{1/50})) integers x in [X,2X]. Consequences: cancellation of mu(n) in almost all [x, x+psi(x)] with psi->inf arbitrarily slowly; |mean of lambda(n)lambda(n+1)| <= 1-delta for some delta>0; x^eps-smooth numbers in [x, x+c(eps) sqrt x].
items.authors_year: K. Matomaki, M. Radziwill, Annals of Math. 183 (2016) 1015-1056 (journal data from the arXiv comment 'to appear in Ann. of Math'; volume/pages UNVERIFIED); arXiv 1501.04585 (v4 Oct 2017)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: 'for the Mobius function we show that there are cancellations in the sum of mu(n) in almost all intervals of the form [x, x+psi(x)] with psi(x)->infinity arbitrarily slowly. This goes beyond what was previously known conditionally on the Density Hypothesis or the stronger Riemann Hypothesis.' Theorem 1 as printed in the arXiv text.
items.fit_T1_T7: Passes T1, T2, T7. Fails T3 (size, exceptional set), T4, T5 (single multiplicative f), T6.
items.relevance: Mobius/Liouville cancellation in short intervals is unconditional and goes beyond RH-conditional ranges, so zero information is not needed (T1, T7). It provides size savings for exponential sums only. Whether the argument carries over to Beurling systems is not known from sources (needs pointwise integer counting regularity); UNVERIFIED.

items.name: Matomaki-Radziwill-Tao: an averaged form of Chowla's conjecture
items.statement: For fixed k and H=H(X)<=X with H->infinity: sum_{h1..hk<=H} sum_{1<=n<=X} lambda(n+h1)...lambda(n+hk) = o(H^k X). Also: integral_0^X sum_{x<=n<=x+H} lambda(n)e(alpha n) dx = o(HX) uniformly in alpha.

items.fit_T1_T7: Passes T1, T7. Fails T3, T4, T5 (averaging over shifts destroys pointwise correlation information), T6.
items.relevance: Shows Chowla on average over shifts; the averaging over h is exactly what a quadratic form <v,Kv> with smoothly spread weights might use, but the saving is o(1), not usable at the 1e-29 level.

items.name: Matomaki-Radziwill-Tao: sign patterns of Liouville and Mobius
items.statement: Each of the eight sign patterns of (lambda(n), lambda(n+1), lambda(n+2)) occurs with positive lower natural density (improving Hildebrand's 'infinitely often'). For Mobius, each of the nine possible sign patterns of (mu(n), mu(n+1)) has positive lower density.

items.name: Tao: logarithmically averaged Chowla/Elliott conjecture, two-point case
items.statement: For Liouville lambda, fixed natural a1,a2 and non-negative integers b1,b2 with a1 b2 - a2 b1 != 0, and any omega(x)->infinity with 1<=omega(x)<=x: sum_{x/omega(x) < n <= x} lambda(a1 n+b1)lambda(a2 n+b2)/n = o(log omega(x)) as x->infinity. Also for general bounded multiplicative functions (log Elliott, two-point). Used to settle the Erdos discrepancy problem.
items.authors_year: T. Tao, arXiv 1509.05422 (v4 July 2016); Forum Math. Pi (the arXiv page only says 'submitted to'; the final journal data are UNVERIFIED)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: '...of the Chowla conjecture as x->infinity ... thus breaking the "parity barrier" for this problem. Our main tools are the multiplicativity of the Liouville function at small primes, a recent result of Matomaki, Radziwill, and the author ..., the Hardy-Littlewood circle method combined with a restriction theorem for the primes, and a novel "entropy decrement argument".'

items.name: Tao-Teräväinen: structure of log-averaged correlations; odd-order log Chowla
items.statement: Logarithmically averaged correlations of 1-bounded multiplicative functions are uniform limits of periodic sequences. If the functions do not weakly pretend to be a Dirichlet character, the correlation sequence vanishes identically; hence the logarithmically averaged Chowla conjecture holds for all odd-order correlations. Applications: logarithmic densities of sign patterns of lambda (length <=3) and mu (length <=4). A second proof without ergodic theory is in arXiv 1710.02112 (J. Théor. Nombres Bordeaux 30 (2018) 997-1015).
items.authors_year: T. Tao, J. Teräväinen, Duke Math. J. 168 (2019) 1977-2027 (arXiv 1708.02610); second proof arXiv 1710.02112 (JTNB 2018)
items.quote_or_locator: From the arXiv abstract page: 'correlation sequences are the uniform limit of periodic sequences'; 'new cases of the logarithmically averaged Elliott conjecture, including the logarithmically averaged Chowla conjecture for odd order correlations'. 1710.02112 abstract: 'In this note, we give a new and shorter proof of the odd order cases of the logarithmically averaged Chowla conjecture.'
items.fit_T1_T7: Passes T1, T7, T5 (structure of correlations). Fails T2 (logarithmic averaging), T3, T4 (limit statement, no rate), T6.
items.relevance: Closest to a structural (not size) statement about correlations: either they vanish or they are character-like. An analogous dichotomy for the prime-weighted kernel could be the right shape, but no sign statement follows, and the even-order case (the one relevant for a positive form) is open.
items.corrected_statement: Duke Math. J. 168(11) (2019) 1977-2027, DOI 10.1215/00127094-2019-0002 (arXiv 1708.02610 v2 27 Nov 2018). Second proof: arXiv 1710.02112, J. Theor. Nombres Bordeaux 30(3) (2018) 997-1015.

items.name: Pilatte (2023, arXiv v3 Aug 2026): power-log saving for two-point log Chowla; follow-up Guo 2026
items.statement: sum_{n<=x} lambda(n)lambda(n+1)/n << (log x)^{1-c} for an absolute constant c>0 (improving Helfgott-Radziwill 2021: << log x/(log log x)^{1/2}). Guo (arXiv 2608.23500, Aug-Sep 2026): for all shifts h<=x outside an exceptional set E_x with |E_x ∩ [1,H]| << _A H (log x)^{-A}, sup_{y<=x}|sum_{n<=y} lambda(n)lambda(n+h)/n| << (log x)^{1-c}; under GRH for Dirichlet L-functions: <= log(2 min{h,y}) + O((log x)^{1-c_G}) for all h.

items.quote_or_locator: Pilatte abstract: 'We prove that sum_{n<=x} (1/n) lambda(n)lambda(n+1) << (log x)^{1-c} for some absolute constant c>0. This appears to be best possible with current methods.'
