items.name: Sarnak's conjecture (Mobius disjointness): status and logical position
items.statement: Conjecture: every continuous zero-entropy map T of a compact metric space X is Mobius disjoint, i.e. (1/N) sum_{n<=N} f(T^n x) mu(n) -> 0 for all continuous f and all x. Chowla's conjecture implies Sarnak's conjecture (Thm 3.4 in the survey). Proven cases: irrational rotations (Davenport estimate), systems with discrete spectrum (Matomaki-Radziwill-Tao), nilsystems (Green-Tao), horocycle flows (Bourgain-Sarnak-Ziegler), and logarithmic versions for singular spectrum (Tao) and countably many ergodic measures (Frantzikinakis-Host). The conjecture is open in general. Positive-entropy systems can be Mobius disjoint.
items.authors_year: P. Sarnak 2010 (conjecture); survey by S. Ferenczi, J. Kułaga-Przymus, M. Lemańczyk, 2017 (arXiv 1710.04039); J. Bourgain, P. Sarnak, T. Ziegler, in Developments in Mathematics 28 (2013) 67-83 (arXiv 1110.0992)
items.quote_or_locator: Survey: 'Each zero entropy continuous map T of a compact metric space X is Mobius disjoint.' 'In particular, the Chowla conjecture implies Sarnak's conjecture.' 'Davenport's estimate (eq. 3) yields the Mobius disjointness of irrational rotations.' BSZ abstract: 'a finite version of Vinogradov's bilinear sum inequality ... Mobius function is disjoint from discrete horocycle flows'.
items.fit_T1_T7: Would pass T1, T2, T5 if proven. Fails T3, T4 as formulated (a limit statement), T6, and is not proven (T7 is satisfied only for special systems).
items.relevance: Sarnak and Chowla are not RH-equivalent (RH gives a rate for M(x) but Chowla's even-order cases are not RH consequences). They say that mu is orthogonal to all deterministic sequences, which is a statement of no correlation between different primes; no sign follows and the position of the log-shift kernel in this framework is not identified.
items.corrected_statement: Statement as in survey eq. (2); Chowla => Sarnak is Thm 3.4 of the survey; proven cases: discrete spectrum (MRT), nilsystems, horocycle flows (Bourgain-Sarnak-Ziegler, arXiv 1110.0992), log versions for singular spectrum (Tao) and countably many ergodic measures (Frantzikinakis-Host). Positive-entropy systems can be Mobius disjoint. ADDITIONS: the survey also records that logarithmic Chowla and logarithmic Sarnak are equivalent (Thm 3.10) and that Tao proved log Chowla at order 2 (Thm 3.15). Survey is Ferenczi-Kulaga-Przymus-Lemanczyk, 'Sarnak's Conjecture -- what's new', arXiv 1710.04039 v1 11 Oct 2017. Year 2010 for Sarnak's conjecture and BSZ journal data (Dev. Math. 28 (2013) 67-83) not seen on opened pages.
items.corrected_status: CONJECTURE (open in general); partial cases PROVEN

items.name: Maynard: primes with restricted digits
items.statement: For any a0 in {0,...,9}, with A the set of integers < X with no digit a0 in base 10: #{p in A} ≍ #A / log X ≍ X^{log 9/log 10}/log X. Thus there are infinitely many primes without the digit a0. Expected asymptotic with the constant kappa_A (not proved).
items.authors_year: J. Maynard, arXiv 1604.01041 (v2 Oct 2019); published in Invent. Math. (journal reference not shown on the arXiv page; UNVERIFIED)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: 'We show there are infinitely many prime numbers which do not have the digit a0 in their decimal expansion.' ... 'rests on obtaining suitable Type I and Type II arithmetic information for use in Harman's sieve to control the minor arcs ... moment estimates obtained by comparison with a Markov process'. Theorem 1.1: '#{p in A} ≍ #A/log X'.
items.fit_T1_T7: Passes T1, T7. Fails T3, T4 (≍ only, no asymptotic), T5, T6.
items.relevance: Interesting here only because the proof uses a Markov-process comparison for a Fourier transform (moment estimates), echoing the Markov/Perron-Frobenius structure of the pole-free bulk; but it gives a lower bound of order, not a sign.

Publication in Invent. Math. (217 (2019) 127-218 from memory) is not on the arXiv page: UNVERIFIED.

items.name: Green-Sawhney: primes of the form p^2 + n q^2
items.statement: Let n ≡ 0 or 4 (mod 6), W in C_0^∞(R^2), N>1. Then sum_{x,y} Lambda(x)Lambda(y)Lambda(x^2+ny^2) W(x/N,y/N) = kappa_n N^2 ∫W + O_{W,n}(N^2 (log log N)^2/log N), with kappa_n an explicit Euler product. In particular there are infinitely many primes x^2+ny^2 with x,y prime; for n=4 this is the Gaussian primes conjecture of Friedlander-Iwaniec.
items.authors_year: B. Green, M. Sawhney, arXiv 2410.04189 (v3 6 June 2026); the arXiv page says 'accepted for publication in Acta Math' (no volume/pages)
items.quote_or_locator: Theorem 1.1 as printed in the arXiv text; abstract: 'we make heavy use of two recent developments in the theory of Gowers norms in additive combinatorics: quantitative versions of so-called concatenation theorems, due to Kuca and to Kuca-Kravitz-Leng, and the quasipolynomial inverse theorem of Leng, Sah and the second author.'
items.fit_T1_T7: Passes T1, T7. Fails T3, T4 (error (log log N)^2/log N), T6; T5 yes (a prime-valued polynomial form of three primes simultaneously), T2 not applicable.
items.relevance: Shows that, with Gowers-norm technology, an asymptotic with a power-of-log error holds for a non-linear correlation of three Lambda values. It is the freshest proven correlation of Lambda at different arguments; the error term still dominates any 1e-29 margin.
items.corrected_statement: Confirmed at abstract level: n = 0 or 4 mod 6; infinitely many primes p^2+nq^2 with p,q prime plus an asymptotic count; n=4 gives the Friedlander-Iwaniec Gaussian primes conjecture; Type I/II sums in Q(sqrt(-n)), Type II via recent Gowers-norm results. arXiv 2410.04189: v1 5 Oct 2024, v3 6 Jun 2026 (v3 'corrects an error with a partial summation argument in Section 8.3'), 59 pp, 'accepted for publication in Acta Math'. NOT verified: the displayed Theorem 1.1 (kappa_n, error O(N^2 (log log N)^2/log N)) and the abstract's exact citation of Kuca/Kuca-Kravitz-Leng/Leng-Sah-Sawhney.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (accepted, Acta Math, per arXiv comment); error-term formula UNVERIFIED
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.04189 : comment 'accepted for publication in Acta Math'; v3 note about error in Section 8.3; abstract summary: n ≡ 0, 4 (mod 6), Gaussian primes conjecture for n=4.

items.name: Beurling systems with PNT-level data and RH failing / holding (barrier for any 'generic prime' axioms)
items.statement: Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer: for 1/2<θ<1 there is a Beurling generalized number system with N(x)=ρx+O(x^θ) whose prime counting function satisfies π(x)=Li(x)+Ω_±(x exp(-c sqrt(log x))), with zeta realising the de la Vallée Poussin zero-free region, so RH fails. Zhang: there are systems with RH and N(x)=ρx+O(x^θ). Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas: a system with RH, π(x)=Li(x)+O(sqrt x) and N(x)=ρx+Ω_±(sqrt x exp(-c sqrt(log x log log x))).
items.authors_year: H. G. Diamond, H. L. Montgomery, U. M. A. Vorhauer, Math. Ann. 334 (2006) 1-36; W.-B. Zhang; F. Broucke, G. Debruyne, J. Vindas, Adv. Math. 370 (2020) 107240 (arXiv 2004.11501)
items.quote_or_locator: BDV intro: 'Diamond, Montgomery, and Vorhauer constructed a Beurling generalized number system with very regularly distributed integers, but whose distribution of prime numbers has large oscillation ... in particular, the Riemann hypothesis (RH) fails for it.' 'Zhang ... showing that there are also Beurling number systems for which, in contrast, the RH and the asymptotic estimate (1.1) both hold.'
items.fit_T1_T7: Barrier statement, not a tool. Shows that any property shared by all Beurling systems of the same density (T7 in its generalized form) cannot prove K>=0, because the Weil-type form is not nonnegative for the DMV system (RH fails there).
items.relevance: For every item above marked NA or UNKNOWN the same test applies: a sign proof for K must use a property that fails for the DMV system. Such properties are additive (Vinogradov, Gowers, Szemeredi-type) or specifically about Z (consecutive integers); the sources show that Vaughan's identity, multiplicativity and PNT-level density do not suffice. Caveat: the claim that the Weil form fails to be positive for DMV is a consequence of 'RH fails' under the Weil criterion for that system; the Weil criterion for Beurling zeta was not checked here (UNVERIFIED).
items.corrected_statement: ERROR in the item: BDV Theorem 1.1 gives pi(x)=Li(x)+O(sqrt x) and N(x)=rho x + Omega_±(x exp(-c sqrt(log x log log x))) for any c>2*sqrt(2) -- the oscillation is of x times exp(...), NOT 'sqrt x exp(...)'. Adv. Math. 370 (2020) 107240, arXiv 2004.11501. DMV: Math. Ann. 334 (2006) 1-36, DOI 10.1007/s00208-005-0638-2, for 1/2<theta<1 system with N(x)=rho x+O(x^theta), pi(x)=Li(x)+Omega_±(x exp(-c sqrt(log x))); zeta has infinitely many zeros on sigma=1-a/log t and none to the right. Zhang: Math. Ann. 337 (2007), 'Beurling primes with RH and Beurling primes with large oscillation' (the item gives no year/venue). The inference that the Weil-type form fails to be nonnegative for the DMV system, and the transfer 'any sign proof must use a property that fails for DMV', are the item's own claims, not supported by any opened source (Weil criterion for Beurling zeta not checked).
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (existence of the systems); relevance claim UNVERIFIED (own inference)

N(x)=rho x+Ω_±(x exp(-c sqrt(log x log log x)))'; DMV 'for 1/2<theta<1'; Zhang 'RH and ... N(x)=rho x+O(x^theta) both hold'. Bombieri-Vinogradov, von Koch (RH => error O(sqrt x log x)) and Selberg 1949 elementary PNT from the user's original brief are outside this domain's item list and were not rechecked here, except Selberg's 1949 parity-problem date (VERIFIED via Wikipedia, secondary).

Conditional / RH-equivalent results (e.g. Goldbach/Hardy-Littlewood under GRH, Chowla/Elliott implications, Mobius sum bounds equivalent to RH) are absent from the item list: the domain has no RH_EQUIVALENT or CONDITIONAL entry except Guo's GRH clause.
Meta-note: several secondary-only items (Vinogradov, Chen, Parity, Vaughan) rely on Wikipedia; primary papers were not opened, so these remain 'CONFIRMED against secondary source' only.

merged.title: Multiplicative structure and positivity tools in analytic number theory
merged.summary:
DIRECT ANSWER: nothing in this domain supplies a proven, lossless, prime-side SIGN valid for all windows. The exact identities (unique factorization, Euler product, Lambda = mu*log, Vaughan, Heath-Brown) are lossless but give STRUCTURE only and hold formally for every Beurling system (YES), so they cannot prove RH alone. The positivity/extremal tools (Selberg lambda^2 sieve, Beurling-Selberg majorants, Montgomery-Vaughan, Turan, Halasz, pretentious 3-4-1 inequality) give SIZE or zero-free regions, are lossy, and the harmonic-analysis ones use no prime input (NA).
NAMED BARRIERS (all sourced): (1) Zhu 2608.24827 Lemma 3.2: sup of the prime comb equals A_L because {log p} are Q-independent by unique factorization and Weyl equidistribution applies, so no pointwise bound on the comb beats it. (2) Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer Beurling system: de la Vallee Poussin zero-free region realized and RH fails, so Euler product plus density axioms cannot give RH. (3) Selberg parity problem, factor 2. (4) Littlewood sign changes of pi-li were proved via zeros, not from the prime side. (5) Davenport-Heilbronn: functional equation without Euler product, no RH (off-line zeros rigor UNVERIFIED here).
BEST CANDIDATE FOR A SIGN: not a proven theorem. It is the open lemma in Zhu Remark 1.6: prove quantitatively that the phases (t log p) cannot align, i.e. a statement on simultaneous Diophantine approximation of {log p}. It must be Z-specific: generic real sequences with Q-independent logs also equidistribute, and Beurling systems exist where RH fails. Zhu's pole term is rank one (2F(i/2)^2, with sign reversal in the odd sector), which matches the project's s_E/s_O split.
ACCOUNTING FOR THE USER'S UNVERIFIED FACTS: Zhu quote VERIFIED verbatim (abstract, Synthesis): "Passing the resulting wall thus requires cancellation in the prime comb, a concrete arithmetic problem"; window [-0.8,0.8] VERIFIED (Theorem 1.2, Q(f) >= 8.9e-18 ||f||^2; autocorrelation support 1.6). Credibility flags: single-author preprint v2 (2 Sep 2026), not refereed (not checked), certified computation that I did NOT rerun, and v1's support-2.38 claim was retracted (Remark 3.3, Section 7). Suzuki 2606.09096: abstract says "obtained without assuming the Riemann Hypothesis" but states NO numeric window; Theorem 1.4 is only "for sufficiently small a>0"; the task's window for Suzuki is UNVERIFIED. Yoshida's window log2/2 is reported via Zhu (abstract), not read in Yoshida (Project Euclid fetch returned HTML). Green-Tao: abstract verified (math/0404188) but outside this domain, hand to the primes-in-progressions agent. von Koch, Bombieri-Vinogradov: NOT verified here (out of domain), no memory padding; the Selberg fact in the request is underspecified, I checked the symmetry formula (Wikipedia only) and the sieve (Soundararajan survey).
CROSS-CHECK: Zhu's table of upper bounds on the smallest eigenvalue gives 5.88e-30 at L=1.0 (support 2.0), 1.65e-17 at L=0.8, 7.94e-49 at L=1.2. The project's margin ~1e-29 matches the L=1.0 row only in order of magnitude; normalizations are not compared, so the match is UNVERIFIED.

items.name: Unique factorization and Euler product
items.statement: Every integer n>=1 is uniquely a product of primes; hence for completely multiplicative f with convergence, sum_{n>=1} f(n) = prod_p (1 - f(p))^{-1}; in particular zeta(s)=prod_p(1-p^{-s})^{-1} for Re s>1, and the Dirichlet series of Lambda is -zeta'(s)/zeta(s) (DLMF 27.4.12).
items.authors_year: Euler 1737 (classical); modern reference DLMF section 27.4
items.quote_or_locator: DLMF 27.4.2: 'If f(n) is completely multiplicative, then each factor in the product is a geometric series and the Euler product becomes sum f(n) = prod_p (1-f(p))^{-1}'; 27.4.12: sum Lambda(n) n^{-s} = -zeta'(s)/zeta(s), Re s>1 (formula text as returned by page fetch; the unique-factorization sentence itself was not quoted from DLMF)
items.fit_T1_T7: Satisfies T1, T2, T4, T7; fails T3 (no sign) and T5/T6 as a tool (it only encodes the correlations, it does not control them). Zhu Lemma 3.2 shows its consequence, Q-independence of {log p}, is exactly what blocks pointwise sign bounds.
items.relevance: Source of the prime-side matrix and of the Weyl-equidistribution barrier. It is the defining axiom of Beurling systems, so by itself it cannot prove RH.
items.corrected_statement: Euler product for completely multiplicative f is DLMF (27.4.2); Dirichlet series of Lambda is -zeta'/zeta, DLMF (27.4.12). The unique-factorization sentence is not in the quoted DLMF lines and the attribution 'Euler 1737' is not sourced here.
items.check_evidence: https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.4 fetched: '(27.4.2) If f(n) is completely multiplicative, then each factor in the product is a geometric series and the Euler product becomes sum f(n) = prod_p (1-f(p))^-1'; '(27.4.12) sum Lambda(n) n^-s = -zeta'(s)/zeta(s), Re s>1'.

items.name: Lambda = mu * log (Mobius inversion of log = 1 * Lambda)
items.statement: log n = sum_{d|n} Lambda(d) is equivalent to Lambda(n) = sum_{d|n} mu(n/d) log d = sum_{d|n} mu(d) log(n/d). Equivalently sum_{ab=n} mu(a) log b = log p if n=p^m, 0 otherwise. VERIFIED: the form Lambda=mu*log is correct (the variant -sum mu(d) log d is equal for n>1 only because sum mu(d)=0).
items.authors_year: Classical (Mobius inversion, 19th c.); DLMF 27.5.5; Granville survey 2014
items.quote_or_locator: DLMF (27.5.5): 'ln n = sum_{d|n} Lambda(d) <=> Lambda(n) = sum_{d|n} (ln d) mu(n/d)'. Granville, Primes in intervals of bounded length (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.8400), eq (2.2) and section 2.4: 'Lambda(n) = sum_{d|n} mu(d) log n/d'
items.fit_T1_T7: T1, T2, T4, T7 pass; T3 fails (mu has no sign), T5 only formally (mu encodes all prime correlations but is itself as hard as PNT).
items.relevance: Exact rewriting of the prime data of K as mu convolved with log; any sign argument via mu needs cancellation in mu, equivalent in strength to PNT-type input, and the identity is formal for every Beurling system.
items.corrected_statement: DLMF (27.5.5) and Granville (2.2) both match. Granville p. numbering: sum_{ab=n} mu(a) log b = log p if n=p^m, 0 otherwise; Lambda(n)=sum_{d|n} mu(d) log(n/d).
items.check_evidence: https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.5: 'ln n = sum_{d|n} Lambda(d) <=> Lambda(n) = sum_{d|n} (ln d) mu(n/d)' (27.5.5). Granville arXiv 1410.8400 (pdftotext of PDF), eq (2.2) and 'Lambda(n) = sum_{d|n} mu(d) log n/d'. Also Granville says this identity is equivalent to PNT in the sense mean of mu -> 0 iff PNT.

items.name: Vaughan identity
items.statement: For parameters U,V >= 1: Lambda_{>=V} = mu_{<U} * L - mu_{<U} * Lambda_{<V} * 1 + mu_{>=U} * Lambda_{>=V} * 1 (L = log, * = Dirichlet convolution, 1 = constant function), an exact decomposition of Lambda into type I and type II bilinear convolutions.
items.authors_year: R. C. Vaughan 1977 (C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris Ser. A 285, 981-983)
items.quote_or_locator: Granville, eq (7.1): 'Vaughan's identity: Lambda_{>=V} = mu_{<U} * L - mu_{<U} * Lambda_{<V} * 1 + mu_{>=U} * Lambda_{>=V} * 1', with the derivation 'Lambda_{>=V} = Lambda - Lambda_{<V} = (mu * L) - Lambda_{<V} * (1 * mu)'. Citation: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaughan%27s_identity (C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 285:981-983)
items.fit_T1_T7: T1, T2, T4 pass (exact algebra); T3 fails; T5 partial (bilinear sums see correlations only through Vinogradov-type bounds, which are lossy); T7 pass.
items.relevance: Exact decomposition of the prime comb into bilinear forms; the estimates applied to type I/II sums are bounds in absolute value and lose sign, so it cannot give s_E<=0 / s_O>=0 at margin 1e-29.
items.corrected_statement: Granville eq (7.1) verbatim: Lambda_{>=V} = mu_{<U} * L - mu_{<U} * Lambda_{<V} * 1 + mu_{>=U} * Lambda_{>=V} * 1. Vaughan's original is cited in Granville [65] as 'Sommes trigonometriques sur les nombres premiers, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris Ser.' (volume/pages/year 285, 981-983, 1977 not seen in the fetched line; only Wikipedia per item).
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (1977 date and C.R. pages: UNVERIFIED by me)
items.check_evidence: pdftotext of arxiv.org/pdf/1410.8400 line 'Vaughan's identity: Lambda>=V = mu<U * L - mu<U * Lambda<V * 1 + mu>=U * Lambda>=V * 1 (7.1)' with the derivation shown.

items.name: Heath-Brown identity
items.statement: For n <= U^k, Lambda(n) = - sum_{j=1}^{k} (-1)^j C(k,j) (mu_{<=U} * ... * mu_{<=U} * log * 1 * ... * 1)(n), an exact k-fold generalization of Vaughan's identity (the exact number of convolution factors in each term was garbled in my text extraction of the survey: UNVERIFIED in detail).
items.authors_year: D. R. Heath-Brown 1982, Canad. J. Math. 34, 1365-1377
items.quote_or_locator: Granville section 7.2: 'The following identity, due to Heath-Brown [33], is used in [57] to get the strongest form of Zhang's theorem: If n <= U^k then Lambda(n) = - sum_{j=1}^k (-1)^j C(k,j) mu_{<=U} * ... * log * 1 * ... * 1 (n)'. Original: https://resolve.cambridge.org/core/journals/canadian-journal-of-mathematics/article/prime-numbers-in-short-intervals-and-a-generalized-vaughan-identity/D6C21FF61C1489E5856AA5ED276CB0A9
items.fit_T1_T7: Same as Vaughan: T1, T2, T4, T7 pass; T3 fails; T5 only via lossy bilinear estimates.
items.relevance: More flexible exact splitting of the comb; no sign mechanism, formal algebra valid in any Beurling system.
items.corrected_statement: Item's formula as printed in Granville (mu_{<=U} * ... * log * 1 * ... * 1) is right in shape but Granville's own gloss ('mu convolved k times, 1 convolved k-1 times') is for the j-th term j times / j-1 times, not k. A secondary survey (additive prime number theory, arXiv math/0412220) gives the standard form: Lambda(k) = sum_{j=1}^J (-1)^{j-1} C(J,j) sum over m_1...m_{2j}=k, m_1...m_j < x^{1/J}, of mu(m_1)...mu(m_j) log m_{2j}, i.e. j copies of mu, j-1 copies of 1, one log. Journal citation confirmed: Canad. J. Math. 34 (1982), no. 6, 1365-1377. Original paper's own statement not opened (Cambridge page shows only extract). Hypothesis 'n <= U^k' is Granville's; the survey uses k <= x.
items.check_evidence: Granville 1410.8400 sec 7.2: 'If n <= U^k then Lambda(n) = - sum_{j=1}^k (-1)^j C(k,j) mu<=U * ... * log * 1 * ... * 1 (n) where mu<=U is convolved k times, and 1 is convolved k-1 times'. Cambridge: https://cambridge.org/core/journals/canadian-journal-of-mathematics/article/prime-numbers-in-short-intervals-and-a-generalized-vaughan-identity/D6C21FF61C1489E5856AA5ED276CB0A9 (vol 34 no 6, 1365-1377).

items.name: Selberg symmetry formula
items.statement: sum_{p<x} (log p)^2 + sum_{pq<x} log p log q = 2 x log x + O(x). Left side is the summatory function of Lambda log + Lambda*Lambda, the coefficients of zeta''/zeta; exact Dirichlet-series form Lambda log + Lambda*Lambda = mu*log^2 is from memory, UNVERIFIED here.
items.authors_year: A. Selberg 1949 (elementary proof of PNT); statement as in Wikipedia
items.quote_or_locator: Wikipedia: 'the crucial starting point in the first elementary proof for the prime number theorem'; left side 'is essentially a sum of coefficients c_n ... of the Dirichlet series zeta''(s)/zeta(s)' (Wikipedia only, original paper not opened)
items.fit_T1_T7: T1, T2, T7 pass; fails T3 (asymptotic, no sign), T4 (O(x) error). It does see pair products pq (T5 partially) but only at the level of size.
items.relevance: The one classical place where products of two different primes appear with a controlled main term; error O(x) is far too coarse for a 1e-29 sign.
items.corrected_statement: Statement and error O(x) confirmed. The Dirichlet-series identity the item left UNVERIFIED is now confirmed: Lambda(n) log n + sum_{d|n} Lambda(d)Lambda(n/d) = sum_{d|n} mu(d) log^2(n/d), coefficients of zeta''/zeta. Original paper (Selberg, Ann. of Math. 50 (1949)) still not opened; Wikipedia only (secondary).
items.check_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selberg%27s_identity fetched: 'sum_{p<x}(log p)^2 + sum_{pq<x} log p log q = 2x log x + O(x)'; 'Lambda(n)log n + sum_{d|n}Lambda(d)Lambda(n/d) = sum_{d|n} mu(d) log^2(n/d)'. Item's 'holds_for_beurling_primes UNKNOWN' is wrong in direction: Selberg's formula is known to be provable in axiomatic Beurling settings only under extra hypotheses (Beurling-type elementary PNT, e.g. Diamond-Zhang book) - не проверено.

items.name: Selberg lambda-squared sieve (and Maynard refinement)
items.statement: For real lambda_d with lambda_1=1 and lambda_d=0 for d>R, a(n) = (sum_{d | (n+h_1)...(n+h_k)} lambda_d)^2 >= 0 and equals 1 when n+h_1,...,n+h_k are all prime (R<x<=n), so sum a(n) upper-bounds the number of prime k-tuples; lambda_d is chosen to minimize the resulting quadratic form. Maynard 2013 refines the weights: prime k-tuples conjecture holds for a positive proportion of admissible k-tuples, liminf (p_{n+m}-p_n) < infinity for every m, liminf(p_{n+1}-p_n) <= 600.
items.authors_year: A. Selberg 1947; J. Maynard 2013 (arXiv 1311.4600)
items.quote_or_locator: Soundararajan survey, eqs (5)-(6): 'Let lambda_d be a sequence of real numbers such that lambda_1=1 ... a(n) = (sum_{d|(n+h_1)...(n+h_k)} lambda_d)^2. Being a square, a(n) is clearly non-negative.' Maynard: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.4600 abstract (verbatim via arXiv API)
items.fit_T1_T7: T1, T3 (sign by construction, a square), T5 (handles several primes n+h_i simultaneously), T7 pass. Fails T4 (upper bound only, parity loses a factor >= 2) and T2/T6 (no matrix-window statement). Maynard weights rest on Bombieri-Vinogradov, not verified here.
items.relevance: Closest existing model of 'positivity by a square' that sees correlations between different primes; the exact analogue would be to write K as a sum of squares of prime-side vectors, but the sieve only majorizes and the parity barrier makes it lossy.
items.corrected_statement: Maynard 2013 (Annals 181 (2015), 383-413): liminf(p_{n+1}-p_n) <= 600, liminf(p_{n+m}-p_n)<infinity for every m (confirmed). The item's phrase 'prime k-tuples conjecture holds for a positive proportion of admissible k-tuples' overstates: the theorem is that for a positive proportion of admissible k-tuples, at least m of the n+h_i are simultaneously prime for infinitely many n (not all k). Maynard's weights are a GPY-type refinement (Goldston-Pintz-Yildirim 2005/2009 is the missing predecessor); the use of Bombieri-Vinogradov is standard but not verified by me. Maynard's independent discovery by Tao (Polymath8b) not mentioned. Soundararajan survey eqs (5)-(6) not re-opened. Under EH: liminf <= 12 (confirmed).
items.check_evidence: https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2015/181-1/p07 and https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.4600 (search result): 'lim inf (p_{n+1}-p_n) <= 600', EH gives '<= 12'. Journal: Ann. Math. 181 (2015) 383-413, DOI 10.4007/annals.2015.181.1.7.

items.name: Selberg parity problem and its partial breaking
items.statement: Sieve methods alone cannot distinguish numbers with an even from those with an odd number of prime factors, so upper bounds are off by a factor >= 2 and no nontrivial lower bound follows from sieve axioms. Tao 2016 proves the logarithmically averaged two-point Chowla conjecture: sum_{x/w(x)<n<=x} lambda(a_1 n+b_1)lambda(a_2 n+b_2)/n = o(log w(x)), 'breaking the parity barrier for this problem'.
items.authors_year: A. Selberg 1949-50; T. Tao 2016 (Forum Math. Pi, arXiv 1509.05422)
items.quote_or_locator: Wikipedia: 'sieve theory is unable to provide non-trivial lower bounds on the size of A'; Friedlander-Iwaniec 'new sieve techniques to break the parity problem'. Tao abstract (https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.05422): 'thus breaking the parity barrier for this problem'
items.fit_T1_T7: Parity is the named obstruction to T3/T4 for any sieve-type argument. Tao's theorem passes T1, T5 (genuine two-point correlation) and T7, but is an o() statement (fails T3, T4) and about lambda, not Lambda.
items.relevance: Explains why a sign from prime-side sieve weights will lose a factor of 2 (margin is 1e-29, no slack); Tao shows correlations between shifts are provable in averaged form but only as o().
items.corrected_statement: Tao: logarithmically averaged two-point Chowla/Elliott, Forum Math. Pi 4 (2016), e8, DOI 10.1017/fmp.2016.6 (refereed, published; item's 'Forum Math. Pi, arXiv 1509.05422' is right, v4 29 Jul 2016). Item's displayed formula lambda(a_1 n+b_1)lambda(a_2 n+b_2) with o(log w(x)) is not verified verbatim by me (arXiv abstract was paraphrased only). Important caveat: Tao's result breaks parity for THIS correlation problem only; it does not break the sieve parity barrier for primes. Friedlander-Iwaniec (bilinear/Type II, 'Opera de Cribro') is the standard parity-breaking for primes (e.g. x^2+y^4) and Heath-Brown cubic forms: not sourced here.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (Tao theorem); parity-barrier statement via Wikipedia only
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.05422: comments 'submitted to Forum of Mathematics, Pi'; abstract paraphrase: 'This breaks the parity barrier for the problem'. Published: https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/forum-of-mathematics-pi/article/logarithmically-averaged-chowla-and-elliott-conjectures-for-twopoint-correlations/48514F53D73B2C1277BD7232630F0694 (vol 4, e8, 2016).

items.name: Halasz theorem on mean values of multiplicative functions
items.statement: For f in C(kappa) (|Lambda_f(n)| <= kappa Lambda(n)) and large x: sum_{n<=x} f(n) << (x/log x) * integral_{1/log x}^{1} max_{|t|<=(log x)^kappa} |F(1+sigma+it)/(1+sigma+it)|^kappa dsigma/sigma + (x/log x)(log log x)^kappa. Consequence: a multiplicative f with |f|<=1 has mean value 0 or is close to n^{it}.
items.authors_year: G. Halasz (original 1968/1971, dating UNVERIFIED: my search found Halasz 1971 Studia Sci. Math. Hungar. 6 but no 1968 source); generalized and reproved by Granville-Harper-Soundararajan 2017/2019 (Compositio)
items.quote_or_locator: GHS Theorem 1.1 (Halasz's Theorem) as printed; abstract: 'a multiplicative function with |f(n)| <= 1 has either mean value 0, or is close to n^{it} for some fixed t.'
items.fit_T1_T7: T1, T2 (uniform in f), T7 pass; fails T3, T4 (<< bound), T5 (depends on f only through f(p)).
items.relevance: Bounds, never signs; no mechanism to supply s_E<=0. Useful only to show mu or lambda cannot correlate with n^{it} at fixed t.
items.corrected_statement: Original date is NOT unverified: G. Halasz, 'Uber die Mittelwerte multiplikativer zahlentheoretischer Funktionen', Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. 19 (1968), 365-403, DOI 10.1007/BF01894515 (Satz 2 is the formulation per Encyclopedia of Math). The 1971 Studia Sci. Math. Hungar. 6 paper is a separate, later one. GHS: A. Granville, A. Harper, K. Soundararajan, 'A new proof of Halasz's Theorem, and its consequences', Compositio Math. 155 (2019), 126-163, arXiv 1706.03749 (v. June 2017). The displayed Theorem 1.1 formula in the item (C(kappa) class, max over |t|<=(log x)^kappa) was not re-verified by me against the PDF text (fetch returned binary).
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03749 (Compositio 155 (2019) 126-163). Halasz 1968: https://encyclopediaofmath.org/wiki/Halasz_mean_value_theorem ('Satz 2'); bibliographic data via search: Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. 19 (3-4): 365-403.

items.name: Pretentious distance and the 3-4-1 inequality
items.statement: D(f,g;x)^2 = sum_{p<=x} (1 - Re f(p) conj g(p))/p satisfies the triangle inequality. For completely multiplicative f,g with |f|,|g|<=1 and sigma>1: sqrt(log(zeta(sigma)/|F(sigma)|)) + sqrt(log(zeta(sigma)/|G(sigma)|)) >= sqrt(log(zeta(sigma)/|F(x)G(sigma)|)). With f=n^{-it}, g=n^{-it}: zeta(sigma)^3 |zeta(sigma+it)|^4 |zeta(sigma+2it)| >= 1. This is a prime-side sign (positivity per prime from 3+4cos(theta)+cos(2theta) >= 0) giving the classical zero-free region at Re s=1.
items.authors_year: A. Granville, K. Soundararajan 2006 (Anatomy of Integers, CRM Proc. 46, 2008); 3-4-1 inequality classical (Mertens)
items.quote_or_locator: GS Proposition 1 and Corollary 2, followed by: 'If we take t1 = t2 in the second inequality of Corollary 2, square out and simplify, we obtain the classical inequality zeta(sigma)^3 |zeta(sigma+it)|^4 |zeta(sigma+2it)| >= 1.' Also 'the insight of Hadamard and de la Vallee Poussin ...'
items.fit_T1_T7: T1, T3, T7 pass. Fails T4 (only a zero-free region near Re s=1, a size statement on zeros), T5 (positivity is per prime and its powers, cos terms of one prime only), T2/T6 (no window or matrix statement).
items.relevance: The only established mechanism where the Euler product itself yields a sign, and it holds in every Beurling system (DMV system realizes exactly this region and RH fails there), so it demonstrably cannot reach RH.
items.corrected_statement: Granville-Soundararajan Prop. 1 (verified in PDF text): for completely multiplicative f,g with |f|,|g|<=1, sigma>1: sqrt(log(zeta(sigma)/|F(sigma)|)) + sqrt(log(zeta(sigma)/|G(sigma)|)) >= sqrt(log(zeta(sigma)/|(F tensor G)(sigma)|)), where (F tensor G)(s)=sum f(n)g(n)n^-s. The item's right-hand side 'F(x)G(sigma)' is garbled; it must be F tensor G. With t1=t2 in Cor. 2 one gets zeta(sigma)^3 |zeta(sigma+it)|^4 |zeta(sigma+2it)| >= 1 (verified verbatim). The paper is arXiv math/0608407 'Pretentious multiplicative functions and an inequality for the zeta-function' (AIM preprint 2006-22); the venue 'Anatomy of Integers, CRM Proc. 46, 2008' is not shown on the arXiv page - UNVERIFIED. Item's phrase 'giving the classical zero-free region at Re s=1' is imprecise: 3-4-1 alone gives non-vanishing on Re s=1; the de la Vallee Poussin region needs additional input.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0608407; pdftotext of arxiv.org/pdf/math/0608407: 'If we take t1 = t2 in the second inequality of Corollary 2, square out and simplify, we obtain the classical inequality zeta(sigma)^3|zeta(sigma+it)|^4|zeta(sigma+2it)| >= 1.'

items.name: Montgomery-Vaughan generalized Hilbert inequality
items.statement: For real lambda_1<...<lambda_N with delta_k = min(lambda_k-lambda_{k-1}, lambda_{k+1}-lambda_k): |sum_{m != n} z_m conj(z_n)/(lambda_m-lambda_n)| <= C_1 sum |z_n|^2/delta_n with C_1 = 3 pi/2; the unweighted case (delta = min gap) has the sharp constant pi/delta; the sharp weighted constant is >= pi (conjecturally pi).
items.authors_year: H. L. Montgomery, R. C. Vaughan 1974, J. London Math. Soc. (2) 8, 73-82
items.quote_or_locator: Yangjit, eq (1.3): '|sum_m sum_{n != m} z_m conj(z_n)/(lambda_m - lambda_n)| <= C_1 sum |z_n|^2/delta_n', page states 'C_1 is the absolute constant 3 pi/2'; unweighted (1.2) constant pi/delta; citation 'Montgomery and Vaughan (1974). Hilbert's inequality. J. Lond. Math. Soc. (2) 8, 73-82'. (3/2 pi form is as returned by page fetch; the earlier 'pi+1' recollection was not confirmed)
items.fit_T1_T7: Pure harmonic analysis (no prime input), so T1 vacuous; fails T3 (absolute value bound), T4, T5, T6. T2 pass (uniform).
items.relevance: Bounds off-diagonal Hilbert-type forms with nodes log n; our K has Gamma-term and Lambda(n)/sqrt(n) weights with sign needed at 1e-29, a bound with constant pi or 3pi/2 is hopeless.
items.corrected_statement: Weighted inequality with C_1=3pi/2 is MV 1974 (J. London Math. Soc. (2) 8, 73-82) - confirmed via Yangjit. The item omits that Preissmann improved the constant to pi*sqrt(1+(2/3)sqrt(6/5)) ~ 1.3154 pi < 4pi/3, so the known range for the optimal constant is pi <= C <= 4pi/3 (not just '>= pi'). Conjectural value pi. Preissmann's paper (Mathematika 1984, 'A further generalization' per search hit) not opened. Unweighted sharp pi/delta not re-verified by me.

items.name: Beurling-Selberg extremal majorants and minorants
items.statement: Find real entire functions G <= f <= H of exponential type at most 2pi minimizing the integrals of f-G and H-f. For f=sgn(x) the extremal solution was found by Beurling in the 1930s (rediscovered by Selberg for the large sieve) with integral of (B-sgn)=1; majorants/minorants of the interval indicator have Fourier transforms supported in [-1,1]. Carneiro-Vaaler give extremal G,H for exp(-lambda|x|): integral(e^{-lambda|x|}-L)=lambda^{-1}... as in (1.7)-(1.8).
items.authors_year: A. Beurling (1930s, unpublished); A. Selberg; J. D. Vaaler 1985 Bull. AMS 12, 183-216 (not opened); Carneiro-Vaaler, Trans. AMS 362 (2010) 5803-5843
items.quote_or_locator: Carneiro-Vaaler II, Section 1: 'In the special case f(x)=sgn(x), an explicit solution to this problem was found in the 1930s by A. Beurling, but his results were not published ... rediscovered by A. Selberg, who recognized its importance in connection with the large sieve inequality'; (1.1) 'G(x) <= f(x) <= H(x)'. Pointwise sign constraint with Fourier support in [-1,1]. (The PDF opened is Carneiro-Vaaler II, not Vaaler 1985.)
items.fit_T1_T7: Exact sign-constrained functions (T3-like), uniform (T2), but contain no prime input (T1 vacuous) and are extremal with positive loss integral (T4 fails); applications to the explicit formula (Carneiro-Chandee-Milinovich, bounds on S(t)) are CONDITIONAL on RH.

items.name: Turan power sum method
items.statement: For complex z_1..z_N with |z_1|=1 >= |z_n| (ordered decreasing) and s_nu = sum b_n z_n^nu, some nu in [M+1, M+N] satisfies |s_nu| >= 2 (N/(8e(M+N)))^N min_{1<=j<=N} |sum_{n<=j} b_n| (constant as in Wikipedia, Montgomery Ten Lectures not opened). Related: Montgomery's lower bound sqrt(n B) for max_{nu<=n^B}|sum z_k^nu| with |z_k|=1; Andersson shows inf max_{nu<=n^h} |sum z_k^nu| <= (h-1+o(1)) sqrt n, right order.
items.authors_year: P. Turan 1953 / book 1984; H. L. Montgomery 1994 (CBMS 84); J. Andersson 2007 (arXiv 0706.4131)
items.quote_or_locator: Wikipedia (article carries a 'lacks inline citations' tag): '|s_nu| >= 2 (N/(8e(M+N)))^N min_j |sum_{n=1}^j b_n|'; Andersson abstract (https://arxiv.org/abs/0706.4131): 'We prove that inf max_{v=1,...,n^h} |sum z_k^v| <= (h-1+o(1)) sqrt n'
items.fit_T1_T7: T2 pass (uniform in nodes); fails T1 (no prime input), T3 (lower bound on size of an exponential sum), T4.
items.relevance: Could force some shift nu to have a large exponential sum over nodes p^{it}, i.e. a size non-cancellation, not a sign; wrong direction for s_E<=0.
items.corrected_statement: Constant 2(N/(8e(M+N)))^N min_j|sum_{n<=j} b_n| belongs to Turan's SECOND theorem (hypothesis |z_n|<=1, ordered decreasing, |z_1|=1) - consistent with item. Turan's FIRST theorem (all |z_n|>=1) gives c(M,N)=(sum_{k=0}^{N-1} C(M+k,k)2^k)^-1 - not in item. Andersson arXiv 0706.4131 is 'On some power sum problems of Montgomery and Turan' (Katz's character sum estimate); his (h-1+o(1))sqrt n claim is only paraphrased in the abstract page I saw, and no journal ref listed. Montgomery's sqrt(nB) lower bound is NOT stated on the Wikipedia page; cited to Montgomery's Ten Lectures (CBMS 84, 1994) which I did not open: UNVERIFIED.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (Turan thm per Wikipedia; Montgomery bound UNVERIFIED)
items.check_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tur%C3%A1n%27s_method fetched: second theorem '|s_nu| >= 2(N/(8e(M+N)))^N min_j |sum_{n=1}^j b_n|'. https://arxiv.org/abs/0706.4131 abstract: 'We use an estimate for character sums over finite fields of Katz to solve open problems of Montgomery and Turan.'

items.name: Weil explicit-formula positivity criterion with Bochner's theorem
items.statement: Weil's quadratic functional Q(f) built from the explicit formula (prime sum with Lambda(n)/sqrt(n), archimedean Gamma term, pole) is positive semidefinite iff RH holds; on the zero side Q(f) = sum_rho g^((rho-1/2)/i) = 2 sum_{gamma>0} |f^(gamma)|^2 (RH). Bochner: a continuous normalized positive-definite function on a locally compact abelian group is the Fourier transform of a unique probability measure; this converts positivity of the prime-side distribution into positivity of a zero measure, hence circular.
items.authors_year: A. Weil 1952 (Comm. Sem. Math. Univ. Lund, Tome Supplementaire, 252-265); E. Bombieri 2000, Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. 11, 183-233; Bochner 1932-33
items.quote_or_locator: Bombieri abstract: the functional 'is positive semidefinite if and only if the Riemann Hypothesis is true' (as returned by page fetch). Bochner: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bochner%27s_theorem ('For any normalized continuous positive-definite function f: G -> C there exists a unique probability measure mu on G^ such that ...'). Zhu eq (7): 'Q(f) >= 0 for all admissible f if and only if RH holds [1]'
items.fit_T1_T7: Exact identity (T4) and uniform in windows (T2), but T1 and T7 fail: any positivity proved on the prime side equals RH (the circularity of the 65 attempts).
items.relevance: This is the identity <v,Kv> = sum F_v(z)^2 itself; Bochner-type reasoning only restates it.
items.corrected_statement: Weil 1952, Comm. Sem. Math. Univ. Lund, Tome Supplementaire, 252-265 (bibliography in Zhu and Suzuki); Bombieri, Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. 11 (2000), 183-233 (EuDML abstract). Weil's criterion: RH iff Q_W(v)>=0 for all v in C_c^infty. Bochner step and 'hence circular' are the item's own interpretation, not sourced from a theorem; circularity here means positivity is equivalent to RH, which is the stated criterion. Suzuki notes Weil did not state the criterion in terms of compactly supported smooth test functions.
items.check_evidence: Suzuki arXiv 2606.09096 intro (pdftotext): 'A fundamental result due to Weil [15] states that RH is equivalent to the condition that Q_W(v) >= 0 for all v in C_c^infty(R) ... (although Weil did not formulate the criterion in terms of compactly supported smooth test functions)'. Zhu abstract: 'Weil's criterion states that RH is equivalent to the non-negativity of an explicit quadratic form Q(f)'.

items.name: Yoshida (1992) and Bombieri (2000): Weil positivity on a small support
items.statement: The Weil quadratic functional is positive definite when the support of the test function is small enough; Zhu reports the classical range as supp f within [-(log 2)/2, (log 2)/2] (autocorrelation support log 2). Bombieri also proves the minimum on the unit ball of L^2 functions supported in [-t,t] is attained, and that if finitely many zeros are off-line the number of negative eigenvalues of large truncations is half their number.
items.authors_year: H. Yoshida 1992, On Hermitian forms attached to zeta functions, Adv. Stud. Pure Math. 21, 281-325; E. Bombieri 2000, Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. 11, 183-233
items.quote_or_locator: Bombieri (EuDML abstract): 're-proves Yoshida's theorem that the functional is positive definite when t is small'. Zhu abstract: 'Positivity on bounded support is classical for supp f in [-log2/2, log2/2] (Yoshida; Connes-Consani by a different method).' Window value reported via Zhu, not read in Yoshida (Project Euclid page returned HTML)
items.fit_T1_T7: Unconditional and zero-free (T1, T7 pass) with sign (T3), but only for a bounded window (fails T2) and mechanism not verified by me (T4, T5, T6 UNVERIFIED).
items.relevance: Existence proof that a prime-side sign argument can work on small windows; Yoshida's mechanism was not opened, so its dependence on Gamma factor versus prime comb is unknown to me.
items.corrected_statement: Yoshida 1992 (Adv. Stud. Pure Math. 21, 281-325) proved positivity for 2L <= log 2 per Zhu (supp f within [-log2/2, log2/2]); Bombieri 2000 reproves Yoshida's small-t theorem (EuDML abstract). Item's Bombieri extras (minimum attained; negative eigenvalues = half the number of off-line zeros) also match the EuDML abstract summary. Suzuki adds: Yoshida Lemma 2 gives positivity for sufficiently small a on K(a); Yoshida Prop. 1: positivity on odd functions implies RH, on even functions implies RH except possibly real zeros. Yoshida's own mechanism still not opened. Note Suzuki dates Bombieri '2001, 2003' while the Lincei volume is 2000 (Suzuki's [2] is a different Bombieri paper, probably Part II/lecture notes: not checked).
items.check_evidence: Zhu 2608.24827 intro: 'Yoshida [3] proved positivity for 2L <= log 2, and Connes-Consani [6] re-proved this range by trace-formula and von Neumann algebra methods'. https://eudml.org/doc/252338 via search: 're-proves Yoshida's theorem that the functional is positive definite when t is small'.

items.name: Connes-Consani: Weil positivity and trace formula, archimedean place
items.statement: A conceptual reason for positivity of the Weil functional in the semi-local trace formula: the root of the positivity is the trace of the scaling action compressed onto the orthogonal complement of the range of cutoff projections (cutoff parameter 1); the difference between the Weil distribution and the Sonin trace is expressed via prolate spheroidal wave functions and controlled by hermitian Toeplitz matrix theory. Exact window theorem statement not verified by me.
items.authors_year: A. Connes, C. Consani 2020 (arXiv 2006.13771), Selecta Math. (N.S.) 27 (2021), no. 4, Paper 77 (journal reference as in Zhu's bibliography)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract (arXiv API): 'The root of the positivity is the trace of the scaling action compressed onto the orthogonal complement of the range of the cutoff projections associated to the cutoff in phase space, for cutoff parameter equal to 1 ... All the ingredients and tools used above make sense in the general semi-local case, where Weil positivity implies RH.' Zhu cites it as positivity on a bounded support 'by a different method'
items.fit_T1_T7: Single archimedean place only (primes enter through the semi-local extension, not proved), so fails T5/T6 as a full tool; T7 pass.
items.relevance: Provides the prolate/Sonin-trace decomposition that explains why the archimedean part has a positive bulk, close to the PF structure found in the project; extension to the prime comb is open.
items.corrected_statement: arXiv 2006.13771 (submitted 24 Jun 2020, 57 pp, 17 figs); arXiv page lists no journal ref. Selecta Math. (N.S.) 27 (2021), no. 4, Paper No. 77 is taken from Zhu's bibliography [6] only, not from Springer: treat as secondary. Abstract paraphrase matches item (prolate spheroidal wave functions, Hermitian Toeplitz matrices, cutoff parameter 1 phrase NOT re-verified verbatim). IMPORTANT: Suzuki's 'Connes-Consani (2023)' [3] is a DIFFERENT paper: 'Spectral triples and zeta-cycles', Enseign. Math. 69 (2023), 93-148, so do not equate the two. Item's claim that primes enter only 'through the semi-local extension, not proved' is the item's reading.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (the paper's results; precise window theorem not verified)

Connes and C. Consani, Weil positivity and trace formula, the archimedean place, Selecta Math. (N.S.) 27 (2021), no. 4, Paper No. 77'; Suzuki ref [3]: 'Spectral triples and zeta-cycles, Enseign. items.name: Suzuki: Weil's quadratic form via the screw function
items.statement: Operator-theoretic framework (screw function, de Branges spaces) unifying Weil-form results of Yoshida (1992), Bombieri (2001, 2003), Connes-Consani (2023) and Connes-Consani-Moscovici (2025+); Theorem 1.3: lowest eigenvalue lambda_a on [-a,a] is continuous in a without assuming RH; Theorem 1.4: for sufficiently small a>0 the lowest eigenvalue is positive, simple, and its eigenfunction is even; a conjecture that a self-adjoint operator with eigenvalues the imaginary parts of the zeros arises as the limit a -> infinity.
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: 'All these results are obtained without assuming the Riemann Hypothesis.' Theorem 1.4 (text of PDF): 'For sufficiently small a > 0, the lowest eigenvalue lambda_a is positive, simple, ... Furthermore, the corresponding eigenfunction is even.' No numeric window stated in the abstract or in Theorem 1.4; the task's claim of an explicit unconditional window for Suzuki is UNVERIFIED
items.fit_T1_T7: T1, T7 pass; positivity only for small a (fails T2); no treatment of the comb correlations (T5) or the rank-one pole (T6) beyond the framework.
items.relevance: Supplies the simple-even-ground-state structure for small windows, parallel to the project's s_E / s_O split; does not extend the window.
items.corrected_statement: Abstract, Thm 1.3 and Thm 1.4 verified in the PDF text (arXiv 2606.09096v3, 23 Sep 2026; v1 8 Jun 2026; 33 pp; single author; NOT refereed, no journal ref). Thm 1.3: 'The lowest eigenvalue lambda_a is continuous in a.' Thm 1.4: 'For sufficiently small a > 0, the lowest eigenvalue lambda_a is positive, simple, and satisfies lambda_a = log(1/a) + mu_1 - log(2 pi) + psi(2) - 1 + O(a) as a->0+ for some mu_1>0. Furthermore the eigenfunction is even.' So Thm 1.4 does give an ASYMPTOTIC (not a numeric window) - item says 'no numeric window' which is right, but it omits the explicit asymptotic formula. Positivity of lambda_a for small a is Yoshida [17, Lemma 2]; the new content is simplicity/evenness and continuity without RH. The abstract's 'All these results are obtained without assuming RH' is verbatim. Suzuki's 'Connes-Consani (2023)' and 'CCM (2025+)' refer to [3] Enseign. Math. 69 and [4] arXiv 2511.22755.
items.check_evidence: pdftotext of https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.09096: 'Theorem 1.3. The lowest eigenvalue lambda_a is continuous in a.' ; 'Theorem 1.4. For sufficiently small a > 0, the lowest eigenvalue lambda_a is positive, simple, and satisfies lambda_a = log 1/a + mu_1 - log(2 pi) + psi(2) - 1 + O(a) ... Furthermore, the corresponding eigenfunction is [even]'.

items.name: Zhu: certified Weil positivity on [-0.8,0.8]
items.statement: Theorem 1.2: for every real even f in L^2 with supp f within [-0.8,0.8], Q(f) >= 8.9e-18 ||f||_2^2 (autocorrelation support 1.6, 2.3 times the classical range); extended to complex test functions via an odd-sector certificate (Q >= 8.2e-15 for real odd f); window ground state simple and even. Geometric side: Q(f) = 2F(i/2)^2 + (1/2pi) integral |F(t)|^2 Psi_L(t) dt with Psi_L(t) = Re psi(1/4+it/2) - log pi - sum_{log n<2L} 2Lambda(n)/sqrt(n) cos(t log n), a rank-one pole plus a frequency multiplier. Certified upper bounds: lambda*(0.8) <= 2.27e-17, ~1e-48 at L=1.2, 3.2e-283 at L=2 (scaling law (5) is fitted, not proved).
items.authors_year: Xuefeng Zhu 2026 (arXiv 2608.24827 v2, 2 Sep 2026; single-author preprint, not refereed to my knowledge; computation not rerun by me; v1's support-2.38 claim retracted in v2, Remark 3.3 and Section 7)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: 'We prove, by certified computation, that Q(f) >= 8.9 x 10^-18 ||f||_2^2 for all supp f within [-0.8, 0.8], that is, for autocorrelation support 1.6, which is 2.3 times the classical range.' Synthesis: 'Passing the resulting wall thus requires cancellation in the prime comb, a concrete arithmetic problem.' (verified verbatim in the PDF text)
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 (geometric side only), T3 (certified sign), T4 (exact reduction to one finite PSD matrix with coupling to the tail ~1e-100), T6 (pole separated, odd-sector sign reversal), T7 pass. Fails T2 (one window by computation; cost doubly exponential in L), T5 (comb bounded pointwise, no cancellation).
items.relevance: Existing template for how s_E, s_O-type margins are certified and how they collapse (L=1.0 eigenvalue 5.88e-30, same order as the project's 1e-29, normalization match UNVERIFIED); shows pointwise methods stall near support ~3.2.
items.corrected_statement: All quoted numbers verified in the PDF text of arXiv 2608.24827v2 (2 Sep 2026; v1 25 Aug 2026 was a 9-page announcement; single author at Dalian University of Technology; no journal ref, i.e. unrefereed): Thm 1.2 'For every real even f in L^2 with supp f within [-0.8,0.8], Q(f) >= 8.9e-18 ||f||_2^2'; odd sector Q >= 8.2e-15 (Section 6, Cor 6.3 complex f); 8.9e-18 <= lambda*(0.8) <= 2.27e-17; 3.2e-283 at L=2; L=1.0 table entry 5.88e-30 (first eigenvalue column; sector labelling of that column not checked); v1's support-2.38 claim retracted ('We retract the claim', Remark 3.3). Two refinements: (1) the paper itself says 'Claims beyond log 2 exist in unrefereed preprints' - so 'classical range' is the Yoshida range 2L<=log 2; (2) under RH it proves lambda*(L) <= exp(-L e^L) for large L, and the scaling law (5) is 'fitted, not derived' (confirmed). Computation not rerun by me - certified status = author's claim.

items.name: Prime-comb barrier: Q-independence of log p, Weyl equidistribution (Zhu Lemma 3.2, Theorem 1.4, Remark 1.6)
items.statement: Lemma 3.2: for the prime comb P_L(t) = sum_{log n<2L} 2Lambda(n)/sqrt(n) cos(t log n), sup_t P_L(t) = A_L = sum_{log n<2L} 2Lambda(n)/sqrt(n), because {log p} are linearly independent over Q by unique factorization, so (t log p) equidistributes on the torus. Theorem 1.4: any certificate of one-stroke type needs frequencies up to T_1(L) = 2 pi e^{A_L}, A_L = (4+o(1)) e^L, doubly exponential in L; no pointwise bound on the comb lowers it. Remark 1.6 (open): beating it requires proving the phases (t log p)_p cannot align, an arithmetic statement about simultaneous Diophantine approximation of {log p}.
items.quote_or_locator: Lemma 3.2 proof: 'The numbers {log p}_p are linearly independent over Q by unique factorization, so the phases (t log p_1, ..., t log p_r) equidistribute mod 2 pi on the full torus.' Remark 1.6: 'To improve on pointwise envelopes one must prove that the phases (t log p)_p cannot align, an arithmetic statement about simultaneous Diophantine approximation of {log p}, of the same nature as the information carried by the zeros themselves.' Remark 1.5 (measured, not proved): margin collapses at the Landau-Widom rate
items.fit_T1_T7: Identifies precisely why T5 (cancellation/correlation between primes) is the missing ingredient; the barrier itself is unconditional (Theorem 1.4) but its optimality claim is only for pointwise-envelope methods; Remark 1.5 scaling is empirical.
items.relevance: Names the open lemma that could supply the sign: a quantitative, Z-specific non-alignment of (t log p) (generic real sequences with Q-independent logs also equidistribute, and Beurling systems with RH false exist, so Weyl-type qualitative statements are not enough). Statement NO for Beurling: Q-independence of the generalized primes can fail, UNVERIFIED.
items.corrected_statement: Lemma 3.2, Thm 1.4 (T_1(L)=2 pi e^{A_L}, A_L=(4+o(1))e^L) and Remark 1.6 are verified verbatim. Correction on scope: the barrier is for certificates that bound the comb POINTWISE (Thm 1.4 says 'within the class of certificates that bound the comb pointwise the threshold T_1 cannot be lowered'); it is not a general barrier for the positivity route. Lemma 3.2 proof says sup P_L = A_L is 'approached at arbitrarily large t' (a supremum, attained at t=0 trivially and approached again by Weyl); 'Remark 1.6' also states A_L attained only in the limit for the last sign change. Item's gloss 'generic real sequences with Q-independent logs also equidistribute, so Weyl-type qualitative statements are not enough' is the item's own commentary. Item's 'holds_for_beurling_primes NO' is the item's own UNVERIFIED guess, not from Zhu.
items.check_evidence: pdftotext 2608.24827: 'Lemma 3.2 (Optimality of the crude constant) ... sup_t P_L(t) = A_L'; 'The numbers {log p}_p are linearly independent over Q by unique factorization, so the phases (t log p_1,...,t log p_r) equidistribute mod 2 pi on the full torus.'; 'To improve on pointwise envelopes one must prove that the phases (t log p)_p cannot align, an arithmetic statement about simultaneous Diophantine approximation of {log p}'.

items.name: Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer Beurling system (and RH-true Beurling systems)
items.statement: There are Beurling generalized number systems with N(x) = rho x + O(x^theta) (1/2<theta<1) whose prime counting function has pi(x) = Li(x) + Omega_{+-}(x exp(-c sqrt(log x))), whose zeta function realizes the de la Vallee Poussin zero-free region and for which RH fails. Conversely Zhang showed Beurling systems with both RH and (1.1) exist, and Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas built one with RH and extremal oscillation of the integer counting function.
items.authors_year: H. G. Diamond, H. L. Montgomery, U. M. A. Vorhauer 2006, Math. Ann. 334, 1-36; W.-B. Zhang 2007, Math. Ann. 337, 671-704; F. Broucke, G. Debruyne, J. Vindas (arXiv 2004.11501)
items.quote_or_locator: BDV introduction: 'Their Beurling number system has the additional feature that its associated zeta function ... also realizes the classical de la Vallee Poussin zero-free region; in particular, the Riemann hypothesis (RH) fails for it.' and 'The number system constructed by Diamond, Montgomery, and Vorhauer also provides the valuable information that a zeta function might not have a wider zero-free region than that of de la Vallee Poussin if we only require that Beurling's property that the integers have multiplicative structure and (1.1) hold.' (DMV original page was not fetchable, 403)
items.fit_T1_T7: Defines T7's real content: a proof must use more than Euler product plus regular density. Caveat: Beurling systems lack the archimedean Gamma factor and functional equation, so there is no canonical Beurling analogue of K; the barrier applies to arguments that use only the axioms Euler product + PNT-type density.
items.relevance: Any argument using only prime-like axioms (unique factorization, Lambda=mu*log, PNT-strength density) cannot prove window positivity for the true K, since counterexample systems with the same axioms violate RH.
items.corrected_statement: DMV: Math. Ann. 334 (2006), 1-36, DOI 10.1007/s00208-005-0638-2, 'Beurling primes with large oscillation'. Abstract (search summary of Springer abstract): N_B(x)=kappa x+O(x^theta), kappa>0, 1/2<theta<1, pi_B(x)=li(x)+Omega(x exp(-c sqrt(log x))) [Omega, not necessarily Omega_pm in the Springer abstract; Omega_pm used by BDV]; zeta_B has infinitely many zeros on the curve sigma=1-a/log t, t>=2, none to the right, a>(4/e)(1-theta). Item writes N(x)=rho x (kappa in abstract; cosmetic). Zhang: Math. Ann. 337 (2007), 671-704, 'Beurling primes with RH and Beurling primes with large oscillation' (confirmed). BDV: arXiv 2004.11501 'Beurling integers with RH and large oscillation' (confirmed title; journal not checked). The item's caveat (no Gamma factor/functional equation in Beurling systems, so no direct analogue of K) is the item's own and correct in spirit.
