items.name: Davenport-Heilbronn / Titchmarsh function: functional equation without Euler product
items.statement: A linear combination of two Dirichlet L-functions for complex-conjugate characters mod 5 satisfies a Riemann-type functional equation but has no Euler product; it was suspected (Potter-Titchmarsh 1934) and later numerically found (Spira) to have zeros off the critical line. The rigorous status of the off-line zeros (Davenport-Heilbronn 1936 theorem on zeros in sigma>1 for related Epstein/Hurwitz functions; Bombieri-Ghosh 2011) was NOT opened and is UNVERIFIED here; one 2016 opinion paper contests the Spira/Titchmarsh zeros.
items.authors_year: Potter-Titchmarsh 1934; Spira (numerics); Bombieri-Ghosh 2011 (Russian Math. Surveys 66:2, 221-270); Ferry-Ghisa-Muscutar 2016 (contested opinion)
items.quote_or_locator: Ferry-Ghisa-Muscutar intro (uncontested history only): 'In 1934 Potter and Titchmarsh ... have shown that a certain linear combination of two Dirichlet L-functions ... satisfies a Riemann-type of functional equation. Since the corresponding Dirichlet series cannot be represented as an Euler product, they suspected that this function might have off critical line non trivial zeros.' Bombieri-Ghosh abstract only: 'analytic properties of certain Dirichlet series considered by Davenport and Heilbronn' (https://geodesic.mathdoc.fr/item/RM_2011_66_2_a1)
items.fit_T1_T7: Shows (if the off-line zeros are rigorous) that the Gamma factor and a functional equation without the Euler product do not give RH, so unique factorization is load-bearing for any proof; fails as a tool (no positive statement).
items.relevance: Supports the requirement that the sign must come from the multiplicative (prime) side, not from the archimedean term alone; the rigorous off-line zero statement still has to be sourced.
items.corrected_statement: Search yields: the Davenport-Heilbronn function has a Riemann-type functional equation, no Euler product, and infinitely many zeros off the critical line plus infinitely many zeros in the half-plane of absolute convergence (Re s>1) per Davenport-Heilbronn 1936 and Bombieri-Ghosh (their Theorem 7, cited secondhand). Spira's off-line zeros are widely cited; a 2016 note (Ferry et al.) and a 2025 preprint contest the numerics. I did not open Davenport-Heilbronn 1936 or Bombieri-Ghosh (Russian Math. Surveys 66:2 (2011), 221-270). The rigorous off-line zeros statement therefore stays UNVERIFIED, as the item says. Do not quote Ferry-Ghisa-Muscutar as an authority.
items.check_evidence: Search summaries only: arXiv 1506.05716 'On the density of zeros of linear combinations of Euler products for sigma>1' and 1602.06328; no primary text opened.

items.name: Littlewood: pi(x) - li(x) changes sign infinitely often (and why it is not a prime-side sign)
items.statement: pi(x) - li(x) takes both positive and negative values without bound (Littlewood 1914; full proof Hardy-Littlewood 1918; first crossing not located, Skewes-type bounds). The proof is a case split on RH: if RH is false the argument is much simpler.
items.authors_year: J. E. Littlewood 1914; S. Skewes 1933 (under RH), 1955 (unconditional)
items.quote_or_locator: Wikipedia: Littlewood 'had proved ... that there is such a number (and so, a first such number)'; proof uses 'Dirichlet's approximation theorem to show that sometimes many terms have about the same argument'; 'In the event that the Riemann hypothesis is false, the argument is much simpler.' (secondary source; original not opened)
items.fit_T1_T7: A genuine unconditional sign statement about primes but proved through zeros of zeta (fails T1 in its proof), concerns a single function not a window family (fails T2), and is an existence of alignment of phases, the opposite of the non-alignment needed here.
items.relevance: Illustrates the same Dirichlet-approximation phase alignment that appears in Zhu Lemma 3.2: sign changes of prime-count errors come from aligned phases of zeros, so a sign proof for K needs the dual non-alignment.
items.corrected_statement: Confirmed (Wikipedia): Littlewood (1914) showed the sign changes infinitely often, without exhibiting a crossing; Skewes 1933 gave bound under RH (~e^e^e^79), Skewes 1955 unconditional (~e^e^e^e^7.705). The item's attribution 'full proof Hardy-Littlewood 1918' and the RH case split ('if RH is false the argument is much simpler') were NOT re-verified in this pass (the fetched Wikipedia text did not show the case-split sentence); keep UNVERIFIED. Also the item's classification of this theorem as a 'prime-side sign' needs care: it is PROVEN unconditionally (case split on RH) but via zeros of zeta. Missing modern refinements: Bays-Hudson, Saouter-Demichel, Platt-Trudgian (crossing below ~1.4e316) - не проверено.
items.check_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skewes%27s_number fetched: 'Littlewood's proof did not, however, exhibit a concrete such number x'; 'assuming that the Riemann hypothesis is true' (Skewes 1933); 'Without assuming the Riemann hypothesis, Skewes (1955)'.

items.name: Connes-Consani-Moscovici zeta spectral triples and Connes-van Suijlekom quadratic forms
items.statement: Self-adjoint operators obtained as rank-one perturbations of the spectral triple of the scaling operator on [1/lambda, lambda] using only Euler products over primes p <= x = lambda^2, with spectra numerically matching low zeros of zeta; 'A rigorous proof of this convergence would establish the Riemann Hypothesis.' Connes-van Suijlekom: if a lower-bounded quadratic form with kernel D(x-y) has a simple, isolated lowest eigenvalue with even eigenfunction xi, then all zeros of xi^ are real (Caratheodory-Fejer for Toeplitz matrices plus Hurwitz).
items.authors_year: A. Connes, C. Consani, H. Moscovici 2025 (arXiv 2511.22755); A. Connes, W. D. van Suijlekom 2025 (arXiv 2511.23257, Commun. Math. Phys. 2025 per CCM abstract)
items.quote_or_locator: CCM abstract: 'The construction only involves the Euler products over the primes p <= x = lambda^2 ... A rigorous proof of this convergence would establish the Riemann Hypothesis.' CvS abstract: 'whose lowest spectral value lambda is a simple, isolated eigenvalue with even eigenfunction xi, then all the zeros of the entire function xi^(z) ... lie on the real line.'
items.fit_T1_T7: CvS reality theorem is PROVEN but is conditional on the spectral hypothesis (simple even ground state at finite scale); CCM convergence is a program. T1 pass; T2 requires infinitely many scales; T5/T6 not addressed.
items.relevance: Supplies the Perron-Frobenius-style simple even ground state hypothesis that Zhu certifies at lambda=e^0.8; the sign of the window form still needs the open non-alignment input.
items.corrected_statement: CCM: arXiv 2511.22755, 'Zeta Spectral Triples', submitted 27 Nov 2025; comments: 'to appear in EMS series Lectures Notes in Mathematics'; abstract: 'A rigorous proof of this convergence would establish the Riemann Hypothesis' (paraphrase on page; the sentence in the item matches the summary). Their self-adjointness rests on an extension of the Caratheodory-Fejer theorem. CvS: arXiv 2511.23257 'Quadratic Forms, Real Zeros and Echoes of the Spectral Action' (math.OA), submitted 28 Nov 2025; the arXiv page lists no journal ref, but alainconnes.org's publication list (via search, page not opened) gives Commun. Math. Phys. vol. 406, 2026, article 312. So the item's 'Commun. Math. Phys. 2025 per CCM abstract' is wrong on both counts: the CCM abstract does not state it, and the year is 2026 (vol 406). CvS statement verified: lower-bounded form with kernel D(x-y), lowest eigenvalue simple, isolated, even eigenfunction xi => all zeros of Fourier transform of xi are real (Caratheodory-Fejer + Hurwitz). 'Isolated' appears in the item's quoted abstract; the arXiv-page summary I saw says 'simple, isolated'.
items.corrected_status: CvS reality theorem PROVEN (conditional on spectral hypothesis); CCM convergence CONJECTURE
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.22755; https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.23257; https://alainconnes.org/?p=73 (search snippet: CMP vol 406, 2026, 312).

missing: Chebyshev/Mertens and de la Vallee Poussin / Hadamard PNT (1896) with zero-free region and Vinogradov-Korobov improvement (zero-free region sigma>1-c/(log t)^{2/3}(loglog t)^{1/3}): the domain's classical analytic positivity base (positive-definite trig polynomial 3+4cos+cos2 is covered, but the quantitative region is not).

Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem (1965) and Elliott-Halberstam conjecture: referenced in the Maynard item but never listed; also Goldston-Pintz-Yildirim (2005/2009), Zhang (2014, Annals 179), Polymath8b (2014): the sieve+positivity chain to bounded gaps.

Large sieve inequality (Linnik 1941; Renyi; Bombieri 1965; Montgomery-Vaughan 1973-74 sharp form N+Q^2): positivity via duality with Hilbert-type inequalities; Montgomery-Vaughan's sharp large sieve constant is the same line as item 'Hilbert inequality' and should be a separate entry.
Montgomery pair correlation (1973) and Rudnick-Sarnak/Katz-Sarnak: positivity of the Fejer-type kernel gives lower bounds for simple zeros / pair-correlation; direct 'positivity tool in ANT'.
Brun sieve (1919), Selberg sieve upper bound, Rosser-Iwaniec, Friedlander-Iwaniec asymptotic sieve with parity-breaking (Annals 1998/2010 'Opera de Cribro'); only parity problem is listed.
Matomaki-Radziwill (2016, Annals) multiplicative functions in short intervals and Matomaki-Radziwill-Tao correlations: the main modern positivity-free mean-value tools beyond Halasz.
Chowla and Elliott conjectures (Chowla 1965); Tao-Teravainen odd-order logarithmic Chowla (2019/2021); Pretentious framework (Granville-Soundararajan book) beyond the single 3-4-1 inequality.

Newman conjecture / de Bruijn-Newman constant: Rodgers-Tao 2018 (Lambda >= 0, Forum Math Pi 2020) and Polymath15 (Lambda <= 0.2): positivity tools directly tied to RH (not verified here, не проверено).
Li's criterion (1997), Nyman-Beurling-Baez-Duarte criterion, Lagarias/Bombieri-Lagarias (1999) Li-type positivity: RH_EQUIVALENT positivity criteria that complement Weil's.

de Branges positivity / Hilbert spaces of entire functions; Connes' 1999 trace formula (Selecta 5, 29-106); Connes-Moscovici prolate (PNAS 119 (2022) e2123174119): referenced only through Zhu's bibliography.
Siegel-Walfisz, Linnik's theorem (and Heath-Brown 1992 exponent 5.5, Xylouris 5), Siegel zero / Landau-Page: positivity of Dirichlet convolution 1*chi used to exclude real zeros.

Positivity of coefficients of 1 + chi_0 + ... (Dirichlet's convolution trick): Landau-type theorem on Dirichlet series with non-negative coefficients (Landau 1905): fundamental sign-based tool, absent.

Beurling's generalized-prime PNT theory (Beurling 1937, Diamond-Zhang book 'Beurling Generalized Numbers', AMS 2016) and Zhang's PNT conditions: the item set cites counterexamples but not the positive Beurling PNT.

merged.title: Barriers and analogues: what prime-like axioms can and cannot prove
merged.summary: No item satisfies T1-T7. The domain splits into two parts. (A) Barriers: Euler product plus a PNT with a regular N(x) (DMV 2006), RH-strength prime regularity obtained by pure random selection (Zhang 2007; Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas 2020; Broucke-Vindas 2024: |pi_P-F|<=2), and an uncertainty principle max(alpha,beta,gamma)>=1/2 (Hilberdink-Neamah 2020) show that no argument using only 'Euler product + counting-function size/regularity' can give K>=0. Davenport-Heilbronn (1936), Saias-Weingartner 2009, Righetti 2015: a functional equation of Riemann type + Dirichlet series without Euler product gives zeros with Re s>1; the mechanism is Bohr equivalence = free twisting of the phases of primes (log p linearly independent over Q), the same fact that drives Voronin universality in 1/2<Re s<1. Pólya and Mertens (natural sign/size statements on prime sums) are false, so an 'easy' sign statement does not exist. (B) Analogues: only the function-field world has a proven SIGN, and it comes from effectivity (nonnegative integer intersection numbers on C x C: Hodge index/Castelnuovo-Severi-Weil, Weil positivity Tr(Z*Z')>=2d'(Z)>=0 after Riemann-Roch makes Z effective), or from Landau-Rankin positivity of log-coefficients with tensor powers (Deligne), or from Stepanov-Bombieri upper bound + Galois-cover lower bound + amplification over all constant-field extensions (needs finitely many Frobenius eigenvalues). All three need objects absent over Z (surface C x C, Frobenius flow, rational zeta); van Frankenhuijsen: 'spec Z x spec Z = spec Z is one-dimensional'. Best candidate for a SIGN mechanism to imitate (not to cite): Weil effectivity positivity, i.e. writing the quadratic form as (explicit positive term) + (sum of nonnegative integer-valued terms), matching rule 18 (m = B0 + sum C_n, C_n >= 0). Most useful negative lesson: whatever proves s_E<=0, s_O>=0 must use the functional equation AND Euler product jointly AND some arithmetic property not shared by random Beurling primes; it must be sensitive to correlations among primes (Maier, Cramér failure). Gaps: DMV paper itself not opened (HTTP 403), its content taken from Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas intro; Bombieri-Hejhal, Kaczorowski-Perelli (Annals 2011) taken from secondary text; Titchmarsh section 10.25, Diamond-Zhang book, Weil 1948 book, Granville 1995 not opened. Whether a Beurling system with BOTH an Euler product and a Gamma-type functional equation (Hilberdink-Lapidus Thm 3.2 style) can have zeros off the line is not settled in anything I opened (HL: 'We do not give a complete answer to the latter difficult question'); I found no such counterexample, absence of evidence only. Dropped as unreliable: arXiv 1602.06328 (Ferry-Ghisa-Muscutar) and arXiv 2010.03521 (Liu-Wu), both fringe claims about the Davenport-Heilbronn zeros.

items.name: Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer: Beurling system with regular integers, PNT, but RH false
items.statement: For every theta in (1/2,1) there exists a Beurling generalized number system with N(x)=rho*x+O(x^theta) (rho>0) whose primes satisfy pi(x)=Li(x)+Omega_{+-}(x*exp(-c*sqrt(log x))) for some c>0; its zeta function realizes only the classical de la Vallee Poussin zero-free region, so RH fails for it (the PNT itself holds, with the de la Vallee Poussin error). Construction: probabilistic (random prime selection) combined with classical analytic number theory.
items.authors_year: H. G. Diamond, H. L. Montgomery, U. M. A. Vorhauer, Math. Ann. 334 (2006) 1-36, DOI 10.1007/s00208-005-0638-2
items.source_url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.11501 (statement as recalled in the intro of Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas; paper record: https://deepblue.lib.umich.edu/items/80a3d22b-2022-435e-9bcb-360f281fb998)
items.quote_or_locator: BDV 2020, Sect. 1: "also realizes the classical de la Vallée Poussin zero-free region; in particular, the Riemann hypothesis (RH) fails for it." The DMV paper itself was NOT opened (HTTP 403); 'zeros near a curve just inside Re s=1' is from a search-tool summary of the abstract, not verified verbatim.
items.fit_T1_T7: Not a tool but the central barrier. A Beurling system satisfies the Euler product and has N(x)=rho*x+O(x^theta); any property true for all such systems cannot imply RH. Separating property (inference, not verified in a source): exact integrality/arithmetic of the integers and the functional equation with Gamma factor, neither of which the DMV system is known to have. Fails T7 for any tool based only on Euler product + regular N.
items.relevance: Shows that a sign for <v,Kv> cannot come from the Euler product plus a size/regularity hypothesis on N(x). Any proof must inject something Z-specific (functional equation with the archimedean Gamma term, integrality) in the very same quadratic form.
items.corrected_statement: Statement matches the secondary source. Primary DMV text still not opened (deepblue PDF returned 403). Title of the paper is 'Beurling primes with large oscillation', Math. Ann. 334 (2006) 1-36, DOI 10.1007/s00208-005-0638-2. The 'zeros near a curve' remark stays unverified.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (verified via BDV 2020 intro, not via DMV itself)
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.11501 Sect. 1 (read locally): 'given 1/2 < theta < 1, they showed the existence of Beurling numbers with integer counting function N satisfying N(x)=rho x+O(x^theta) ... whose primes realize the de la Vallee Poussin error term ... pi(x)=Li(x)+Omega_pm(x exp(-c sqrt(log x)))'; 'its associated zeta function ... also realizes the classical de la Vallee Poussin zero-free region; in particular, the Riemann hypothesis (RH) fails for it.' Reference [10] in the same paper gives Math. Ann. 334 (2006), 1-36. Search snippet (deepblue abstract, https://deepblue.lib.umich.edu/items/80a3d22b-2022-435e-9bcb-360f281fb998): N has error x^theta with 1/2<theta<1, prime oscillation 'of the de la Vallee Poussin size'.

items.name: Beurling 1937 PNT and its sharpness; Landau / Malliavin / Hilberdink-Lapidus transfer theorems
items.statement: (i) Beurling 1937: N(x)=ax+O(x/(log x)^gamma) with gamma>3/2 implies pi(x)~x/log x; false in general for gamma=3/2 (Beurling's example; sharp by Diamond 1970). (ii) Landau (abstract PNT, Beurling form): N(x)=rho*x+O(x^theta), theta<1, implies pi(x)=Li(x)+O(x*exp(-c*sqrt(log x))), optimal by DMV. (iii) Hilberdink-Lapidus (improving Malliavin): pi(x)=Li(x)+O(x^theta), 0<theta<1, implies N(x)=rho*x+O(x*exp(-c*sqrt(log x*log log x))) with c=min{sqrt(1-theta)/4, sqrt(2)/8}, optimal up to c by Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas.
items.authors_year: A. Beurling 1937; H. G. Diamond 1970 (sharpness); E. Landau 1911; P. Malliavin 1961; T. W. Hilberdink and M. L. Lapidus, Acta Appl. Math. 2006
items.quote_or_locator: Hilberdink-Lapidus Sect. 1.2: "Beurling ([4], 1937) showed that N(x)=ax+O(x/(log x)^gamma) for some gamma>3/2 implies pi(x) ~ x/log x ... he showed by example that this is false in general for gamma=3/2". BDV Thm 1.2 (= HL result) and the lines after it for the constant c.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 yes (prime-side data), T2 yes, T3 no (size), T4 no (loses constants, lossy), T5 no, T6 no, T7 yes (proven). These are theorems ABOUT Beurling systems, so they cannot prove RH for Z by themselves.
items.relevance: Defines the Beurling-level dictionary 'regularity of N <-> regularity of pi' with exactly known losses; zeros enter only through analytic continuation of zeta_P. It marks the region where size information is exhausted without arithmetic.
items.corrected_statement: (i) Beurling 1937 gamma>3/2 and the counterexample at gamma=3/2 are Beurling's own (HL says 'he showed by example that this is false in general for gamma = 3/2'); the item's attribution of sharpness to 'Diamond 1970' is NOT supported (HL cites Diamond only for the converse direction pi=x/log x+O(x/(log x)^(1+delta)) => N~ax, and as Diamond (1977, J. reine angew. Math. 295) in HL's list; Diamond 1970 is Illinois J. Math. 14). (ii) Landau's abstract PNT is Math. Ann. 56 (1903) 645-670 per HL, not 1911; BDV's wording is 'N(x)=rho x+O(x^theta) always implies pi(x)=Li(x)+O(x exp(-c sqrt(log x)))'; optimality shown by DMV. (iii) HL result confirmed with c=min{sqrt(1-theta)/4, sqrt(2)/8}; BDV Appendix A further improves it to any c<min{sqrt(2(1-theta)),1} (using Balazard's technique), so the item's c is not the strongest known. In HL's arXiv text the theorem is stated for psi(x)=x+O(x^alpha) (their Thm 2.2); BDV restate it for pi (their Thm 1.2). Journal: Acta Appl. Math. 94 (2006) 21-48.
items.check_evidence: HL arXiv math/0410270 Sect. 1 (read locally): 'Beurling ([4], 1937) showed that N(x)=ax+O(x/(log x)^gamma) for some gamma>3/2 implies pi(x) ~ x/log x ... Furthermore, he showed by example that this is false in general for gamma=3/2.'; 'Landau ([23], 1903) proved that N(x)=ax+O(x^theta) for some theta<1 implies pi(x)=li(x)+O(x e^{-c sqrt(log x)})'; reference list: '[23] E. Landau, Neuer Beweis des Primzahlsatzes und Beweis des Primidealsatzes, Math. Ann. 56 (1903), 645-670'. BDV arXiv 2004.11501 Thm 1.2 and following lines: 'Hilberdink and Lapidus have actually proved that (1.7) holds with the constant c=min{sqrt(1-theta)/4, sqrt(2)/8}'; 'one might improve this value to any c<min{sqrt(2(1-theta)),1} ... Appendix A'. Journal data: search result https://centaur.reading.ac.uk/5075 lists 'Acta Applicandae Mathematicae, 94 (1). pp. 21-48'.

items.name: Zhang: Beurling systems satisfying RH together with regular integers
items.statement: There exist Beurling generalized number systems whose zeta function continues to Re s>1/2 (except the simple pole at 1) with no zeros there (RH holds), with psi_P(x)=x+O_eps(x^{1/2+eps}) and N_P(x)=a*x+O_eps(x^{1/2+eps}) for every eps>0; Zhang also gives a system with the same N-regularity realizing exactly the classical zero-free region (de la Vallee Poussin error).
items.authors_year: W.-B. Zhang, 'Beurling primes with RH and Beurling primes with large oscillation', Math. Ann. 337 (2007) 671-704
items.quote_or_locator: Broucke-Debruyne-Revesz, Sect. 1: "The first unconditional example of a well-behaved system was established by Zhang [17], who used this probabilistic method to show the existence of a system satisfying psi_P(x)=x+O_eps(x^{1/2+eps}) and N_P(x)=ax+O_eps(x^{1/2+eps})". Also BDV 2004.11501 Sect. 1: "Zhang complemented these results by showing that there are also Beurling number systems for which, in contrast, the RH and the asymptotic estimate (1.1) both hold." Zhang's paper itself not opened.
items.fit_T1_T7: Counter-evidence to the idea that 'RH-type regularity of primes' is special to Z: it is realized by random primes with no arithmetic. Fails T5 (random primes are independent) and T7 for Z.
items.relevance: RH-true is not a distinguishing property of the integers; a Beurling system with RH exists. So the sign of <v,Kv> cannot follow from the Euler product + Dirichlet-series axioms alone; but note these systems have no known functional equation, hence no Gamma term and no analogue of K (inference).
items.corrected_statement: Existence of a Zhang system with RH and regular integers is confirmed (Math. Ann. 337 (2007) 671-704). Two sources differ on the prime error term of Zhang's example: BDR quote psi_P(x)=x+O_eps(x^{1/2+eps}), N_P(x)=a x+O_eps(x^{1/2+eps}); BDV say Zhang's example satisfies (1.4), i.e. pi(x)=Li(x)+O(sqrt x). Use the BDR form (the eps-weaker one) until Zhang is opened. The second claim (a Zhang system with exactly the classical zero-free region and same N-regularity) is only supported by the paper's title and a search summary, not by a quote.
items.check_evidence: BDR arXiv 2309.01567 Intro (read locally): 'The first unconditional example of a well-behaved system was established by Zhang [17], who used this probabilistic method to show the existence of a system satisfying psi_P(x)=x+O_eps(x^{1/2+eps}) and N_P(x)=ax+O_eps(x^{1/2+eps}) for all eps>0.' Reference [17]: 'W.-B. Zhang, Beurling primes with RH and Beurling primes with large oscillation, Math. Ann. 337 (2007), no. 3, 671-704.' BDV 2004.11501: 'Zhang complemented these results by showing that there are also Beurling number systems for which, in contrast, the RH and the asymptotic estimate (1.1) both hold.'

items.name: Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas: Beurling system with RH and maximally oscillating integers
items.statement: There is a Beurling system with pi(x)=Li(x)+O(sqrt(x)) (so RH holds: zeta_P extends to Re s>1/2 with only the pole at 1, no zeros) and, for every constant c>2*sqrt(2), N(x)=rho*x+Omega_{+-}( sqrt(x)*exp(-c*sqrt(log x*log log x)) ), rho>0 the density. This shows optimality (up to c) of the Hilberdink-Lapidus transfer theorem.
items.authors_year: F. Broucke, G. Debruyne, J. Vindas, Adv. Math. 370 (2020) 107240, arXiv 2004.11501
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract (opened via local PDF): "We construct a Beurling generalized number system satisfying the Riemann hypothesis and whose integer counting function displays extremal oscillation"; Theorem 1.1, eqs (1.4)-(1.5).
items.fit_T1_T7: Barrier. Shows that RH for the primes does not force any regularity of the integers beyond the Hilberdink-Lapidus bound; method: Bohr's extremal example for the convexity bound + saddle point + DMV random approximation.
items.relevance: A Beurling zeta with RH can be as wild as allowed on the integer side: positivity-type structure must therefore come from a relation between integers and primes that is rigid only for Z (e.g. N(x)=floor(x), functional equation).
items.corrected_statement: Theorem 1.1 is exactly as stated (pi=Li+O(sqrt x); N=rho x+Omega_pm(sqrt x ... ) for any c>2*sqrt(2)). Strongest current version is NOT this one: Broucke-Vindas (Math. Z., arXiv 2102.08478v2, Thm 4.1) improve the prime regularity to pi_{P1}(x)=Li(x)+O(1) (and Pi_{P2}(x)=Li(x)+O(log log x)) with the same integer oscillation exp(-c sqrt(log x loglog x)), c>2*sqrt(2). Note the displayed oscillation is x*exp(-c sqrt(log x loglog x)) times... as printed: N(x)=rho x+Omega_pm(x exp(-c sqrt(log x loglog x))) in the arXiv abstract wording used by BDV; the item's 'sqrt(x)*exp(...)' prefactor does NOT match the extracted text: the printed formula is Omega_pm( x exp(-c sqrt(log x log log x)) ) with the 'sqrt' being the one inside the exponent. Treat the item's factor sqrt(x) as an error.
items.check_evidence: arXiv 2004.11501 Thm 1.1 (read locally; PDF layout garbles the radical): '(1.4) pi(x)=Li(x)+O(sqrt x) and, for any constant c>2 sqrt 2, (1.5) N(x)=rho x+Omega_pm( x exp(-c sqrt(log x log log x)) )' - in the extracted text the sqrt after 'x' sits over 'log x log log x' (abstract line: 'N(x)=rho x+Omega_pm x exp(-c sqrt(log x log log x))'). Broucke-Vindas arXiv 2102.08478 Thm 4.1: 'There exist discrete Beurling prime systems P1 and P2 which satisfy pi_P1(x)=Li(x)+O(1) and Pi_P2(x)=Li(x)+O(log log x), and for any c>2 sqrt 2 ... N_Pj(x)=rho_j x+Omega_pm(x exp(-c sqrt(log x log log x)))'. Remark: 'the zeta function associated to P2 has no zeros in the right half plane {Re s>0}'. NOTE: the sqrt(x)-prefactor point rests on garbled PDF text; confirm against the typeset arXiv HTML before using.

items.name: Broucke-Vindas: random Beurling primes with bounded error, and a [0,1/2,1/2]-system
items.statement: Thm 1.2: for any non-decreasing right-continuous F with F(1)=0, F(x)<<x/log x, F->infinity, there is a Beurling prime set P with |pi_P(x)-F(x)|<=2 (absolute value signs lost in text extraction) and sum_{p_j<=x} p_j^{-it} - int_1^x u^{-it}dF(u) << sqrt(x)+sqrt(x*log(|t|+1)/log(x+1)) for all real t, x>=1. Thm 3.1: there is a Beurling system with Pi_P(x)=Li(x)+O(log log x), N_P(x)=x+O(x^{1/2}exp(c(log x)^{2/3})), M_P(x)=O(same), and N_P(x)=x+Omega_eps(x^{1/2-eps}), M_P(x)=Omega_eps(x^{1/2-eps}). Consequence (Prop. 1.4): a general Dirichlet series with coefficients in {-1,0,1}, abscissa 1/2, and its only zero in Re s>1/2 at s=1 (Beurling analogue of 1/zeta).
items.authors_year: F. Broucke, J. Vindas, Math. Z. 307 (2024) Art. 62, arXiv 2102.08478
items.quote_or_locator: Theorem 1.2, Theorem 3.1, Proposition 1.4 in the arXiv v2 PDF (opened and read).
items.fit_T1_T7: Barrier: prime counting at the level O(log log x) (far below RH size x^{1/2}) is attainable with no arithmetic; prime-DISTRIBUTION in x^{it} twisted sums is also controlled. Fails T5, T7 for Z.
items.relevance: Shows that 'prime sums are small' (even smaller than RH predicts) is not an arithmetic fact about Z; the nonnegativity of K must use something that random primes with perfectly regular density lack, because the Euler product + regular density of random primes is already available there.

items.name: Hilberdink / Hilberdink-Neamah uncertainty principle for well-behaved Beurling systems
items.statement: Define alpha, beta, gamma by psi_P(x)=x+O(x^{alpha+eps}), N_P(x)=rho*x+O(x^{beta+eps}), M_P(x)=O(x^{gamma+eps}) (sharp exponents, abscissa of zeta_P equal to 1). Then the two largest of alpha,beta,gamma are equal and at least 1/2. Earlier (Hilberdink 2005): it is impossible to have both alpha and beta less than 1/2. For Z: beta=0, alpha=gamma>=1/2 (equal to 1/2 under RH).
items.authors_year: T. W. Hilberdink, J. Number Theory 112 (2005) 332-344; A. A. Neamah, T. W. Hilberdink, Int. J. Number Theory 16 (2020) 1005-1011, arXiv 1901.06866
items.quote_or_locator: Theorem 1: "Of the numbers alpha, beta, gamma, the two largest must be the same and at least 1/2." (Introduction: "it was shown in [6] that it is impossible to have both alpha and beta less than 1/2").
items.fit_T1_T7: Theorem about all Beurling systems (uses only Euler product, discreteness of the semigroup). T3/T4 not met (exponents, not signs). T7 yes.
items.relevance: Unconditional lower bound alpha>=1/2 for any system with beta<1/2: a proven 'RH is optimal' statement that holds for ALL Beurling systems, hence cannot distinguish Z. Conjectured in the paper that [1/2,1/2,0]-systems do not exist (so gamma<1/2 may be impossible).
items.corrected_statement: Theorem 1 confirmed verbatim. Title: 'The average order of the Mobius function for Beurling primes', Int. J. Number Theory 16 (2020) 1005-1011 (page range confirmed by Broucke-Vindas abstract). Hilberdink 2005 = 'Well-behaved Beurling primes and integers', J. Number Theory 112 (2005) 332-344. items.name: Hilberdink-Lapidus: Beurling analogue of the RH <-> psi(x)-x equivalence; functional equation <-> modular identity
items.statement: Thm 2.1: if psi(x)=x+O(x^{alpha+eps}) for all eps>0 (alpha in [0,1)), then zeta_P continues to Re s>alpha with only a simple pole at 1 and has no zeros there. Conversely, if zeta_P continues to Re s>alpha with only that pole, has no zeros, and |phi(sigma+it)|=O(|t|^eps) uniformly for sigma>=alpha+delta (phi=zeta'/zeta), then psi(x)=x+O(x^{alpha+eps}). Thm 3.2: Mellin transforms Psi_1(1-s)=Psi_2(s) (suitable continuation, decay) iff F_1(x)=(1/x)F_2(1/x)+H(x) with H a finite sum of x^mu (log x)^nu; for G_1(1-s)zeta_1(1-s)=G_2(s)zeta_2(s) this is a theta-type modular identity (Bochner 1951 had a similar result).
items.authors_year: T. W. Hilberdink, M. L. Lapidus, Acta Appl. Math. 90 (2006), arXiv math/0410270
items.quote_or_locator: Sect. 2, Theorem 2.1 ("Suppose that for some alpha in [0,1), we have psi(x)=x+O(x^{alpha+eps}) for all eps>0. Then zeta(s) has an analytic continuation to the half-plane {Re s>alpha} except for a simple (non-removable) pole at s=1 and zeta(s) != 0 in this region."); Sect. 3.2, Theorem 3.2; Sect. 1.1 'We do not give a complete answer to the latter difficult question' on existence of a functional equation.
items.fit_T1_T7: The RH <-> prime-size equivalence is an exact equivalence (T4 yes) but it is an RH-EQUIVALENT statement (fails T7) and gives size, not sign (T3 no). It holds verbatim for all Beurling systems, so by itself it has no arithmetic content.
items.relevance: Confirms at the Beurling level that the circularity (sign of the prime side = sign of zero sum) is structural, not an artifact of Z. The only piece of structure that is not part of the Beurling equivalence is the Gamma-type functional equation, which HL characterize only as a modular identity; whether it forces RH for Euler-product Beurling systems is left open there.
items.corrected_statement: Content of Thm 2.1 and Thm 3.2 confirmed. Correction: journal volume is Acta Appl. Math. 94 (2006) 21-48 (item says 90). Bochner reference: Ann. of Math. 53 (1951) 332-363 (confirmed). The phrase 'We do not give a complete answer to the latter difficult question' is in the abstract-level intro (about existence of a generalised functional equation) - confirmed. Also: the equivalence in Thm 2.1 is not 'RH-equivalent' for Z-specific content; it is the Beurling-level analogue, as the item says.

items.name: Davenport-Heilbronn 1936 (Potter-Titchmarsh 1934; Bombieri-Ghosh 2011): Riemann-type functional equation without Euler product does not give RH
items.statement: The Hurwitz zeta function zeta(s,a), 0<a<1 transcendental or rational a!=1/2, has infinitely many zeros with Re s>1 (Davenport-Heilbronn 1936; irrational algebraic a: Cassels). For a=l/k, k^{-s}zeta(s,l/k) is a linear combination of Dirichlet L-functions L(s,chi), chi mod k. The 'Davenport-Heilbronn function' (a combination of two L-functions for conjugate complex characters mod 5) satisfies a Riemann-type functional equation, has no Euler product, and has infinitely many zeros off Re s=1/2 and in Re s>1 (the explicit formula f(s)=((1-i*kappa)/2)L(s,chi)+((1+i*kappa)/2)L(s,conj chi) with kappa=(sqrt(10-2*sqrt5)-2)/(sqrt5-1) is from memory: UNVERIFIED). Mechanism (Davenport-Heilbronn via Bohr equivalence): a completely multiplicative phi with |phi(n)|=1 is chosen so that the twisted series F^phi has a zero in Re s>1; by Bohr's equivalence theorem, F then has the same values in every strip, and by almost periodicity and Rouche >>T zeros in any window of length T.
items.authors_year: H. Davenport, H. Heilbronn, J. London Math. Soc. 11 (1936) 181-185, 307-312; Bombieri-Ghosh, Russian Math. Surveys 66(2) (2011) 221-270

The mod-5 functional-equation statement comes only from search snippets / the fringe arXiv 1602.06328 (not relied upon): не проверено in a primary source. Titchmarsh section 10.25 not opened.
items.fit_T1_T7: Barrier. The DH function is not a Beurling system; it shows that analytic continuation + Riemann-type functional equation + Dirichlet series with arithmetic coefficients does NOT imply RH. Separating property: the Euler product (multiplicativity). With it, no zeros in Re s>1; without it, phases of primes can be twisted independently.
items.relevance: Any positivity proof must use the Euler product beyond the half-plane of absolute convergence, i.e. correlations between primes (T5 is NECESSARY, not optional). The matrix K is a quadratic form in (prime-indexed) data; for a DH-type non-Euler function the same formal quadratic form is NOT positive, so positivity cannot be derived from the functional equation + a Dirichlet series with the right gamma-factor alone.
items.corrected_statement: Hurwitz-zeta part confirmed (transcendental a, or rational a != 1/2; Cassels for irrational algebraic). Mechanism via Bohr's equivalence theorem confirmed (credited by Righetti to Bombieri-Ghosh). kappa=(sqrt(10-2 sqrt5)-2)/(sqrt5-1) evaluates to about 0.2840, matching the value 0.2841 in a secondary source; still not verified in a primary source. 'DH function has zeros in Re s>1' is supported indirectly: Saias-Weingartner gives >>T zeros in 1/2<sigma_1<sigma_2<1+eta for any non-P*L_chi periodic series, which includes combinations of L(s,chi), L(s,chibar) mod 5; no direct primary quote found. Functional equation and absence of Euler product of the DH function: only secondary sources (a 2021 arXiv paper, an IAS lecture abstract via search). Journal data for DH 1936 and Bombieri-Ghosh (Russian Math. Surveys 66(2) (2011) 221-270) from search results only.

items.name: Zeros of non-monomial combinations of L-functions in Re s>1 (Saias-Weingartner; Booker-Thorne; Righetti)
items.statement: Saias-Weingartner 2009: for periodic coefficients a_n, if F_a(s) is not of the form P(s)L_chi(s) (P Dirichlet polynomial, L_chi a Dirichlet L-function), then there is eta=eta(a)>0 such that for all 1/2<sigma_1<sigma_2<1+eta, c_1*T<=N_a(sigma_1,sigma_2,T)<=c_2*T for large T; equivalently F_a has no zeros in sigma>1 iff it is P*L_chi (as stated in a later paper). Booker-Thorne: same for L-functions of unitary cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_r (under Ramanujan; unconditional for r<=2). Righetti 2015: for Dirichlet series with Euler product, natural bounds on coefficients and Selberg-type orthogonality, any non-monomial polynomial P(F_1,...,F_N) with coefficients in p-finite Dirichlet series has infinitely many zeros in sigma>1 (applies to Artin and automorphic L-functions and, under Selberg orthonormality, to Selberg-class elements with polynomial Euler product). Righetti 2016: real parts of such zeros need not be dense in [1,sigma*]: for infinitely many coefficient vectors c, sum c_j F_j has zero-free vertical strips in 1<sigma<sigma*.
items.authors_year: E. Saias, A. Weingartner, Acta Arith. 140 (2009) 335-344; A. Booker, F. Thorne (cited in Righetti); M. Righetti, arXiv 1412.6331 (2015) and arXiv 1506.05716 (2016)
items.quote_or_locator: SW abstract: "if Fa(s) is not of the form P(s)L_chi(s) ... then there exists an eta=eta(a)>0 such that for all 1/2<sigma_1<sigma_2<1+eta, we have c_1*T <= N_a(sigma_1,sigma_2,T) <= c_2*T". Righetti 1412.6331 abstract: "then P(F_1(s),...,F_N(s)) has infinitely many zeros for sigma>1".
items.fit_T1_T7: Barrier on all non-Euler-product combinations; proofs use Brouwer fixed point to realize prescribed values of L^phi(sigma,chi_j) by free choice of completely multiplicative phi (weak joint universality). Righetti's result for Selberg-class elements is conditional on Selberg orthonormality.
items.relevance: Any 'positivity' argument that treats L-functions only through linear structure (sums, mixtures, Gram matrices of several L-functions) will fail; K>=0 must be proven for the single object with an Euler product. T6 note: a rank-2 pole term can be seen as a degenerate mixture, so a proof must not rely on linear independence arguments that would also apply to DH-type mixtures.
items.corrected_statement: Saias-Weingartner abstract quote, Righetti 2015 abstract and Righetti 2016 (zero-free vertical strips; Thm 1.1/1.2 for infinitely many coefficient vectors; Thm 1.7 even with functional equation, no Euler product) are confirmed. Booker-Thorne: unconditional for r<=2, GRH-free Ramanujan assumption otherwise, also non-linear combinations with Dirichlet-polynomial coefficients (Righetti Intro). REFUTED sub-claim: 'equivalently F_a has no zeros in sigma>1 iff it is P*L_chi' - not in the SW abstract, and false as an iff for arbitrary Dirichlet polynomial P (e.g. P(s)=1+3*2^{-s} has zeros with sigma=log_2 3>1, so P*L_chi has zeros in sigma>1). Only the direction 'not of the form P*L_chi => positive-proportion zeros in 1/2<sigma<1+eta' is in the source. Acta Arith. 140 (2009) 335-344 confirmed.

items.name: Selberg class S: axioms and proven structure results
items.statement: S = Dirichlet series F(s)=sum a_F(n)n^{-s} (abs. conv. Re s>1, a_F(1)=1) such that (2) (s-1)^k F(s) entire of finite order; (3) Phi(s)=Q^s prod Gamma(alpha_i s+beta_i)F(s) satisfies Phi(s)=w*conj-type Phi(1-s), |w|=1 (functional equation as in the source); (4) Euler product with log F_p(s)=sum b_{p^k}p^{-ks}, b_{p^k}=O(p^{k*theta}), theta<1/2; (5) Ramanujan: a_F(n)=O(n^eps). Degree d_F=2*sum alpha_i. Proven: Conrey-Ghosh 1993: F=1 or d_F>=1; Kaczorowski-Perelli: 1<=d_F<2 implies d_F=1, and degree-1 elements are exactly zeta, Dirichlet L(s+i*theta,chi) (primitive chi); Kaczorowski-Perelli (Annals 2011): the degree conjecture holds for d<2 (earlier d<5/3); Murty-Murty: if a_F(p)=a_G(p) and a_F(p^2)=a_G(p^2) for all but finitely many p then F=G. Euler product gives no zeros in Re s>1; functional equation gives trivial zeros; GRH for S (all zeros in the strip on Re s=1/2) is a CONJECTURE, unproved even for zeta. S is closed under multiplication but not addition.
items.authors_year: A. Selberg 1989/1992; J. B. Conrey, A. Ghosh, Duke 1993; J. Kaczorowski, A. Perelli (1999; Annals of Math. 173 (2011) 1397-1441); M. R. Murty, V. K. Murty
items.quote_or_locator: Dixit, Def. 2.1 (axioms 1-5), Thm 3.1 (Conrey-Ghosh), Thm 3.2 (Kaczorowski-Perelli: "For F in S, if 1<=d_F<2 then d_F=1"), Conjecture 2 (GRH), Thm 6.1 (Murty-Murty), Sect. 8: "it is not closed under addition. This is because of the rigidity of functional equation and the Euler product." Annals page (search snippet only): "The degree conjecture has been proved for d<5/3, and in this paper we extend its validity to d<2."
items.fit_T1_T7: Axioms include the functional equation, so S is the right 'minimal axiomatic' frame (T7 yes for the structure theorems), but no theorem of S implies GRH or any sign of K. Gives no SIGN and no sizeable correlation control (that is orthonormality, still conjectural).
items.relevance: Fixes which axioms are available when one tries to prove the sign: Dirichlet series + analytic continuation + functional equation + Euler product (+ Ramanujan). Together with items on Beurling (Euler product only) and Davenport-Heilbronn (functional equation only), it shows that neither half of the axioms alone works and that no one has proven GRH from both.
items.corrected_statement: Axioms (Dirichlet series with a(1)=1, meromorphic continuation with (s-1)^k F entire of finite order, functional equation, Euler product with b_{p^k}=O(p^{k theta}), theta<1/2, Ramanujan a(n)=O(n^eps)), Conrey-Ghosh (F=1 or d>=1), Kaczorowski-Perelli (1<=d<2 => d=1; Annals 173 (2011) 'On the structure of the Selberg class, VII: 1<d<2'; earlier d<5/3), classification of degree 1 (zeta, L(s+i theta,chi), proved later by Kaczorowski-Perelli), Murty-Murty, closed under multiplication not addition: all confirmed in Dixit's survey. Dixit prints the functional equation as Phi(s)=w Phi(1-s) without the conjugation (standard form: Phi(s)=w conj(Phi(1-conj s))); the item's 'conj-type' is the standard reading. GRH for S is a conjecture. Item's wording 'Murty-Murty: a_F(p)=a_G(p) and a_F(p^2)=a_G(p^2) for all but finitely many p' confirmed.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (structure results); GRH for S CONJECTURE

For F in S, if 1<=d_F<2 then d_F=1.'; 'The elements in the Selberg class are not closed under linear combination. But, the Selberg class is closed under multiplication'; 'Theorem 6.1 (Murty-Murty). For F,G in S, if a_F(p)=a_G(p) and a_F(p^2)=a_G(p^2) for all but finitely many primes p, then F=G.' items.name: Selberg's orthonormality conjectures A and B (prime correlations of L-functions)
items.statement: Conjecture A: for F in S there is a constant n_F with sum_{p<=x}|a_F(p)|^2/p = n_F*log log x + O(1). Conjecture B (orthonormality): for primitive F,G in S, sum_{p<=x} a_F(p)*conj(a_G(p))/p = log log x + O(1) if F=G, and O(1) otherwise. Consequences proved from B in the literature: unique factorization into primitives in S, every pole at s=1 comes from zeta, non-vanishing of F on Re s=1, algebraic independence of distinct primitive elements (Molteni). Known cases: Dirichlet L-functions, automorphic via Rankin-Selberg.
items.authors_year: A. Selberg 1992 (conjectures); consequences: Conrey-Ghosh, Molteni, Murty (see Dixit)
items.quote_or_locator: Dixit, Conjecture 6: "Conjecture B is known as the Selberg's orthogonality conjecture."; Prop. 5.3, Lemma 5.6, Prop. 5.8, Prop. 5.9.
items.fit_T1_T7: This is the only item in the domain that directly states a correlation law between DIFFERENT primes' coefficients (T5), but it is an asymptotic size statement (fails T3, T4) and is a conjecture in general (fails T7 as a proven theorem).
items.relevance: Says that distinct L-functions are asymptotically independent at the level of sum a_F(p)conj(a_G(p))/p; it is the quantitative form of 'primes behave independently across L-functions'. Voronin/Davenport-Heilbronn show that independent phases are exactly what makes sign statements fail; so orthonormality supports the barrier rather than a sign.
items.corrected_statement: Conjectures A and B stated correctly (B for primitive F,G). Dixit: 'Conjecture B implies Conjecture A'. The claims 'known for automorphic L-functions via Rankin-Selberg' and the list of consequences (Molteni algebraic independence, pole only from zeta, non-vanishing on Re s=1) were not checked in a source in this session: UNVERIFIED. Known verified case: Dirichlet L-functions.

items.name: Bombieri-Hejhal: 100% of zeros of linear combinations of Euler products lie on the line (conditional)
items.statement: For finite linear combinations of L-functions with Euler products satisfying the same functional equation, under a hypothesis of 'near orthogonality' (statistical asymptotic independence of the logs of the L-functions; secondary sources also mention GRH for the individual L-functions and a pair-correlation-type spacing hypothesis), almost all (100%) zeros of the combination lie on Re s=1/2, although GRH fails in general for such combinations (no Euler product). Exact hypotheses: не проверено (conflicting secondary descriptions).
items.quote_or_locator: cw.pdf, Introduction: "But Bombieri and Hejhal proved in [2] that nonetheless 100% of the zeros of such linear combinations are still on the critical line (under an extra assumption of 'near orthogonality' which ensures that the log of the L-functions are statistically asymptotically independent)." The original paper was not opened.
items.fit_T1_T7: Uses asymptotic independence of prime sums of different L-functions (T5 in spirit) and gives a proportion statement (fails T3, T4, T7: conditional, density not sign).
items.relevance: Indicates that even for objects without Euler product, 'independence of primes' heuristics yield on-the-line zeros almost always; thus independence is a heuristic for RH-like statements but cannot be a proof tool for a sign with margins ~1e-29.
items.corrected_statement: Hypotheses are more specific than the item's 'near orthogonality'. Righetti (arXiv 1506.05716) states: under GRH and a weak pair correlation of the zeros, linear combinations WITH REAL COEFFICIENTS of Euler products with the same functional equation have asymptotically almost all zeros on Re s=1/2. Barhoumi et al. (cw.pdf) phrase it as 'near orthogonality'. Another secondary source says GRH plus Montgomery pair correlation for Hecke L-functions (Epstein zeta case). Original paper not opened. Duke Math. J. 80 (1995) 821-862, DOI 10.1215/S0012-7094-95-08028-4 confirmed by search.
items.corrected_status: CONDITIONAL (on GRH for the individual L-functions + pair-correlation-type hypothesis; exact hypotheses UNVERIFIED in the primary paper)
items.check_evidence: Righetti arXiv 1506.05716 Intro (read locally): 'Bombieri and Hejhal [6] have shown that, under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis and a weak pair correlation of the zeros, linear combinations with real coefficients of Euler products with the same functional equation have asymptotically almost all of their zeros on the line sigma=1/2.' Item's own source https://www.math.uzh.ch/en/fileadmin/user/ashkan/publikation/cw.pdf: '...under an extra assumption of near orthogonality'. items.name: Weil 1940-48: RH for curves over finite fields via Hodge index / Castelnuovo-Severi-Weil on C x C
items.statement: For a smooth projective curve C of genus g over F_q, the Frobenius eigenvalues satisfy |omega_nu|=sqrt(q) (nu=1..2g), equivalently |N_n-q^n-1|<=2g*q^{n/2}. Weil's route: the intersection form on N(V) of a surface V has index 1 (Hodge index theorem); on V=C_1 x C_2 with d_i=D.C_i this gives Castelnuovo-Severi: (D^2)<=2*d_1*d_2; applied to D=graph of Frobenius gives the sign needed.
items.authors_year: A. Weil, announced 1940-41, letter to Artin 1942, full proof 'Sur les courbes algebriques et les varietes qui s'en deduisent', Hermann, Paris 1948 (book not opened)
items.quote_or_locator: Milne, Sect. 1: "Corollary 1.3. The intersection form on N(V) has index 1."; "Theorem 1.5 (Castelnuovo-Severi inequality). Let D be a divisor on V; then (D^2) <= 2 d_1 d_2." and the criterion "Q has index 1 if and only if there exists an x such that Q(x,x)>0 and Q(y,y)<=0 for all y in <x>^perp".
items.fit_T1_T7: T3 yes (a sign), T4 yes (exact inequality of an intersection form, no loss), T5 yes (global correlation via geometry), T7 yes (proven). T1/T2 fail in the sense that the objects are geometric, not prime-side; no analogue of C x C for Z: van Frankenhuijsen: 'spec Z x spec Z = spec Z is one-dimensional and not two-dimensional like C x C'.
items.relevance: The one proven mechanism in which a lossless sign about primes (points of the curve) follows from structure. Positivity comes from an index-1 (Lorentzian) form: negative on the orthogonal complement of one positive direction. That is structurally like 'one positive direction (pole term/rank-2) + negative definite remainder', which parallels s_E<=0, s_O>=0 and the single negative eigenlevel of G_E. What separates it from Z: a surface C x C with an effective-cycle cone, Frobenius endomorphism, and finite zeros.
items.corrected_statement: Milne's Corollary 1.3 (index 1), the index-1 criterion and Theorem 1.5 (Castelnuovo-Severi, (D^2)<=2 d_1 d_2) confirmed verbatim. Weil announced in 1941 (Weil 1941) and gave the book 'Sur les courbes algebriques et les varietes qui s'en deduisent' in 1948 (Weil 1948a). The '1942 letter to Artin' detail was not found in the text and is UNVERIFIED. Not a sign statement about primes of Z; no analogue of C x C (van Frankenhuijsen: spec Z x spec Z = spec Z is one-dimensional).

items.name: Weil positivity via effectivity (Riemann-Roch) and Weil's positivity criterion for number fields
items.statement: Function fields: for a nontrivial correspondence Z on C x C, Tr(Z * Z') > 0. Proof: using Riemann-Roch, add a principal correspondence so that Z is effective; then Z*Z' = d'(Z)*Delta + Y with Y effective, (Delta.Delta)=2-2g, Y.Delta<=(4g-4)d'(Z), hence Tr(Z*Z') >= (4g-2)d'(Z)-(4g-4)d'(Z)=2d'(Z)>=0. Number fields (Weil 1952, in the Connes-Consani-Marcolli formulation, Prop. 6.2): RH for all L-functions with Grossencharakter on a global field K is equivalent to <Delta^{-1/2} f, Delta^{-1/2} f^*> >= 0 for all f in S(C_K) (positivity of Weil's explicit-formula quadratic form). Bombieri 2000: Weil's quadratic functional is positive semidefinite exactly when RH holds; if finitely many zeros violate RH, the number of negative eigenvalues of large finite truncations equals half their number.
items.authors_year: A. Weil 1952 (explicit formulae, positivity criterion); A. Connes, C. Consani, M. Marcolli 2007; E. Bombieri, Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. 11(3) (2000) 183-233
items.quote_or_locator: CCM Sect. 2.3: "Weil positivity is the statement that, if Z is a nontrivial correspondence in P(C) ... then Tr(Z*Z') > 0. This is proved using the Riemann-Roch formula on C to show that one can achieve effectivity." eq. (2.46); Prop. 6.2: "All L-functions with Grossencharakter on K satisfy the Riemann Hypothesis" iff the trace pairing satisfies positivity (6.10). Bombieri abstract: only seen as summary by a fetch tool (not verbatim).
items.fit_T1_T7: Function-field half satisfies T3/T4/T5/T7 but is geometric; number-field half is exactly the project's identity (T1, T2, T4 yes) and is RH-equivalent (fails T7). The CCM paper states the gap explicitly: 'This leaves open the more difficult question of identifying the correct analog of the principal divisors'.
items.relevance: Shows precisely where the sign is produced in the only solved case: effectivity (a divisor class represented by a nonnegative integer-valued cycle) turns an unknown sign into a sum of nonnegative terms plus an explicit positive diagonal. The target analogue for Z is an exact decomposition of <v,Kv> into an explicit term plus nonnegative terms not defined through the zeros (cf. rule 18).
items.corrected_statement: CCM formulas confirmed: positivity is eq. (2.35) Tr(Z*Z')>0; the genus-g computation is eq. (2.46): Tr(Z*Z')=2g d'(Z)+(2g-2)d'(Z)-Y.Delta >= (4g-2)d'(Z)-(4g-4)d'(Z)=2d'(Z)>=0, with Delta.Delta=2-2g and Y.Delta<=(4g-4)d'(Z). Prop. 6.2 confirmed, including (6.10). CCM 'leaves open ... the correct analog of the principal divisors' confirmed. Bombieri 2000 statement about number of negative eigenvalues of truncations equalling half the number of RH-violating zeros: only seen as a fetch-tool summary, UNVERIFIED. The statement 'RH_EQUIVALENT' is right for the number-field half; the function-field half is PROVEN.

items.name: Stepanov-Bombieri (+ Schmidt) elementary proof for curves, with amplification over constant-field extensions
items.statement: Thm 3.6 (vF's exposition): for q>(g+1)^4 a square, N_C(1)=|C(F_q)| <= q+(2g+1)*sqrt(q). A lower bound N_C(1) >= q-(|G|-1)(2g'+1)sqrt(q)+|G| follows from the upper bound applied to a Galois cover C'->P^1 with group G, using sum_{sigma in G} N_{C'}(1,sigma)=|G|(q+1). Lemma 3.1 (amplification): if for every eps>0 there is m with |N_C(nm)-q^{nm}-1|<=B*q^{nm(1/2+eps)} for all n, then RH holds for zeta_C (proof by Dirichlet approximation, using that there are only 2g Frobenius eigenvalues omega_nu). The method uses Riemann-Roch, the Frobenius flow, auxiliary function vanishing to high order at F_q-points, and (in Bombieri's version) Cartier operator = p-th power.
items.authors_year: S. A. Stepanov 1969; W. M. Schmidt, Acta Arith. 24 (1973) 347-367; E. Bombieri, Sem. Bourbaki exp. 430 (1972/73), LNM 383 (1974) 234-241
items.quote_or_locator: van Frankenhuijsen, Theorem 3.6, Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.8; Sect. 1: "Therefore, one might conclude that the right approach to the Riemann hypothesis is to first prove the prime number theorem with a good bound for the error term." and Sect. 4: "since Q has no field of constants, there is no analogue of the points on C. Therefore there is no Frobenius flow".
items.fit_T1_T7: Uses point counts only (T1 in function-field sense), uniform in extensions (T2 analogue), but the core is a size bound (fails T3); the exactness comes from amplification which requires finitely many eigenvalues (rational zeta) and unlimited constant extensions: neither exists for Z or Beurling systems. T7 yes.
items.relevance: Documents the strategy 'weak size bound for ALL extensions + exact structure (finite spectrum, Galois covers) => exact line'. For Z there is no tower of constant extensions and the spectrum is infinite, so Dirichlet/Kronecker amplification does not apply (zeros' ordinates are conjectured linearly independent).
items.corrected_statement: Thm 3.6 (q>(g+1)^4 square: N_C(1)<=q+(2g+1)sqrt q), Lemma 3.1 (amplification), Thm 3.7 and 3.8 including the lower bound N_C(1)>=q-(|G|-1)(2g'+1)sqrt q+|G| and sum over G of N_{C'}(1,sigma)=|G|(q+1) confirmed. Stepanov 1969, Schmidt, Bombieri attributions confirmed in the text; Bourbaki exp. 430 citation not checked. Note Thm 3.7 is stated with q>(g+1)^4 (g of C) though the bound uses g'.
items.check_evidence: van Frankenhuijsen arXiv 0806.0044 (read locally): 'Theorem 3.6. For q>(g+1)^4, a square, we have N_C(1)=|C(F_q)| <= q+(2g+1) sqrt q'; 'Lemma 3.1. If for every eps>0 there exists a natural number m such that |N_C(nm)-q^{nm}-1|<=B q^{nm(1/2+eps)} for every n, then the Riemann hypothesis holds for zeta_C.'; 'Therefore, one might conclude that the right approach to the Riemann hypothesis is to first prove the prime number theorem with a good bound for the error term.'; Sect. 4: 'since Q has no field of constants, there is no analogue of the points on C. Therefore there is no Frobenius flow'.

items.name: Deligne 1974 (Weil I): RH for varieties over finite fields via Landau-Rankin positivity and tensor powers
items.statement: RH for all smooth projective varieties over F_q (eigenvalues of Frobenius on H^i have absolute value q^{i/2}; exact form from memory: UNVERIFIED). Mechanism as told in Milne: (a) Landau: a Dirichlet series with real nonnegative coefficients has a singularity at its abscissa of absolute convergence; for an Euler product prod_p prod_j (1-a_{p,j}p^{-s})^{-1} with nonnegative coefficients and abscissa sigma_0 one gets |a_{p,j}|<=p^{sigma_0}; (b) Rankin: for sigma = rho tensor conj(rho), log D(s,sigma)=sum_p sum_n trace(sigma^n(t_p))/n * p^{-ns} has nonnegative coefficients because trace(sigma^n)=|trace(rho^n)|^2; (c) apply to m-th tensor powers rho^{(m)}, giving |lambda(t_p)|<=p^{1/2m} and let m->infinity. Deligne combined this with Grothendieck's trace formula, Lefschetz pencils and the monodromy of local systems.
items.authors_year: P. Deligne, 'La conjecture de Weil I', Publ. Math. IHES 43 (1974) 273-307, DOI 10.1007/BF02684373; Weil II: Publ. Math. IHES 52 (1980)
items.quote_or_locator: Milne Sect. 5, Deligne quote: "the idea was that when you had a product defining a zeta function you could get information on the local factors out of information on the pole of the zeta function itself"; Langlands' remark: "The same is therefore true of the series for D(s,sigma). We can now apply Landau's theorem to deduce that |lambda(t_p)|<=p. ... On letting m -> infinity, we see that |lambda(t_p)|<=1"; Rankin 1939: |c(n)|=O(n^{k-1/5}). Numdam page opened only as a search result.
items.fit_T1_T7: T3 yes: positivity of log-coefficients (squares |trace|^2) is a lossless sign mechanism; T4 yes after m->infinity (the tensor power trick kills the constant loss); T5 yes (Euler product + Rankin-Selberg correlation of the prime data of rho and conj rho); T7 yes (theorem). It needs information on poles of the Rankin-Selberg L-functions (supplied by Grothendieck's cohomology), not available for number fields (Rankin only gets exponent 1/5 loss).
items.relevance: Best template for 'an exact sign from a positive log-coefficient identity (sum of squares) plus amplification by powers'. The Dirichlet-series analogue for the zeta of Q would use log of a Rankin-Selberg-type product with nonnegative coefficients, but the missing input (location of the pole/continuation) is again RH-strength. Compare with the Markov/Perron-Frobenius structure of the pole-free bulk.
items.corrected_statement: The quoted mechanism is Langlands' 1970 remark (Rankin idea + Landau's theorem + tensor powers, m->infinity) as reported by Milne; Milne says Deligne studied Rankin's paper to understand this remark (Katz 1976). It is NOT a complete description of Deligne's proof of RH (which needs Grothendieck's trace formula, Lefschetz pencils, monodromy); the item states this. The item's wording 'Deligne's mechanism' should read 'Langlands-style Rankin-Landau argument that inspired Deligne'. Rankin 1939: |c(n)|=O(n^{k-1/5}) confirmed. Deligne's IHES 43 (1974) pages 273-307 is a standard reference (reference confirmed in Milne list; page range not seen verbatim). Exact form of RH statement is from memory.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (RH for varieties over F_q); the cited mechanism is heuristic motivation, not the proof

items.name: Cramer 1936 random model, Granville 1995 correction, Banks-Ford-Tao 2023 model
items.statement: Cramer model C: each n>=3 is in C independently with probability 1/log n. Almost surely pi_C(x)=int_2^x dt/log t + O(x^{1/2+eps}) (the analogue for primes is equivalent to RH) and limsup G_C(x)/log^2 x =1 (largest gap), indeed G_C(x)~log^2 x a.s. Flaw: C predicts |{n<=x: n+h in C for all h in H}| ~ x/log^{|H|}x for every finite H, false for primes (no equidistribution mod p; singular series S(H)). Granville's model G (sieve by primes <=A=log^{1-o(1)}x, probability Q/(phi(Q)log n) on survivors) restores Hardy-Littlewood k-tuple counts and gives G_G(x) >~ xi*log^2 x a.s., xi=2e^{-gamma}=1.1229...; Banks-Ford-Tao (Invent. 2023) introduce a model R from random residue classes mod every prime below a bound, with bounds on the largest gap in [1,x] in terms of the interval sieve problem, and relate the Hardy-Littlewood conjecture for any set to lower bounds for its largest gaps.
items.authors_year: H. Cramer, Acta Arith. 2 (1936) 23-46; A. Granville, Scand. Actuarial J. (1995) 12-28 (volume/pages disputed in search results); W. Banks, K. Ford, T. Tao, Invent. Math. 233 (2023), arXiv 1908.08613 v3
items.quote_or_locator: BFT Sect. 1.1: "for any fixed eps>0 one has pi_C(x)=int dt/log t + O(x^{1/2+eps}) with probability one. The analogous statement for primes is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis."; Sect. 1.1 "the Cramer model has several well-documented weaknesses, the most dramatic one being that the model does not predict the expected asymptotics for prime k-tuples"; Sect. 1.2 Granville model G_G(x) >~ xi log^2 x. Cramer 1936 and Granville 1995 originals not opened.
items.fit_T1_T7: The model theorems are PROVEN about random sets (probabilistic), but their applicability to primes is a conjecture. Independent random sets already satisfy an RH-strength size law with probability one, so RH-size is not arithmetic; T5 fails by construction for C (no correlations), partially restored by G and R (sieve correlations mod small primes).
items.relevance: A random set can have 'RH'-size error without any zero structure; the arithmetic correlations (bias mod p) are what random models must add. For K>=0 uniformly over windows, a proof must use those local correlations (prime k-tuple structure), which is exactly what Cramer's model omits.
items.corrected_statement: All quoted statements confirmed in BFT. BFT published: Invent. Math. 233 (2023) 1471-1518, DOI 10.1007/s00222-023-01199-0 (arXiv v3 dated 12 Aug 2025). Granville model: G_G(x) >~ xi log^2 x a.s., xi=2e^{-gamma}=1.1229...; Cramer's original proof of limsup G_C/log^2 x=1 a.s.; (1.2) G_C(x)~log^2 x a.s. is noted by BFT as not observed before. Cramer 1936 (Acta Arith. 2, 23-46) and Granville 1995 originals not opened; Granville's volume/pages remain disputed in the item. The special case H={0} of Hardy-Littlewood (1.16) being equivalent to RH is also in BFT.
items.corrected_status: CONJECTURE (applicability to primes); theorems about the random models are PROVEN
items.check_evidence: BFT arXiv 1908.08613 Sect. 1.1 (read locally): 'by Hoeffding's inequality ... for any fixed eps>0 one has pi_C(x) = int_2^x dt/log t + O(x^{1/2+eps}) (1.1) with probability one. The analogous statement for primes is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis.'; 'Despite its utility, the Cramer model has several well-documented weaknesses, the most dramatic one being that the model does not predict the expected asymptotics for prime k-tuples.'; Sect. 1.2: 'Granville's random set G satisfies G_G(x) >~ xi log^2 x, xi := 2e^{-gamma} = 1.1229... with probability one.' items.name: Maier 1985: irregularities of primes in short intervals
items.statement: For fixed a>1 (the Montgomery-Soundararajan text writes 'any fixed a>0'; Wikipedia-type summaries say lambda>1; check Michigan Math. J. 32, MR0783576), limsup (pi(x+(log x)^a)-pi(x))/(log x)^{a-1} > 1 and liminf < 1 as x->infinity, contradicting Cramer's model prediction that the ratio tends to 1. Method: Buchstab's function for quasi-primes and Gallagher's theorem on primes in long arithmetic progressions (matrix method). Pintz later gave a second and a simpler proof.
items.authors_year: H. Maier, Michigan Math. J. 32 (1985) 221-225; J. Pintz, Funct. Approx. Comment. Math. 37 (2007)
items.quote_or_locator: Montgomery-Soundararajan, Sect. 0: "Cramer's model suggests that pi(x+(log x)^a)-pi(x) ~ (log x)^{a-1} as x->infinity with a fixed, a>2. This, however, is known to be false, since Maier [11] showed that lim (pi(x+(log x)^a)-pi(x))/(log x)^{a-1} (symbol 'neither <= nor >= 1') for any fixed a>0"; same page: "Selberg showed that on RH, (23) holds if a>2 for almost all x".
items.fit_T1_T7: A proven failure of independence heuristics for actual primes; fits T5 negatively (primes are correlated through small-prime sieve structure). No sign information.
items.relevance: Primes in short windows (shift lengths ~ log n) have a proven irregularity from correlation with small primes, a regime directly relevant to matrices indexed by log p; positivity arguments that average prime fluctuations as independent will lose this structure. Maier-type irregularities occur independently of the zeros (uses sieve/AP structure), a candidate source of unremovable local correlation.
items.corrected_statement: Maier, Michigan Math. J. 32 (1985) 221-225 confirmed. Range of the exponent: Montgomery-Soundararajan print 'for any fixed a>0'; Wikipedia-type summaries and the standard statement use lambda>1 (a search summary). For 0<a<=1 the statement is trivial by integrality of pi, so the substantive theorem is a>1; the item's 'a>1' with a check note is the right form. The Cramer model predicts ratio->1 for a>2 (MS: 'Cramer's model suggests ... with a fixed, a>2'), not for all a>1. Maier's method (Buchstab function, Gallagher on primes in long APs) and Pintz's later proofs (Funct. Approx. Comment. Math. 37 (2007) 361-376) confirmed by search/abstract only. Selberg: on RH, (23) holds for a>2 for almost all x - confirmed in MS.
items.check_evidence: Montgomery-Soundararajan arXiv math/0409258 (read locally): 'Cramer's model suggests that pi(x+(log x)^a)-pi(x) ~ (log x)^{a-1} as x->infinity with a fixed, a>2. This, however, is known to be false, since Maier [11] showed that lim (pi(x+(log x)^a)-pi(x))/(log x)^{a-1} (neither <= nor >= 1) for any fixed a>0'; ref '12. H. Maier, Primes in short intervals, Michigan Math. J. 32 (1985), 221-225'. 'Selberg [18] showed that on RH, (23) holds if a>2 for almost all x.' Pintz abstract (https://www.projecteuclid.org/euclid.facm/1229619660): 'Helmut Maier discovered in 1985 that the model gives wrong predictions for the distribution of primes in short intervals.' The a>1 range is from a Wikipedia-derived search summary, not a primary source: UNVERIFIED.

items.name: Landau's positivity lemma (nonnegative coefficients force a singularity at the abscissa) and the Polya/Mertens/Turan sign conjectures
items.statement: Landau's lemma: if F is real, locally bounded and integrable and of constant sign on [x_0,infinity), then s*int_1^infinity F(x)x^{-s-1}dx is holomorphic for Re s>sigma_c and has a singularity at s=sigma_c; for a Dirichlet series with real nonnegative coefficients the abscissa of absolute convergence is a singularity. Corollary (Humphries Cor. 1.3): if L(x)=sum_{n<=x}lambda(n) has constant sign for large x then RH holds (via zeta(2s)/zeta(s)=s*int L(x)x^{-s-1}dx). Polya's conjecture L(x)<=0 for x>=2 (1919) is FALSE (Haselgrove 1958 non-constructively; Lehman 1960 explicit; smallest counterexample x=906,150,257, Tanaka 1980); Ingham: Polya's conjecture would force the positive ordinates of the zeros to be linearly dependent over Q. Mertens conjecture |M(x)|<sqrt(x), known to imply RH, is false: limsup M(x)x^{-1/2} > 1.06 (Odlyzko-te Riele 1985, computed from zeros of zeta, no explicit counterexample).
items.authors_year: E. Landau; G. Polya 1919; C. B. Haselgrove, Mathematika 5 (1958) 141-145; M. Tanaka 1980; A. M. Odlyzko, H. J. J. te Riele, J. reine angew. Math. 357 (1985) 138-160
items.quote_or_locator: Humphries 1108.1524: "Lemma 1.2 (Landau ...)", "Corollary 1.3. If L(x) is of constant sign for all sufficiently large x, then the Riemann hypothesis holds."; "Ingham [12] showed that Polya's conjecture implies that the positive imaginary parts of the zeroes of the Riemann zeta function are linearly dependent over the rationals."; Odlyzko-te Riele report abstract: "This paper disproves the Mertens conjecture by showing that limsup M(x)x^{-1/2} > 1.06"; Milne Sect. 5: "Landau's theorem states that, if the c_n are real and nonnegative, then D(s) has a singularity at s=sigma_0."
items.fit_T1_T7: Landau's lemma is lossless and uses only positivity of coefficients, so it is valid for Dirichlet series and for Beurling systems (T3, T4, T2 yes). But the useful direction (RH => constant sign) is false in the natural instances (Polya, Mertens): natural sign statements about prime/Mobius/Liouville sums are false, so the converse sign is unavailable. Fits T7 for the lemma, fails for the sign claims.
items.relevance: A proven, lossless sign-to-analytic tool; it explains why Deligne's proof works for nonnegative log-coefficients. The negative results show that 'positivity of an accessible prime-side sum' (L(x), M(x)) does not hold even though RH is believed; any prime-side positivity must be of the finer Weil form (a quadratic form on test functions), not a pointwise sign.
items.corrected_statement: Landau Lemma 1.2, Corollary 1.3, Ingham's linear-dependence consequence, Haselgrove 1958 disproof and Tanaka's smallest counterexample x=906,150,257 are confirmed. Odlyzko-te Riele: limsup M(x)x^{-1/2}>1.06 and liminf<-1.009 confirmed (report NM-R8412; published J. reine angew. Math. 357 (1985) 138-160 not seen in the text). The item is outdated on the strongest version: Kotnik-te Riele 2006 gave limsup>1.2184 (Wikipedia snippet; the -1.229 figure unverified), and Hurst (Math. Comp., arXiv 1610.08551, 2016/17) gives liminf about -1.837625, limsup about 1.826054 (reported by arXiv abstract summary/Wikipedia). Still no explicit counterexample to Mertens known. Lehman 1960 and the 'Turan' conjecture were not verified. 'Mertens conjecture implies RH' is standard (Odlyzko-te Riele report intro: 'its truth was known to imply the truth of the Riemann hypothesis').
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (Landau lemma, disproofs); sign conjectures FALSE
items.check_evidence: Humphries arXiv 1108.1524 (read locally): 'Lemma 1.2 (Landau [24, Lemma 15.1]) ...'; 'Corollary 1.3. items.name: Voronin universality (1975) and Kronecker-Weyl: independence of log p in 1/2<Re s<1
items.statement: For every compact K in the strip D(1/2,1) with connected complement, every f continuous on K and holomorphic and non-vanishing inside, and every eps>0: liminf_{T->infinity} (1/T)*meas{tau in [0,T]: sup_{s in K}|zeta(s+i*tau)-f(s)|<eps} > 0. Proof structure (Matsumoto): a finite truncation of the Euler product approximates zeta in a mean-value sense; since {log p} is linearly independent over Q, the Kronecker-Weyl theorem lets the truncation approximate any target f. Generalizes to zeta and L-functions with Euler products (Matsumoto Sect. 3, joint universality Sect. 4); if f were allowed to vanish somewhere, Rouche would give >>T zeros with real part >1/2+eps (this is the known reason RH is equivalent to a 'universality with f nonvanishing only' statement; not verified in a primary source).
items.authors_year: S. M. Voronin 1975; K. Matsumoto, survey arXiv 1407.4216 (2014)
items.quote_or_locator: Matsumoto Sect. 1, Theorem 1 (Voronin's universality theorem) and: "since {log p}_p is linearly independent over Q, we can apply the Kronecker-Weyl approximation theorem to obtain that any target function f(s) can be approximated by the above finite truncation. This is the basic structure of the proof of Theorem 1."
items.fit_T1_T7: Barrier: inside the critical strip the Euler-product phases behave as independent uniform variables, so log zeta takes every value; no positivity of Re log zeta or of any pointwise functional of the Euler product can hold in 1/2<Re s<1. T5 (correlations) is the issue: universality says prime phases are asymptotically independent. For Beurling systems universality needs linear independence of log p_j plus mean-value estimates (not verified).
items.relevance: Together with Davenport-Heilbronn this is the mechanism-level reason why positivity cannot be derived by manipulating the Euler product freely: free phases give zeros and values anywhere. The Weil quadratic form avoids this because it pairs the whole spectrum through the explicit formula (a lossless identity) rather than through values of the Euler product.
items.corrected_statement: Theorem statement, the Euler-product-truncation + Kronecker-Weyl proof structure and linear independence of log p are confirmed in Matsumoto. The item's last sentence (zero-vanishing f and Rouche gives >>T zeros; 'RH equivalent to a universality with f nonvanishing') is not in that survey. The sourced RH-equivalent statement is Bagchi's theorem: RH holds iff zeta is strongly recurrent, i.e. liminf (1/T) meas{tau in [0,T]: sup_{s in K}|zeta(s+i tau)-zeta(s)|<eps}>0 for compact K in D(1/2,1) (Theorem 20 in Matsumoto). Also missing from the item: Steuding's recurrence/universality result for Beurling zeta functions, which makes 'holds_for_beurling_primes' not simply UNKNOWN. Voronin's 1975 date: reference [205] in Matsumoto (year in bibliography not read in this session).
