merged.title: 2019-2026 frontier results on primes and on Weil positivity
merged.summary: Verified by opening: Guth-Maynard 2405.20552 (zero density N(sigma,T)<=T^{30(1-sigma)/13+o(1)}); Connes-Consani-Moscovici 2511.22755 (conjectural convergence, numerics); Connes 2602.04022 (survey/letter, finite-prime extremizers); Connes-van Suijlekom 2511.23257 (PF-type simple even ground state implies real zeros of its Fourier transform); Suzuki 2606.09096 and Zhu 2608.24827 (2026 Weil-form preprints); Alpoge-Furman 2608.13637 (read the PDF text); BGSTB 2306.04799; Rodgers-Tao; Polymath15; MTY 2212.06867; Platt-Trudgian; Tao and Tao-Terävainen. No fetched source, at any date, proves a sign for the Weil form from primes alone. Named barriers: (1) circularity: the lossless identities (Weil explicit formula, Bombieri 2000 inertia count, BGSTB) express prime-side quantities through the zeros, so any prime-side sign is RH; (2) Rodgers-Tao Lambda>=0 and Zhu's Landau-Widom decay show there is no slack (RH is the borderline case); (3) Beurling systems (Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer; Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas) show that density/Chebyshev-type properties of primes cannot prove RH, so a sign must use specific arithmetic (Gamma factor, functional equation, true correlations of Lambda); (4) sieve, large-value and zero-density methods (Bombieri-Vinogradov, Maynard, Guth-Maynard, Green-Tao, Tao) are all lossy or averaged, exploiting size or asymptotic cancellation, never an exact sign. Best candidates for a SIGN mechanism: (a) the Hodge-index/Castelnuovo positivity that proves the Weil criterion for function fields (PROVEN there, but needs a surface structure over Spec Z that is missing); (b) the Connes-van Suijlekom transfer principle, whose hypothesis (simple, isolated, even lowest eigenvector) is the Perron-Frobenius property you already observed in the pole-free bulk; it holds for any distribution and so cannot alone give RH, but is the closest proven 'PF gives reality of zeros' theorem I found. (c) the inertia/rank method of Bombieri 2000 + Alpoge-Furman, which gives lossless sign counting without termwise positivity, but only for proportions. Caution: the 2026 papers (Alpoge-Furman, Connes-van Suijlekom, Connes, Suzuki, Zhu, CCM) are preprints; Alpoge-Furman is stated to be AI-generated with a Lean formalisation I did not check. Not covered or not verified: Bourgain decoupling bounds, Ford-Green-Konyagin-Maynard-Tao large gaps, Harper's random multiplicative function moments, the Goldston-Suriajaya papers GS25/GS26, and the Aksman/Toupin items seen in search (unrefereed, ignored). Gaps and conflicts: DMV details and the Montgomery formula were taken from search summaries only; Kedlaya's notes host was unreachable; two fetched summaries (Connes 2602.04022, Connes-van Suijlekom) are paraphrases by the fetch tool, not verbatim quotes.

items.name: Bombieri 2000: truncations of Weil's quadratic functional; negative eigenvalues count off-line zeros
items.statement: Weil's functional (explicit-formula quadratic form on test functions) is positive semidefinite iff RH holds. For its finite Fourier truncations: if RH fails with only finitely many off-line zeros, the number of negative eigenvalues of the truncation equals exactly one half of the number of off-line zeros, once the truncation is large enough. The minimum of the Rayleigh quotient on L^2 functions supported in [-t,t] is attained, and the form is positive definite for t small (Yoshida's theorem, re-proved).
items.authors_year: E. Bombieri, 2000 (Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. 11(3), 183-233)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract (via WebFetch of EuDML record): the functional is 'positive semidefinite if and only if the Riemann Hypothesis is true'; negative eigenvalues equal one half of the off-line zeros 'provided the truncation is big enough'. Journal data: Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. 11 (2000), no. 3, 183-233. The abstract was only paraphrased by the fetch tool; the 'half the off-line zeros' sentence also appears in a search-result snippet of the same abstract.
items.fit_T1_T7: Satisfies T4 (exact inertia statement) and T2 in spirit (any truncation). Fails T1/T3/T7: the count of negative eigenvalues is expressed through zeros, so it is the RH-circular direction; it says what a failure would look like, not that sign holds. The argument seems to use only the explicit formula, so a Beurling analogue is plausible but I did not verify it.
items.relevance: This is the exact form of your s_E <= 0 / s_O >= 0 reduction seen from the zero side: the negative index of the finite window equals (half) the number of off-line zeros the window can see. Any prime-side sign proof for a window is a proof that this index is 0 for that window. It also fixes what 'no slack' means: one off-line pair is exactly one negative direction.
items.corrected_statement: Bombieri, 'Remarks on Weil's quadratic functional in the theory of prime numbers, I', Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. 11(3) (2000) 183-233. Functional is positive semidefinite iff RH; minimum on unit ball of L^2 functions supported in [-t,t] is attained; Yoshida's theorem (positive definite for small t) re-proved; if RH fails via finitely many off-line zeros, #negative eigenvalues of a large enough truncation = half of the number of those zeros.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (published). Title added; 'half the off-line zeros' is stated for the finite-off-line-zeros case only.
items.check_evidence: https://eudml.org/doc/252338 : 'positive semidefinite if and only if the Riemann Hypothesis is true'; negative eigenvalues equal half the zeros 'provided the truncation is large enough' (fetch tool paraphrase of abstract; I did not see the paper body). Independently, Alpoge-Furman (arXiv 2608.13637, sec 7.1) cite [Bom00] for the same observation and give the same title/journal.

items.name: Alpoge-Furman 2026: unconditional >= 2/3 of zeta zeros simple and on the critical line, via rank-trace inequality on a finite compression of Weil's Hermitian form (PREPRINT, AI-generated, not refereed)
items.statement: Theorem A (as stated in the preprint): N0s(T,2T) >= (2/3 - o(1)) N(T,2T) (simple zeros on the critical line) and Nd(T,2T) >= (5/6 - o(1)) N(T,2T) (distinct zeros); constants 0.6725 / 0.8362 with the Montgomery-Taylor window. Method: restrict Weil's Hermitian form W(f,g)=sum_rho m_rho fhat(gamma_rho) ghat(gamma_rho) to d ~ N(T,2T) modulated copies of a window; the matrix G = P + Q with P rank-one positive pieces from on-line zeros and Q blocks of signature (1,1) from off-line pairs; unconditional prime-side second moment ||G||_HS^2 = (R(psi)+o(1))N; matrix inequality rank P1 >= 2 tr P1 + 4 tr Q' - 4b - ||P1+Q'||_HS^2. Uses Weil's explicit formula, Chebyshev-Mertens sums of Lambda(n), Montgomery-Vaughan inequality for frequencies log n; no mollifier, zero-density or zero-free region.
items.authors_year: L. Alpoge, R. Furman, arXiv 2608.13637 (v1 13 Aug 2026, v2 19 Aug 2026)
items.quote_or_locator: I opened the PDF text. Abstract: 'the Riemann hypothesis, classically needed to read the zero side as a positive sum over real ordinates, is replaced by a rank-trace inequality applied to a finite compression of Weil's Hermitian form, with Sylvester's law of inertia handling off-line pairs.' Front matter: 'The mathematical argument in this paper was discovered and written by Claude, an AI developed by Anthropic. The listed authors verified the proof and take responsibility for its content.' Sec. 1.4: 'The theorems are lower bounds only' and the inputs 'hold for Davenport-Heilbronn and Epstein zeta functions, for which the analogue of RH is false.' Sec. 1.3: 'The observation that the negative index of truncations of W counts off-line pairs is Bombieri's [Bom00].' Appendix A: Lean 4 formalisation claimed (tag v1.0, no axioms beyond Mathlib's). I did not check the Lean repository or the proof; no peer review.
items.fit_T1_T7: Uses T1-style prime-side input (unconditional second moment from primes) and an exact-form structure (T4 for the form, but the final inequality is a lower bound with o(N) loss); works at the scale of many windows at once (partial T2). Fails T3 for RH itself: gives a proportion, not a sign; fails T6 (no non-Markov pole handling); T7 is formally satisfied (no RH assumed) but the result is an unrefereed preprint.
items.relevance: This is the only 2026 source I found that turns a prime-side quantity (a Hilbert-Schmidt norm of a window Gram matrix, computed from Lambda(n)/sqrt(n) via Montgomery-Vaughan) into a rigorous sign-free statement about the zero side by inertia (Sylvester), not by positivity. Same ingredient family as your <v,Kv> = sum F_v(z)^2. It is also evidence that a rank/inertia count, not a termwise sign, is where unconditional information lives; their own Sec. 1.4 says it is sharp at 2/3 and cannot reach RH.
items.corrected_statement: The item reports the preprint faithfully. Verified in PDF text: Theorem A: N0s(T,2T) >= (2/3 - o(1))N(T,2T), Nd >= (5/6 - o(1))N; Montgomery-Taylor window gives 0.67250... and 0.83625...; previous unconditional records 5/12 for N0s/N [PRZZ20] and 0.6603 for Nd/N [Wu15]. Theorem B: same for primitive Dirichlet L(s,chi). Analytic inputs credited to Aryan [Ary22] and BGSTB24. Authors: Levent Alpoge, Ralph Furman; v2 19 Aug 2026; no journal reference. items.name: Baluyot-Goldston-Suriajaya-Turnage-Butterbaugh 2023/24: unconditional Montgomery pair-correlation theorem
items.statement: Montgomery's formula for the pair-correlation form factor F(alpha) (prime-side Dirichlet-polynomial mean value) holds as a statement about the sum over ALL zeros, without RH. Consequence: if the zeros with T^{3/8} < gamma <= T lie within 1/(2 log T) of the critical line, then at least 61.7% of them are simple. The method neither needs nor gives information on whether zeros lie on the line. Follow-up arXiv 2501.14545 (Jan 2025) treats zeros in a narrow box around the line and gives a horizontal-distribution result.
items.authors_year: S. A. C. Baluyot, D. A. Goldston, A. I. Suriajaya, C. L. Turnage-Butterbaugh, arXiv 2306.04799, Acta Arith. 214 (2024) 357-376
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: 'Here we obtain an unconditional form of Montgomery's theorem' (fetched abstract page). Acta Arith. reference and the 61.7% statement from a search-result summary; follow-up at https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14545 was seen only in search results.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 yes for the prime side; T4 yes (identity-based, asymptotic with o(1) error, not margins 1e-29); fails T3 (a moment, not a sign) and T5 only in the Fourier-support-1 range alpha<1; T7 satisfied.
items.relevance: It shows that the prime-side second moment of window functions is computed unconditionally and equals the zero-side sum of squares over complex zeros. That is the same identity as <v,Kv> = sum F_v(z)^2 for specific v. What is missing is exactly what is missing in your case: termwise positivity of the zero side off the line.
items.corrected_statement: Theorem 1 (verbatim form): F(alpha) is real, even and nonnegative, and F(alpha) = T^{-2 alpha}(log T + O(1)) + alpha + O(1/sqrt(log T)) uniformly for 0 <= alpha <= 1, with F defined via weight w(u)=4/(4-u^2) over all zeros (not literally the pair-correlation sum unless RH). Theorem 2: if all zeros with T^{3/8} < gamma <= T lie in |beta-1/2| < 1/(2 log T), at least 61.7% of zeros are simple (60.8% with Fejer kernel per secondary search snippet). Acta Arith. 214 (2024) 357-376. Follow-up arXiv 2501.14545 is now titled 'Pair Correlation of Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function I: Proportions of Simple Zeros and Critical Zeros' (v3 1 Sep 2026, under review): under box width b/log T with b=0.3185, at least 2/3 of zeros are simple AND on the critical line.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (Theorem 1, unconditional; published Acta Arith.). Item's 'Fourier support alpha<1' should read alpha<=1. Follow-up 2501.14545 = UNREFEREED, CONDITIONAL on box hypothesis.
items.check_evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.04799 : 'Here we obtain an unconditional form of Montgomery's theorem'; 'The method of proof neither requires nor provides any information on whether any of these zeros are on or not on the critical line'; Theorem 1 text 'F(alpha) is real, even, and nonnegative ... uniformly for 0 <= alpha <= 1'. https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.04799 : 'Acta Arith. 214 (2024), 357-376'. https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.14545 : v3 1 Sep 2026, 'under review', b = 0.3185.

items.name: Connes-Consani-Moscovici 2025: Zeta spectral triples (PREPRINT)
items.statement: Self-adjoint operators are built as rank-one perturbations of a spectral triple for the scaling operator on an interval, using only Euler products over primes up to a cutoff; their spectra closely match the lowest nontrivial zeros even for small cutoffs, appear numerically to converge to the zeros as parameters grow, and regularized determinants are suggested to converge to the Xi function. The authors state that a rigorous proof of this convergence would establish RH. Convergence is NOT proved.
items.authors_year: A. Connes, C. Consani, H. Moscovici, arXiv 2511.22755 (Nov 2025)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract (paraphrase by the fetch tool, which could not quote it verbatim): 'a spectral realization of its non-trivial zeros'; 'a rigorous proof of this convergence would establish the Riemann Hypothesis'. Preprint, no journal status seen.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 yes (Euler products up to a cutoff); T7 satisfied as a construction but the key statement (convergence to zeros) is a conjecture, equivalent in strength to RH-type spectral realization. Fails T2, T3, T4 as stated.
items.relevance: Same family as your window operator K: finite Euler-product cutoff gives a self-adjoint operator whose spectrum numerically approximates zeros. It supplies a prime-side finite object and an RH-equivalent limiting claim, but no sign proof.

Not proved. arXiv comments: to appear in an EMS Lecture Notes in Mathematics volume (Applications of Noncommutative Geometry to Gauge Theories, Field Theories, and Quantum Space-Time).

items.name: Connes 2026: The Riemann Hypothesis: Past, Present and a Letter Through Time (PREPRINT survey)
items.statement: A 165-year survey of approaches to RH, including a 'Letter to Riemann' that extremizes a quadratic form (a restriction of Weil's form) to approximate zeros; the abstract states that using only primes less than 13 the optimization yields approximations to the first 50 zeros, that the author proves these approximations lie on the critical line, and connects the Weil form to information theory. Final sections outline a possible strategy based on convergence of zeros from finite to infinite Euler products via trace formulas.
items.authors_year: A. Connes, arXiv 2602.04022 (Feb 2026)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract (fetch-tool summary): 'Using only primes less than 13, this optimization procedure yields approximations to the first 50 zeros.' The 'proves that these approximations lie on the critical line' claim is the summary's wording of the abstract; the proof was not read by me. Preprint.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 yes (finite prime set); the on-line statement is for finite-prime approximants, which is a different object from the full Weil form. Fails T2/T3 for RH; T7 conditional on the final convergence step.
items.relevance: Closest direct neighbour of your approach: a finite-prime restriction of Weil's form whose extremizers have all zeros on the line. If the on-line property for each finite Euler product is a proven theorem (via the Connes-van Suijlekom theorem below), the open step is the limit, i.e. exactly the uniformity over windows (T2).

Abstract: 'Using only primes less than 13, this optimization procedure yields approximations to the first 50 zeros' and 'Moreover we prove a general result that these approximating values lie exactly on the critical line.' The claim is about finite-prime approximants, not zeta zeros. I did not read the proof.

items.name: Connes-van Suijlekom 2025: Quadratic forms, real zeros and echoes of the spectral action (PREPRINT)
items.statement: If a quadratic form built from a real even distribution on [-L,L] gives a lower-bounded self-adjoint operator whose lowest eigenvalue is simple, isolated, and has an even eigenfunction, then all zeros of the Fourier transform of that eigenfunction lie on the real line. Proof steps: a C*-algebraic proof of a Caratheodory-Fejer corollary for Toeplitz matrices, a continuous analogue for convolution operators, analysis of finite truncations, an extension of the zero-localization result, and Hurwitz's theorem.
items.authors_year: A. Connes, W. D. van Suijlekom, arXiv 2511.23257 (28 Nov 2025, math.OA)
items.quote_or_locator: Fetch-tool summary of the abstract (not verbatim): 'the paper proves that if a quadratic form built from a real, even distribution on [-L, L] yields a lower-bounded self-adjoint operator whose lowest eigenvalue is simple, isolated, and has an even eigenfunction, then all zeros of that eigenfunction's Fourier transform lie on the real line.' Preprint; proof not read.
items.fit_T1_T7: The theorem uses only the operator-theoretic hypothesis (simple even ground state, no arithmetic), so it holds for any distribution including Beurling ones: fails T7-style 'arithmetic' content but meets T3/T4 as a transfer principle. Its hypothesis (simple, isolated, even lowest eigenvector) is a Perron-Frobenius-type property.
items.relevance: This is a direct match for your finding that the pole-free bulk has a simple strictly positive even bottom (Perron-Frobenius). It converts the PF property of the lowest eigenvector into reality of zeros of ITS Fourier transform, i.e. a sign-type conclusion for the eigenfunction, not for the zeta zeros. Because it holds for any distribution, it cannot by itself give RH; the arithmetic input must supply the missing bridge from eigenfunction zeros to zeta zeros.
items.corrected_statement: arXiv 2511.23257 (28 Nov 2025, math.OA, cross-list math.NT, 26 pp). For a real distribution on [0,L] (even extension to [-L,L]), if the quadratic form gives a lower-bounded self-adjoint operator whose lowest eigenvalue is simple and isolated with an even eigenfunction, then all zeros of the Fourier transform of that eigenfunction are real. Five-step proof (C*-algebraic Caratheodory-Fejer for Toeplitz, continuous analogue, truncations, zero-localization, Hurwitz). The item's claims that it 'holds for Beurling' and that the hypothesis is 'Perron-Frobenius-type' are the item author's inferences, not in the abstract.
items.corrected_status: PREPRINT, proof not read (UNVERIFIED); abstract-level statement confirmed. Beurling applicability = inference, not sourced.

items.name: Connes-Consani 2020: Weil positivity and trace formula, the archimedean place
items.statement: A conceptual explanation of Weil positivity at a single archimedean place: the positivity is located in the trace of the scaling action compressed onto the orthogonal complement of the range of cutoff projections at cutoff 1. The gap between the Weil distribution and the Sonin trace is expressed with prolate spheroidal wave functions and controlled via Hermitian Toeplitz matrices. The authors note the tools also apply to the semi-local case, where 'Weil positivity implies RH'.

items.quote_or_locator: Abstract (fetch summary): 'locate the source of positivity in the trace of the scaling action, compressed onto the orthogonal complement of the range of cutoff projections'. Phrase 'Weil positivity implies RH' from the same abstract summary.
items.fit_T1_T7: T4 yes (exact trace formula); T1 yes for the archimedean place only; does not treat the prime places, so fails T5/T6 and T2 for the full form.
items.relevance: Supplies the archimedean (Gamma) part of the positivity mechanism with exact operators. Your s_E/s_O reduction needs the same archimedean term; the open part is the prime part and your rank-2 pole term.

For the general semi-local case Weil positivity would imply RH. It is a conceptual/partly rigorous single-place result, not a theorem about RH; arXiv page lists no journal reference.

items.name: Suzuki 2026: Weil's quadratic form via the screw function (PREPRINT)
items.statement: A unified operator-theoretic framework (screw functions, de Branges spaces) for results on Weil's quadratic form by Yoshida, Bombieri, Connes-Consani and Connes-Consani-Moscovici, working with continuous functions instead of distributions. Conjecture: an operator whose eigenvalues are the imaginary parts of the nontrivial zeros is the limit as a->infinity of self-adjoint operators on [-a,a]. 'All these results are obtained without assuming the Riemann Hypothesis.'

items.quote_or_locator: Abstract (fetch summary): 'All these results are obtained without assuming the Riemann Hypothesis.' The limit statement is explicitly a conjecture.

items.name: Zhu 2026: Weil positivity in compact windows (PREPRINT, numerical/certified)
items.statement: Normalized infimum of Weil's form for test functions supported in [-L,L] is studied with certified computation: positivity is shown for support in [-0.8,0.8]; upper bounds are computed in interval arithmetic and become very small at L=2, following an empirical decay law linked to the Landau-Widom eigenvalue-plunge rate. Under RH an additional bound for large L is given. The author concludes that the positivity approach alone cannot reach RH without additional assistance.
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract (fetch summary, not verbatim): 'positivity on bounded support is classical'; conclusion that the positivity approach alone cannot reach RH. Preprint; not independently checked.
items.fit_T1_T7: T1 yes (certified prime+Gamma computation); fails T2 (specific windows), T3 only as finite certificates. Numerical, not a theorem for all windows.
items.relevance: Independent evidence that the smallest eigenvalue of the window form decays super-exponentially in L, i.e. margins like your 1e-29 are the expected Landau-Widom behaviour, not an accident, and that any lossy bound dies. Useful as a calibration of T4.
items.corrected_statement: arXiv 2608.24827, Xuefeng Zhu (single author), v1 25 Aug 2026 (9-page announcement), v2 2 Sep 2026. Title: 'Weil positivity in compact windows: a finite reduction, certified two-sided bounds, and a Landau-Widom decay law'. Certified positivity for supports in [-0.8,0.8]; reduction of window positivity to PSD of one finite matrix; ground state simple and even; interval-arithmetic unconditional upper bounds reaching about 3.2e-283 at L=2; at L=0.8 the minimum eigenvalue enclosed between 8.9e-18 and 2.27e-17; under RH min eigenvalue <= exp(-L e^L) for large L; author argues positivity approach cannot reach RH without extra help since required frequency resolution grows doubly exponentially. The item's 'positivity on bounded support is classical' quote is not verified verbatim.

items.name: Pratt-Robles-Zaharescu-Zeindler 2020: more than 5/12 of zeta zeros on the critical line
items.statement: Unconditionally, slightly over 5/12 (about 41.7%) of the nontrivial zeros of zeta lie on the critical line, computed via a twisted second moment with a mollifier built from convolutions of Mobius and powers of von Mangoldt (building on Selberg 1942 positive proportion, Levinson 1/3, Conrey 2/5).

items.fit_T1_T7: Fails T3, T4 (proportion), T5, T6. Uses functional equation and mollifier analysis for zeta specifically.
items.relevance: Shows what lossy sum-over-primes (mollifier) methods give: a proportion, never all zeros. Alpoge-Furman claims 2/3 in 2026; neither approaches a sign for all windows.

items.name: Rodgers-Tao 2018: the de Bruijn-Newman constant is non-negative, Lambda >= 0
items.statement: Newman's conjecture holds: Lambda >= 0, where Lambda is the de Bruijn-Newman constant (H_t has only real zeros iff t >= Lambda). Hence for every t<0, H_t has a non-real zero. RH is equivalent to Lambda <= 0. Proof: assume Lambda<0 and derive a contradiction with Montgomery-type local zero statistics.
items.authors_year: B. Rodgers, T. Tao, arXiv 1801.05914 (2018; v5 2021)
items.quote_or_locator: Abstract: 'The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to Lambda <= 0, and Newman conjectured the reverse inequality. The authors prove that conjecture' (fetch summary).
items.fit_T1_T7: T4 exact, but T3 fails: RH is at the boundary Lambda=0 'if true', so no slack exists. It is a statement about the heat flow, not about window positivity. T7 satisfied.
items.relevance: This is the formal reason your margins are razor-thin: RH, if true, is the borderline case, so any argument must be sharp. Polymath15 gives the unconditional upper bound Lambda <= 0.22 (arXiv 1904.12438, abstract: 'a new unconditional upper bound of Lambda <= 0.22').
items.corrected_statement: B. Rodgers, T. Tao, 'The de Bruijn-Newman constant is non-negative', Forum Math. Pi 8 (2020) e6, DOI 10.1017/fmp.2020.6 (arXiv 1801.05914, v1 18 Jan 2018, v5 3 Jul 2021). RH <=> Lambda <= 0; proof by contradiction from Lambda<0 using Montgomery pair-correlation-type local spacing. Polymath15 (arXiv 1904.12438): unconditional Lambda <= 0.22 (improving Ki-Kim-Lee Lambda < 1/2), 'To appear, Research in the Mathematical Sciences' per arXiv comments. Statement that 'RH, if true, is the borderline Lambda=0' is a correct reading (Lambda>=0 and RH <=> Lambda<=0 give RH <=> Lambda=0).
items.check_evidence: https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/forum-of-mathematics-pi/article/de-bruijnnewman-constant-is-nonnegative/D4B85BA067E2D5A71D87E4FFB0D21E46 (search result: Forum of Mathematics, Pi, vol. 8 (2020), e6); https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.05914 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.12438 : 'unconditional upper bound of Lambda <= 0.22'.

items.name: Mossinghoff-Trudgian-Yang 2022: explicit zero-free regions
items.statement: zeta(sigma+it) has no zeros in sigma >= 1 - 1/(55.241 (log|t|)^{2/3} (loglog|t|)^{1/3}) for |t| >= 3, and none in sigma >= 1 - 1/(5.558691 log|t|) for |t| >= 2. These enlarge the known zero-free region for 3e12 <= |t| <= exp(64.1) and for |t| >= exp(1000). (Platt-Trudgian 2021, arXiv 2004.09765: RH verified for all zeros with |Im| <= 3e12, numerically with interval arithmetic.)
items.authors_year: M. J. Mossinghoff, T. S. Trudgian, A. Yang, arXiv 2212.06867 (Dec 2022); D. Platt, T. Trudgian, arXiv 2004.09765 (2021)

items.name: Tao 2016 and Tao-Terävainen 2017-19: logarithmically averaged Chowla/Elliott (two-point; odd order); Matomäki-Radziwill-Tao averaged Chowla
items.statement: Tao: for fixed naturals a1,a2,b1,b2 with a1 b2 - a2 b1 != 0 and any omega(x) -> infinity with 1<=omega(x)<=x, sum_{x/omega(x)<n<=x} lambda(a1 n+b1) lambda(a2 n+b2)/n = o(log omega(x)) (log-averaged two-point Chowla, 'breaking the parity barrier'). Tao-Terävainen: logarithmically averaged correlations of 1-bounded multiplicative functions are uniform limits of periodic sequences; this yields the odd-order cases of the log-averaged Chowla conjecture and logarithmic densities of sign patterns of lambda (length up to 3) and mu (length up to 4). MRT 2015: an averaged form of Chowla (correlations small on average over shifts).
items.authors_year: T. Tao, arXiv 1509.05422 (2015/16); T. Tao, J. Terävainen, arXiv 1708.02610, Duke Math. J. 168 (2019) 1977-2027; arXiv 1710.02112, J. Théor. Nombres Bordeaux 30 (2018); K. Matomäki, M. Radziwill, T. Tao, arXiv 1503.05121, Algebra Number Theory 9 (2015) 2167-2196
items.quote_or_locator: Tao abstract (fetch): 'breaking the parity barrier for this problem' with the displayed o(log omega(x)) formula. Tao-Terävainen: 'The results yield new cases of the logarithmically averaged Elliott conjecture, including the odd-order Chowla conjecture' (https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.02610). MRT: Chowla 'still unproven for any collection of at least two shifts' (https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.05121). Full unaveraged Chowla for k>=2 is OPEN.
items.fit_T1_T7: T5 yes in the strongest sense (correlations between different primes' multiplicative structure, parity barrier broken), T1 yes; fails T3 (they give o(1) cancellation, not a sign) and T4 (averaged, asymptotic).
items.relevance: This is the best proven tool that sees correlations between prime structures. It would be useful only if the cancellation you need in the quadratic form is of Elliott type with logarithmic weights; the 1/n weighting matches your Lambda(n)/sqrt(n) at shifts log n only partially. Chowla itself would also imply information on the size of M(x) near sqrt(x) only on average.

items.name: Bounded gaps between primes: Zhang 2013, Maynard 2013, Polymath8b (H1 <= 246)
items.statement: liminf (p_{n+m} - p_n) < infinity for every m (Maynard), liminf (p_{n+1}-p_n) <= 600 (Maynard); with Polymath8b (with Maynard's ideas) H1 <= 246. Zhang first proved a finite bound 70,000,000. Conditionally on Elliott-Halberstam the bound drops to 12 (Maynard abstract).

items.fit_T1_T7: T5 yes (sieve weights see correlations of prime k-tuples) but T3/T4 fail: existence statements via lossy sieves with a level-of-distribution 1/2 barrier.

items.name: Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem (1965): level of distribution 1/2
items.statement: For any fixed A>0 there exist c=c(A), B=B(A) with sum_{N<=Q} max_{m in (Z/NZ)*} |psi(x;N,m) - x/phi(N)| <= c x (log x)^{-A} for Q = x^{1/2}(log x)^{-B}. Elliott-Halberstam would extend this to Q = x^{1-epsilon}; no improvement of the exponent 1/2 is known.
items.authors_year: E. Bombieri (1965), A. I. Vinogradov (1965); statement as in K. Kedlaya, 18.785 notes
items.quote_or_locator: 'For any fixed A>0, there exist constants c=c(A) and B=B(A) such that sum_{N<=Q} max_{m} |psi(x;N,m) - x/phi(N)| <= c x (log x)^{-A} for Q = x^{1/2}(log x)^{-B}' (Theorem 1 in Kedlaya's notes, quoted on the linked Tao page; Kedlaya's host kskedlaya.org was unreachable from here, so I did not open the original notes).
items.fit_T1_T7: T1/T2 yes, T7 yes; T3/T4 fail (on average, with (log x)^-A saving, ineffective constants).
items.relevance: A unconditional average-over-moduli GRH substitute. Only useful if your matrix entries can be averaged over arithmetic-progression moduli, which the shift structure log n does not obviously allow.
items.corrected_statement: The statement (A>0, Q = x^{1/2}(log x)^{-B}, bound c x (log x)^{-A}) is confirmed. But 'no improvement of the exponent 1/2 is known' is only true for the full unrestricted statement (all moduli, arbitrary residue classes, no weights). For restricted settings levels above 1/2 are PROVEN: Maynard (arXiv 2006.07088) level 3/5 for well-factorable weights; Maynard arXiv 2006.06572 moduli to x^{11/21} for a fixed residue class; Lichtman (arXiv 2309.08522) 66/107 ~ 0.617 for triply well-factorable weights, 5/8 conditional on Selberg eigenvalue conjecture. The original BFI result was 4/7 (as quoted in Maynard's abstract). Original authors/year (1965) were not checked against a primary source.
items.corrected_status: PROVEN (BV, level 1/2 for the general statement); 'exponent 1/2 never improved' REFUTED for weighted/restricted variants
items.check_evidence: https://teorth.github.io/optimizationproblems/constants/66a.html : 'For any fixed A>0, there exist constants c=c(A) and B=B(A)... Q=x^{1/2}(log x)^{-B}'; 'best established range currently is 1/2 <= C_66 <= 1'. https://ar5iv.arxiv.org/html/2006.07088 (search result): moduli as large as x^{3/5-eps} with well-factorable weights. https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.08522 (search result): level 66/107, 'improves on the prior record level 3/5'.

items.name: Green-Tao 2004/08 and Green-Tao-Ziegler 2012: arbitrarily long APs in the primes; inverse theorem for Gowers norms; Hardy-Littlewood for finite-complexity linear systems
items.statement: The primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions (transference principle + Szemeredi + Goldston-Yildirim pseudorandom majorant). Green-Tao-Ziegler: inverse theorem for the U^{s+1}[N] norm for all s>=3; combined with earlier work this implies the Hardy-Littlewood prime tuples conjecture for any linear system of finite complexity (asymptotic count). Annals of Mathematics 176 (2012) 1231-1372.
items.authors_year: B. Green, T. Tao, arXiv math/0404188 (2004); B. Green, T. Tao, T. Ziegler, arXiv 1009.3998, Ann. of Math. 176 (2012)
items.quote_or_locator: GTZ abstract (fetch): 'Combined with earlier results, the authors note this implies the Hardy-Littlewood prime tuples conjecture for any linear system of finite complexity.' Green-Tao abstract: 'We prove that there are arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions of primes.' (https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0404188).
items.fit_T1_T7: T5 yes (correlations of primes along linear forms), T1 yes; T3/T4 fail: asymptotic counts, not signs; cancellation is exploited in L^infty-type structural form.
items.relevance: Establishes that finite-complexity linear correlations of Lambda are asymptotically what the random model predicts. Your K entries are two-point correlations at shifts log n, which are of infinite complexity in the relevant range, so these theorems do not apply directly. Still the most precise proven statements on correlations between different primes.

items.name: Beurling barrier: Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer 2006 and Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas 2020
items.statement: There are Beurling generalized number systems with regular integer counting function N(x) but with prime counting function strongly oscillating, with zeta having infinitely many zeros near sigma = 1 - a/log t and none to the right (Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer, Math. Ann. 334 (2006) 1-36). Conversely Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas construct a Beurling system satisfying RH, with pi(x)=Li(x)+O(sqrt x), whose integer counting function oscillates: N(x)=rho x + Omega_{+-}(x exp(-c sqrt(log x loglog x))).
items.authors_year: H. Diamond, H. Montgomery, U. Vorhauer (2006); F. Broucke, G. Debruyne, J. Vindas, Adv. Math. 370 (2020), arXiv 2004.11501
items.quote_or_locator: 'We construct a Beurling generalized number system satisfying the Riemann hypothesis' and 'pi(x) = Li(x) + O(sqrt x)' (fetch of arXiv abstract page); DMV statement from a search-result summary of https://deepblue.lib.umich.edu/items/80a3d22b-2022-435e-9bcb-360f281fb998 (DOI 10.1007/s00208-005-0638-2), which I did not open.
items.fit_T1_T7: This is the benchmark for T7: any property shared by all Beurling systems with the same density cannot prove RH. Also shows RH-type bounds on pi(x) do not control N(x), so a prime-side sign must use the multiplicative/integer structure, not the density of the primes.
items.relevance: Pin-points what the sign must use: not the Chebyshev/Mertens-type facts (which hold for Beurling primes with such densities), but arithmetic structure of Z (the specific correlations of Lambda, the Gamma term, the functional equation). The Alpoge-Furman authors use exactly such Beurling controls (with planted off-line zeros) to test mechanisms.

The same argument is not available for Spec Z because Spec Z x Spec Z = Spec Z is one-dimensional.

critic:
**Answer first.** The atlas is strong on size bounds and on barriers. It is thin in exactly the three places our tool needs: proven prime-side correlations, positivity by structure (not by size), and the number-field analogue of Weil's Hodge-index sign. Several statuses are inconsistent between domains. The one item to fix first is Davenport–Heilbronn (DH) (item 2c below).

## (1) Missing landmark classes (max 15)

Sources are the URLs from my searches. Everything else is marked «не проверено» (unverified).

1. **Averaged Hardy–Littlewood for prime pairs (Mikawa; Perelli–Pintz; Bombieri–Davenport tradition).** This is the only proven unconditional statement about Λ(n)Λ(n+h), the correlation between different primes (T5). It holds on average over h, with a small exceptional set.
   - It is also the "BHP-like" proven side of Goldston–Montgomery. The atlas has only the conditional side.
   - Source: https://www.numdam.org/item/CM_1992__82_3_355_0/ (Perelli–Pintz, Compositio 82 (1992) 355–372). Search snippet: "Hardy–Littlewood asymptotic ... for all but a small exceptional set of even shifts h".
   - The exponent range X^{1/3+ε} ≤ H ≤ X came from garbled OCR. «не проверено».
2. **Rudnick–Sarnak n-level correlations of zeros (Duke 1996), plus Hughes–Rudnick and Katz–Sarnak.** These are proven for test functions with restricted Fourier support, and they are derived from prime sums. This is the prime-pair → zero-statistics bridge.
   - Source: https://portal.mardi4nfdi.de/wiki/Publication:1919610. Survey: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.00595v1.
   - Degrees n ≥ 4 are conditional on "Hypothesis H". A 2025 claim to remove it (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.20653) is «не проверено».
3. **Speiser (1934) and Levinson–Montgomery (1974): RH ⟺ ζ′ has no zeros in 0<σ<1/2.** Levinson–Montgomery also show that ζ and ζ′ have equally many zeros there, up to O(log T).
   - It is a proven, RH-equivalent bridge between a *derivative-type* object and the zero locations. It matters for our case because the Markov renewal series is −ζ′/ζ-structured (see item 3).
   - Sources: https://projecteuclid.org/download/pdf_1/euclid.acta/1485889821 and https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.03064v1. Quote: "The Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to ζ′(s) having no zeros in 0 < σ < 1/2."
4. **Krein extension / Carathéodory–Toeplitz / Bochner–Schoenberg theory of positive-definite functions on an interval.** Window positivity of K is positive-definiteness of a distribution on (−L, L).
   - The atlas has Bochner only inside the Weil criterion. Krein's extension theorem says: positive definite on an interval ⟹ extends to ℝ. That is a lossless structural statement.
   - «не проверено» (no source opened).
5. **de Branges spaces, Hermite–Biehler, and Lagarias's Li-type positivity.**
   - Present only as a passing mention in the project memory ("SUPPORT = Hermite–Biehler/Lagarias = RH"). The atlas has no entry.
   - «не проверено».
6. **Li's criterion, Nyman–Beurling–Báez-Duarte, Robin.** These are RH-equivalent positive-definite Gram-matrix criteria.
   - Three of the four checkers list them as missing.
   - Why they matter: Nyman–Beurling is a Gram-matrix positivity with an explicit lattice of arithmetic data. It is the closest "lossless Gram" cousin of K.
   - «не проверено».
7. **Arithmetic Hodge index / Arakelov positivity (Faltings–Hriljac; Moriwaki) and Deninger's program, Connes' adèle class space, F_1-geometry.** This is the number-field analogue of the mechanism that proves Weil's RH for curves (positivity from intersection theory, no zeros involved, so no circularity).
   - The atlas has the function-field proof but nothing on its failed or open number-field lift.
   - «не проверено», no source opened.
8. **Mean-value theorems for Dirichlet polynomials (Montgomery–Vaughan 1974) as quantitative orthogonality of p^{it}, and Selberg's central limit theorem for log ζ.**
   - They give proven near-orthogonality of distinct primes in t-averages, with an exact diagonal term.
   - Why they are not enough: they are size bounds (fail T3 and T4). But they define the correct baseline for "what cancellation between primes is provable".
   - «не проверено».
9. **Rankin–Selberg / Selberg orthogonality for GL(n) (proven for automorphic cases).**
   - The atlas lists only the *conjectures* A and B. Rankin–Selberg gives proven Σ_p a(p) conj b(p)/p asymptotics for pairs of L-functions.
   - «не проверено».
10. **Bilinear (Type II) forms: Linnik dispersion; Duke–Friedlander–Iwaniec bilinear Kloosterman-fraction estimates.** These are the proven tools that see two primes jointly. They are lossy.
    - Only the Vaughan identity is in the atlas.
    - «не проверено».
11. **Explicit PNT remainder in the style of Rosser–Schoenfeld / Dusart / Platt–Trudgian / Fiori–Kadiri–Swidinsky.** This gives a computable sign-safe envelope on [0, X]. Our "no slack" requirement (T4) rules it out, but it is the standard comparison point.
    - Three checkers list it. «не проверено».
12. **Levinson-type and Selberg-class converse theorems (Hamburger; Hecke; Kaczorowski–Perelli).** They state what the functional equation alone fixes. They are needed to say which of "Euler product" and "functional equation" a tool actually uses.
    - «не проверено».
13. **Ng, Gonek–Montgomery, Gallagher: true size of (ψ(x)−x)/√x and its moments.** They connect the prime-side variance to the zero side. «не проверено».
14. **Beurling PNT positive theory (Diamond–Zhang monograph).** The atlas has the counterexamples but not the positive theory that says which hypotheses the Beurling barrier does and does not constrain.
    - «не проверено».
15. **Guth–Maynard (2024), published in Annals per a search listing, and zero-density → short-interval primes.** The atlas lists it in some domains but not in all. Only "proven/size" matters here. «не проверено» for the publication status.

Note on the sign requirement. Only one prime-side sign datum in the entire atlas is *used*, which is Λ ≥ 0 (de la Vallée Poussin's 3 + 4cos t + cos 2t; Landau's lemma). Everything in the Markov picture is the same datum. The atlas should say so explicitly.

## (2) Overclaimed or misclassified items

a. **Inconsistent `gives` for the same theorem across domains.**
   - Littlewood is SIGN in the distribution domain and BARRIER in the multiplicative one.
   - Rubinstein–Sarnak is SIGN in the distribution domain and SIZE in the progressions one.
   - Tao's logarithmically averaged Chowla is SIZE in the sieve and patterns domains and STRUCTURE in the frontier one.
   - Selberg's Λ² sieve is SIGN in the sieve domain and SIZE in the multiplicative one. The *device* is a sign by squaring, but the *output* is a size bound.
   - The Weil-type items are inconsistent in the same way.
   - Fix: split `gives` into "mechanism" (sign by squares, by positivity of coefficients) and "output" (size, existence, equivalence).

b. **Davenport–Heilbronn verdicts conflict.** The zeros domain says REFUTED, the multiplicative domain says UNVERIFIED, and the barriers domain says CONFIRMED.
   - REFUTED looks wrong. A 2024 arXiv paper says "in the late 90s, A. Selberg proved that a positive proportion of non-trivial zeros of the Davenport–Heilbronn function lie on the critical line" (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.18492 or https://arxiv.org/html/2501.00551v1; my search snippet was cut off, so I do not know which of the two carries the sentence).
   - Voronin and Karatsuba lower bounds are also in the search results (https://www.mathnet.ru/eng/cheb850).
   - Recommended status: «не проверено», not REFUTED.
   - The barrier use of DH (functional equation without Euler product, off-line zeros exist) is the safe part. The "positive proportion on the line" part needs the primary Selberg source.

c. **Alpoge–Furman 2026 (AI-generated, unrefereed).** It is the nearest neighbour of our problem: a rank-trace argument on a finite compression of the Weil form.
   - It must not carry a "barrier" label ("band-width 1", "two thirds = all") as if proven. Your own checkers mark those quotes UNVERIFIED for v2.
   - Lamzouri's competing proof is also unrefereed.
   - Both should have status PREPRINT, with "gives: TOOL" for the claim only, and no downstream use.

d. **Bombieri 2000 `lossless: true`.** The "lossless" tag and the circularity reading are the item author's. Mark them as interpretation.

e. **Yoshida 1992 "only genuine unconditional K ≥ 0".** This is overstated. Bombieri's re-proof and Zhu's certified computation (preprint) also exist.

f. **Zhu 2026, "Passing the resulting wall thus requires cancellation in the prime comb".** The atlas treats it as a claim, but it is the author's own abstract wording. Also check the support figures: the zeros domain says 1.6 and the multiplicative domain says [−0.8, 0.8] (consistent only if the support is a full width of 1.6).

g. **Beurling YES/NO columns.** They are inferences by the item authors in at least four domains (zeros, frontier, multiplicative, sieve).
   - A concrete problem: the Diamond–Montgomery–Vorhauer (DMV) barrier has *no functional equation and no Γ-factor*. Our K has both.
   - So the Beurling barrier does not kill tools that use the Γ-terms. It kills tools that use only Λ ≥ 0 plus PNT-level data. Say this in the atlas.

h. **Weil criterion date.** It is 1952, not 1941/48 (already flagged by one checker).

i. **Primary papers not opened for most "CONFIRMED" items.** CONFIRMED means "consistent with a secondary source" here. Rename the verdict class.

## (3) The one question the atlas does not answer

**Is there a proven, zero-free, exact representation of the window-localized renewal measure of the prime walk, with its pole term carrying its sign?**

Why this is the question. This is my own derivation. I did not find it in any source, so treat it as предположение.

- For fixed v the form ⟨v, Kv⟩ is *linear* in Λ. Correlations between different primes can enter only through resolvent or Neumann-series terms. These are the k-fold Dirichlet convolutions Λ^{*k}(n)/√n, which are ≥ 0 termwise. That is exactly the "C_n ≥ 0" structure.
- The generating function of the walk is Σ_k (−ζ′/ζ)^k = 1/(1+ζ′/ζ) = ζ/(ζ+ζ′), up to the shift s → s+½ for the 1/√n weight. It converges only where |ζ′/ζ| < 1.
- Its singularities are the zeros of ζ+ζ′ = e^{−s}(e^{s}ζ)′. These are neither the zeros of ζ nor of ζ′.
- Speiser and Levinson–Montgomery (item 3 above) are the nearest proven theorems. They address ζ′, not ζ+ζ′.

So the missing atlas entry is a theorem of the following type, proven from the Euler product alone with no use of zeros:

- a sign for Σ_{k≥1} Λ^{*k}(n)/√n summed over n in a window, after subtraction of the pole contribution at s = 1, and
- the location of zeros of ζ+ζ′ relative to Re s = ½.

Cheapest probe, which I did not run. For m = 40..120 and small windows, compare the arb-computed truncated Σ_k Λ^{*k} mass with the residue term. See whether s_E and s_O keep their signs for k up to a modest bound.

- ЕСЛИ_A (the signs persist and the partial sums are monotone): the Markov/renewal picture gives a one-sided finite certificate. The remaining question is the pole's rank-2 correction.
- ЕСЛИ_B (the partial sums fluctuate at the 1e-3 level seen in the entropy probe): the renewal series is not the sign carrier. Go back to the Krein/Gram route (items 4–6).

## Gaps and conflicts

- I opened no primary papers. Everything above rests on search snippets and on your checkers' reports.
- Statements about Guth–Maynard, Alpoge–Furman, Lamzouri and Rezvyakova are from the checkers or from search snippets only. «не проверено».
- Conflicting verdicts for DH and for Rubinstein–Sarnak are listed in (2b) and (2a).

Sources: [Levinson–Montgomery, Acta](https://projecteuclid.org/download/pdf_1/euclid.acta/1485889821), [Garunkštis–Tamošiūnas arXiv:1902.03064](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.03064v1), [Rudnick–Sarnak entry](https://portal.mardi4nfdi.de/wiki/Publication:1919610), [Rudnick–Sarnak survey arXiv:2002.00595](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.00595v1), [On Hypothesis H arXiv:2507.20653](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.20653), [Perelli–Pintz, Compositio 82](https://www.numdam.org/item/CM_1992__82_3_355_0/), [DH zeros, Chebyshevskii Sbornik](https://www.mathnet.ru/eng/cheb850), [Rezvyakova arXiv:2411.18492](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.18492), [arXiv:2501.00551](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.00551v1).
synthesis:
# Синтез атласа: какое доказанное свойство простых может дать знак

**Как читать.** Здесь только пункты с вердиктом CONFIRMED или CORRECTED, в исправленной формулировке. Непроверенное помечено «не проверено». Вердикт CONFIRMED значит «согласуется со вторичным источником». Первоисточники открыты не везде. Столбец «Бёрлинг» часто содержит вывод авторов карточек, а не теорему. Такие места помечены.

**Термины, один раз.**
- **Обобщённые простые Бёрлинга** — произвольный набор «простых» с эйлеровым произведением, но без арифметики настоящих целых чисел. Из них собирают «целые» и строят свою дзета-функцию.
- **Эйлерово произведение** — запись дзета-функции через произведение по простым.
- **Функциональное уравнение и Γ-множитель** — симметрия s ↔ 1−s и архимедова часть. В нашей матрице K они есть.
- **Знак против размера** — знак отвечает «≥ 0 или нет». Размер отвечает «насколько велико».
- **Без потерь** — точное тождество или точное представление без запаса. У нас запаса нет, поля ~1e-29.

---

## 1. Ответ одним абзацем

Доказанные свойства простых, дающие настоящий знак, есть, но все они не годятся для знака s_E ≤ 0, s_O ≥ 0 на всех окнах сразу. Вот эти свойства.
- Неотрицательность Λ(n) вместе с неравенством 3+4cos t+cos 2t = 2(1+cos t)² ≥ 0.
- Лемма Ландау о неотрицательных коэффициентах.
- Квадраты Сельберга (Σλ_d)² ≥ 0.
- Положительность логарифмических коэффициентов в стиле Рэнкина и Ленглендса.
- Положительность Вейля через эффективные циклы для кривых над конечным полем.
- Положительность Йошиды на малых окнах.

Каждое из них упирается в одну из четырёх стен.
1. Свойство верно в любой системе Бёрлинга. Тогда оно останавливается у зоны без нулей σ ≥ 1−c/log t, потому что Diamond–Montgomery–Vorhauer построили систему с этой зоной, где RH ложна.
2. Знак получается только как одностороннее неравенство с потерей множителя 2 (проблема чётности Сельберга).
3. Нужна геометрия поверхности C×C с конусом эффективных циклов. Над Z её нет.
4. Положительность доказана только для малых окон (Йошида: 2L ≤ log 2).

Доказанные свойства, которые видят корреляции разных простых, дают только асимптотику или среднее с потерей. К ним относятся Tao, Tao–Teräväinen, Green–Tao–Ziegler, Bombieri–Vinogradov и Maynard. Из них нельзя вытянуть знак при запасе 1e-29. Точные тождества (явная формула Вейля, подсчёт отрицательных собственных значений у Bombieri 2000) работают без потерь, но содержат сумму по нулям. Знак слева через них становится знаком суммы по нулям, то есть RH. Итог: сегодня нет доказанного свойства простых, которое даёт знак для всех окон. Ближе всего идея разложения «явный положительный член + сумма неотрицательных членов» (правило 18 проекта), построенного из эйлерова произведения и Γ-члена вместе.

---

## 3. Главный урок барьера: что нельзя доказать и что обязано быть в любом доказательстве

**Бёрлинг (эйлерово произведение плюс регулярные целые).**
- Diamond–Montgomery–Vorhauer (Math. Ann. 334 (2006), 1–36). Для 1/2 < θ < 1 есть система с N(x) = ρx + O(x^θ). У неё π(x) = Li(x) + Ω(x·exp(−c√log x)). Её дзета имеет бесконечно много нулей на кривой σ = 1 − a/log t, правее нулей нет, a > (4/e)(1−θ). RH для неё ложна. Саму статью мы не открывали, содержание взято из введения Broucke–Debruyne–Vindas и из карточки с аннотацией.
- Zhang (Math. Ann. 337 (2007), 671–704). Есть системы с RH и с регулярными целыми. Ошибки там порядка x^{1/2+ε}.
- Broucke–Debruyne–Vindas (Adv. Math. 370 (2020), 107240). Система с RH, π(x) = Li(x) + O(√x). Колебание целых при этом порядка x·exp(−c√(log x log log x)), c > 2√2. Эта точная форма записана по извлечению текста PDF. Её стоит сверить по оригиналу.
- Broucke–Vindas (Math. Z., 2024). RH-системы с ошибкой простых O(1) и O(log log x). RH-подобная регулярность простых не говорит ничего об арифметике.
- Hilberdink–Neamah (Int. J. Number Theory 16 (2020), 1005–1011). Два наибольших из α, β, γ равны и ≥ 1/2. Это верно для всех систем.
- Hilberdink–Lapidus (Acta Appl. Math. 94 (2006), 21–48). Аналог эквивалентности «RH ⟺ ошибка ψ(x)−x» верен в любой системе Бёрлинга. Вывод: круговорот «знак простой стороны = знак нулей» не артефакт Z.

**Вывод 1.** Любой довод, который использует только эйлерово произведение, Λ ≥ 0 и регулярность счётных функций, не докажет RH для Z. Есть системы с теми же аксиомами, где RH ложна.

**Davenport–Heilbronn.**
- Davenport–Heilbronn (1936). Дзета Гурвица ζ(s,a) при трансцендентном a или рациональном a ≠ 1/2 имеет бесконечно много нулей при σ > 1. Идея доказательства — теорема эквивалентности Бора (в изложении Bombieri–Ghosh): фазы простых можно подкручивать свободно.
- Saias–Weingartner (Acta Arith. 140 (2009), 335–344). Если ряд с периодическими коэффициентами не имеет вида P(s)·L_χ(s), то в полосе 1/2 < σ₁ < σ₂ < 1+η число нулей порядка T. Остаётся только одно направление. Равносильность «нулей при σ > 1 нет ⟺ P·L_χ» неверна: у 1+3·2^{−s} нули лежат при σ = log₂3 > 1.
- Righetti (2015). Любой «непростой» многочлен от функций с эйлеровым произведением, при выполнении ортогональности Сельберга, имеет бесконечно много нулей при σ > 1.
- Подробности для конкретной комбинации по модулю 5 (нули вне прямой, доля нулей на прямой) — **не проверено**. На них мы не опираемся.

**Вывод 2.** Функциональное уравнение и Γ-множитель без эйлерова произведения тоже не дают RH. Эйлерово произведение нужно как произведение, чтобы фазы простых были связаны мультипликативностью.

**Важная тонкость.** У систем Бёрлинга DMV нет ни функционального уравнения, ни Γ-множителя. У нашей K они есть. Поэтому барьер Бёрлинга не убивает инструменты, использующие Γ-члены. Он убивает инструменты, использующие только Λ ≥ 0 и данные уровня ПТЧ.

**Что обязан использовать любой доказательный ингредиент.**
1. Эйлерово произведение и мультипликативность (уроки DH, Saias–Weingartner, Righetti).
2. Γ-член и функциональное уравнение (урок DMV).
3. Совместное использование обоих, в одной и той же квадратичной форме. Выполнима ли RH из пары «эйлерово произведение + функциональное уравнение»? В классе Сельберга GRH остаётся гипотезой. Hilberdink–Lapidus прямо пишут, что полного ответа на вопрос о функциональном уравнении у систем Бёрлинга они не дают. Контрпримера к RH с обеими структурами мы не нашли, но это отсутствие свидетельств, а не теорема.
4. Свойство, которого нет у случайных простых. Это наш вывод, не теорема. Основания: Zhang показывает, что RH-подобная малость ошибки достигается случайным выбором. Maier показывает, что настоящие простые скоррелированы через малые простые. Zhu, Замечание 1.6, называет открытую лемму: количественная невозможность выстроить фазы (t·log p)_p в одну сторону, то есть одновременное диофантово приближение для {log p}. Она должна быть специфична для Z. Qualitative-теоремы типа Вейля тут не хватает, они выполняются и для обычных Q-независимых логарифмов.

Оговорка по Zhu. Барьер Теоремы 1.4 относится только к сертификатам, ограничивающим гребёнку поточечно. Это не общий барьер на путь через положительность. Цитата «Passing the resulting wall thus requires cancellation in the prime comb, a concrete arithmetic problem» — формулировка самого автора, не теорема.

## 4. Шорт-лист: до 5 кандидатов для знака s_E, s_O

Все проверки предложены, но не запускались. Параметры m = 2..12 берутся из ваших матриц K_m.

**1. Представление без нулей: m = B₀ + Σ C_n, C_n ≥ 0 (правило 18), через свёртки Λ^{*k}(n)/√n.**
- *Почему может сработать.* При фиксированном v форма <v,Kv> линейна по Λ. Корреляции разных простых входят только через k-кратные свёртки Λ^{*k}/√n ≥ 0. Это ровно структура C_n ≥ 0. Образец знакового механизма — лемма Ландау и приём Рэнкина.
- *Предположение (наш вывод, не источник).* Производящая функция Σ_k(−ζ'/ζ)^k = ζ/(ζ+ζ'), с точностью до сдвига s→s+½. Она сходится только где |ζ'/ζ| < 1. Особенности — нули ζ+ζ', а не нули ζ или ζ'. Ближайшие доказанные теоремы — Speiser (1934) и Levinson–Montgomery (1974): RH ⟺ ζ' не имеет нулей при 0 < σ < ½. Они **не проверено** по первоисточникам.
- *Что нужно.* Теорема из одного эйлерова произведения: знак суммы Σ_{k≥1} Λ^{*k}(n)/√n по окну после вычитания полюса при s=1. Положение нулей ζ+ζ' относительно Re s = ½.
- *Первая проверка.* Для m=2..12 и K=1..K_max посчитать в arb усечённую сумму по k ≤ K и сравнить с вкладом полюса. Смотреть, сохраняют ли s_E, s_O знак при росте K и монотонны ли частичные суммы.
  - ЕСЛИ_A (знак сохраняется, суммы монотонны): появляется односторонний конечный сертификат. Остаётся поправка ранга 2 от полюса.
  - ЕСЛИ_B (колебания порядка 1e-3, как в зонде энтропии на m=40..120): ряд перенормировки не несёт знак. Перейти к кандидату 2.

**2. Разложение «явный положительный член + неотрицательные» по образцу Вейля для функциональных полей.**
- *Почему.* Там знак получается так. Добавляют главный дивизор, цикл Z становится эффективным (целые неотрицательные кратности). Дальше Tr(Z·Z') = d'(Z)·Δ + Y, Y эффективен, и оценка (4g−2)d' − (4g−4)d' = 2d'(Z) ≥ 0 даёт знак. Структура «одно положительное направление, остальное отрицательно» (индекс 1) похожа на наш расклад: полюс ранга 2 плюс PF-блок с одним отрицательным уровнем в G_E.
- *Что нужно.* Аналог эффективного конуса над Z. Connes–Consani–Marcolli прямо пишут, что аналог главных дивизоров остаётся открытым вопросом.
- *Первая проверка.* Для m=2..12 взять подпространство полюса ранга 2 и ограничить K на его ортогональное дополнение. Проверить, определена ли ограниченная форма (критерий индекса 1: есть x с Q(x,x) > 0 и Q ≤ 0 на x^⊥). Сравнить запас ограниченной формы с s_E, s_O. Отдельно проверить в подходящем базисе, образует ли −(PF-блок) Z-матрицу (внедиагональные элементы одного знака).

**3. Перенос Connes–van Suijlekom: простое чётное основное состояние ⇒ вещественные нули преобразования Фурье собственной функции.**
- *Почему.* Ваш PF-блок даёт ровно такую гипотезу: простое изолированное чётное нижнее собственное значение. Теорема в аннотации: тогда все нули преобразования Фурье собственной функции вещественны. Доказательство: Carathéodory–Fejér для тёплицевых матриц, затем теорема Гурвица.
- *Статус.* Препринт (arXiv 2511.23257), доказательство не читано, **не проверено**. Выдача о применимости к системам Бёрлинга и о «PF-типе» — вывод карточки, не источник.
- *Ограничение.* Теорема выполняется для любого распределения. Сама по себе она вещественности нулей ζ не даёт. Нужен мост от нулей собственной функции к нулям ζ. Он эквивалентен RH по силе.
- *Первая проверка.* Для m=2..12 в секторах E и O: простота и зазор нижнего собственного значения, чётность и PF-положительность собственного вектора, вещественность нулей его преобразования Фурье (численно, в arb).

**4. Усреднённые корреляции простых (Type II / билинейные формы, Tao, Matomäki–Radziwiłł, Green–Sawhney) как оценка перекрёстных членов p ≠ q.**
- *Почему.* Это единственный доказанный класс, который видит корреляции разных простых. Для Green–Sawhney (p²+nq²) асимптотика с ошибкой (log log N)²/log N, но статус «не проверено» (формулу не читали).
- *Что нужно.* Знак не получится, только размер перекрёстных членов.
- *Первая проверка.* Для m=2..12 разделить <v,Kv> на диагональ (p=q) и перекрёстные члены (p≠q). Сравнить их размер с запасом 1e-29. Если перекрёстные члены много больше запаса, никакая потеря log^{-A} не годится, и от размерных оценок можно отказаться окончательно.

**5. Неспособность выстроить фазы гребёнки: Zhu, Замечание 1.6.**
- *Почему.* Это точно сформулированная недостающая лемма о Z-специфичной диофантовой структуре {log p}. Сама форма Zhu разделяет полюс ранга 1 и смену знака в нечётном секторе, что совпадает с вашим расщеплением E/O.
- *Что нужно.* Количественное утверждение, что (t·log p)_p не могут одновременно выстроиться. Формально оно того же рода, что и информация в нулях.
- *Первая проверка.* Для m=2..12 найти sup_t гребёнки P_L(t) на фактическом носителе и сравнить с A_L. Посмотреть, на каком t мультипликатор Ψ_L(t) = Re ψ(¼+it/2) − log π − P_L(t) достигает минимума. Совпадение порядка запаса с таблицей Zhu (5,88e-30 при L=1,0, нормировки не сравнивали) — **не проверено**.

**Порядок.** 1, 2, 3, 5, 4. Кандидат 1 дешевле всего проверить и сразу различает ветки. Кандидат 2 — единственный с доказанным аналогом знака, но без перевода на Z. Кандидат 3 даёт структуру, но не мост. Кандидаты 5 и 4 определяют, что именно недостаёт.

---

## 5. Проверка фактов из памяти наблюдателя

**von Koch 1901 — ИСПРАВЛЕНО.**
- Верно: RH ⟺ ψ(x) − x = O(x^{1/2+ε}) при каждом ε > 0 (Ng 2025, ф. 1.3). RH ⇒ ψ(x) − x = O(√x log² x). Значит, ψ(x) − x = O(√x log² x) ⟺ RH.
- Статья: von Koch, Acta Math. 24 (1901), 159–182.
- Расхождение источников. Ng в тексте пишет «1905», но ссылается на работу 1901 года. Wikipedia пишет 1901. Принять 1901.
- Форму π(x) = li(x) + O(√x log x) как эквивалент RH цитируют, но саму цитату не видели. Для π-формы «RH ⇒» подтверждена, «эквивалентно» — не проверено.

**Сельберг, Λ² и чётность — ИСПРАВЛЕНО.**
- Формула симметрии. (1/N)Σ_{n≤N} Λ₂(n) = 2 log N (1+o(1)), где Λ₂ = Λ·log + Λ*Λ = μ*log² (McNamara, Теорема 2.5). Эквивалентно ψ(x) log x + Σ Λ(n) ψ(x/n) = 2x log x + O(x).
- Исправление ссылки. Сельберг, Canad. J. Math. 2 (1950), 66–78 — это про ПТЧ в прогрессиях. Erdős: J. Indian Math. Soc. 13 (1949), 131–144. Работа Сельберга в Annals of Math. 50 (1949) 305–313 — по памяти, не проверено.
- Сито Λ² (квадрат делительной суммы). a(n) = (Σ_{d|n}λ_d)² ≥ 0 при λ₁ = 1 — неравенство и квадратичная форма подтверждены по обзору Soundararajan, уравнения (5)–(6). Страницы оригинала 1947 года (64–67) — только из Wikipedia.
- Проблема чётности. Названа Сельбергом в 1949 г. Пример a_n = 1 + λ(n) (Ford 2005; Maynard, ICM 2022). Любая верхняя оценка ситом для простых промахивается минимум вдвое. Из чистых ситовых данных нет нетривиальной нижней оценки — подтверждено.
- Bombieri (1975–76): асимптотика для Σ a_n f(n) верна ⟺ f одинаково весит числа с чётным и нечётным числом простых делителей. У Λ_k, k ≥ 2, это есть. У самой Λ — нет. Ford 2005 (Trans. AMS 357, 1663–1674): R(ν) при любом фиксированном ν < 1 для этого недостаточно.

**Green–Tao — ПОДТВЕРЖДЕНО.**
- arXiv math/0404188, апрель 2004 г., v6 сентябрь 2007, Annals of Math. 167 (2008), 481–547.
- Три ингредиента: теорема Семереди, принцип переноса, мажоранта Goldston–Yıldırım.
- Уточнения. «Linear equations in primes» (Annals 171 (2010), 1753–1850) сама была условной от GI(s) и MN(s). Безусловной она стала вместе с Green–Tao (Annals 175 (2012), 541–566) и GTZ (Annals 176 (2012), 1231–1372). В GTZ исправлена ошибка (Lemma 13.2). То, что веса мажоранты — квадраты Сельберга, в аннотации не сказано, не проверено.

**Bombieri–Vinogradov — ИСПРАВЛЕНО.**
- Утверждение. Для любого A > 0: Σ_{q≤Q} max_{(a,q)=1} sup_{y≤x} |ψ(y;q,a) − y/φ(q)| ≪_A x (log x)^{−A} + x^{1/2} Q (log xQ)^6 (по заметкам Vaughan). Отсюда уровень ½: Q = x^{1/2}(log x)^{−B}. Годы 1965, Bombieri (Mathematika 12) и A. I. Vinogradov (Izv. AN SSSR 29 (1965)). Номера страниц у Bombieri не проверены.
- Исправление. Фраза «выше ½ ничего не известно» верна лишь для общего утверждения (все модули, все классы, без весов). Для частных случаев уровень выше ½ доказан: Zhang (гладкие модули); Polymath 8a: 1/2+7/300; Stadlmann: 1/2+1/40, принято в Adv. Math.; Maynard: 3/5 для хорошо факторизуемых весов (Mem. AMS 306 (2025)). Lichtman: 66/107, препринт, не проверено. Метка «форма Галлахера» источниками не подтверждена.
- Гипотеза Эллиотта–Хальберстама. Для θ = 1 ложна (Friedlander–Granville, Annals 129 (1989), 363–382).

**Цитата Zhu 2026 — ПОДТВЕРЖДЕНО (препринт).**
- arXiv 2608.24827 v2 (2 сентября 2026), один автор, без рецензии. Слово в слово из текста PDF: «Passing the resulting wall thus requires cancellation in the prime comb, a concrete arithmetic problem.»
- Окно [−0,8; 0,8] подтверждено: Q(f) ≥ 8,9·10⁻¹⁸‖f‖₂², носитель автокорреляции 1,6, то есть 2,3 классического диапазона. Для нечётных f в сертификате Q ≥ 8,2·10⁻¹⁵ (Раздел 6).
- Утверждение первой версии о носителе 2,38 автор сам отозвал (Замечание 3.3).
- Расчёт мы не пересчитывали. Закон затухания −ln λ*(L) подобран, а не выведен. Это слова автора.
- Suzuki 2606.09096 численного окна не называет. Теорема 1.4 лишь «при достаточно малом a > 0» с асимптотикой нижнего собственного значения. Любое окно, приписанное Suzuki в задании, **не проверено**.

Он сразу различает ветки: при ЕСЛИ_A появляется односторонний сертификат, при ЕСЛИ_B идём к кандидату 2 (индекс 1 на дополнении к полюсу). Это ближе всего к цели «самый быстрый путь к доказательству», так как отсекает бесконечный выбор за один прогон.
